title: Coconut Natilla Recipe
instructions: Place 1 cup of milk in a small bowl, add the cornstarch and stir to dissolve it, then set aside.
Place the coconut milk and grated coconut in the blender and blend until smooth and set aside.
Place the rest of the milk and cinnamon sticks in a medium pot and bring the mixture to boil over medium-low heat. When the milk is a little warm, but not boiling, add the coconut mixture.
When the milk starts boiling, add the condensed milk, sugar and salt. Stir well with a wooden spoon. Add the milk and cornstarch mixture and continue stirring constantly.

Add the vanilla extract. Reduce the heat to low and continue stirring until the Natilla thickens, about 10 to 20 minutes. Add the butter, stir and remove from the heat. Discard the cinnamon sticks. Ladle into a serving dish or individual custard cups. Sprinkle cinnamon powder on top and let it cool at room temperature for at least 2 hours. Refrigerate until ready to serve.

title: Ají de Aguacate Recipe (Colombian Spicy Avocado Sauce)
instructions: Place all the ingredients in a food processor. Process until the mixture is well combined.
If the mixture is too thick, add more lime juice until you reach the desired consistency.

title: Colombian Style Stuffed Potatoes
instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut them into chunks, put them in a medium pot and cover with water and ¼ teaspoon of salt.
Bring the potatoes to a boil over medium high heat, then reduce the heat to medium and cook until fork tender about 20 minutes.
Drain the potatoes and mash with a fork or masher and set aside. Filling:

In a large sauce pan, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat and add the onion, tomato, scallions, garlic, cumin, azafran, pepper and salt. Cook for 5 minutes or until the onions are translucent, add the beef and cook stirring occasionally about 10 – 15 minutes. Set aside to cool.

In a medium bowl place all the batter ingredients and whisk until smooth and set aside.
To Form the Stuffed Potatoes

Divide the potato mash into 10 equal sized portions, about ⅓ cup each, and form each portion into a ball by rolling between the palms of your hands. Flatten into patties and place 1 ½ tablespoons of the filling in the center of each one. Shape the potato mixture with the filling into balls to enclose the filling completely.
Fill a large heavy pot with vegetable oil and heat over medium-high heat to 360° F.
Dip the stuffed potato into the batter and carefully place them in the hot oil and fry for about 4 minutes or until golden, turning over halfway through.
Remove the potatoes from the oil using a slotted spoon and drain in a plate with paper towels.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve with Ají.
Notes

title: Achiote Oil (Aceite Achiotado) Recipe
instructions: Heat the vegetable or olive oil and Achiote seeds in a small skillet over medium heat for about 2 to 3 minutes.

title: Chuletas de Cerdo a la Criolla (Pork Chops in Creole Sauce)

Divide the chops among plates, spoon the sauce over the top, add the cilantro and serve immediately.

title: Almojábanas (Colombian Cheese Bread)

Mix the masarepa and cheese in a food processor.
Add the remaining ingredients and mix well.
Divide into 8 equal-size portions and shape into a ball.

title: Creamy Mustard Chicken
instructions: Pat the chicken dry and season the pieces with salt, pepper and paprika.

title: Chicken in Orange Sauce Recipe (Pollo a la Naranja)

title: Creamy Corn Soup Recipe
instructions: Place the corn, water, chicken or vegetable bouillon, garlic, salt, pepper, cilantro, potatoes and scallions in a large pot and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium low and simmer for approximately 4 minutes or until the corn is tender.

title: Breaded Steak Recipe (Lomo de Res Apanado)
instructions: Place each piece of steak in between two large pieces of plastic and using a mallet, pound it until it is about ¼″ to ½″ thick. Place the pounded steak in a glass container, add the aliños sauce and let it rest for about 3 hours or overnight in the fridge.

title: Papas Chorreadas Recipe (Potatoes with Cream and Cheese Sauce)

title: Tamal De Maicena
instructions: Preheat the oven at 350F.
In a non-stick medium pot, add the milk, butter, sugar, and vanilla; bring to a boil, and reduce heat to low.

In a large bowl, add the eggs and the cornstarch and mix well. Slowly add 1 cup of the milk mixture, mixing constantly to temper the eggs. Keep adding more milk until the mixture is soft and has no lumps. ​
Add the mixture to the pot SLOWLY and mix constantly using a wooden spoon.
Keep cooking and mixing for a few more minutes until the mixture gets thick, you will know when it is ready when passing a spoon at the bottom of the pot creates a line that separates the mixture.
Remove from heat and pour into the pyrex (no need to grease it ( I use an 11 by 8-inch pyrex).

title: Pan De Yucca

title: Dulce de Leche Cheesecake with a Maria Cookie Crust.

title: CAFE LA LLAVE ESPRESSO ICE CREAM
instructions: A note about the espresso: I like using the fine ground espresso brick and making the coffee in a regular moka pot, but you can certainly also use the Nespresso style capsules if you have that type of espresso maker.
FULL DISCLOSURE: I personally prefer the decaf espresso, which the Cafe La Llave brand makes to perfection.

In a medium saucepan, heat the cream, milk, sugar and salt over medium heat; whisking to dissolve the sugar (this should take about 4 to 5 minutes).
In a separate bowl, whisk the egg yolks.

Add the tempered egg yolk mix back into the pan while whisking until it just comes to a simmer.
Remove the pan from the heat, then add the vanilla extract and espresso.
you can use any ice cream maker. It doesn’t have to be fancy.

title: Ropa Veija
instructions: Step 1
Cut steak into 4 rectangular pieces. Pat dry with paper towels; season all over with 1 1/2 teaspoons salt. Step 2
In a large pot over medium-high heat, heat 2 tablespoons oil. Working in batches, cook steak until browned on both sides, 5 to 6 minutes. Transfer to a plate. Step 3

In same pot over medium heat, heat remaining 2 tablespoons oil. Cook bell peppers, onion, and 1 1/2 teaspoons salt, stirring occasionally, until slightly softened, 4 to 5 minutes. Add garlic, tomato paste, paprika, cumin, and oregano and cook, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are softened and spices are aromatic, 1 to 2 minutes more. Step 4

Add wine, scraping any browned bits from bottom of pan, and cook, stirring occasionally, until reduced by half, about 2 minutes. Add tomatoes with their juices and bay leaves. Mash down on tomatoes to break up, then nestle beef into stew. Add water to cover beef, if needed, and bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low; cover and simmer until steaks are tender enough to shred, 2 1/2 to 3 hours. Transfer steaks to a plate and finely shred with 2 forks. Step 5
Stir shredded steak back into stew. Bring to a simmer and cook, stirring, until liquid has reduced to a sauce that coats steak, 5 to 10 minutes. Stir in olives; season with salt. Step 6
Spoon ropa vieja over rice and beans. Top with cilantro.

title: Black Bean soup
instructions: Step 1

In a large pot over medium heat, heat oil. Add onion and cook until soft and translucent, about 5 minutes. Add jalapeños and garlic and cook until fragrant, about 2 minutes. Add tomato paste, stir to coat vegetables, and cook about a minute more. Season with salt, pepper, cumin, and chili powder and stir to coat. Step 2

Add black beans and broth. Stir soup, add bay leaf, and bring to a boil. Immediately reduce to a simmer and let simmer until slightly reduced and thickened, 15 to 20 minutes. (If a thinner soup is desired, add more broth as needed.) Step 3
Remove bay leaf and let cool slightly. Using an immersion blender or food processor, blend soup to desired consistency. Step 4
Serve with a dollop of sour cream, sliced avocado, and cilantro.

title: Cuban Sandwich
instructions: Step 1
Place pork chops in a 3-qt. glass baking dish. Using a fork, poke holes into pork all over; season all over with 1 tsp. salt. Drizzle with oil and toss to coat. Step 2
In a small bowl, combine orange zest and juice, lime zest and juice, oregano, pepper, garlic powder, cumin, and onion powder. Add half of marinade to pork and let rest 10 to 15 minutes. Step 3
Meanwhile, arrange a rack in center of oven; preheat to 425°. Add mustard and mayonnaise to remaining marinade and stir until smooth. Step 4
Transfer pork to oven and roast until an instant-read thermometer inserted into thickest part registers 140°, 15 to 20 minutes. Step 5

To build sandwiches, cut loaf in half crosswise, then cut each piece in half lengthwise for 4 pieces total. Spread butter on outside of bread on the top and bottom. Spread mustard mixture on cut sides of bread. On 2 bread pieces, layer each with 2 oz. cheese, 4 oz. ham, half of roast pork, 4 pickle slices, and remaining 2 oz. cheese. Close with remaining bread pieces and wrap each sandwich in foil. Step 6

Heat a large cast-iron skillet over medium heat. Place foil-wrapped sandwiches in skillet, then place another heavy skillet on top to create a homemade sandwich press. If you don’t have another heavy skillet, weigh the pan down with another lighter skillet or baking sheet, then top with couple of canned goods. Step 7
Grill sandwiches, turning halfway through, until toasted and cheese is melted, 3 to 4 minutes per side. Cut each sandwich in half and serve.

title: Baked Yuca Fries
instructions: Step 1

Preheat oven to 450°. Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Trim ends of yuca and cut each one in half, widthwise. Stand them on their ends and use a sharp knife to cut the waxy peel off. Cut each piece in half lengthwise and then cut in half lengthwise one more time to create 16 pieces total. Trim the fibrous center out of each piece. Step 2

Place cut yuca into boiling water and let boil until fork tender, 8 to 10 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, remove from pot and place on a paper towel lined cutting board. Pat dry with another paper towel. Step 3
Place dried yuca into a large bowl and toss with oil. Season with chili powder, salt, and pepper and toss again to evenly coat. Place yuca on a large baking sheet in an even layer. Step 4
Bake until golden and crispy, about 25 minutes, tossing halfway through. Step 5
Meanwhile make dipping sauce: In a small food processor or blender, combine avocado, sour cream, lime juice, and cilantro and blend until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Step 6
Serve fries immediately with dipping sauce.

title: Chicken Salad With Mushrooms and Bacon
instructions: Place chicken breast in a saucepan and cover with water. Bring to a boil, add 1 tsp salt and simmer for approximately 15 minutes. Allow chicken to cool and then shred meat with two forks.
Finely chop shallot/red onion.
Stir mayonnaise, crème fraîche, Dijon mustard and apple cider vinegar to combine. Season with salt, pepper and extra Dijon mustard to taste. Combine with onion and chicken.
Fry bacon until crisp and transfer to plate lined with paper towels.
Rinse mushrooms, slice and fry in the same pan as bacon until golden (approximately 5 minutes). Season with a bit of salt and pepper.
Arrange your chicken salad in a serving dish, topped with crisp bacon, mushrooms and chopped parsley. Serve on a slice of light or dark bread.

title: Strawberry tart
instructions: Tart shell
Heat oven to 175°C / 347 °F
Grate the marzipan and mix thoroughly with the sugar. Whip the mixture with butter until fluffy.

Whip the eggs into the mixture and then folk the flour into the dough. Line an approximately 24 cm springform pan with baking paper and grease with butter. Then roll out the dough and transfer to the pan. Bake in the middle of the oven for approximately 25 minutes. Prepare the vanilla custard while the dough bakes.
Finely chop the chocolate and sprinkle over the shell after baking. Spread out the chocolate with a spatula as it melts. Allow the shell to cool to room temperature.
Vanilla custard

Mix vanilla sugar, egg yolks, sugar and corn starch in a saucepan. Turn the heat to medium and whisk in the milk. Heat the mixture while stirring until it thickens. Transfer the custard to a container and cool completely.
Whip the double cream to a light foam and folk into the cooled vanilla custard.
Tart assembly
Rinse the strawberries, remove the stems and quarter from top to bottom
Spread the vanilla custard in a thick layer on top of the tart shell. Top with the fresh strawberries and fresh mint (optional). Bon appétit!

title: Old-fashioned Danish Apple Trifle
instructions: Peel and cut the apples into cubes. Discard the cores. Transfer apple cubes to a saucepan with water, vanilla and lemon juice. Bring apples to a boil, cover and reduce heat to medium-low.

Add the sugar to taste after the apples release their juices. The amount of sugar depends on the tartness of the apples and your preferred level of sweetness. Remember that the breadcrumb mixture and whipped cream are also sweet, so it is okay if the apple sauce is still a bit tart.
Cook the apples for about 15 minutes until you have a coarse apple sauce. If you prefer, cook the apples longer for a finer consistency.
Refrigerate the applesauce.
Breadcrumbs mixture:
Melt butter in a pan. The butter must not brown. Add breadcrumbs and sugar and stir to combine.
Slowly toast the mixture as you stir with a spatula. Do not heat the mixture for too long – it only takes a short time to make.
Once the breadcrumbs are lightly golden, remove from the pan and cool on a sheet of baking paper.
Assembling the apple trifle:
Do not assemble the trifle until right before serving. Otherwise, the rasp will become soggy. Serve the trifle in individual small glasses or a large glass bowl.
Lightly whip the double cream.

Layer the ingredients in the glasses or bowl, starting with breadcrumbs in the bottom, followed by chilled apple sauce and breadcrumbs again. You can make several layers of breadcrumbs and apple sauce, then top with a generous layer of whipped cream. Serve immediately.

title: Open-faced Sandwich With Potato
instructions: Scrub the potatoes clean and place in a small saucepan with water and 1 tablespoon of salt. Bring to a boil and simmer the potatoes for about 10 minutes. Turn off the heat and let the potatoes stand in the water for 5 minutes. Drain the potatoes and allow to cool slightly. Remember that potatoes come in various sizes, so the cooking time may vary – if they do not easily glide off of a fork when speared and lifted out of the water, they are not done yet.
Fry bacon slices and transfer to a dish lined with paper towels.
Peel the red onion and slice in thin rings.
Transfer the flour to a bowl and toss the onions in the flour. Remove onions and shake off excess flour.
Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. You can test whether the oil is hot enough by adding a small piece of onion to the saucepan. If the oil bubbles around the onion, the oil is ready.
Transfer as many onion rings to the saucepan as can fit in one layer. Do not add too many onion rings at once.
Fry the onions for a couple of minutes until they are golden brown. Transfer onions to a dish lined with paper towels and sprinkle with salt. Repeat the process until all onions are fried.

Butter a slice of dark rye bread and arrange round potato slices (or, if the potatoes are very small, halved potatoes) on top. Top your open potato sandwich with a good mayonnaise, crispy fried onions, fried bacon and sliced chives.

title: Classic Potato Salad
instructions: Boil potatoes in lightly salted water for 10 to 12 minutes. Drain water when a potato speared with a fork and lifted out of the water easily glides off the fork and falls back into the pot. Let potatoes stand and cool.

Break off and discard the stringy ends of the asparagus spears, then chop into small pieces. You can pour boiling water over the chopped asparagus and let it soak for 2 minutes if you prefer a less raw taste.
Finely chop chives, red onion and radish.
Stir the dressing ingredients together and season with salt and pepper.
Reserve some of the chives for garnish and combine the rest of the vegetables with the dressing.
Season with salt and pepper, garnish with chives and serve as a side dish. Tip
When in season, you can add fresh peas to this potato salad

title: Extra crispy chicken wings
instructions: Wash chicken and pat dry
Place in a large bowl
Season with garlic, salt, pepper and turmeric (you can expand your seasoning options if you'd like.
Marinate for at least an hour
Pour some tapioca flour on a plate
Coat the wings with the cassava flour and place them on a rack or plater to set. Leave them for at least 30minutes to an hour.
Heat the oil in the saucepan until it’s hot.
Place wings in pan on medium heat, until light brown.
Drain on a paper towel, and let the wings rest for at least 10 minutes, then return the wings to the hot pan on high heat and fry until golden brown. Enjoy!

title: Stuffed plantain cups
instructions: Peel and wash plantains
Pat them dry
Cut them into one and a half inch slices
Heat oil to deep fry plantains
Toss in plantains into hot oil so they are submerged
Fry them for about 7 minutes
Place them on paper towel for about five minutes. You don't want them to be too dry
Using your citrus squeezer, press the plantain slices into cups
Place on paper towel or tray

Remove when golden brown

title: Baked brie with sorrel jam
instructions: Sorrel jam instructions
Combine sugar, sorrel, lemon zest, water in a medium sized pot.
Bring to a boil as petal becomes soft
Reduce heat, and cook until thickened.
Let it rest before using on brie
Baked brie instructions
You can slice the brie in half to create a sandwich-like effect. Or you can leave the brie wheel intact and just trim the top rind of the wheel.
Add a generous portion of jam to the top of the wheel, or one side of the sandwich
Roll dough out with a rolling pin on a floured surface
Trim excess dough. You can also use it to decorate .
Wrap the pastry up around the sides and over the top of cheese wheel, wrapping completely and pressing the edges of dough together to form a tightly sealed package.
Carefully flip the dough-wrapped cheese over, so that the gathered dough is on the bottom.Place the package, seam side down, on a baking sheet sprayed with non-stick cooking spray.
The brie can be prepared up to this point and refrigerated for 2 days before baking.
Be sure to bring the brie to room temperature before baking.
Preheat the oven to 400° F.
Combine the egg and water and brush the mixture over the top and sides of the pastry.
Add design from leftover dough if you'd like, and brush with egg mixture
You can use leftover sorrel pulp from your juice to make the jam. It will be a little less acidic and the color will be a brighter red instead of darker red.
Make my jam a day ahead, so I don’t feel rushed and the jam will have time to settle.
Add the jam to the center of the brie by slicing the brie in half and having the jam as a filler.
Next time, I’ll use a larger pot, so that I don’t need to add water frequently to tenderize the sorrel.

instructions: Combine the flour, the sugar, yeast, and salt in a mixing bowl or large bowl
Add warm milk and start kneading dough

Allow the dough to rise in a covered bowl until it’s doubled in bulk, about 90 minutes.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface, divide dough and round all of the pieces into smooth balls.
Lightly grease pans
Place dough on pan
Cover the pans, and let the loaves rise until they're puffy and soft
Using a brush, add egg whites to loaves
Towards the end of the rising time, preheat the oven to 375°F
Uncover the loaves, and bake them for 28 to 32 minutes, until their crust is golden brown
Remove from oven and enjoy

title: Pizza Margherita

lines.text: 600 g Fermented pizza dough (divided into 4 balls)
300 g Canned San Marzano tomatoes (crushed with a pinch of salt)
250 g Fresh mozzarella di bufala or fiordilatte (torn into chunks and drained)
16 leaves Fresh basil leaves (whole fresh leaves)
2 tbsp Extra virgin olive oil (DOP Campania preferred)
1 tsp Fine sea salt (to season tomato sauce)

instructions: Preheat an oven equipped with a heavy baking stone or steel to its maximum temperature (260°C / 500°F or higher) for at least 45 minutes.
Gently stretch one portion of room-temperature dough on a lightly floured peel by pressing from center outwards, leaving a puffy 2 cm border (cornicione).
Ladle 75g crushed San Marzano tomatoes in a circular spiral over the dough, disperse torn mozzarella pieces, and drizzle with half a tablespoon of olive oil.
Slide the pizza onto the blistering hot stone and bake until the cornicione is charred with leopard spots and the cheese is gently melted and bubbly.
Transfer onto a cutting board, immediately scatter fresh basil leaves over the melted cheese, finish with a light olive oil drizzle, and slice immediately.

title: Lasagne alla Bolognese

lines.text: 400 g Fresh green spinach pasta sheets (blanched and dried)
500 g Coarsely ground beef chuck (for ragù alla bolognese)
250 g Ground pork belly or pancetta (minced finely)
150 g Minced onion, carrot, and celery (equal parts brunoise)
300 g Tomato passata and purée (concentrated sauce)
150 ml Dry Italian white wine (Trebbiano or similar)
800 ml Whole milk (for béchamel and finishing meat)

instructions: Sauté pancetta and soffritto in butter until translucent; add ground beef and pork, browning thoroughly without scorching.
Deglaze with white wine, cook off alcohol, then stir in tomato passata and warm milk; simmer uncovered on lowest heat for 2.5 hours into a thick ragù.
Melt butter, whisk in flour for 2 minutes, then slowly pour in hot whole milk, whisking constantly until silky smooth and thickened; season with salt and nutmeg.
In a buttered baking dish, layer ragù, a sheet of green spinach pasta, béchamel, and a generous snow of Parmigiano-Reggiano; repeat for 5 to 6 distinct layers.
Bake at 190°C (375°F) for 30 minutes until bubbling and golden-crusted on top; rest for 15 minutes before slicing into neat squares.

title: Risotto alla Milanese

lines.text: 320 g Carnaroli or Vialone Nano rice (superfino risotto rice)
40 g Fresh beef bone marrow (minced finely (traditional))
1 medium Yellow onion or shallot (finely minced)
100 ml Dry white wine (dry Italian white)
0.5 g Saffron threads (steeped in 60ml warm broth)
1200 ml Rich beef and capon stock (kept at a gentle simmer)

instructions: Infuse crushed saffron threads in 4 tablespoons of hot broth for at least 20 minutes to draw out deep amber color and perfume.
In a heavy copper or cast saucepan, sweat the minced onion and beef bone marrow with 30g butter over gentle heat until translucent.
Add the carnaroli rice and toast (tostatura) for 3 minutes until grains are translucent and hot to the touch; pour in white wine and let evaporate completely.
Gradually ladle simmering broth into the rice one cup at a time, stirring steadily; halfway through cooking (around 12 minutes), stir in the saffron infusion.
Remove from heat when grains are al dente. Vigorously beat in remaining cold cubed butter and grated Parmigiano (mantecatura all'onda) until creamy and wavy; rest covered 2 minutes before plating.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara

lines.text: 400 g Spaghetti or rigatoni (bronze-cut Italian semolina pasta)
180 g Cured pork jowl (guanciale) (cut into thick lardons)
5 whole Fresh large egg yolks (plus 1 whole egg)
1.5 tbsp Whole black peppercorns (freshly cracked and toasted in dry pan)

instructions: In a heavy skillet over medium-low heat, slowly render the guanciale lardons until deeply browned and crispy on the outside while tender inside; transfer meat to a plate and keep warm fat in pan.
Boil spaghetti in moderately salted water until 2 minutes shy of al dente.
In a heatproof ceramic bowl, whisk egg yolks, whole egg, grated Pecorino Romano, half the cracked black pepper, and 2 tablespoons of warm rendered pork fat into a thick cream (carbocrema).
Transfer hot pasta directly into the skillet with rendered fat and a splash of starchy pasta water, tossing vigorously over low heat to glaze the noodles.

Remove pan completely from heat, allow pan to cool slightly, pour in egg-cheese mixture, and toss rapidly with starchy pasta water to emulsify into a silky, glossy coating; toss in crispy guanciale and garnish with black pepper.

title: Pasta al Pesto Genovese

lines.text: 400 g Fresh trofie or trenette pasta (traditional Ligurian shape)
70 g Fresh Genoese DOP basil (young, small tender leaves, thoroughly dried)
25 g Pecorino Fiore Sardo DOP (finely grated)
100 ml Ligurian extra virgin olive oil (mild and sweet)
1 pinch Coarse sea salt (for grinding leaves)
100 g Green beans (trimmed and cut into 3cm lengths)
1 medium Waxy yellow potato (peeled and sliced thin)

instructions: In a marble mortar with a wooden pestle, crush the garlic cloves and pine nuts with a pinch of coarse sea salt into a smooth, creamy paste.
Add fresh basil leaves in handfuls, using a rotational grinding motion against the mortar walls to release fragrant oils without bruising or blackening the leaves.
Stir in grated Parmigiano and Pecorino, then trickle in Ligurian olive oil in a steady stream, beating gently into a luminous bright-emerald emulsified pesto.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil; add sliced potatoes and green beans, cooking for 4 minutes before dropping in fresh trofie pasta until tender.
Drain pasta and vegetables, reserving 4 tablespoons of warm starchy cooking water; toss in a large warm serving bowl with the raw pesto and cooking water until creamy and vibrant.

title: Paella Valenciana

lines.text: 450 g Arroz Bomba or Senia (short-grain Spanish paella rice)
500 g Bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks (chopped into small pieces)
400 g Rabbit meat (chopped into small bite-size pieces)
200 g Flat green beans (bajoqueta) (trimmed and snapped)
120 g Large white lima beans (garrofó) (cooked or fresh)
2 medium Ripe tomato (finely grated pulp without skin)
0.5 g Spanish saffron threads (toasted and crushed)
1 tsp Pimentón dulce (sweet smoked paprika) (Spanish paprika)
1 sprig Fresh rosemary sprig (added in final simmer)
80 ml Extra virgin olive oil (Spanish olive oil)
1400 ml Water or light poultry stock (measured to pan rivets)

instructions: Level the paella pan over medium-high heat, heat olive oil around the perimeter with coarse salt, and sear chicken and rabbit pieces thoroughly until deeply golden brown and crisp.
Push meat to outer rim of pan, add flat green beans and garrofó to the center, sautéing until browned, then stir in grated tomato and paprika for 2 minutes without burning.
Pour in water up to the inner handle rivets, add steeped saffron and salt; boil vigorously for 15 minutes to extract meat flavors into a concentrated rich cooking broth.
Evenly scatter Bomba rice in a cross pattern, distribute grains submerged across the pan, and lay a sprig of rosemary on top; boil vigorously for 8 minutes without stirring.

Lower heat to gentle simmer for 10 minutes until broth is fully absorbed; in the final 2 minutes, turn heat up to listen for crackling to create the coveted caramelized crunchy crust (socarrat); rest 5 minutes before serving directly from the pan.

title: Tortilla Española

lines.text: 750 g Waxy Yukon Gold or Monalisa potatoes (peeled and sliced into 3mm half-moons)
300 ml Spanish extra virgin olive oil (for poaching (most is strained and reused))
1.5 tsp Fine sea salt (to season potatoes and eggs)

instructions: Heat olive oil in a deep skillet over medium-low heat; add sliced potatoes, onions, and 1 tsp salt, confiting slowly until fork-tender and melting without turning brown.
Strain potatoes and onions in a colander, reserving the fragrant cooking oil for other uses; let cool for 5 minutes.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs with 0.5 tsp salt until frothy; gently fold in warm strained potatoes and onions, letting the mixture soak and thicken for 10 minutes.
Heat 1 tablespoon reserved oil in a 24cm nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until hot; pour in egg-potato mixture, smoothing edges with a rubber spatula for 2 minutes.

Place a flat plate over skillet, invert swiftly, and slide tortilla back into the pan to cook the second side for 1.5 minutes, keeping the center tender and juicy (jugosa); slide onto a wooden board and rest 10 minutes.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz

lines.text: 1000 g Ultra-ripe vine or Roma tomatoes (cored and coarsely chopped)
1 medium Spanish or Persian cucumber (partially peeled)
1 medium Italian green frying pepper (seeded and chopped)
50 g Stale white rustic bread (crust removed, soaked in water and squeezed)
25 ml Sherry vinegar (Vinagre de Jerez) (aged Spanish vinegar)
80 ml Spanish extra virgin olive oil (Hojiblanca or Picual)

instructions: Place chopped tomatoes, cucumber, green pepper, garlic, and squeezed soaked bread into a high-speed blender container.
Blend at high speed for 3 minutes until completely pureed and smooth.
With blender running on medium-low, slowly drizzle in sherry vinegar and extra virgin olive oil to emulsify the soup into a creamy coral-orange velvet texture; season with salt.
Strain through a fine-mesh chinois into a glass pitcher to remove all remaining seeds and fibers; chill in refrigerator for at least 2 hours until ice-cold.
Pour into chilled ceramic bowls or tumblers; garnish with finely diced cucumber, bell pepper, and a drizzle of aromatic green olive oil.

title: Bacalhau à Brás

lines.text: 400 g Desalted shredded cod (bacalhau) (soaked for 48 hours and flaked)
250 g Shoestring matchstick potatoes (batata palha) (crisp fried straw potatoes)
2 medium Yellow onions (thinly sliced into half-moons)
6 whole Fresh eggs (beaten lightly with salt and white pepper)

instructions: Simmer shredded desalted cod gently in water for 5 minutes; drain thoroughly and flake into bite-sized fibers, discarding any stray bones.
In a wide skillet, heat olive oil over low heat and gently sweat onions and garlic until translucent and sweet without browning.
Add flaked cod to the skillet, stirring over medium heat for 4 minutes to absorb the garlicky olive oil.
Turn heat to low, add crispy matchstick potatoes, and pour in beaten eggs; stir continuously with a wooden spoon until eggs are softly scrambled, creamy, and custard-like without drying out.
Immediately remove from heat, transfer to a heated serving platter, and scatter with glossy black olives and plenty of chopped fresh parsley.

title: Pastel de Nata

lines.text: 400 g Laminated puff pastry dough (rolled tightly into a spiral log)
220 g Granulated white sugar (for sugar syrup)
1 whole Ceylon cinnamon stick (for infusing syrup)
1 strip Lemon peel strip (wide zest strip)
1 tbsp Ground cinnamon and powdered sugar (for dusting)

instructions: Boil sugar, water, cinnamon stick, and lemon peel in a saucepan without stirring until syrup reaches 100°C (212°F) thread stage.
Whisk flour with 100ml cold milk until smooth; scald remaining milk in a pot, whisk in flour mixture, and cook until thickened into a silky pudding base.
Slowly pour hot sugar syrup into the thickened milk pudding while whisking constantly; cool for 10 minutes, then whisk in egg yolks until glossy and strain into a pitcher.
Slice cold rolled puff pastry log into 12 equal rounds; place each swirl cut-side down into metal tart molds and press thin up the sides with wet thumbs to form crisp cups.

Fill pastry shells 3/4 full with custard; bake at maximum heat (270°C / 520°F or highest oven setting) for 10-12 minutes until pastry is blistered and custard tops develop dark caramelized spots; serve warm dusted with cinnamon.

title: Bouillabaisse

lines.text: 1800 g Mixed Mediterranean fish (rascasse/red scorpionfish, sea robin, conger eel, sea bream) (gutted and scaled, heads reserved for broth)
1 bulb Fresh fennel bulb (finely sliced, fronds reserved)
1 stalk Leek (white and pale green part) (sliced)
1 g Saffron threads (steeped in warm stock)
1 piece Dried orange peel strip (for broth aroma)
30 ml Pastis or anise liqueur (traditional Marseille touch)
120 g Rouille sauce (garlic, chili, potato, saffron and olive oil emulsion)
12 slices Toasted baguette slices (rubbed with raw garlic)

instructions: In a massive pot, sauté onions, leeks, fennel, and garlic in olive oil until tender; add fish heads/bones, chopped tomatoes, orange peel, pastis, and saffron.
Cover with boiling water, bring to an energetic rapid boil (bouillir et abaisser) for 25 minutes so oil and water emulsify into a rich golden soup base; pass broth through a food mill.
Return strained saffron broth to heat; add sliced potatoes and firm fish cuts (conger, rascasse), boiling briskly for 8 minutes.
Add delicate fish cuts (sea bream, mullet) and simmer for 5 minutes until tender and just cooked through.
Transfer fish and potatoes onto a large warm serving platter; ladle steaming saffron broth into wide bowls and serve with garlic croutons generously slathered with spicy red rouille.

title: Classic French Coq au Vin

lines.text: 1400 g Bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks (skin-on, patted dry)
750 ml Full-bodied dry red wine (Pinot Noir) (1 bottle Burgundian red)
180 g Thick-cut smoked bacon lardons (sliced into matchsticks)
200 g Small white pearl onions (peeled whole)
30 g Butter and flour paste (beurre manié) (equal parts butter and flour to thicken sauce)
1 bundle Bouquet garni (thyme, parsley, bay leaf) (tied fresh herbs)

instructions: In a heavy enameled cast iron cocotte, render smoked lardons over medium heat until crispy; remove with a slotted spoon, keeping rendered fat in the pot.
Season chicken pieces with salt and pepper; sear in hot bacon fat in batches until deep golden brown on both sides, then remove.
Sauté pearl onions and mushrooms until nicely browned and set aside; add carrots and garlic to the pot, pour in Cognac and flambé carefully.

Return chicken and crispy lardons to pot; pour in the entire bottle of red wine, chicken stock, and bouquet garni; bring to a boil, cover tightly, and simmer gently on low heat for 45 minutes until chicken is meltingly tender.

Remove chicken to a plate; whisk beurre manié into simmering red wine sauce for 5 minutes until glossy and thick enough to coat a spoon; return chicken, mushrooms, and onions to warm through, then serve garnished with chopped parsley.

title: Ratatouille Niçoise

lines.text: 400 g Globe or Italian eggplant (cut into 2cm cubes)
450 g Medium zucchini and yellow squash (cut into 2cm pieces)
2 peppers Red and yellow bell peppers (seeded and cut into chunks)
500 g Ripe plum tomatoes (peeled, seeded and chopped)
80 ml Provençal extra virgin olive oil (divided for browning veggies)
2 sprigs Fresh thyme and rosemary (plus 1 bay leaf)
12 leaves Fresh basil leaves (torn before serving)

instructions: In a wide heavy skillet, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil over medium-high heat and sear eggplant cubes in a single layer until golden; transfer to a plate.
Add another splash of oil and sear zucchini pieces until lightly colored; transfer to the plate with the eggplant.
In the same skillet, cook onions and bell peppers over medium heat for 8 minutes until softened; add sliced garlic and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chopped tomatoes and fresh herb sprigs; simmer for 10 minutes until tomatoes release their juices and break down into a thick sauce.

Return eggplant and zucchini to the pan, season with salt and pepper, cover partially, and gently braise over low heat for 25 minutes until all vegetables are meltingly tender while retaining their shapes; fold in fresh basil and a final drizzle of olive oil.

title: Crêpes Bretonnes

lines.text: 250 g Type 45 or all-purpose wheat flour (sifted)
50 g Breton salted butter (melted and slightly cooled)
0.5 tsp Fleur de sel de Guérande (enhances flavor)

instructions: In a mixing bowl, whisk flour, sugar, and salt; form a well in the center and add eggs, whisking gradually from the inside out.
Gradually stream in whole milk while whisking vigorously to avoid lumps, then incorporate melted salted butter and vanilla until the batter has the consistency of light heavy cream.
Rest the batter at room temperature for at least 30 minutes to relax gluten and produce exceptionally tender crêpes.

Heat a crêpe pan or billig griddle over medium-high heat and brush lightly with butter; pour a small ladle (approx. 50ml) of batter, immediately tilting and swirling the pan in a circular motion to coat the surface paper-thin.
Cook for 60 seconds until the edges curl and turn golden lace; flip with a thin spatula and cook the reverse side for 30 seconds; fold into quarters with a smear of salted butter and sugar.

title: Traditional Greek Moussaka

lines.text: 700 g Ground lamb or beef (lean minced meat)
2 medium Yukon gold potatoes (peeled and sliced 5mm thick (traditional foundation))
1 tsp Ground cinnamon and allspice (characteristic Greek spices)
2 whole Egg yolks (whisked into cooled béchamel)
100 g Grated Kefalotyri or Pecorino cheese (salty hard Greek cheese)
60 ml Extra virgin olive oil (for brushing eggplant and potatoes)

instructions: Brush sliced eggplant and potatoes with olive oil, season with salt, and roast at 200°C (400°F) on baking sheets for 20 minutes until tender and caramelized.

Sauté chopped onion in olive oil until golden, add ground lamb and brown thoroughly; stir in crushed tomatoes, garlic, cinnamon, allspice, and salt, simmering for 25 minutes into a rich, reduced meat sauce.
Make béchamel by cooking butter and flour for 2 minutes, then whisking in warm milk until thick and glossy; remove from heat, stir in nutmeg, half the grated cheese, and egg yolks.

In a deep baking dish, arrange roasted potato slices across the bottom, top with half the eggplant, spread all the spiced lamb sauce, cover with remaining eggplant, and pour the thick béchamel over the top, smoothing evenly and sprinkling with remaining cheese.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 45 minutes until top is deep golden brown and bubbling; let cool and set for 25 minutes before slicing into neat squares.

title: Souvlaki

lines.text: 700 g Pork neck or boneless chicken thighs (cut into 2.5cm cubes)
50 ml Greek extra virgin olive oil (for marinade)
1.5 tbsp Dried Greek rigani (wild oregano) (aromatic dried oregano)
4 whole Greek pita flatbreads (thick pocketless pitas)
150 g Tzatziki sauce (strained Greek yogurt, cucumber, garlic)
1 small Red onion (thinly sliced with chopped parsley)

instructions: Toss meat cubes with olive oil, lemon juice, crushed garlic, wild oregano, salt, and black pepper; marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Thread meat tightly onto wooden or stainless steel skewers (soak wooden skewers 20 minutes prior).
Grill skewers over high direct heat or charcoal for 8-10 minutes, turning frequently until charred and caramelized at edges while remaining juicy inside.
Brush pita breads lightly with olive oil and warm on the grill for 1 minute per side until pliable and marked.
Slide meat off skewer onto warm pita, add a generous dollop of tzatziki, tomato wedges, sliced red onion, and fold tightly in wax paper to serve street-food style.

title: Spanakopita

lines.text: 16 sheets Phyllo pastry sheets (thawed in refrigerator)
800 g Fresh mature spinach (washed, wilted, thoroughly squeezed dry)
80 g Unsalted butter (melted with 40ml olive oil for brushing phyllo)

instructions: Chop wilted spinach coarsely and wrap in a clean kitchen towel, wringing out all excess moisture until bone dry (crucial to prevent soggy pastry).
In a large mixing bowl, combine squeezed spinach, scallions, fresh dill, crumbled feta cheese, beaten eggs, nutmeg, and black pepper; mix well.
Brush a 23x33 cm baking pan with melted butter-oil mixture; layer 8 phyllo sheets in the pan, brushing each generously with the butter-oil mixture before adding the next.
Spread spinach-feta filling evenly over the phyllo base; cover with the remaining 8 phyllo sheets, brushing each sheet with melted butter mixture as before.
Score the top phyllo layers into squares or diamonds with a sharp knife; bake at 180°C (350°F) for 45 minutes until golden brown and deeply crisp; cool 10 minutes before slicing fully.

title: Fish and Chips

lines.text: 700 g Fresh thick skinless haddock or cod fillets (divided into 4 portions)
900 g Maris Piper or Russet potatoes (peeled and cut into chunky thick chips)
200 g All-purpose flour (plus 50g for dusting fish)
50 g Cornstarch or rice flour (for extra crunch)
1 tsp Baking powder (for airy batter texture)
280 ml Ice-cold British pale ale or lager (very cold)
1500 ml Beef dripping or sunflower oil (for deep frying)
250 g Marrowfat mushy peas (seasoned with butter and mint)
3 tbsp Malt vinegar and sea salt (for serving)

instructions: Parboil cut chips in salted water for 6 minutes until edges are tender; drain and cool completely on wire racks to dry surface starch.
Fry chips first in oil heated to 130°C (265°F) for 7 minutes until cooked through but pale; drain and spread out to cool.
Whisk flour, cornstarch, baking powder, a pinch of salt, and ice-cold beer together briefly until just combined (leave small lumps to ensure lightness).
Dust dry fish fillets lightly in flour, dip into beer batter, and lower gently into oil heated to 185°C (365°F); fry for 6-7 minutes, turning once, until crust is deep golden brown and hyper-crispy.
Flash-fry the par-cooked chips at 190°C (375°F) for 3 minutes until crunchy and golden; serve fish immediately atop chips alongside mushy peas, tartare sauce, and malt vinegar.

title: Shepherd's Pie

lines.text: 700 g Ground lamb (minced lamb) (traditional lamb (cottage pie uses beef))
900 g Fluffy potatoes (Maris Piper or Russet) (peeled and quartered)
80 ml Warm milk or cream (for mash)
120 g Frozen green peas (sweet garden peas)
350 ml Rich lamb or beef stock (unsalted)
1.5 tbsp Fresh rosemary and thyme (finely minced)

instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until fork-tender (15 minutes); drain thoroughly and mash vigorously with butter, warm milk, salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg until smooth.
In a deep skillet, brown minced lamb over high heat, breaking it up with a wooden spoon; remove excess rendered fat.
Add onions, carrots, and garlic to the lamb, cooking until softened; stir in tomato paste, herbs, and Worcestershire sauce for 2 minutes.
Pour in stock, bring to a simmer, and cook uncovered for 15 minutes until gravy is thick and glossy; fold in green peas in the last minute.

Spread meat filling in a ceramic baking dish; spread or pipe mashed potato over top, raking ridges with a fork; bake at 200°C (400°F) for 25 minutes until potato peaks are toasted deep golden brown and gravy bubbles up edges.

title: Classic British Beef Wellington

lines.text: 900 g Center-cut beef tenderloin (chateaubriand) (trimmed and tied into a uniform cylinder)
450 g All-butter puff pastry sheet (high-quality chilled sheet)
10 slices Prosciutto di Parma slices (to wrap duxelles)
500 g Cremini and wild mushrooms (finely minced in food processor for duxelles)
2 tbsp English or Dijon mustard (to brush seared beef)
2 yolks Egg yolk beaten with 1 tsp milk (for brilliant golden gloss)
1 tsp Maldon flaky sea salt (to finish pastry)

instructions: Season tenderloin aggressively; sear in smoking hot oil for 1.5 minutes per side just to form a dark exterior crust without cooking interior; immediately brush all over with Dijon mustard while hot and chill.
Cook finely minced mushrooms, shallots, garlic, and thyme in a dry skillet over medium heat until all moisture evaporates and mixture becomes a spreadable, dry paste (duxelles); cool completely.

Lay plastic wrap on work surface, arrange overlapping prosciutto slices, spread mushroom duxelles evenly over prosciutto, place chilled beef in center, and roll tightly into a taught sausage log; chill in fridge for 30 minutes to hold shape.
Roll puff pastry into a rectangle; unwrap beef cylinder and place on pastry; brush borders with egg wash, roll pastry securely around beef, seal edges, trim excess, and chill for 20 minutes.

Score decorative diamond lattice pattern onto cold pastry, brush thoroughly with egg wash, sprinkle with flaky salt, and bake at 210°C (425°F) for 32-35 minutes until pastry is glossy deep golden and internal temperature registers 52°C (125°F) for medium-rare; rest 15 minutes before carving thick medallions.

title: Gulyás (Hungarian Goulash)

lines.text: 900 g Beef shank or chuck roast (cut into 2.5cm cubes)
3 tbsp Pork lard or vegetable oil (traditional fat)
3 large Yellow onions (finely diced (key flavor base))
3 tbsp Authentic sweet Hungarian paprika (édesnemes) (fresh Kalocsa or Szeged paprika)
1 tsp Whole caraway seeds (toasted and lightly crushed)
500 g Waxy potatoes (peeled and cubed into 2cm pieces)
3 medium Carrots and parsnips (sliced into coins)
100 g Pinched noodles (csipetke) (egg and flour dough pinched into tiny bits)

instructions: Melt lard in a heavy kettle (bogrács) or Dutch oven over low heat; sauté diced onions slowly for 15 minutes until meltingly tender and golden.
Pull kettle off the heat, stir in the sweet Hungarian paprika and caraway seeds immediately to infuse the lard without scorching the delicate paprika.
Add beef cubes, garlic, salt, diced tomato, and wax pepper; return to low heat, cover tightly, and braise the meat gently in its own juices for 1 hour until tender.
Pour in 1.2 liters of water or beef stock, add carrots, parsnips, and potato cubes; bring to a gentle simmer for 25 minutes until vegetables are cooked through.
Drop pinched csipetke noodle bits into the simmering stew-soup; cook for 4-5 minutes until they float to the surface; serve hot with crusty rye bread.

title: Pierogi

lines.text: 200 ml Warm water (with 1 tbsp melted butter and 1 egg yolk)
250 g Polish twaróg or farmer's cheese (dry curd white cheese)
2 large Yellow onions (diced and deeply caramelized in butter)
70 g Unsalted butter (for frying and onions)
1 tsp Freshly ground black pepper (peppery filling)

instructions: Knead flour, warm water, melted butter, egg yolk, and a pinch of salt into a soft, elastic dough; cover with a warm bowl and rest for 30 minutes.
In a bowl, combine warm riced potatoes, crumbled twaróg cheese, half the caramelized buttered onions, salt, and generous black pepper until cohesive.

Roll rested dough on a lightly floured board to 2mm thickness; cut 8cm circles with a glass or cutter, place a heaping tablespoon of filling in the center, fold into half-moons, and pinch ruffled edges firmly to seal.
Drop pierogi in batches into boiling salted water; simmer gently for 3-4 minutes until they float to the top; lift out with a slotted spoon.

Melt butter in a large skillet and pan-fry boiled pierogi for 2 minutes per side until golden and slightly blistered; serve smothered with remaining caramelized onions, a dollop of sour cream, and fresh chives.

title: Wiener Schnitzel

lines.text: 600 g Milk-fed veal topside (leg cutlets) (4 cutlets, pounded evenly to 4mm thickness)
3 whole Fresh eggs (beaten lightly with a fork, not whisked)
150 g Fine dried white breadcrumbs (Semmelbrösel) (from Kaiser rolls, not pressed onto meat)
300 g Clarified butter (Butterschmalz) or lard (for shallow frying)
4 wedges Fresh lemon wedges (for squeezing over meat)
1 tsp Fine sea salt (to season meat right before dredging)

instructions: Place veal cutlets between plastic wrap and gently pound with a flat meat mallet to an even 3-4 mm thickness; season lightly with salt.
Set up a standard breading station in three shallow bowls: flour, lightly beaten eggs, and fresh dry breadcrumbs.
Dredge each cutlet in flour (shaking off excess), coat in egg, then lay gently into breadcrumbs without pressing (pressing prevents the crust from souffléing into waves).

Heat clarified butter in a wide skillet to 170°C (340°F); the cutlet must float freely. Slide cutlet in and swirl pan constantly so hot butter ripples over top; fry 2 minutes per side until puffed, wavy, and golden bronze.
Drain on wire racks for 1 minute; serve immediately garnished with a lemon slice and accompanied by Austrian warm potato salad (Erdäpfelsalat) and wild lingonberry jam.

title: Fondue Moitié-Moitié

lines.text: 400 g Gruyère AOP cheese (aged 8-12 months, coarsely grated)
400 g Vacherin Fribourgeois AOP cheese (creamy, coarsely grated)
300 ml Crisp dry Swiss white wine (Chasselas/Fendant) (high acid)
1 clove Garlic clove (halved, to rub pot)
20 ml Kirsch cherry brandy (traditional aromatic spirit)
0.5 tsp Freshly grated nutmeg and black pepper (to taste)
500 g Day-old crusty rustic bread (cut into 2.5cm cubes with crust)

instructions: Rub the entire interior of a ceramic fondue pot (caquelon) with the cut garlic clove.
Pour dry white wine and dissolved cornstarch slurry into the caquelon and bring to a gentle bubble over medium-low heat on the stovetop.
Add grated Gruyère and Vacherin Fribourgeois in handfuls, stirring continuously in a figure-eight pattern with a wooden spoon until cheese melts into a smooth, bubbling velvet emulsion.
Stir in Kirsch, freshly grated nutmeg, and freshly ground black pepper; cook gently for 2 minutes without letting the mixture boil furiously.
Transfer caquelon immediately to a tabletop burner (réchaud) set on low flame; dip crusty bread cubes on long fondue forks, swirling to coat with hot stringy cheese.

title: Ukrainian Borshch

lines.text: 700 g Pork ribs or bone-in beef shank (for deep stock)
3 tbsp Tomato paste or pureed tomatoes (for color and acidity)
1.5 tbsp Apple cider vinegar or lemon juice (to preserve brilliant ruby beet color)
40 g Cured pork fatback (salo) or butter (mashed with garlic)
150 g Sour cream (smetana) (to dollop in each bowl)

instructions: In a large stockpot, simmer meat and bone in 2.5 liters of water with a bay leaf, skimming foam periodically, for 60 minutes to create a rich broth.
In a skillet, braise julienned beets with 1 tbsp butter, tomato paste, and vinegar over medium-low heat for 15 minutes to lock in brilliant ruby pigmentation.
In another pan, sauté onions and grated carrots in fat until golden (smazhennya).
Add diced potatoes to the simmering stock pot; cook for 10 minutes, then add shredded cabbage, braised beets, and sautéed vegetables; simmer gently for 10 minutes.

Mash cured fatback (salo) and garlic with salt into a paste in a mortar; stir into the hot borshch with fresh dill; take off heat and rest 15 minutes before ladling into bowls with a heaping spoon of smetana and garlic pampushky rolls.

title: Nigiri Sushi (Edomae-style)

lines.text: 300 g Japanese short-grain rice (koshihikari) (rinsed thoroughly and steamed)
50 ml Aged red rice vinegar (akazu) seasoning (blended with sea salt and a touch of sugar)
320 g Sashimi-grade tuna (maguro) and sea bream (madai) (sliced into 8g nigiri draperies (neta))
15 g Real grated wasabi rhizome (freshly grated on sharkskin or ceramic grater)
40 ml Nikiri soy glaze (simmered soy sauce, mirin, sake, and dashi)

instructions: Cook Japanese short-grain rice in a rice cooker with kombu; transfer hot rice to a wooden hangiri bowl.
Drizzle akazu vinegar seasoning over the rice, cutting and folding gently with a rice paddle while fanning to cool grains to body temperature (36°C / 97°F) with a glossy sheen.
Slice sashimi-grade fish across the grain into precise angled rectangles (neta) with a single pull of a yanagiba knife.

Dampen hands with tezu (vinegar water), shape a 15-gram oblong rice pillow with gentle finger pressure, smear a trace of fresh wasabi onto the fish underside, press fish onto rice and shape with two-finger press.
Brush the fish surface with a sheer layer of nikiri shoyu glaze, place on a dark hinoki wood or ceramic geta block, and serve immediately alongside gari.

title: Ramen

lines.text: 480 g Fresh alkaline ramen noodles (medium wavy or straight noodles)
1800 g Pork trotter, neck bones, and chicken carcass (for creamy rich bone stock)
500 g Pork belly slab (rolled and tied into chashu log)
120 ml Shoyu tare seasoning (soy sauce simmered with kombu, bonito flakes, and mirin)
40 ml Garlic-shallot scallion aroma oil (mayu) (poured over broth)
4 whole Soy-marinated soft-boiled eggs (ramen eggs) (halved, runny jammy yolks)
4 sheets Roasted nori seaweed squares (tucked into bowl edge)
4 stalks Japanese negi or scallions (finely sliced)

instructions: Blanch bones in boiling water, wash clean, then boil vigorously with ginger and green onion in a deep stockpot for 3 hours, skimming continuously to produce a rich, collagenous broth.
Roll and tie pork belly slab, sear until browned, then braise in soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, and garlic for 1.5 hours until fork-tender; chill and slice thinly into chashu rounds.
Boil eggs for exactly 6 minutes and 15 seconds, shock in ice water, peel, and marinate in reserved chashu braising liquid for 2 hours.
In each heated ramen bowl, pour 30ml shoyu tare and 10ml scallion aroma oil; ladle in 350ml boiling hot bone broth, whisking to combine.

Boil fresh alkaline noodles for 75 seconds until springy, shake vigorously in a noodle basket to remove excess water, fold into broth, and top with seared chashu slices, jammy egg halves, menma, nori, and sliced scallions.

title: Tempura

lines.text: 12 whole Large black tiger prawns or shrimp (peeled, deveined, tails on, belly scored to keep straight)
100 g Lotus root (renkon) (peeled and sliced into rounds)
8 leaves Fresh green shiso leaves (stem intact, dried)
200 ml Ice-cold water with ice cubes (very cold)
1000 ml Neutral vegetable oil blended with 20% untoasted sesame oil (traditional Tokyo aroma)
120 ml Tentsuyu dipping sauce (dashi, mirin, soy sauce, grated daikon and ginger)

instructions: Prep prawns: make small diagonal snips along the belly side and gently press until tendons pop, ensuring they remain completely straight during frying.

Whisk cold water and egg yolk in a bowl; dump in sifted flour all at once and stir with chopsticks only 8-10 times, leaving visible lumps and dry flour pockets (never overmix, to prevent gluten formation).
Heat oil in a heavy deep pan to 175°C (350°F); dust vegetables lightly in dry flour, dip into ice batter, and lower gently into hot oil, frying vegetables for 2-3 minutes until crisp and pale.
Dip prepared prawns by tail into batter and slide into oil; flick drops of loose batter over them with chopsticks (hana o sakaseru) to create delicate crispy lace fritters; fry for 2 minutes.
Drain immediately on paper-lined wire tempura racks; serve piping hot with warm tentsuyu dipping broth mixed with freshly grated white daikon radish and ginger.

title: Okonomiyaki

lines.text: 400 g Fresh green cabbage (finely shredded or chopped)
160 g Wheat flour or okonomiyaki mix (with baking powder)
60 g Grated mountain yam (nagaimo) (provides signature fluffy interior)
200 g Thinly sliced pork belly (laid on top of pancake)
25 g Red pickled ginger (beni shoga) (finely chopped)
60 ml Okonomiyaki brown sauce (Otafuku) (sweet savory glaze)
40 ml Japanese Kewpie mayonnaise (piped in fine zig-zag stripes)
10 g Bonito flakes (katsuobushi) and aonori (for dancing garnish)

instructions: Whisk flour, dashi stock, and grated nagaimo yam together into a smooth batter; chill for 15 minutes.
In individual bowls, combine shredded cabbage, 1 egg, a ladle of batter, tempura scraps, and pickled ginger; mix gently with a spoon just until cabbage is coated with batter without compacting.
Heat an oiled griddle or nonstick skillet to 200°C (400°F); pour cabbage mixture into a 20cm round disc about 2.5cm thick; arrange slices of pork belly across the top.
Cover with a lid and cook for 5 minutes; flip carefully with two spatulas, cover again, and cook for 5 minutes until pork is crispy and pancake is cooked through.

Flip one last time to bring pork side up; brush liberally with dark okonomiyaki sauce, drizzle zig-zags of Kewpie mayo, dust with green aonori flakes, and top with katsuobushi flakes that dance in the heat.

title: Peking Duck

lines.text: 2200 g Whole white Pekin duck (head and neck on, innards removed)
80 g Maltose syrup or honey (for glassy skin glaze)
40 ml Chinese red vinegar or rice vinegar (for skin tension)
18 pancakes Steamed thin mandarin pancakes (chunbing) (steamed fresh)
120 g Sweet bean sauce (tianmianjiang) or hoisin (seasoned with sesame oil)
6 stalks Scallions cut into fine matchsticks (white parts only)
1 cucumber Seedless English cucumber (julienned into crisp batons)
2 tbsp Fine white sugar (for dipping purest crispy breast skin)

instructions: Separate duck skin from meat by inflating air between skin and fat with an air pump; scald whole duck skin in boiling water for 30 seconds to tighten skin pores.
Brush entire exterior with a hot solution of maltose, vinegar, and warm water; hang duck in a dry, breezy, refrigerated area for 24 hours until skin feels like dry parchment paper.

Roast duck suspended vertically in a preheated oven at 200°C (400°F) for 30 minutes, then lower to 160°C (320°F) for 45 minutes until fat renders out completely and skin turns a radiant, uniform mahogany crisp.
Rest duck for 10 minutes; carve the thinnest glassy breast skin first into bite-sized rectangles, then carve remaining skin and meat into uniform angled slivers.
Serve immediately: spread sweet bean sauce on a warm thin pancake, lay crispy duck skin and meat, add scallion matchsticks and cucumber batons, roll neatly and eat by hand.

title: Xiaolongbao

lines.text: 250 g Medium-protein wheat flour (kneaded with hot and cold water into elastic dough)
300 g Ground pork shoulder (70% lean, 30% fat) (minced finely)
250 g Pork skin collagen aspic broth gelatin (cooked down, chilled firm, finely diced)
1.5 tbsp Shaoxing rice wine (for meat seasoning)
2 tbsp Light soy sauce and ginger water (infused aromatics)
60 ml Zhenjiang (Chinkiang) aged black vinegar (for dipping sauce)
30 g Fresh ginger julienned into hair-thin threads (served in black vinegar)

instructions: Prepare aspic: simmer pork skin with aromatics until collagen dissolves, strain broth, pour into a pan, and chill overnight until set firm; chop into tiny 3mm cubes.
Vigorously beat ground pork with ginger water, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, white pepper, and sesame oil until sticky and emulsified; fold in chopped aspic cubes and chill cold.
Roll rested dumpling dough into a rope, cut into 10g pieces, and roll each into a thin circular wrapper with a slightly thicker center and paper-thin translucent edges.
Place 20g filling in center; pleat edges with quick clockwise pinching movements into at least 18 neat folds, twisting and pinching the top crown tightly closed.

Arrange dumplings in a bamboo steamer lined with perforated parchment or cabbage leaves; steam over high boiling water for exactly 8 minutes until skins are translucent and puffed with hot liquid soup inside; serve immediately on a soup spoon with black vinegar and ginger.

title: Mapo Tofu

lines.text: 500 g Medium-firm or soft silken tofu (cut into 2cm cubes and parboiled in salted water)
120 g Ground beef chuck or pork (minced finely (authentic Chengdu style uses beef))
2.5 tbsp Pixian fermented chili bean paste (doubanjiang) (finely chopped)
1 tbsp Fermented black beans (douchi) (rinsed and crushed)
2 tbsp Sichuan chili powder and chili oil (for vibrant red color)
3 stalks Garlic greens or scallions (cut into 2cm lengths)
250 ml Chicken or vegetable stock (simmering base)
2 tbsp Potato starch or cornstarch slurry (divided into 3 additions)
1 tsp Freshly roasted and ground red Sichuan peppercorns (for mala numbing finish)

instructions: Gently simmer cubed tofu in lightly salted boiling water for 2 minutes to strengthen curd and eliminate raw soy taste; drain gently.
In a seasoned carbon steel wok over medium heat, fry ground beef in oil until dark brown, deeply crispy, and fragrant (酥); push to side.
Add chopped Pixian doubanjiang, chili flakes, and black beans, stirring over low heat until the oil becomes brilliant crimson red and aromatic; stir in minced garlic and ginger.
Pour in broth and soy sauce; gently slide in the drained tofu cubes and simmer for 5 minutes, swirling the wok gently rather than using a spatula to keep tofu intact.

Drizzle starch slurry in three separate stages, swirling between each until the sauce forms a glossy, clinging red glaze around each tofu cube; toss in garlic greens and dust lavishly with roasted Sichuan pepper powder before plating.

title: Char Siu

lines.text: 1000 g Pork collar or pork shoulder butt (cut into long 4cm thick strips)
2 cubes Red fermented bean curd (nam yu) (plus 1 tbsp brine for natural red glaze)
80 g Maltose syrup or clover honey (for basting and glaze)
3 tbsp Light and dark soy sauce blend (for savory depth and color)
0.75 tsp Chinese five-spice powder (cinnamon, clove, fennel, star anise, Sichuan pepper)

instructions: Whisk red fermented bean curd, hoisin sauce, soy sauces, Shaoxing wine, grated garlic, five-spice powder, and half the maltose into a smooth marinade.
Coat pork strips thoroughly in marinade; cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 6 hours or overnight.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F); place pork strips on a wire roasting rack suspended over a water-filled baking sheet; roast for 20 minutes.
Brush pork on all sides with reserved marinade; return to oven for another 15 minutes until interior reaches 70°C (158°F).

Brush generously with warm melted maltose/honey glaze, switch oven to broil, and caramelize for 3-4 minutes until edges develop crispy, blackened barbecue char marks; rest 10 minutes and slice into thick succulent slices.

title: Bibimbap

lines.text: 600 g Cooked Korean short-grain rice (piping hot)
250 g Lean beef sirloin or flank steak (cut into matchstick strips)
2 tbsp Korean soy sauce (jin-ganjang) (for beef and namul)
3 tbsp Toasted sesame oil (divided for seasoning and lining stone bowl)
150 g Blanched seasoned spinach (sigeumchi-namul) (with sesame and garlic)
4 mushrooms Fresh or rehydrated shiitake mushrooms (sliced and sautéed)
4 whole Fresh eggs (fried sunny-side up or raw yolk)
4 tbsp Gochujang bibim sauce (gochujang mixed with sesame oil, sugar, and vinegar)

instructions: Marinate beef strips in 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 clove minced garlic, and 1 tsp sugar for 15 minutes, then sear quickly in a hot skillet for 2 minutes.
Prepare individual namul: blanch spinach and bean sprouts separately, squeeze dry, toss with sesame oil, minced garlic, and salt; sauté julienned carrots and sliced shiitakes separately.
Coat the interior of heavy granite stone bowls (dolsot) generously with toasted sesame oil; place over medium-high heat until the oil sizzles.
Scoop warm rice into sizzling stone bowls; arrange seasoned vegetables and cooked beef in neat colorful segments radiating like wheel spokes over the rice.

Top center with a sunny-side-up fried egg; let stone sizzle for 3 minutes to form crunchy golden scorched rice (nurungji) at the bottom; serve immediately with sweet-spicy gochujang sauce to stir and mix vigorously before eating.

title: Kimchi Jjigae

lines.text: 400 g Fully fermented aged sour baechu kimchi (chopped, with 80ml sour kimchi brine)
250 g Pork belly or pork shoulder (cut into bite-sized pieces)
250 g Firm or medium-firm tofu (sliced into thick rectangles)
600 ml Dried anchovy and kelp stock (traditional Korean broth base)
1.5 tbsp Korean chili pepper flakes (gochugaru) (for heat and rich red broth)
1 tbsp Toasted sesame oil (for stir-frying kimchi)

instructions: In an earthenware pot (ttukbaegi) or heavy Dutch oven, sauté pork belly with sesame oil over medium heat until edges begin to crisp and fat renders.
Add chopped sour kimchi and minced garlic, stir-frying with the pork fat for 7 minutes until the kimchi becomes translucent and deeply aromatic.
Pour in anchovy-kelp broth and sour kimchi juice; stir in gochugaru, gochujang, and a dash of soup soy sauce.
Bring to a vigorous boil, then lower heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until pork is tender and kimchi flavors have permeated the broth.
Arrange sliced tofu rectangles and diagonal scallion slices neatly across the top; simmer for 4 minutes until tofu absorbs the fiery broth; serve bubbling hot with steamed rice.

title: Bulgogi

lines.text: 650 g Prime beef ribeye or top sirloin (partially frozen and sliced paper-thin across the grain)
100 g Grated Asian / Korean pear (natural meat tenderizer)
2 tbsp Brown sugar or honey (for caramelization)
12 leaves Crisp red leaf lettuce and perilla leaves (for ssam wraps)

instructions: In a bowl, blend grated Korean pear, soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, minced garlic, grated ginger, and black pepper into a smooth marinade.
Add thinly shaved beef slices, sliced onion, and scallions to the marinade; massage thoroughly with hands so every ribbon of beef absorbs the liquid; marinate 30 minutes.
Heat a cast-iron grill pan or barbecue plate over high heat until smoking hot; brush lightly with oil.
Spread marinated beef in a single uncrowded layer; cook without moving for 90 seconds until edges char and caramelize, then flip and cook for another 60 seconds until just cooked through.
Transfer onto a sizzling cast-iron platter, sprinkle generously with toasted sesame seeds, and serve immediately with fresh lettuce, ssamjang dip, and steamed rice.

title: Tteokbokki

lines.text: 450 g Cylindrical rice cakes (garaetteok) (cut into 5cm cylinders, soaked in warm water)
150 g Korean sheet fish cakes (eomuk) (sliced into triangles)
600 ml Dried anchovy and dashima broth (aromatic base)
3 tbsp Gochujang (Korean chili paste) (savory chili paste)
1.5 tbsp Gochugaru (Korean chili flakes) (for clean heat)
2 tbsp Sugar and Korean rice syrup (mulyeot) (for glossy glaze and sweet balance)
2 whole Hard-boiled eggs (halved, to soak up sauce)

instructions: Bring anchovy-kelp broth to a boil in a wide shallow pan; whisk in gochujang, gochugaru, sugar, rice syrup, and minced garlic until fully dissolved.
Add soaked rice cakes to the bubbling sauce; cook over medium-high heat for 5 minutes, stirring continuously so rice cakes don't stick to the bottom.
Add sliced fish cake triangles and continue simmering for 6-8 minutes until sauce reduces into a thick, glossy, bright red gravy that clings to the rice cakes.
Toss in sliced scallions and hard-boiled egg halves, simmering for 2 minutes more until scallions wilt slightly.
Transfer onto a wide plate or bowl, sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds, and serve piping hot with street-food toothpicks.

title: Biryani

lines.text: 600 g Long-grain aged Basmati rice (soaked for 45 minutes, parboiled to 70%)
900 g Bone-in goat or lamb shoulder pieces (cut into curry pieces)
250 g Thick whole milk yogurt (dahi) (whisked with ginger-garlic paste and chili)
180 g Crispy fried golden onions (birista) (deeply browned)
2 tbsp Whole garam masala (green cardamom, black cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, mace, shahi jeera) (for rice and meat)
100 ml Saffron threads steeped in warm whole milk (with 1 tsp kewra water)
50 g Fresh mint leaves and coriander cilantro (chopped)

instructions: Marinate meat in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, half the fried onions, fresh mint, coriander, and salt for at least 4 hours.
Parboil soaked basmati rice in heavily salted water infused with whole spices (cinnamon, cloves, cardamom) until grains are 70% cooked (firm core remaining); drain immediately.
In a heavy-bottomed brass or cast iron handi, lay marinated meat and juices across the bottom (kacchi biryani style); spread drained hot basmati rice evenly over meat in an airy layer.
Scatter remaining crispy fried onions, chopped mint, melted desi ghee, and drizzle aromatic saffron milk across the rice in vibrant golden streaks.

Seal handi lid tightly with a strip of wheat flour dough (dum); cook on high heat for 15 minutes to generate steam, then place on a cast iron tawa over low heat for 45 minutes; rest 15 minutes before gently fluffing and carving from the bottom.

title: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)

lines.text: 800 g Boneless skinless chicken thighs (cut into large chunks)
150 g Thick hung yogurt (mixed with kashmiri chili, ginger-garlic paste, and lemon)
800 g Ripe red tomatoes (quartered and pureed smooth)
50 g Raw cashews (soaked and ground into a silky cream)
100 ml Heavy dairy cream (for finishing gravy)
2 tbsp Kashmiri red chili powder (imparts rich natural crimson hue without harsh heat)
1.5 tbsp Dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi) (crushed between palms (essential signature aroma))
1 tsp Royal garam masala (fragrant spice blend)

instructions: Marinate chicken in yogurt, lemon juice, Kashmiri chili, ginger-garlic paste, and salt for at least 2 hours; skewer and broil at maximum heat (260°C / 500°F) for 12 minutes until charred and cooked through.
In a pot, simmer pureed tomatoes with ginger, garlic, green cardamoms, and Kashmiri chili for 20 minutes until oil separates and raw tomato flavor vanishes.
Strain tomato sauce through a fine sieve into a clean pan for ultimate silkiness; stir in the smooth cashew paste and simmer for 5 minutes.
Whisk in unsalted butter and heavy cream over low heat until sauce becomes glossy and velvety (makhani); add grilled chicken pieces along with their charred juices.
Crush toasted kasuri methi leaves between palms and sprinkle over the curry along with garam masala and a tiny pinch of sugar; simmer 3 minutes and serve with warm garlic naan.

title: Masala Dosa

lines.text: 600 g Fermented dosa batter (parboiled rice & urad dal) (fermented 12 hours until airy and tangy)
400 g Boiled potatoes (peeled and coarsely smashed)
1 tsp Brown mustard seeds (popped in hot oil)
1 tbsp Chana dal and urad dal (fried until nutty golden)
0.5 tsp Ground turmeric (gives potato filling its golden color)
2 chilies Green bird's eye chilies and ginger (finely chopped)
40 ml Gingelly (sesame) oil or ghee (for roasting dosa crispy)
150 g Fresh white coconut chutney (tempered with mustard and curry leaves)
300 ml Vegetable sambar lentil stew (hot lentil-tamarind broth)

instructions: Make potato filling: pop mustard seeds in 1 tbsp oil, add chana dal, curry leaves, chopped green chilies, ginger, and sliced onions; sauté until soft.
Add turmeric, salt, coarsely smashed potatoes, and 3 tablespoons water; simmer for 4 minutes into a moist, fragrant spiced potato mash; set aside warm.
Heat a heavy cast-iron tawa until water droplets dance on the surface; wipe with an oiled cloth.
Pour a ladleful (approx. 80ml) of fermented batter in the center and swiftly spread outward in a spiral motion with the back of the ladle into a paper-thin, expansive round disc.

Drizzle ghee or oil around the edges and cook over medium-high heat until the underside turns golden brown and deeply crisp; place potato masala in the center, fold both sides into a roll, and serve on a banana leaf with coconut chutney and hot sambar.

title: Chole Bhature

lines.text: 300 g Dried kabuli chickpeas (soaked overnight with black tea bag for deep dark color)
50 g Fine semolina (sooji) (gives bhatura crisp exterior)
1.5 tbsp Pomegranate seed powder (anardana) (signature Amritsari tartness)
2 tbsp Punjabi chole masala spices (coriander, cumin, amchur, black cardamom) (fragrant spice blend)
2 tbsp Fresh ginger cut into needle juliennes (for tempering)
50 ml Ghee or vegetable oil (for curry and deep frying)
60 g Pickled red onions and green chilies (classic accompaniment)

instructions: Knead flour, semolina, yogurt, baking powder, pinch of salt, and warm water into a smooth dough; rest covered in a warm spot for 2 hours.
Pressure cook soaked chickpeas with tea bag, black cardamom, and salt for 6 whistles until melt-in-the-mouth soft and dark-tinted.
In a kadai, heat ghee, sauté finely chopped onions, ginger, garlic, and tomato puree; add chole masala and roasted anardana powder, cooking until oil separates.
Add cooked chickpeas and simmering liquid; mash a few chickpeas with the back of a ladle to thicken gravy, simmering for 15 minutes into a dark, robust curry.

Roll rested bhatura dough into large ovals, slide gently into smoking hot oil (190°C / 375°F), pressing lightly with a slotted spoon until it instantly puffs into a huge hollow golden balloon; serve immediately with dark chole, pickled onions, and lemon.

title: Rogan Josh

lines.text: 900 g Bone-in lamb shoulder or shank pieces (cut into curry chunks)
80 g Pure desi cow ghee (traditional Kashmiri cooking medium)
2.5 tbsp Mild Kashmiri chili powder (dissolved in 4 tbsp warm water for radiant crimson color)
1.5 tbsp Fennel seed powder (saunf) (signature Kashmiri aromatic)
1 tbsp Dry ginger powder (saunth) (essential Kashmiri spice)
200 g Whisked plain whole milk curd (dahi) (whisked smooth)
0.25 tsp Asafoetida (hing) (traditional Kashmiri Pandit style (no onion/garlic))
1 tbsp Whole green cardamoms, black cardamom, cloves, cinnamon (aromatic tempering)

instructions: Heat ghee in a heavy copper degh or Dutch oven; crack whole spices (cloves, black cardamom, cinnamon, hing) until fragrant.
Add lamb pieces and sear vigorously over medium-high heat for 12 minutes until deeply browned and sealed.
Lower heat, stir in Kashmiri red chili paste, stirring rapidly for 1 minute until the ghee turns an intense, shimmering jewel-ruby red.
Slowly pour in whisked yogurt in a steady stream while stirring vigorously to prevent curdling; cook until yogurt reduces and fat floats to the surface.

Add fennel powder, dry ginger powder, salt, and 300ml warm water; cover tightly and simmer on lowest heat for 60 minutes until lamb is meltingly tender and sauce is rich, silken, and deeply perfumed; rest 10 minutes before serving.

title: Samosa

lines.text: 250 g All-purpose flour (maida) (for samosa pastry crust)
50 g Warm ghee or oil (moyen) (rubbed into flour for flaky crust (khasta))
450 g Boiled potatoes (coarsely crushed, not mashed)
1.5 tbsp Whole coriander seeds and cumin (coarsely crushed and toasted)
2 tbsp Green chilies and fresh ginger (finely minced)
1000 ml Vegetable oil or ghee (for slow deep frying)
100 g Sweet tamarind and spicy mint-coriander chutneys (for dipping)

instructions: Rub warm ghee and ajwain seeds into flour with fingertips until mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs; add cold water gradually to knead into a very stiff, firm dough; rest covered for 30 minutes.

In a skillet, toast crushed coriander seeds and cumin in 1 tbsp oil; add ginger, chilies, green peas, crushed potatoes, amchur, garam masala, and salt; sauté 4 minutes into a dry spiced filling; cool completely.
Divide dough into smooth balls, roll into thin ovals, slice each oval in half horizontally to make semi-circles.

Wet straight edge with water, fold into a neat cone, overlap and pinch seal tightly; fill cone 3/4 full with potato filling, moisten top rim, and pleat the back before pressing closed to form a self-standing pyramid samosa.

Lower samosas into medium-low oil (140°C / 285°F); fry slowly for 10 minutes until pale crust forms, then increase heat slightly and fry another 6 minutes until deep golden brown, blister-free, and shatteringly crisp; serve with mint and tamarind chutneys.

title: Dal Makhani

lines.text: 250 g Whole black lentils (sabut urad dal) (soaked overnight for at least 10 hours)
90 g Unsalted white or yellow butter (makkhan) (divided throughout slow cooking)
80 ml Heavy dairy cream (for finishing richness)
2 tbsp Fresh ginger and garlic paste (finely ground)
1.5 tbsp Kashmiri chili powder (adds crimson color)

instructions: Wash soaked black lentils and rajma thoroughly; boil in a deep heavy pot with 1.5 liters of water, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, salt, and 1 tsp chili powder for 60 minutes until soft.
In a separate pan, melt 40g butter and cook tomato purée with remaining ginger-garlic paste and Kashmiri chili until oil separates.
Pour cooked tomato masala into the lentils; mash some lentils against the side of the pot with a heavy wooden dal masher to release natural starch.
Simmer on the lowest possible heat for 45 minutes, adding small splashes of warm water and half the remaining butter, stirring regularly as it turns creamy and dark brown.
Stir in heavy cream, remaining butter, crushed kasuri methi, and garam masala; simmer gently for 5 minutes until luxurious and velvety; serve hot with jeera rice or butter naan.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala

lines.text: 800 g Chicken breast or thigh meat (cut into 3cm bite-size pieces)
150 g Greek or hung plain yogurt (for chicken marinade)
400 g Canned crushed plum tomatoes (finely pureed)
120 ml Heavy cream (for creamy masala gravy)
2 tbsp Garam masala, cumin, coriander, and turmeric (balanced spice blend)
1.5 tbsp Kashmiri chili powder or paprika (for vibrant color without excessive heat)

instructions: Toss chicken with yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp paprika, lemon juice, and salt; marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Thread chicken onto skewers and broil on highest oven setting for 10-12 minutes, turning once until charred at edges; set aside.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil/butter in a wide pan, sauté finely diced onions until golden brown; add remaining garlic-ginger paste and dry spices, blooming for 1 minute.
Pour in pureed tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes until sauce reduces and darkens; stir in heavy cream until sauce is creamy orange-red.
Slide the charred chicken pieces into the bubbling sauce, simmer for 5 minutes to infuse flavors, and garnish with chopped fresh cilantro before serving with fragrant pilau rice.

title: Appam / Hoppers

lines.text: 300 g Raw white rice (soaked for 4 hours and ground smooth)
50 g Cooked rice (ground with batter for softness)
250 ml Fresh thick coconut milk (first and second extract)
0.5 tsp Active dry yeast or toddy (for natural fermentation)
1.5 tbsp Granulated sugar (feeds fermentation and adds sweetness)
80 ml Thick coconut cream (spooned into the soft center)
4 whole Fresh eggs (optional, for egg hoppers (biththara appa))
60 g Sri Lankan lunu miris or coconut sambol (spicy onion-chili relish)

instructions: Grind soaked rice and cooked rice with coconut milk, sugar, yeast, and salt into a smooth pourable batter; let ferment at warm room temperature for 8 hours until light and bubbly.
Thin fermented batter with a splash of coconut water or warm water to the consistency of light cream.
Heat a small curved appachatti (hopper pan) over medium heat; wipe lightly with oil.
Pour a ladleful of batter into the pan center, hold the pan handles, and immediately swirl in a circular motion so a thin layer coats the sloping walls while excess gathers in the center.

Crack an egg into center (for egg hopper), spoon 1 tbsp thick coconut cream over it, cover tightly with dome lid, and steam on medium-low for 3-4 minutes until edges are golden crispy lace and center egg is softly set; slide onto plate and serve with spicy lunu miris.
