title: Kottu Roti

lines.text: 6 pieces Godamba flatbreads (or parotta) (sliced into thin ribbons)
300 g Cooked chicken curry meat and spicy gravy (chopped, plus 150ml curry gravy)
3 whole Fresh eggs (cracked directly onto griddle)
3 chilies Green bird's eye chilies (finely chopped)
2 tbsp Fresh curry leaves and ginger-garlic (aromatic base)

instructions: Heat a flat cast-iron griddle or large heavy skillet over high heat with oil; sauté onions, green chilies, ginger-garlic paste, and curry leaves until fragrant.
Add shredded cabbage, carrots, and leeks, flash-frying on high heat for 3 minutes until crisp-tender.
Push vegetables to side, crack eggs onto the empty half of the griddle, scramble rapidly until just set, then toss into vegetables.
Toss in sliced roti strips and chopped curry chicken; pour hot spicy curry gravy over everything.

Using two heavy metal bench scrapers or spatulas, chop and toss the mixture vigorously against the griddle with rapid rhythmic strokes for 4 minutes until thoroughly integrated and piping hot; serve with a lime wedge.

title: Phở

lines.text: 2000 g Beef marrow and knuckle bones (blanched clean for sparkling clear broth)
500 g Beef brisket or flank (simmered in broth and thinly sliced)
300 g Beef eye of round or sirloin (sliced paper-thin for raw topping (tái))
600 g Fresh flat rice pho noodles (bánh phở) (scalded in hot water)
250 g Charred yellow onions and fresh ginger (charred black over open flame, washed clean)
2 tbsp Star anise, cassia bark, black cardamom, cloves, coriander seeds (lightly toasted in a dry pan and bagged in cheesecloth)
60 ml Vietnamese fish sauce (nước mắm) (added at end of broth cooking)
30 g Yellow rock sugar (rounds out savory depth)
100 g Scallions, cilantro, culantro (ngò gai), Thai basil, lime wedges (fresh herb garnishes)

instructions: Parboil beef bones in boiling water for 10 minutes to purge impurities; drain, scrub bones under cold running water, and wash pot thoroughly.

Return cleaned bones and brisket to pot with 5 liters fresh water; add charred onions, charred ginger, rock sugar, and salt; simmer on lowest heat, skimming surface frequently, for 3 hours without letting water boil violently.
Add toasted spice pouch (star anise, cinnamon, black cardamom, coriander seeds) to simmering broth during the final 45 minutes; remove brisket when tender and chill before slicing.
Season broth with high-grade fish sauce and keep at a rolling boil; scald fresh rice noodles in boiling water for 10 seconds, shake dry, and divide among warm soup bowls.

Arrange sliced cooked brisket and paper-thin slices of raw beef eye of round over noodles; ladle boiling hot broth directly over the raw beef to gently cook it; garnish with thinly sliced scallions and sweet white onions, serving with fresh herbs and lime.

title: Bánh Mì

lines.text: 4 loaves Vietnamese-style mini baguettes (ultra-light, airy interior with wafer-thin crispy crust)
100 g Silky pork liver pâté (spiced Vietnamese style)
160 g Vietnamese pork sausage roll (chả lụa) (thinly sliced)
120 g Pickled daikon and carrots (đồ chua) (tangy and sweet matchsticks)
1 cucumber Cucumber (sliced lengthwise into long spears)
1 bunch Fresh cilantro sprigs (washed and dried)
2 chilies Red bird's eye chilies (thinly sliced)
40 g Vietnamese egg mayonnaise (bơ) (rich egg-yolk and oil emulsion)
1 tbsp Maggi seasoning liquid (a few drops shaken onto sandwich)

instructions: Warm baguettes in a 200°C (400°F) oven for 3 minutes until the exterior crust is crackly and shatteringly crisp.
Slice warm baguette lengthwise down one side, opening like a book without cutting all the way through.
Spread rich egg mayonnaise along one side of the bread; spread a generous layer of pork liver pâté along the opposite side.
Layer slices of chả lụa pork sausage and cucumber spears into the cavity; add a handful of drained pickled daikon and carrots.
Stuff with long sprigs of fresh cilantro, fresh chili slices, and shake three drops of Maggi seasoning over the filling; press sandwich closed and slice diagonally to serve.

title: Bún Chả

lines.text: 400 g Ground pork shoulder (seasoned for grilled patties (chả viên))
300 g Pork belly (sliced thin for grilled strips (chả miếng))
1.5 tbsp Caramel sauce (nước màu) (adds deep smoky sweetness and color to pork)
80 ml High-grade fish sauce (nước mắm) (for marinade and dipping broth)
400 g Fresh or dried rice vermicelli noodles (bún) (cooked and coiled into nests)
100 g Green papaya or kohlrabi and carrots (thinly sliced and lightly pickled)
400 ml Warm sweet-and-sour dipping broth (fish sauce, lime juice, rice vinegar, sugar, water)
150 g Vietnamese herbs (mint, perilla/tía tô, cilantro, butterhead lettuce) (fresh and washed)

instructions: Marinate sliced pork belly and ground pork separately with minced shallots, garlic, fish sauce, caramel sauce, sugar, and black pepper; form ground pork into small flattened patties.
Arrange pork patties and belly slices in a grilling wire basket; grill over glowing natural charcoal embers until deeply caramelized and charred with smoky edges.
Prepare dipping broth: whisk warm water, fish sauce, sugar, rice vinegar, and lime juice until balanced sweet, salty, and sour; stir in minced garlic, chili, and pickled green papaya slices.
Drop hot charcoal-grilled pork patties and sizzling belly slices directly into individual warm bowls of the seasoned dipping broth.
Serve accompanied by a platter of cool white rice vermicelli noodles and an overflowing basket of fresh herbs; diners dip noodles and herbs into the warm pork-filled broth with chopsticks.

title: Authentic Bangkok Pad Thai

lines.text: 300 g Medium flat rice noodles (sen lek) (soaked in room temperature water for 60 minutes)
300 g Fresh prawns or shrimp (peeled, deveined)
150 g Yellow firm pressed tofu (cut into small batons)
60 ml Tamarind pulp concentrate (sour base for sauce)
45 ml Thai fish sauce (nam pla) (savory umami)
150 g Fresh bean sprouts (rinsed and drained)
25 g Sweet preserved salted radish (chai pow) (finely minced)

instructions: Whisk tamarind concentrate, shaved palm sugar, and fish sauce in a small pot over low heat until sugar is completely dissolved into a balanced tart-sweet amber sauce.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a wok over high heat; sear shrimp for 2 minutes until pink; remove to a plate.
In remaining wok oil, stir-fry firm tofu cubes, dried shrimp, minced preserved radish, and shallots until golden and aromatic.
Add soaked drained rice noodles and ladle in the tamarind sauce; toss vigorously for 3 minutes until noodles absorb sauce and turn translucent, soft, and chewy.

Push noodles aside, crack in eggs and scramble gently; fold back noodles, add cooked shrimp, bean sprouts, and garlic chives; toss for 1 minute and serve immediately with lime wedges, crushed peanuts, and chili flakes.

title: Tom Yum

lines.text: 450 g Fresh head-on river prawns or shrimp (heads reserved for rich broth)
3 stalks Fresh lemongrass stalks (bruised and sliced diagonally)
40 g Fresh galangal root (sliced into coins)
6 leaves Fresh makrut lime leaves (torn, center vein removed)
6 chilies Thai bird's eye chilies (prik kee noo) (crushed lightly with side of knife)
150 g Straw mushrooms or oyster mushrooms (halved)
2 tbsp Thai roasted chili jam (nam prik pao) (for smoky aromatic red swirl)
50 ml Fresh lime juice (added strictly off heat to preserve brightness)
60 ml Evaporated milk (for creamy Tom Yum Nam Khon style)
2 tbsp Fresh cilantro and sawtooth herb (garnish)

instructions: In a pot, lightly sauté prawn heads in 1 tbsp oil, crushing them to release flavorful orange tomalley fat; add 1 liter water and simmer 10 minutes, then strain out heads.
Bring the rich prawn stock to a boil; add bruised lemongrass, sliced galangal, torn makrut lime leaves, and crushed bird's eye chilies; simmer for 4 minutes until intensely fragrant.
Whisk in roasted chili jam (nam prik pao), fish sauce, and mushrooms; bring back to a rolling simmer.
Add fresh peeled prawns and evaporated milk; cook gently for 2 minutes just until prawns curl and turn opaque and tender.
Turn off heat completely; immediately stir in fresh lime juice (crucial to add off heat to avoid bitterness); garnish with cilantro and serve piping hot.

title: Thai Green Curry (Gaeng Khiao Wan)

lines.text: 500 g Boneless skinless chicken thighs (sliced into bite-sized pieces)
70 g Fresh authentic Thai green curry paste (pounded green chilies, lemongrass, galangal, shrimp paste, kaffir peel)
250 ml Thick coconut cream (first press, cracked for frying paste)
250 ml Coconut milk (for simmering curry base)
6 whole Round green Thai eggplants (quartered and soaked in salted water)
40 g Pea eggplants (makhuea phuang) (small round bitter clusters)
1.5 tbsp Shaved palm sugar (for sweet balance)
5 leaves Makrut lime leaves (shredded into fine chiffonade)

instructions: In a heavy pot, heat half the coconut cream over medium heat, stirring steadily for 5 minutes until it 'cracks' and fragrant clear coconut oil separates from the milk solids.
Add the green curry paste to the split coconut oil; fry over medium-low heat for 4 minutes until paste is deeply aromatic and releases a glossy green sheen.
Add sliced chicken pieces, stirring to coat and sear gently in the curry paste for 3 minutes.

Pour in remaining coconut milk, bring to a gentle boil, then add Thai eggplants, pea eggplants, shredded lime leaves, palm sugar, and fish sauce; simmer uncovered for 8 minutes until eggplants are tender.
Turn off heat, stir in fresh Thai sweet basil leaves and red chili slivers, letting them wilt instantly; serve hot alongside jasmine rice or khanom jeen rice noodles.

title: Som Tam

lines.text: 400 g Unripe green papaya (peeled and finely shredded into crisp crunchy matchsticks)
4 chilies Thai bird's eye chilies (to taste)
4 cloves Thai garlic cloves (unpeeled small cloves)
60 g Yardlong green beans (cut into 3cm segments and bruised)
3 tbsp Fresh lime juice (plus spent lime hulls squeezed into mortar)

instructions: In a tall clay mortar (krok), pound garlic cloves and bird's eye chilies with a wooden pestle until coarsely crushed.
Add palm sugar, dried shrimp, and peanuts, pounding into a coarse paste; add yardlong bean segments and lightly bruise to absorb dressing.
Add lime juice, lime hulls, and fish sauce; use pestle and a large spoon to dissolve palm sugar and emulsify the dressing.
Add halved cherry tomatoes and shredded crisp green papaya; pound gently with the pestle in one hand while using a spoon in the other to continuously toss and fold the salad from the bottom.
Taste and balance for the harmonious symphony of sour, spicy, sweet, and salty; transfer immediately to a plate and serve alongside warm sticky rice (khao niao) and grilled chicken.

title: Nasi Goreng

lines.text: 600 g Day-old chilled long-grain white rice (grains separated, slightly dry for best texture)
3 tbsp Indonesian sweet soy sauce (kecap manis) (caramelized sweet soy)
4 tbsp Shallots, garlic, red chilies, candlenuts, and toasted shrimp paste (terasi) (ground in cobek stone mortar)
200 g Cooked shredded chicken or prawns (bite-sized)
4 whole Fresh eggs (fried sunny-side up with crispy frilly edges (telur ceplok))
100 g Sliced cucumber, tomato, and shallot pickles (crisp fresh garnish)

instructions: Grind shallots, garlic, red chilies, candlenuts, and toasted terasi shrimp paste into a fine paste (bumbu) in a stone mortar.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a wok over high heat; fry bumbu paste for 3 minutes until deeply fragrant and oil separates.
Add shredded chicken, tossing for 1 minute; dump in chilled day-old rice, breaking up any clumps with the wok spatula.

Drizzle kecap manis in a circle around the hot wok perimeter so it caramelizes slightly; toss rice vigorously over maximum heat for 3 minutes until every grain is glossy, dark brown, and infused with smoky wok hei.
Toss in sliced scallions; transfer onto plates and top each portion with a crispy fried sunny-side egg, crunchy krupuk prawn crackers, cucumber slices, and sweet Indonesian pickle (acar).

title: Rendang

lines.text: 1000 g Beef chuck or shank (cut into thick 4cm cubes)
1200 ml Fresh thick coconut milk (extracted from 3 mature coconuts)
180 g Shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, lemongrass, turmeric, and curly red chilies (finely ground in stone cobek)
2 leaves Fresh turmeric leaves (daun kunyit) (tied in knots (vital signature aroma))
2 pieces Dried garcinia (asam kandis) or tamarind (subtle tartness)
50 g Toasted grated coconut paste (kerisik) (ground until oily and brown)

instructions: In a large heavy wok or Dutch oven, bring coconut milk, ground rempah paste, knotted turmeric leaves, bruised lemongrass, and lime leaves to a boil, stirring constantly to prevent curdling.
Add beef cubes and asam kandis; reduce heat to medium and simmer uncovered for 1 hour, stirring occasionally, until liquid reduces by half into a thick yellow curry (gulai stage).
Continue simmering for another 45 minutes as sauce thickens into a rich oily red-brown gravy (kalio stage); stir in toasted coconut paste (kerisik).
Lower heat to gentle flame; cook for another 60 minutes, stirring continuously as water evaporates completely and the beef begins to slow-fry in its own rendered spiced coconut oil.

Stir constantly for the final 20 minutes until the coconut solids turn dark chocolate brown, dry, and crumbly (rendang stage), coating each tender beef chunk in dark, deeply concentrated savory crust; rest 30 minutes before serving with steamed rice.

title: Satay

lines.text: 600 g Boneless skinless chicken thighs (cut into 2cm cubes)
1.5 tbsp Ground coriander and turmeric (gives signature yellow hue)
4 tbsp Indonesian sweet soy sauce (kecap manis) (for basting glaze)
200 g Roasted skinless peanuts (ground coarsely for peanut sauce)
2 tbsp Palm sugar and tamarind paste (sweet-sour balance)
150 g Compressed rice cakes (lontong) and raw shallots (traditional accompaniment)

instructions: Blend shallots, garlic, lemongrass, ginger, ground coriander, turmeric, salt, and 1 tbsp oil into a smooth marinade; toss with chicken cubes and marinate for 30 minutes.
Thread 4 pieces of chicken tightly onto soaked bamboo skewers.

Make peanut sauce: fry minced chili and garlic in oil, add ground roasted peanuts, coconut milk, tamarind paste, palm sugar, and kecap manis; simmer 8 minutes into a thick, coarse, fragrant brown dip.

Grill skewers over glowing coconut charcoal or high grill heat for 3 minutes per side; baste generously with a mixture of kecap manis and oil, grilling 2 minutes more until charred, glossy, and caramelized.
Arrange skewers on a platter, ladle warm chunky peanut sauce generously over the chicken, shower with crispy fried shallots, and serve with cubed lontong rice cakes.

title: Laksa

lines.text: 400 g Thick round rice noodles (laksa vermicelli) (scalded in boiling water)
350 g Fresh prawns (peeled, heads and shells reserved for stock)
10 pieces Fried tofu puffs (tau pok) (halved to soak up curry broth)
40 g Dried shrimp (hae bee) (soaked and pounded for rempah)
150 g Shallots, garlic, galangal, lemongrass, fresh turmeric, belacan, and dried red chilies (ground into smooth spice paste)
1 bunch Fresh Vietnamese coriander / laksa leaf (daun kesum) (finely chopped (essential aroma))
4 tsp Sambal belacan chili paste (served on soup spoon with calamansi lime)

instructions: Sauté reserved prawn heads and shells in oil until fragrant; add 1 liter water and simmer for 20 minutes, then press shells and strain to extract concentrated seafood stock.
In a heavy pot, fry the pounded rempah paste and soaked dried shrimp in oil over medium heat for 12 minutes until oil separates and the aroma fills the kitchen.
Pour the hot prawn stock and coconut milk into the fried rempah; add halved tofu puffs, fresh laksa leaves (daun kesum), and salt; simmer gently for 15 minutes.
Add fresh prawns and sliced fish cakes into the bubbling curry broth; poach for 3 minutes until prawns turn pink and cooked through.

Place blanched thick rice noodles and bean sprouts into deep bowls; ladle the boiling rich coconut curry broth, prawns, fish cakes, and spongy tofu puffs over noodles; garnish with finely chopped fresh laksa leaves and serve with sambal and calamansi lime.

title: Chicken Adobo

lines.text: 900 g Bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks (skin-on)
120 ml Filipino cane vinegar (sukang maasim) or coconut vinegar (mild, fruity acidity)
80 ml Filipino dark soy sauce (toyo) (Silver Swan or Datu Puti)
4 leaves Dried bay leaves (dahon ng laurel) (aromatic leaves)
1 tsp Brown sugar (rounds sharp vinegar edges)

instructions: Combine chicken pieces with smashed garlic, soy sauce, cracked black peppercorns, and bay leaves in a bowl; marinate for 20 minutes.
Transfer chicken and marinade into a heavy pot; bring to a boil over medium heat.
Pour in cane vinegar and brown sugar; allow to boil vigorously uncovered for 5 minutes without stirring (crucial to cook off raw acid harshness).
Lower heat, cover tightly, and simmer for 25 minutes until chicken is tender and cooked through.

Remove chicken pieces and sear in a hot skillet with 1 tbsp oil until skin is deeply caramelized and crisp; return to the reduced simmering adobo sauce until coated in a thick, glossy, savory-tangy glaze; serve over garlic sinangag rice.

title: Classic Levantine Hummus

lines.text: 400 g Cooked dried chickpeas (cooked with baking soda until ultra-soft and skins slip off)
160 g Pure Lebanese or Palestinian sesame tahini (runny, smooth and unroasted)
60 ml Ice water or ice cubes (whips tahini into a pale, airy cream)
40 ml Levantine extra virgin olive oil (for pooling in center)
1 tbsp Ground sumac, whole chickpeas, and fresh parsley (garnish)

instructions: Simmer cooked chickpeas with 0.5 tsp baking soda in water for 15 minutes until so soft they crush effortlessly between two fingers; drain.
In a high-powered food processor, blend tahini, fresh lemon juice, crushed garlic, and salt for 2 minutes until thick and pale.
Drizzle in ice water while running processor; blend until tahini whips into an airy, cloud-white emulsified cream.
Add the warm soft chickpeas and cumin; process continuously for 4-5 minutes, scraping down sides, until the hummus is silkily smooth with zero graininess.

Spoon into a shallow ceramic bowl, using the back of the spoon to create a deep circular well; pool generous extra virgin olive oil in the center, and decorate with reserved whole chickpeas, sumac, and chopped parsley.

title: Crispy Herb Falafel

lines.text: 350 g Dried chickpeas (or peeled dried fava beans) (soaked in cold water for 18 hours, NEVER boiled)
1 bunch Fresh flat-leaf parsley (leaves and tender stems)
2 tbsp Toasted cumin and ground coriander seeds (fragrant spice blend)
0.75 tsp Baking soda (provides light, airy, fluffy interior)
2 tbsp White sesame seeds (for pressing onto exterior before frying)
1000 ml Vegetable or sunflower oil (for deep frying)

instructions: Drain soaked chickpeas thoroughly and pat dry with paper towels (excess moisture causes falafel to crumble in hot oil).

In a food processor, pulse chickpeas, onion, garlic, parsley, cilantro, dill, cumin, coriander, salt, and black pepper in short pulses until mixture forms a fine, sandy meal that holds together when squeezed (do not purée into paste).
Transfer mixture to a bowl, fold in baking soda, cover, and chill in refrigerator for 30 minutes to firm up.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 180°C (355°F); shape mixture using a falafel scoop (aleb falafel) or wet hands into 3.5cm discs, pressing raw sesame seeds onto the outside.

Fry falafel in batches for 3.5 to 4 minutes, turning occasionally until exterior is deep golden brown and hyper-crunchy while inside remains bright herbaceous green, moist and steaming; drain on paper towels and serve with tahini dip.

title: Shakshuka

lines.text: 2 peppers Red and yellow bell peppers (seeded and diced)
500 g Crushed whole peeled plum tomatoes (canned or fresh ripe)
1.5 tbsp Tunisian harissa chili paste (adjust to heat preference)
1.5 tbsp Ground cumin and smoked paprika (aromatic spices)
3 tbsp Extra virgin olive oil (for sautéing)
2 tbsp Fresh cilantro and parsley (chopped for garnish)

instructions: Heat olive oil in a wide heavy cast-iron skillet over medium heat; sauté onions and diced bell peppers for 8 minutes until soft and caramelized.
Add sliced garlic, harissa paste, ground cumin, and smoked paprika, stirring constantly for 2 minutes to bloom the spices.
Pour in crushed tomatoes, season with salt and freshly ground black pepper; simmer uncovered over medium-low heat for 12 minutes until sauce thickens into a rich, chunky ragout.
Use the back of a large spoon to make 4 distinct wells in the bubbling tomato sauce; crack an egg directly into each well.

Cover the skillet with a lid and cook on low heat for 5-7 minutes until egg whites are just opaque and set while yolks remain liquid and runny; scatter chopped cilantro, parsley, and crumbled feta, serving immediately right from the skillet with crusty bread.

title: Moroccan Tagine

lines.text: 1000 g Bone-in lamb shanks or bone-in chicken thighs (trimmed)
2 large Yellow onions (finely grated or grated with box grater for melting sauce)
2 tbsp Ground ginger, turmeric, and cinnamon (warm Moroccan spices)
0.5 g Taliouine saffron threads (crushed and soaked in warm water)
1 whole Moroccan preserved lemon (l'hamd marakad) (pulp removed, rind rinsed and sliced into strips)
100 g Purple or green Moroccan cured olives (meslalla) (blanched)
50 ml Moroccan olive oil (for gentle cooking)
1 bundle Fresh cilantro and flat-leaf parsley (tied with string)

instructions: Rub meat with ginger, turmeric, cinnamon, saffron water, half the garlic, and salt; marinate for 30 minutes.
In the base of an earthenware tagine over a heat diffuser on low flame, combine olive oil, grated onions, and remaining garlic; arrange seasoned meat over the onions.
Add herb bouquet and 150ml water; place conical tagine lid on top, cooking gently on low heat for 60 minutes as steam condenses on cone walls and bastes meat continuously.
Add preserved lemon rind strips and blanched olives; simmer covered for an additional 20 minutes until meat is fork-tender and falling off the bone.

Remove tagine lid, increase heat slightly for 5 minutes until onion sauce reduces into a thick, syrupy golden glaze (daghmira); scatter toasted blanched almonds over top and serve hot with crusty khobz bread.

title: Couscous

lines.text: 600 g Medium durum wheat couscous semolina (hand-worked with water and oil)
800 g Bone-in lamb shoulder or shank (cut into large pieces)
150 g Cooked dried chickpeas (soaked and boiled)
800 g Couscous vegetables (carrots, zucchini, turnips, butternut squash, cabbage) (cut into large uniform wedges)
300 g Grated ripe tomatoes and onion (for stew base)
40 g Aged fermented butter (smen) or sweet butter (worked into hot steamed couscous grains)
2 tbsp Ras el hanout, ginger, and turmeric (aromatic spices)
50 ml Olive oil (for couscous and stew)

instructions: In bottom pot of a couscoussier, brown lamb pieces with olive oil, grated onions, tomatoes, ginger, turmeric, salt, and pepper; add 2 liters of water and simmer for 30 minutes.

Moisten raw couscous semolina with water, a splash of oil, and salt in a wide shallow dish (gsaa); rake with fingers to separate all grains, transfer to perforated steamer top (kiskas), and steam over the stew for 20 minutes.
Tip steamed couscous back into gsaa, sprinkle with cold water, and fluff with fingers or a whisk to break all clumps; let rest for 10 minutes.

Add firm vegetables (carrots, turnips, cabbage, chickpeas) to the broth pot; return couscous to steamer top for second steaming (20 minutes); repeat aeration and add delicate squash and zucchini to broth for third and final steaming.

Turn out fluffy couscous into the large gsaa, work in fragrant smen butter with fingers until airy and glistening; mound couscous into a pyramid, hollow the peak, arrange tender meat on top, drape colorful vegetables in radiant spokes down the sides, and serve piping hot with bowls of spiced broth.

title: Harira

lines.text: 300 g Lean beef or lamb shoulder (cut into tiny 1cm cubes)
120 g Dried chickpeas (soaked overnight and skins pinched off)
3 stalks Celery ribs and leaves (finely chopped (distinctive flavor))
1 cup Fresh cilantro and parsley (finely minced)
600 g Ripe tomatoes (pureed with 2 tbsp tomato paste)
1 tbsp Aged Moroccan butter (smen) or butter (subtle pungent depth)
1.5 tbsp Ginger, turmeric, cinnamon, and black pepper (warm Moroccan spices)
80 g Tedouira slurry (flour whisked with water and lemon) (gives signature velvety thickness)
50 g Broken angel hair or vermicelli (chaariya) (added at end)

instructions: In a heavy soup pot, sauté diced beef, smen, chopped celery, half the cilantro, and grated onion in olive oil for 5 minutes.
Add soaked peeled chickpeas, brown lentils, ginger, turmeric, cinnamon, black pepper, and salt; pour in 1.8 liters water, bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 40 minutes until pulses are tender.
Stir in tomato purée and tomato paste; simmer for 10 minutes to blend flavors.
Slowly pour the tedouira flour-water slurry into the boiling soup while whisking continuously to prevent lumps; simmer on medium-low for 10 minutes until soup becomes silky, glossy, and velvety.
Add broken vermicelli noodles and remaining fresh cilantro; cook for 4 minutes until noodles are tender; serve hot with fresh lemon wedges, sweet dates, and chebakia pastries.

title: Egyptian Street-Style Koshari

lines.text: 200 g Brown Puy or brown lentils (kushari lentils) (cooked tender)
250 g Egyptian short-grain rice and vermicelli (toasted vermicelli cooked with rice in lentil water)
200 g Ditalini or elbow macaroni pasta (boiled tender)
150 g Cooked chickpeas (hummus) (canned or fresh boiled)
3 large Yellow onions (thinly sliced and deep-fried until deeply crispy and brown)
400 ml Garlicky spiced tomato sauce (salsa) (simmered with vinegar, cumin, and coriander)
80 ml Garlic-cumin vinegar dressing (da'ah) (white vinegar, garlic, cumin, and lime)
30 ml Spicy shatta chili oil (crushed red pepper fried in hot oil)

instructions: Deep fry thinly sliced onions in vegetable oil until dark golden brown, crispy, and fragrant; drain on paper towels; reserve the fragrant onion cooking oil for all other components.
Boil brown lentils in water with cumin until tender; drain, reserving dark cooking liquid. Toast broken vermicelli in 2 tbsp onion oil, add rice and lentil cooking liquid, and steam until fluffy.
Boil macaroni pasta separately in salted water until al dente; toss with 1 tbsp reserved onion oil.

Make sauce: fry minced garlic in 2 tbsp onion oil, add tomato paste, crushed tomatoes, cumin, coriander, and vinegar; simmer 10 minutes. In a small jar, shake vinegar, crushed garlic, cumin, and water for the da'ah dressing.

Assemble in large bowls: layer lentil-rice mixture, top with macaroni, then a ring of chickpeas, spoon boiling garlicky tomato sauce generously over everything, and crown with a massive mound of crispy fried onions; serve with side cruets of da'ah vinegar and fiery shatta chili oil.

title: Ful Medames

lines.text: 400 g Small dried brown fava beans (ful) (soaked and slow-simmered until buttery soft)
50 ml Extra virgin olive oil or flaxseed oil (zeit har) (traditional dressing)
3 cloves Garlic cloves (crushed with sea salt)
1 medium Ripe tomatoes (finely diced for garnish)
2 whole Hard-boiled eggs (halved and dusted with cumin (optional))

instructions: Warm cooked fava beans in a pot with a few tablespoons of their cooking liquor over medium-low heat until bubbling gently.
Use a potato masher or the back of a ladle to partially crush the fava beans against the pot, leaving half the beans whole for textural contrast.
Stir in crushed garlic, ground cumin, salt, half the lemon juice, and 2 tablespoons olive oil; heat through for 2 minutes.
Ladle hot fava beans into shallow earthenware bowls; drizzle tahini and remaining lemon juice over top.
Pour a generous pool of olive oil over the surface, scatter diced tomatoes and chopped parsley, top with halved hard-boiled eggs, and serve immediately with hot Egyptian baladi flatbread.

title: Mansaf

lines.text: 1400 g Bone-in lamb shoulder or shank pieces (large stewing cuts)
250 g Jameed (dried fermented goat-milk yogurt stone) (soaked overnight and blended smooth into thick tangy yogurt liquid)
600 g Medium-grain Egyptian or short-grain rice (cooked with turmeric and clarified butter)
3 sheets Paper-thin Bedouin shrak or markook flatbread (lines base of communal platter)
60 g Clarified sheep's butter (smen baladi) (adds authentic Bedouin aroma)
1 tbsp Green cardamom pods, bay leaves, cinnamon stick (whole aromatics for meat)
80 g Pine nuts and slivered almonds (toasted in smen until golden)

instructions: Break jameed stone into chunks, soak in warm water overnight, then blend in a high-speed blender into a silky, tangy goat-milk yogurt broth; strain through a sieve.
Boil lamb pieces in water with cardamom, cinnamon, bay leaf, and onion for 45 minutes, skimming foam until broth is clear.

In a separate pot, bring strained jameed liquid to a boil, stirring constantly in one direction to prevent curdling; pour boiling jameed into the simmering lamb pot and simmer together for 45 minutes until lamb is spoon-tender.
Cook rice with turmeric and a spoonful of smen until fluffy and golden.

On a massive round communal platter (sidiya), lay paper-thin shrak flatbread across the base and ladle hot jameed sauce over it; mound fragrant golden turmeric rice over the bread, arrange tender lamb cuts on top, shower with toasted pine nuts, almonds, and chopped parsley, and serve hot with bowls of warm jameed broth to pour over.

title: Kibbeh

lines.text: 300 g Fine brown or blonde bulgur wheat (#1 grind) (rinsed, drained and rested)
400 g Ultra-lean ground lamb or beef (kibbeh meat) (free of fat and sinew, pureed fine in food processor for shell)
350 g Ground lamb (20% fat) (for savory spiced hashweh filling)
2 medium Yellow onions (finely chopped for filling)
60 g Pine nuts (toasted golden in ghee)
2 tsp Levantine seven-spice (bharat) (allspice, cinnamon, clove, nutmeg, coriander, cumin, black pepper)

instructions: Make filling (hashweh): sauté chopped onions in ghee until soft, add ground lamb, seven-spice, cinnamon, salt, and pepper; cook until browned and dry; fold in toasted pine nuts and cool completely.

Make dough: knead soaked fine bulgur, ultra-lean pureed lamb, grated onion, salt, and cumin in a meat grinder or food processor with ice cubes until it forms a completely smooth, pliable meat dough paste.
Dip fingers in ice water, roll a golf-ball-sized portion of meat dough, hollow it out with your index finger into a thin, elongated cone cup.
Stuff the hollow cavity with 1.5 tablespoons of cooled spiced lamb-pine nut filling; pinch the open top closed into a tapered point, forming a neat pointed football/torpedo shape.

Deep fry kibbeh in hot oil at 180°C (355°F) for 5-6 minutes until mahogany brown and hyper-crispy on the outside while tender inside; drain on paper towels and serve with cool yogurt and lemon wedges.

title: Fattoush

lines.text: 2 rounds Thin Arabic pita breads (torn into bite-sized shards and fried or baked until crispy)
1 cup Fresh purslane (bakleh) or watercress (tender sprigs (traditional))
3 cucumbers Persian or Lebanese cucumbers (sliced into half-moons)
1 cup Fresh mint leaves and flat-leaf parsley (leaves coarsely torn)
1.5 tbsp Pomegranate molasses (dibs remman) (tangy sweet syrupy dressing)
1.5 tbsp Tart ground wild sumac (adds citrusy tang and burgundy flecks)
50 ml Extra virgin olive oil and lemon juice (emulsified dressing)

instructions: Tear pita bread into rough bite-sized pieces, toss with 1 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt, and bake at 190°C (375°F) for 8 minutes until golden and deeply crispy.
In a small bowl, whisk extra virgin olive oil, fresh lemon juice, pomegranate molasses, crushed garlic, ground sumac, and sea salt into a tangy, ruby-tinted vinaigrette.
In a large salad bowl, combine chopped romaine, fresh purslane, cucumbers, tomatoes, radishes, scallions, fresh mint, and parsley.
Pour dressing over vegetables and toss gently to coat every leaf evenly.
Scatter the crispy toasted pita chips over the top right before serving so they maintain maximum crunch; dust with an extra pinch of bright purple sumac.

title: Baklava

lines.text: 40 sheets Paper-thin phyllo pastry sheets (thawed and kept covered with damp towel)
400 g Vibrant green Antep pistachios or walnuts (finely ground)
280 g Clarified butter (ghee) or unsalted butter (melted and skimmed clear of milk solids)
1 tbsp Fresh lemon juice (prevents sugar crystallization)
1 tsp Orange blossom water or rosewater (traditional Levant aroma)

instructions: Boil sugar, water, and lemon juice in a saucepan for 10 minutes until syrup slightly thickens; stir in orange blossom water, remove from heat, and cool completely to room temperature.
Brush a 28x38cm metal baking pan with clarified butter; layer 20 sheets of phyllo into the pan, brushing each layer generously with warm clarified butter before adding the next.
Spread the finely crushed emerald pistachios in an even, dense layer across the buttered phyllo base.
Layer the remaining 20 phyllo sheets over the pistachios, brushing each layer with clarified butter; using a very sharp chef's knife, score all the way through into neat diamond or square shapes.

Bake at 160°C (325°F) for 50-55 minutes until the pastry is puffed, deeply flaky, and light golden; remove from oven and immediately ladle the cold sugar syrup over the piping hot pastry (creates intense sizzling sound and maximum crispness); rest 4 hours before serving.

title: Jollof Rice

lines.text: 500 g Long-grain parboiled rice (Nigerian) or fragrant jasmine rice (Ghanaian) (washed thoroughly until water runs clear)
3 large Red bell peppers (tatashe) (stemmed and seeded for pepper base)
2 peppers Scotch bonnet peppers (ata rodo) (for fruity heat)
2 large Red onions (1 blended, 1 sliced for frying)
100 g Double concentrated tomato paste (fried in oil for deep red hue)
100 ml Vegetable or sunflower oil (essential for frying pepper base)
2 tbsp Nigerian curry powder, dried thyme, and bay leaves (signature West African seasoning)
500 ml Rich chicken or vegetable stock (piping hot)

instructions: Blend red bell peppers, Scotch bonnet chilies, tomatoes, and 1 onion in a blender until smooth; boil in a saucepan for 15 minutes to reduce excess water into a concentrated paste.
Heat oil in a heavy Dutch oven, sauté sliced red onions for 5 minutes, then add tomato paste and fry for 7 minutes, stirring continuously until dark red and oil separates.
Pour in the boiled pepper puree, curry powder, dried thyme, bay leaves, and bouillon seasoning; fry over medium heat for 15 minutes until rich, thick, and glistening.
Add washed drained rice to the pot, stirring thoroughly to coat every grain in the tomato stew; pour in hot stock to barely level with the rice.

Cover the pot tightly with heavy aluminum foil and the lid (sealing in steam); cook over low heat for 25 minutes; allow bottom layer to catch slightly over medium heat for the final 5 minutes to infuse the signature smoky party-jollof flavor; fluff with a fork.

title: Thiéboudienne (Ceebu Jën)

lines.text: 1000 g Firm white fish (grouper, sea bass or white carp) (cut into thick steaks)
1 cup Rof stuffing: parsley, scallions, garlic, bird's eye chili (pounded into paste to stuff fish slits)
600 g Double-broken jasmine rice (ceeb) (rinsed and steamed over the stew)
120 g Tomato paste (for deep red ceebu jën rouge)
800 g Cassava root, sweet potato, carrots, eggplant, cabbage, and okra (cut into large chunks)
50 g Fermented dried fish (guéy) or dried conch (yeet) (essential Senegalese umami depth)
40 g Tamarind paste and green sorrel leaves (bissap) (for sour contrast relish)

instructions: Cut deep slits into fish steaks; stuff each pocket tightly with the pounded rof herb paste (parsley, garlic, chili, bouillon).
In a heavy pot, brown onions and yeet (fermented conch) in peanut oil; add tomato paste and cook for 8 minutes until oil reddens, then add 2 liters water, salt, and bring to a boil.

Carefully lower stuffed fish steaks and whole vegetables (cassava, sweet potato, carrots, eggplant, cabbage) into the bubbling broth; simmer gently for 30 minutes until fish is cooked through and vegetables are tender.
Remove fish and all vegetables with a slotted spoon onto a large platter; keep warm with a ladle of broth.

Stir rinsed broken rice into the remaining red tomato-fish broth; cover tightly and cook on low heat for 30 minutes until the rice absorbs every drop of flavor, developing a crispy browned bottom crust (xooñ); spread rice across a communal platter and arrange fish and vegetables on top.

title: Injera

lines.text: 400 g Brown or ivory teff flour (ancient Ethiopian gluten-free grain)
600 ml Filtered water (for natural wild yeast fermentation)
60 ml Fermented teff starter (ersho) (from previous batch or active wild yeast)
100 ml Cooked teff starter gel (absit) (boiling a cup of fermented batter with water to gelatinize, then whisking back in)

instructions: Mix teff flour, ersho starter, and water into a thin paste in a glass or ceramic container; cover with a cloth and let ferment at warm room temperature for 3 days until bubbly, tangy, and separated.
Pour off the yellowish water accumulated on top of the fermented batter.

Make absit: take 100ml of fermented batter, whisk into 150ml boiling water in a saucepan for 2 minutes until glossy and thick like pudding; let cool to lukewarm, then whisk back into the main batter (this creates the signature air pockets).
Rest the batter for 1 hour until vigorous bubbles form across the surface; the batter should be the consistency of thin pancake batter.

Heat an electric crêpe maker or nonstick electric mitad to 200°C (400°F); pour batter in a spiral from the outer edge inward; when thousand eyes (ayen) bubbles appear across the surface (approx 45 seconds), cover with lid and steam for 2 minutes without flipping; slide off and cool on a straw mesob.

title: Doro Wat

lines.text: 1300 g Whole chicken (cut into 12 traditional pieces and soaked in lemon water)
1200 g Red onions (finely minced in food processor without oil)
120 g Ethiopian spiced clarified butter (niter kibbeh) (infused with koseret, korarima, and fenugreek)
60 g Authentic Ethiopian berbere spice blend (sun-dried chili, fenugreek, korarima, ginger)
3 tbsp Fresh garlic and ginger paste (finely ground)
6 whole Hard-boiled eggs (peeled and pierced with fork to absorb spicy sauce)
0.5 tsp Ethiopian black cardamom (korarima) (ground for finishing aroma)

instructions: In a dry heavy pot with no oil, cook the finely minced red onions over low heat for 45 minutes, stirring continuously until reduced to a deep purple-brown caramelized jam.
Stir in half the niter kibbeh spiced butter and let melt into the onions; add authentic berbere spice and cook on low for 15 minutes, stirring constantly as the paste darkens and blooms.
Add garlic-ginger paste and 200ml warm water, simmering for 10 minutes into a rich, dark crimson sauce (wat).
Add cleaned chicken pieces and remaining niter kibbeh; cover and simmer gently over low heat for 35 minutes until chicken is tender and sauce clings heavily.

Prick hard-boiled eggs with a fork and gently submerge into the bubbling sauce; dust with ground korarima, simmer for 10 minutes until eggs are coated in dark red sauce, and ladle over fresh spongy injera.

title: Ugali

lines.text: 350 g White cornmeal (unga wa mahindi) (finely ground African style)
800 ml Water (brought to a rolling boil)

instructions: Bring water to a vigorous rolling boil in a heavy saucepan or sufuria.
Gradually pour in half the cornmeal, whisking rapidly with a wooden spoon (mwiko) to prevent any lumps from forming until a smooth porridge forms.
Add the remaining cornmeal in stages while stirring and pressing the mixture firmly against the sides of the pot with the flat side of the wooden mwiko.
Continue kneading, turning, and pressing the thickening dough vigorously over medium-low heat for 6-8 minutes until it pulls cleanly away from the pot walls and emits a toasty roasted corn aroma.

Gather the dough into a smooth rounded dome inside the pot, invert the sufuria onto a serving plate to release a perfect steaming mound, and serve immediately with sukuma wiki greens and grilled meat.

title: Nyama Choma

lines.text: 1200 g Fresh bone-in goat ribs or beef short ribs (trimmed of excess tallow)
1.5 tbsp Coarse sea salt and black pepper (traditional purist seasoning)
2 tbsp Garlic, ginger, and lemon rub (optional modern marinade)
250 g Kachumbari (fresh diced tomatoes, red onions, bird's eye chilies, cilantro, lime) (sharp refreshing side salsa)

instructions: Score meat lightly; rub generously with coarse salt, crushed garlic, and lemon juice; rest at room temperature for 20 minutes.
Prepare an open grill with white-hot acacia lump charcoal, setting the cooking grate 15cm above embers for medium-indirect heat.
Place goat ribs over coals, turning every 10 minutes to render fat slowly and prevent flare-ups.
Continue roasting for another 20 minutes until the exterior develops a crispy, deep amber-brown crust while the interior stays tender and succulent.
Transfer charred meat to a thick wooden butcher block; hack with a cleaver into bite-sized morsels, pile high, and serve immediately with fresh kachumbari salsa, salt dip, and hot ugali.

title: Bunny Chow

lines.text: 2 loaves Unsliced white farmhouse bread loaf (cut in half, soft white interior hollowed out leaving thick sturdy crust walls)
800 g Bone-in mutton or lamb pieces (cut into small curry chunks)
2 medium Waxy potatoes (quartered to absorb curry gravy)
3 tbsp Fiery Durban masala curry powder (dark roasted spices, chili, coriander, cumin)
15 leaves Fresh curry leaves and star anise (tempered in oil)
250 g Crushed tomatoes and ginger-garlic paste (rich gravy base)
120 g Grated carrot sambal with green chili and vinegar (crisp tangy side)

instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a heavy pot; fry cinnamon, star anise, curry leaves, and chopped onions until translucent and fragrant.
Add ginger-garlic paste and Durban masala; fry for 1 minute until spices bloom and release fragrant oils without burning.
Add mutton pieces, browning them on all sides; stir in tomatoes, 300ml water, and salt; cover and simmer for 35 minutes.
Add potato chunks into the pot; simmer for another 20 minutes until meat is meltingly tender and gravy is rich and thick.

Slice white bread loaves in half, hollow out the soft center crumb in one piece (the 'virgin' lid); ladle piping hot mutton curry and tender potatoes into the bread cavity until gravy soaks into the walls; top with the reserved bread plug and serve with carrot sambal.

title: Bobotie

lines.text: 800 g Lean ground beef or lamb (minced)
2 slices White sandwich bread slices (crusts removed, soaked in milk and squeezed dry)
2 tbsp Cape Malay mild sweet curry powder and turmeric (fragrant and warm)
60 g Golden sultana raisins (plumped in warm water)
2 tbsp Smooth apricot jam and lemon juice (signature sweet-sour Cape balance)
3 whole eggs + 250ml milk Eggs beaten with whole milk (creamy custard topping)
5 leaves Fresh bay leaves or lemon leaves (pressed into custard topping)

instructions: Sauté chopped onions in butter for 6 minutes until golden; add curry powder, turmeric, and garlic, stirring for 1 minute.
Add minced meat, cooking until browned; break squeezed soaked bread into small pieces and mix into meat with sultanas, apricot jam, flaked almonds, salt, and pepper.
Transfer meat mixture into a buttered rectangular casserole baking dish; pack down firmly and smooth the top with the back of a spoon.
Whisk eggs, whole milk, and a pinch of salt together; pour evenly over the meat surface; press fresh bay leaves upright or flat into the custard.
Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 35 minutes until the egg custard is golden brown, puffed, and softly set; serve warm with yellow turmeric raisin rice (geelrys) and fruit chutney.

title: Moambe Chicken (Poulet Moambé)

lines.text: 400 g Red palm fruit pulp / sauce concentrate (moambé / nyembwe) (pure natural palm fruit pericarp sauce)
2 tbsp Garlic cloves and fresh ginger (minced)
1 whole Whole red habanero or Congo chili (floated whole in stew for fragrance without breaking)
2 tbsp Unrefined red palm oil (dendê) (for searing chicken)
200 g Pounded cassava leaves (saka-saka / pondu) (classic accompaniment)

instructions: Season chicken pieces with salt, black pepper, half the minced garlic, and ginger; marinate 20 minutes.
Heat red palm oil in a heavy pot over medium heat; brown chicken pieces on all sides until golden; remove to a plate.
In the same pot, sauté onions, remaining garlic, and ginger for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the red palm fruit pulp (moambé) and 250ml water; whisk together and bring to a simmer, floating the whole chili on top.

Return browned chicken to the pot; cover and simmer gently over low heat for 40 minutes until chicken is meltingly tender and the sauce has reduced to a thick, buttery, deep scarlet-orange gravy; serve with boiled cassava root or kwanga.

title: Tacos al Pastor

lines.text: 900 g Pork shoulder or pork collar (sliced paper-thin into large sheets)
60 g Achiote paste (annatto seed seasoning) (for signature red-orange hue)
4 chiles Dried guajillo chiles and ancho chiles (stemmed, seeded and rehydrated)
80 ml Fresh pineapple juice and white vinegar (natural tenderizer)
1.5 tbsp Mexican oregano, cumin, cloves, and garlic (fragrant aromatics)
1 whole Fresh ripe pineapple (carved into wedges for roasting on top of spit)
18 tortillas Small fresh corn tortillas (taqueras) (warmed on the comal)
150 g Finely diced white onion, chopped cilantro, and salsa verde (classic taco toppings)

instructions: Blend rehydrated guajillo chiles, achiote paste, pineapple juice, vinegar, garlic, oregano, cumin, and salt into a smooth, thick crimson adobo marinade.
Coat thin pork sheets in the adobo paste; cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
Stack marinated pork sheets tightly onto skewers capped with a fresh pineapple crown, or sear in a blazing hot cast-iron pan until edges are deeply charred and caramelized.
Finely shave the crispy charred pork meat and caramelize fresh pineapple spears on the comal.

Double-layer warm fresh corn tortillas, pile with shaved charred pork, flick a piece of caramelized roasted pineapple from the knife directly onto each taco, top with diced white onion, cilantro, a squeeze of fresh lime, and spicy salsa verde.

title: Mole Poblano

lines.text: 1200 g Braised turkey pieces or chicken thighs (poached in aromatic broth)
180 g Dried mulato, ancho, and pasilla chiles (stemmed, seeded and lightly toasted in lard)
70 g Mexican stone-ground dark chocolate (tableta de chocolate) (with cinnamon and raw sugar)
100 g Pepitas (pumpkin seeds), sesame seeds, almonds, and peanuts (toasted until fragrant)
120 g Charred corn tortilla, toasted bolillo bread, and ripe plantain (traditional thickeners)
2 tbsp Raisins, Mexican cinnamon (canela), cloves, allspice, and aniseed (spiced richness)
300 g Roasted plum tomatoes and tomatillos (charred over open flame)
80 g Pure pork lard (manteca) or vegetable oil (for frying and blooming mole paste)

instructions: Individually toast the dried chiles in hot manteca for 15 seconds without burning; soak in hot poultry broth for 30 minutes to soften.
In the same pan, fry raisins, plantain, almonds, pumpkin seeds, sesame seeds, bolillo bread, and charred corn tortilla until golden and toasted.
Blend the softened chiles with broth into a smooth velvety puree; blend fried seeds, nuts, charred tomatoes, and spices into a separate thick paste in a metate or high-speed blender.
Heat manteca in a heavy clay cazuela over medium heat; add chile puree, frying vigorously for 10 minutes; add seed-nut paste, whisking continuously as the sauce thickens and turns dark mahogany.

Stir in chopped Mexican dark chocolate and remaining poultry broth; simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until the mole develops a glossy, deep dark mahogany sheen; spoon lavishly over poached chicken/turkey, scatter toasted white sesame seeds on top, and serve with warm corn tortillas.

title: Pozole

lines.text: 1000 g Pork shoulder and pork neck bones or trotter (cut into large chunks for rich collagen broth)
750 g Prepared nixtamalized white hominy corn (cacahuazintle) (rinsed, kernels blossomed)
5 chiles Dried guajillo and ancho chiles (seeded, soaked and blended for Pozole Rojo)
1 each White onion and whole garlic head (simmered whole in broth)
1 tbsp Dried Mexican oregano (rubbed between palms)
150 g Finely shredded green cabbage (crisp topping)
6 radishes Red radishes (thinly sliced into coins)
6 servings Crispy corn tostadas and lime wedges (essential accompaniments)

instructions: In a large stockpot, simmer pork pieces, bones, whole onion, garlic head, and bay leaves in 3 liters of water for 45 minutes, skimming foam regularly.
Add blossomed hominy corn kernels to the pot, simmering gently for 30 minutes until pork is fork-tender.
Soften dried chiles in hot water; blend with 2 cloves garlic and 150ml broth until silky smooth; strain through a mesh sieve directly into the bubbling pozole pot.
Shred cooked pork into bite-sized chunks, return to pot, season with Mexican oregano and sea salt, and simmer for 15 minutes to marry the chile broth with hominy.

Ladle steaming red pozole brimming with puffed hominy and tender pork into deep bowls; arrange bowls of crunchy shredded cabbage, sliced radishes, diced onions, Mexican oregano, and limes for diners to customize, accompanied by crisp corn tostadas.

title: Ceviche

lines.text: 500 g Ultra-fresh firm white fish (corvina, sea bass, or flounder) (cut into 2cm pristine cubes, kept ice cold)
10 whole Fresh Peruvian key limes (gently hand-squeezed to avoid bitter rind oils)
1 chili Ají limo chili pepper (finely minced (and 1 cut in half to rub the bowl))
1 medium Red onion (sliced paper-thin (pluma) and rinsed in ice water)
120 g Boiled Peruvian giant corn (choclo) (tender giant white kernels)
1 large Steamed orange sweet potato (camote) (sliced into thick golden discs)
40 g Toasted chulpe corn kernels (canchita) (crunchy salted garnish)

instructions: Rub the inside of a cold glass or ceramic bowl with a halved ají limo chili pepper to infuse subtle essential oils.
Place cold cubed fish in the bowl; toss with fine sea salt and minced ají limo; let salt penetrate the fish flesh for 2 minutes.

Pour freshly squeezed lime juice over the fish along with an ice cube to keep it chilled; toss gently for exactly 90 seconds until the fish exterior just turns milky-opaque while the core stays translucent and sashimi-fresh.
Stir in crisp ice-water-shocked red onion ribbons and chopped fresh cilantro; discard ice cube.

Plate immediately in a chilled shallow bowl, pooling the zesty white leche de tigre broth around the fish; flank with thick slices of sweet camote sweet potato, tender giant choclo corn kernels, and crispy toasted canchita.

title: Lomo Saltado

lines.text: 600 g Beef tenderloin (lomo fino) or sirloin (cut into thick strips)
2 medium Red onions (cut into thick wedges)
2 medium Roma tomatoes (cut into thick wedges, seeds removed)
1 chili Fresh ají amarillo chili (seeded and cut into fine matchsticks)
60 ml Peruvian dark soy sauce (sillao) and red wine vinegar (signature Chifa savory-tangy sauce)
300 g Crispy fried yellow potatoes (papas fritas) (hot and crispy)

instructions: Season beef strips with salt, black pepper, and cumin.
Heat a carbon steel wok over maximum flame until smoking hot; add 2 tablespoons oil and sear beef in batches for 90 seconds until browned and flamed (flambé); remove to plate.
In the hot wok, toss red onion wedges, garlic, and ají amarillo strips over high heat for 1 minute so onions char while staying crisp.
Add tomato wedges, return seared beef, and immediately pour in dark soy sauce and red wine vinegar around the wok edges to flash-vaporize; toss vigorously for 1 minute.

Fold in hot crispy french fries and chopped cilantro, tossing quickly so the fries soak up the savory vinegar juices while retaining partial crunch; serve immediately with a molded dome of white garlic rice.

title: Feijoada

lines.text: 500 g Brazilian black beans (feijão preto) (soaked overnight)
300 g Brazilian salted beef (carne seca) (desalted in cold water for 24 hours and cubed)
400 g Smoked pork ribs and pork loin (cut into pieces)
300 g Paio sausage and linguiça calabresa (sliced into thick rounds)
4 leaves + 1 orange Bay leaves and whole unpeeled orange (orange cuts grease during simmering)
150 g Toasted manioc flour (farofa) (toasted in butter with garlic)
200 g Thinly shredded collard greens (couve à mineira) (sautéed with garlic)

instructions: In a large heavy pot, simmer desalted carne seca and black beans with bay leaves and halved orange in 3 liters of water for 45 minutes.
Add smoked pork ribs, slab bacon, and simmer for another 45 minutes, skimming excess fat from the surface.
Add sliced paio sausage and linguiça calabresa; simmer for 30 minutes until all meats are meltingly tender.

Temper the stew: in a skillet, sauté finely minced garlic and onions in bacon fat; ladle two cups of cooked black beans into the skillet and mash thoroughly with the back of a spoon into a paste; pour back into the main pot and simmer for 15 minutes to create an unctuously thick, creamy black broth.

Ladle steaming black feijoada into clay bowls; serve alongside platters of white rice, buttery golden toasted farofa, shredded garlicky couve collard greens, sweet orange slices, and fiery malagueta chili sauce.

title: Pão de Queijo

lines.text: 300 g Sour tapioca / cassava starch (polvilho azedo) (creates expansion and puff)
100 g Sweet tapioca starch (polvilho doce) (provides chewy mochi-like elasticity)
220 g Cured Queijo Minas / Canastra cheese (or aged parmesan) (finely grated)
200 ml Whole milk and water (for scalding starch)
80 ml Vegetable oil or melted butter (boiled with milk)

instructions: Bring milk, water, oil, and salt to a rolling boil in a small saucepan.
Pour boiling liquid immediately over the mixed cassava starches in a large bowl (scalding/escaldar); stir with a wooden spoon until dough forms a crumbly paste; let cool to lukewarm.
Add eggs one at a time, kneading with hands until dough becomes smooth, glossy, and slightly sticky.

Fold in the finely grated cured cheese until evenly distributed; grease hands with oil and roll dough into golf-ball-sized spheres (approx 35g each); arrange on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.

Bake in a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F) for 20-25 minutes until the rolls puff into golden spheres with crackled crisp exteriors and soft, stretchy, chewy, hollow cheese-filled interiors; serve steaming hot with fresh coffee.

title: Argentine Baked Empanadas

lines.text: 400 g All-purpose wheat flour (for tender pastry dough)
100 g Pure pork lard (grasa vacuna o de cerdo) or butter (melted warm for flaky Argentine crust)
500 g Beef flank or skirt steak (hand-cut with knife into 5mm cubes, never ground)
400 g Yellow onions and fresh scallions (onions equal in volume to beef)
1.5 tbsp Ground cumin and sweet Argentine pimentón paprika (essential Tucumán spices)

instructions: Make dough: mix flour, melted warm lard, warm salted water, and knead into a smooth, elastic dough; wrap and rest for 30 minutes.

Make filling (recado): sauté diced yellow onions in lard until translucent; add knife-cut beef, cumin, pimentón, and salt, searing for just 3 minutes so meat stays juicy; remove from heat, fold in scallion greens, and chill until cold and firm.
Roll dough thin and cut into 13cm round discs (tapas de empanada).

Place 2 tablespoons chilled meat filling in center; top with chopped hard-boiled egg and olive; moisten edges with water, fold into a half-moon, and seal tightly with 13 traditional twisted repulgue rope pleats.
Place on baking sheet, brush lightly with egg wash, and bake at 220°C (425°F) for 15 minutes until blistered, golden-brown, and bubbling juicy inside; serve with lemon wedges and Malbec wine.

title: Arepas

lines.text: 300 g Pre-cooked white cornmeal (Harina P.A.N.) (specifically pre-cooked corn flour)
450 ml Lukewarm water and salt (for soft, crack-free dough)
300 g Poached shredded chicken breast (tender shreds)
2 whole Ripe Hass avocados (mashed with lime and mayo for Reina Pepiada filling)
2 tbsp Fresh cilantro, lime juice, and minced garlic (flavoring for chicken salad)
80 g Grated salty white cheese (queso llanero or cotija) (garnish)

instructions: Dissolve salt in warm water; slowly pour in Harina P.A.N. while stirring with fingers; knead for 2 minutes until dough is smooth, pliable, and moist without cracks; rest for 5 minutes.
Divide dough into 4 balls, flatten with palms into 10cm wide discs about 1.5cm thick, smoothing edges with wet fingers.
Cook on an oiled hot cast-iron griddle (budare) over medium heat for 5 minutes per side until a thin golden crust forms.
Transfer arepas to a 180°C (350°F) oven for 10 minutes until they puff slightly and sound hollow when tapped on the bottom.

Mix shredded chicken with mashed avocado, mayonnaise, lime juice, garlic, and cilantro for Reina Pepiada filling; slice hot arepa 3/4 open like a pocket, butter the inside, stuff generously with chicken salad, and top with grated white cheese.

title: Argentine Gaucho Asado

lines.text: 1200 g Cross-cut beef short ribs (tira de asado) (flanken-style 1.5cm thick strips)
1000 g Flank / flap steak (vacío) with fat cap intact (large continuous piece)
4 links Argentine fresh pork or beef sausages (chorizo criollo) (parrilla sausages)
40 g Coarse Argentine sea salt (sal parrillera) (pure salt crust)
200 ml Fresh chimichurri (flat parsley, oregano, garlic, red wine vinegar, olive oil, ají molido) (traditional herbaceous table condiment)

instructions: Build a hardwood fire (quebracho or fruitwood) in a brasero next to the grill; let logs burn down into glowing red embers.
Generously coat room-temperature beef cuts with coarse sal parrillera 15 minutes before grilling.
Shovel a 3cm carpet of glowing red coals beneath the tilted V-groove iron parrilla grate (moderate heat, hand can be held over grate for 5 seconds).
Place bone-in ribs bone-side-down and vacío fat-side-down; slow-roast undisturbed for 40 minutes to render fat slowly and caramelize bones.
Flip meat and grill meat side for 20 minutes until deeply browned, juicy, and smoky; carve on a thick wooden tabla and serve piping hot with crusty bread and spoonfuls of zesty chimichurri.

title: Ropa Vieja

lines.text: 900 g Beef flank steak or chuck roast (cut along grain into 8cm chunks for long shreds)
2 peppers Red and green bell peppers (sliced into long thin ribbons)
400 g Crushed plum tomatoes and tomato paste (savory sauce base)
120 ml Dry white wine (vino seco) or beef broth with lime (for deglazing sofrito)
70 g Pitted Spanish manzanilla olives and capers (briny punch)
1.5 tbsp Ground cumin, dried oregano, and bay leaf (Cuban sofrito aromatics)

instructions: Boil flank steak in water with onion, carrot, celery, and bay leaf for 60 minutes until tender; remove beef and reserve 250ml flavorful cooking broth.
Allow meat to cool slightly, then pull apart by hand or with two forks into long, thin, thread-like shredded ribbons (resembling frayed clothes).
In a large skillet, sauté sliced onions and bell peppers in olive oil for 8 minutes until soft and caramelized; add minced garlic, cumin, oregano, and bay leaf, cooking for 1 minute.
Stir in tomato paste, crushed tomatoes, white wine, reserved beef broth, sliced green olives, and capers; bring to a simmer.

Fold the shredded beef into the sauce; simmer uncovered on medium-low for 15 minutes until the beef absorbs the savory sofrito and the sauce reduces into a rich, glossy coating; serve with white rice, black beans, and sweet fried maduros.

title: Jerk Chicken

lines.text: 1400 g Bone-in chicken leg quarters (scored deeply to bone)
4 peppers Fresh Jamaican Scotch bonnet peppers (stemmed, fruity and blistering heat)
2 tbsp Freshly ground whole Jamaican pimento (allspice) berries (essential soul of jerk)
1 bunch Fresh Jamaican thyme sprigs (leaves stripped)
3 tbsp Fresh ginger root and garlic cloves (rough chopped)
2 tbsp Dark soy sauce and dark brown sugar (for caramelized color)
40 ml Fresh lime juice and apple cider vinegar (acidity balance)
1 tsp Freshly grated nutmeg and cinnamon (warm spice undertones)

instructions: In a blender, combine Scotch bonnet peppers, scallions, garlic, ginger, fresh thyme, ground allspice berries, nutmeg, cinnamon, brown sugar, soy sauce, lime juice, vinegar, and salt; blend into a thick, coarse fragrant jerk paste.
Make deep diagonal slashes in the chicken meat down to the bone; rub jerk marinade thoroughly into every crevice and beneath the skin; marinate covered for at least 6 hours or overnight.
Prepare a covered barbecue grill or smoker with lump charcoal and soaked allspice/pimento wood chips (or bay leaves) for medium-low indirect smoke (135°C / 275°F).
Lay chicken skin-side up on grill grates away from direct coals; cover tightly and smoke for 45 minutes, basting once with reserved marinade.

Move chicken over direct coals for the final 6-8 minutes, flipping to crisp and char the jerk crust with signature blackened spicy spots; chop into pieces with a heavy cleaver and serve with Jamaican rice and peas and fried festival dumplings.

title: Gumbo

lines.text: 150 g Dark chocolate roux: equal parts vegetable oil and flour (cooked slowly to deep dark mahogany chocolate color)
400 g The Holy Trinity: diced yellow onion, green bell pepper, and celery (classic 2:1:1 ratio)
350 g Smoked Louisiana andouille sausage (sliced into 1cm coins)
500 g Boneless skinless chicken thighs (cut into bite-sized chunks)
200 g Fresh okra (sliced rounds, smothered in oil to remove slime)
1800 ml Rich chicken or shrimp stock (warm)
2 tbsp Cajun seasoning, garlic, bay leaves, and cayenne (spicy aromatics)
1 tbsp Gumbo filé powder (ground sassafras leaves) (stirred off-heat for earthy thickening)

instructions: In a heavy cast-iron Dutch oven over medium-low heat, stir equal parts oil and flour constantly with a flat wooden spoon for 30 minutes until it reaches the shade of dark melted chocolate without burning.
Immediately dump in the chopped Holy Trinity (onion, celery, green bell pepper); the moisture stops the roux from cooking further; cook vegetables for 5 minutes until soft.
Slowly ladle in warm stock while whisking vigorously to incorporate the dark roux smoothly without lumps; add Cajun seasoning, garlic, and bay leaves.
Add browned andouille sausage slices, chicken chunks, and smothered okra; bring to a boil, then simmer on low heat for 40 minutes, skimming oil from the surface as it turns glossy.
Add fresh peeled shrimp and simmer for 4 minutes until pink; turn off heat, sprinkle in aromatic filé powder, and ladle into wide bowls over a scoop of fluffy white rice, topped with green scallions.

title: Jambalaya

lines.text: 300 g Smoked andouille sausage (sliced into coins)
400 g Boneless chicken thighs (cut into bite-sized pieces)
300 g Peeled Gulf shrimp (seasoned with Creole spice)
350 g Holy Trinity: onion, green bell pepper, and celery (diced)
300 g Canned crushed tomatoes and tomato paste (for Creole style (red jambalaya))
2 tbsp Cajun/Creole seasoning, smoked paprika, garlic, oregano, bay leaves (bold seasoning)
4 tbsp Fresh green scallions and parsley (chopped for garnish)

instructions: In a large heavy Dutch oven, brown sliced andouille sausage and seasoned chicken pieces in oil over medium-high heat until deeply caramelized; remove meat.
In the rendered fat, sauté the diced Holy Trinity (onion, bell pepper, celery) and minced garlic for 6 minutes until tender.
Stir in tomato paste, crushed tomatoes, Creole spices, and uncooked rice, toasting rice grains in the mixture for 2 minutes.
Return cooked sausage and chicken to pot; pour in hot chicken broth, bring to a rolling boil, cover tightly with lid, reduce heat to lowest setting, and simmer undisturbed for 20 minutes.
Remove lid, nestle raw seasoned shrimp across top of hot rice, cover for another 5 minutes until shrimp turn pink and tender; fold gently with a fork and garnish with chopped scallions and parsley.

title: New England Clam Chowder

lines.text: 1000 g Fresh littleneck or quahog clams (steamed in wine, meats chopped, nectar strained)
120 g Salt pork or thick-cut slab bacon (finely diced for rendering fat)
400 g Yukon Gold or Russet potatoes (peeled and diced into 1.5cm cubes)
300 ml Heavy cream and whole milk (rich dairy base)
400 ml Reserved strained clam nectar (briny ocean foundation)
250 g Celery ribs and sweet yellow onion (finely diced)
35 g All-purpose flour (for blonde roux thickening)
1 sprig Fresh thyme and bay leaf (classic seasoning)
100 g Traditional Westminster oyster crackers (for floating on top)

instructions: Steam fresh clams in 100ml water for 6 minutes until shells open; remove clam meats and chop coarsely; strain clam broth through cheesecloth to remove any sand.
In a heavy pot, render diced salt pork over medium heat until crispy and golden; remove crispy cracklings for garnish.
In the rendered fat, cook diced onion and celery for 5 minutes until translucent; stir in flour to form a light blonde roux, cooking for 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in warm clam nectar and diced potatoes; add fresh thyme sprig and bay leaf; simmer for 15 minutes until potatoes are fork-tender and broth has thickened.

Pour in heavy cream and stir in chopped tender clams; gently heat for 3 minutes without boiling; ladle into warm bowls, top with freshly cracked black pepper, crispy salt pork bits, and a handful of oyster crackers.

title: Traditional Quebec Poutine

lines.text: 1000 g Russet baking potatoes (cut into 1cm thick fries, soaked in cold water to remove starch)
250 g Fresh white cheddar cheese curds (fromage en grains) (room temperature to ensure signature squeak and gentle melt)
600 ml Equal parts rich beef stock and chicken stock (authentic Québécois gravy foundation)
40 g each Unsalted butter and flour (for roux base)
1 tbsp Cornstarch slurry (gives signature glossy sauce sheen)
1 tsp Freshly cracked black pepper and Worcestershire (sharp seasoning)
1200 ml Canola or peanut oil (for double frying)

instructions: Make sauce: melt butter in saucepan, whisk in flour and cook to a medium-brown roux (4 minutes); whisk in warm beef and chicken stocks, Worcestershire sauce, and plenty of black pepper; simmer 10 minutes until thick, glossy, and piping hot.
Drain soaked potato batons and dry thoroughly with towels.
First fry: cook potatoes in 160°C (325°F) oil for 6 minutes until soft and cooked through but not browned; drain on wire rack.
Second fry: increase oil heat to 190°C (375°F); flash-fry potatoes for 3 minutes until exterior is deeply golden and shatteringly crisp; drain and season with sea salt.

Assemble immediately: heap hot crispy fries into wide paper trays or bowls, interlace generously with room-temperature squeaky cheese curds throughout layers, and ladle boiling hot brown gravy lavishly over top so curds soften into stretchy ribbons while retaining their squeak.

title: Classic Canadian Nanaimo Bars

lines.text: 60 g Finely chopped walnuts or pecans (for nutty bottom layer)
30 g Unsweetened Dutch-process cocoa powder (for crumb base)
220 g Unsalted butter (divided across base, custard, and topping)
35 g Bird's Custard Powder (essential traditional Canadian ingredient for signature yellow middle layer)
250 g Icing / confectioners' sugar (for fluffy custard cream)
45 ml Heavy whipping cream (for custard fluff)
150 g Semisweet or bittersweet chocolate (melted with butter for crack-free shiny glaze)

instructions: Make base: melt 115g butter, 50g sugar, and cocoa powder in a bowl set over simmering water; whisk in 1 beaten egg until thickened; stir in graham crumbs, shredded coconut, and chopped walnuts; press firmly into a parchment-lined 20x20cm square baking pan and chill.
Make custard filling: beat 115g softened butter, heavy cream, and Bird's Custard Powder with an electric mixer; gradually beat in icing sugar until light, creamy, and pale yellow.
Spread the yellow custard cream evenly over the chilled bottom layer with an offset spatula; refrigerate for 20 minutes to set firm.
Make top layer: gently melt semisweet chocolate and 25g butter together until silky smooth; let cool to room temperature (not hot, so it doesn't melt custard).
Pour chocolate over the set custard, tilting pan to coat evenly; chill for 30 minutes until chocolate is just firm, then score and slice into neat squares with a warm, dry knife.

title: Poke

lines.text: 500 g Sashimi-grade yellowfin ahi tuna (cut into clean 2cm cubes, kept ice cold)
40 g Fresh limu kohu or ogo seaweed (rinsed, provides ocean crunch)
1.5 tbsp Pure toasted sesame oil (fragrant dressing)
2 tbsp Japanese shoyu (soy sauce) (savory umami seasoning)
1.5 tbsp Crushed roasted kukui nut (inamona) (traditional native nutty seasoning)
1 tsp Hawaiian red alaea sea salt (mineral crunch)

instructions: Pat pristine ahi tuna dry with paper towels; using a razor-sharp yanagiba or chef's knife, cut fish cleanly into uniform 2cm cubes without tearing flesh.
Place cubed ahi into a chilled bowl set over an ice bath.
Add sliced sweet Maui onions, chopped scallions, rinsed fresh crunchy ogo seaweed, and crushed roasted kukui nuts (inamona).
Drizzle with Japanese shoyu and toasted sesame oil; sprinkle red alaea sea salt and a pinch of chili flakes over the fish.
Toss gently with chopsticks or hands until each glistening jewel of tuna is sheerly coated in fragrant sesame oil without bruising; serve immediately in a wooden bowl or over warm short-grain rice.

title: Australian Meat Pie

lines.text: 2 sheets Shortcrust pastry sheets (for sturdy base that holds gravy without sogginess)
2 sheets All-butter puff pastry sheets (for flaky golden top lid)
500 g Lean minced beef chuck (browned finely)
1.5 tbsp Worcestershire sauce and Vegemite (essential Aussie savory umami kick)
3 tbsp Cornstarch or flour slurry (thickens gravy into thick pipeable filling)
1 egg beaten with milk Egg wash (for golden crust glaze)
4 tbsp Australian tomato sauce (ketchup) (squirted liberally over top crust)

instructions: Brown minced beef and diced onions in a saucepan until browned; stir in Worcestershire sauce, a teaspoon of Vegemite, black pepper, and beef stock.

Whisk cornstarch with 3 tablespoons cold water; pour into bubbling beef gravy, stirring continuously for 3 minutes until filling thickens into a glossy, thick, luscious stew; cool completely to room temperature.
Grease 4 individual 10cm pie tins; line each with shortcrust pastry, pressing firmly into the corners and trimming excess.

Spoon cooled thick beef gravy filling into pastry cases; brush rims with water, top with puff pastry circles, and crimp edges firmly with a fork to seal; trim overhang and brush tops generously with egg wash.
Bake in a preheated oven at 210°C (410°F) for 22-25 minutes until the puff pastry top is puffed high, flaky, and deep golden brown; serve hot with a generous squeeze of Aussie tomato sauce.

title: Pavlova

lines.text: 4 large eggs Fresh egg whites (room temperature, absolutely no yolk trace)
220 g Superfine caster sugar (added one tablespoon at a time)
1 tbsp Cornstarch (cornflour) (creates the signature soft marshmallow interior)
1 tsp White vinegar or lemon juice (stabilizes meringue structure)
1 tsp Pure vanilla bean paste (fragrant aroma)
250 ml Heavy whipping cream (whipped to soft, pillowy clouds without sugar)
3 fruit Fresh passionfruit pulp (tart seeds and pulp)
200 g Fresh strawberries, raspberries, and sliced kiwi fruit (bright seasonal toppings)

instructions: Wipe a glass or metal bowl with lemon juice; whip room-temperature egg whites on medium speed until soft peaks form.
Increase speed to high, adding caster sugar one tablespoon at a time, beating for 30 seconds after each addition until sugar completely dissolves and meringue is glossy, stiff, and pearl-white.
Gently fold in cornstarch, white vinegar, and vanilla paste with a rubber spatula.

Pile meringue onto a parchment-lined baking sheet marked with a 20cm circle; sculpt into a neat disc with flat top and smooth vertical sides, sweeping upward with an offset spatula to create decorative ribs.

Bake at 120°C (250°F) for 75 minutes until crisp and dry to touch; turn off oven and prop door slightly open, allowing pavlova to cool completely inside the oven for 2 hours to prevent collapsing; top with billowy unsweetened whipped cream, fresh berries, kiwi slices, and drizzle with tart passionfruit pulp right before serving.

title: Ogbono Soup

lines.text: 1 lb (450 g) beef chuck, cut into cubes
5 oz (150 g) stockfish, soaked until soft
1 cup (100 g) pure ground ogbono seed, with no additives
4 cups (120 g) chopped kale or ugwu leaves

instructions: Put the beef, onion, chili flakes and salt in a pot with enough water to cover and boil until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the soaked stockfish and cook until it is soft, keeping about four cups of broth in the pot.
Stir the ground ogbono into the hot broth until it dissolves with no lumps.
Add the crayfish and palm oil and cook, stirring now and then, until the soup thickens and draws.
Lower the heat, fold in the kale and simmer until just wilted.
Taste for salt and serve hot with a swallow such as pounded yam, eba or amala.

title: Banga Soup

lines.text: 1.5 lb (680 g) beef chuck, cut into cubes
1 large onion (150 g), half chopped, half blended
5 oz (150 g) stockfish, soaked until soft
14 oz (400 g) canned palm nut cream (palm fruit concentrate), about 25% palm oil (nutrition counted as 100 g palm oil)
1 tbsp (3 g) crushed dried bitter leaf

instructions: Boil the beef with the chopped half of the onion, cayenne and salt in a little water until tender, then add the stockfish for the last 10 minutes.
Lift the beef and stockfish out and keep the broth.
Pour the palm nut cream into the pot, thin it with water and some of the broth, cover and cook until the oil floats on top.
Blend the scotch bonnet with the remaining onion and stir it in.
Return the beef and stockfish, add the crayfish and simmer.
Stir in the bitter leaf, simmer until thickened to taste and serve hot with starch, pounded yam or fufu.

title: Akara

lines.text: 2 slices (55 g) white bread to serve
3 tbsp (40 g) vegetable oil taken up in deep frying

instructions: Soak the peas in water until the skins swell, pulse briefly in a food processor, then swirl in water and skim off the skins until the peas are clean.
Blend the peas with a little water, the bell pepper, habanero, crayfish and salt until smooth.
Whisk the batter by hand or with a mixer until light and fluffy, then fold in the onion.
Heat oil in a pan over medium-high heat until a drop of batter sizzles.
Fry heaped tablespoons of batter in batches, turning until golden on all sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with the white bread.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chicken Peanut Butter Soup

lines.text: 2 lb (900 g) bone-in chicken thighs, about 700 g meat and skin

instructions: Season the chicken with half the onion, the ginger, garlic, one habanero and the salt, then steam it in its own juices over low heat until cooked through.
Blend the tomatoes, the remaining onion and the other habaneros until smooth.
Cook the blended base in a pot until it reduces and the raw tomato smell is gone.
Stir the peanut butter into the base with about 5 cups of water until it dissolves.
Add the chicken and its juices and simmer until the soup thickens and the oil rises.
Taste for salt and serve hot, on its own or with rice or fufu.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Okro Soup with Banku

lines.text: 1 lb (450 g) okra, minced and sliced
2 lb (900 g) turkey wings, about 450 g meat and skin
2 cups (314 g) white cornmeal for the banku
1 cup (120 g) cassava flour for the banku

instructions: Boil the turkey wings with half the onion, one habanero, the ginger and the salt in a little water until tender.
Add the shrimp and cook just until pink.
Mince half the okra and slice the rest, chop the other half of the onion, the second habanero and the bell pepper, and add them all to the pot.
Simmer the soup until the okra is tender but still bright, then take it off the heat.
Whisk the cornmeal and cassava flour with water, then cook over medium heat, stirring hard, until the banku is smooth and stiff.
Shape the banku into rounds and serve with the okro soup.

title: Domoda (Gambian Peanut Stew)

lines.text: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, bite-sized
12 oz sweet potato, peeled and chopped
1 1/2 tsp ground coriander and 1 tsp ground cumin

instructions: Heat the avocado oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and sear the chicken pieces for about 3 minutes; they will not be cooked through yet.
Stir in the onion and garlic and cook for 2 minutes, stirring now and then.
Mix in the peanut butter and tomato paste, then pour in the stock and add the sweet potato, coriander, cumin and salt. Bring to a boil, cover and boil gently for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the okra, return to a boil, cover and simmer for 10 minutes. Cook uncovered for the last couple of minutes if you want it thicker.
Turn off the heat, stir in the lemon juice and taste for salt. Serve hot, with rice if you like.

title: Gbegiri Soup

lines.text: 1 tbsp (8 g) ground fermented locust beans (iru)
1 1/2 cups white rice, cooked on the side for serving

instructions: Soak the black-eyed peas in water for 10 to 15 minutes, then rub them between your palms and rinse away the skins, repeating until most are gone.
Put the peeled beans, onion and 4 to 6 cups of water in a large pot and cook over medium heat for about 1 hour, until very tender, topping up the water if needed.
Blend the cooked beans until smooth and creamy with an immersion or high-speed blender.
Return the puree to the pot, add the palm oil, ground crayfish, locust beans and salt, and simmer over low heat for 3 to 5 minutes until thickened, stirring so it does not catch.
Cook the rice on the side, then serve the soup hot over or beside it.
