title: Poulet DG (Cameroonian Chicken and Plantain)

lines.text: 3 tbsp oil, for frying the plantains and chicken

instructions: Season the chicken with half the salt, the black pepper and half the curry powder, then pan-fry it in a little oil until browned on all sides and set aside.
Fry the plantain pieces in a separate pan in the remaining oil until golden and caramelized, then drain them.
In the chicken pan, saute the onion until soft, then stir in the tomatoes and tomato paste with the remaining curry powder and salt and cook down into a thick sauce.

Return the chicken to the sauce, add the carrots, green beans and bell pepper with a splash of water, cover and simmer until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender but still bright.
Fold in the fried plantain, warm through for a minute and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Okro Soup

lines.text: 1 1/2 lb fresh okra, half minced and half sliced
1 large dried fish, soaked and shredded

instructions: Boil the smoked turkey wings in water with the minced onion until tender, about 20 minutes.
Mince the red bell pepper and habanero, and mince half of the okra, slicing the other half.
Add the minced peppers and the ground crayfish to the turkey and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the shredded dried fish and leave it to soften for 5 minutes.
Pour in the palm oil, then add the shrimp and all the okra and cook for 3 to 5 minutes.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then take the pot off the heat right away and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Tanzanian Angel Fish in Okra Sauce

lines.text: 1 kg firm white fish fillet, cut into chunks

instructions: Heat some of the olive oil in a frying pan and shallow-fry the fish chunks on both sides until golden and cooked through, then set them aside.
In a separate pan, heat the remaining oil and cook the onions until soft, then add the tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the eggplant and cook for 2 minutes, then stir in the okra, lemon juice and orange juice.
Move the sauce to a pot, add the chillies, paprika, chili powder, salt and a splash of water, and boil for 10 minutes.
Add the fried fish and simmer for 20 minutes. Serve with rice or pap.

title: Zanzibar Mix (Urojo)

lines.text: 2 medium potatoes (300 g), boiled, peeled and cubed
1/2 cup (80 g) peeled, grated raw green mango
2 tbsp (30 g) tamarind pulp, soaked and strained

instructions: Boil the potatoes until just tender, then peel and cut them into small cubes. Keep the chickpeas boiled and drained.
Soak the tamarind in a few spoonfuls of hot water, mash it and strain out the seeds and fibre to leave a thin sour liquid.
Whisk the flour, turmeric and salt into 4 cups of water in a pot. Add the whole scotch bonnet and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring so it does not lump.
Add the chickpeas, potatoes and grated raw mango and simmer until the gravy turns thick and glossy.
Stir in the coconut milk, take the pot off the heat and remove the scotch bonnet.
Ladle into bowls, drizzle each with the strained tamarind and scatter over the chopped cilantro.
sourceName: Bohra Rasoi - taste of Mama Rashida

title: Ugandan Rolex

lines.text: 1 cup (125 g) wheat flour (all-purpose) for the chapati
2 tbsp (27 g) vegetable oil, for the chapati and the pan
1/2 cup (35 g) thinly sliced green cabbage
1/2 cup (90 g) finely diced tomato, seeds removed
1 hot chili pepper (10 g), thinly sliced, for topping

instructions: Mix the flour with a pinch of the salt and 1 tbsp of the oil, add warm water a splash at a time and knead into a soft dough. Rest it under a cloth.
Divide the dough in two, roll each piece into a thin round and fry in a dry pan, brushing with a little oil, until golden in patches on both sides. Keep warm.
Crack the eggs into a bowl and whisk in the cabbage, tomato, onion and the remaining salt.
Heat a well-oiled non-stick pan over medium-high heat, pour in half the egg mix and spread it into a flat circle. Cook until set and browned underneath, then flip.
Lay a chapati on top of the egg so it warms through, then slide the pair out, scatter over a few slices of chili and roll up tightly. Repeat with the remaining egg and chapati and serve while hot.

title: Chicken Luwombo

lines.text: 6 boneless skin-on chicken thighs (about 700 g), cut into large pieces
2 large tomatoes (300 g), skinned and chopped
1 medium green bell pepper (120 g), chopped
4 banana leaves, softened for wrapping (not eaten)

instructions: Season the chicken with half the salt and brown the pieces in a hot pan with the oil for about 8 minutes, turning once. Set aside; the chicken will finish cooking in the steamer.
In the same pan, soften the onions and garlic until fragrant, then add the tomatoes, pepper and carrot with the remaining salt and cook until the tomatoes break down into a thick base.
Soften the banana leaves over a flame or in hot water so they bend without tearing, then lay two overlapping pieces crosswise in a bowl or basket.

Layer half the vegetable base, the chicken, then the rest of the base into the leaf. Fold the leaf over firmly, wrapping and tying it with strips of leaf or string into a tight parcel, and cover with a third piece.
Set the parcel on a rack in a pot with about 3 cm of water, cover tightly and steam for about 1 hour, topping up the water if it runs low.
Rest the parcel for 5 minutes, then open at the table and serve the chicken with its juices.

title: Kenyan Githeri

lines.text: 2/3 cup (110 g) dried maize kernels, soaked overnight
2/3 cup (123 g) dried red kidney beans, soaked overnight
1/2 cup (75 g) diced green bell pepper

instructions: Drain the soaked maize and kidney beans, cover with fresh water in a large pot and boil hard for 10 minutes, then lower the heat and simmer until both are tender. Drain, keeping a cup of the cooking water.
Heat the oil in a wide pot and fry the onions until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for a minute, then stir in the tomatoes and salt and cook until they collapse into a thick sauce.
Add the carrots and bell pepper and cook for 5 minutes so they stay slightly firm.
Tip in the boiled maize and beans with a splash of the reserved cooking water, stir well and simmer, mashing a few beans against the pot, until the stew is thick.
Taste for salt and serve hot.

title: Isombe

lines.text: 500 g beef chuck, cut into bite-size pieces
1 medium eggplant (300 g), peeled and finely diced
1 green bell pepper (120 g), finely diced

instructions: Bring 1.5 litres of water and the salt to a boil in a large pot.
Add the beef, cassava leaves, spinach and palm oil, stir, cover and simmer on medium heat until the beef is nearly tender.
Stir in the eggplant, zucchini, onion and bell pepper, cover again and cook until the vegetables are soft.
Add the garlic and peanut butter, stirring until the peanut butter melts into the stew, and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir once more, check the salt and serve hot with rice, plantain or ugali.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Bamia Thabiek (Lamb and Okra Stew)
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the lamb in batches, then set it aside.
Cook the onion in the same pot until soft, then add the garlic, cinnamon, cumin, coriander and pepper and stir for a minute.
Return the lamb, stir in the tomato paste and pour in the broth. Cover and simmer until the lamb is tender.
Add the frozen okra straight from the freezer and simmer, uncovered, until the okra is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Taste, adjust the salt and serve hot with rice, kisra or bread.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Peanut Stew with Beef and Spinach (Combo)

lines.text: 1 1/4 lb (567 g) beef stew meat, cubed

instructions: Brown the beef in the oil in a large pot.
Add the onions and garlic and cook until the onions soften and take on a little color.
Pour in the broth and simmer until the beef is tender and the liquid has reduced by about half.
Stir in the peanut butter until fully mixed; the stew becomes very thick.
Add the tomatoes and spinach and cook until the spinach wilts and the peanut butter releases its oil and the stew turns shiny.
Serve hot with flatbread such as kisra, or with rice.

title: Chicken Mozambique with Coconut Piri Piri

lines.text: 4 whole chicken legs (about 1.2 kg with bone, about 950 g meat and skin)
1 tbsp olive oil (for the piri piri)
1 Thai bird chili, minced (for the piri piri)
1 clove garlic, crushed (for the piri piri)
1/2 tsp red pepper flakes (for the piri piri)

instructions: Whisk the lemon juice, olive oil, minced chili, garlic, pepper flakes and salt into a loose piri piri.
Score the chicken legs, toss them with the coconut milk and about two thirds of the piri piri, then marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours or overnight, turning once or twice.
Heat a grill to medium, around 350 F (175 C).
Grill the chicken just off direct heat for about 40 minutes, turning once and basting with the marinade only in the first 30 minutes, until the juices run clear.
Serve with rice and the remaining piri piri on the side.

title: Peri Peri Prawns

lines.text: 500 g large raw prawns, shells on, deveined
1/2 small red bell pepper (75 g), chopped

instructions: Pulse the chilies, garlic, bell pepper, paprika, lemon juice and salt into a coarse sauce.
Toss the prawns with the olive oil and half of the sauce and leave for 15 minutes, keeping the rest for dipping.
Heat a grill, braai or heavy pan until very hot.
Cook the prawns 2 to 3 minutes per side until pink and just cooked through.
Serve at once with the remaining sauce for dipping.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Zambia's Spiced Tilapia Stew

lines.text: 1 inch (10 g) fresh ginger, peeled and grated
1 small head napa cabbage, shredded (about 600 g)

instructions: Chop the vegetables, then fry the onion in the peanut oil in a large pot until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger, chilies, cumin and mustard seeds and cook for a few minutes until fragrant.
Add the tilapia, tomatoes, napa cabbage, lime juice, salt and a splash of water.
Simmer for about 15 minutes, until the fish flakes apart easily.
Taste, add salt if needed and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Malawian Fish Stew with Nsima

lines.text: 300 g white maize meal, for the nsima

instructions: Season the tilapia fillets with the salt and lemon juice and leave them for 5 minutes.
Fry the fillets in the hot oil for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden, then lift them out onto a plate.
In the same pan, cook the sliced onions and crushed garlic over medium heat until soft.
Stir in the curry powder, add the blended tomatoes and simmer until the gravy thickens and the oil rises to the top.
Return the fish to the pan, spoon the gravy over it and simmer gently for 8 minutes, then scatter the coriander over.
For the nsima, bring 1 litre of water to a boil, whisk in about a third of the maize meal to make a thin porridge and boil it for 5 minutes.
Stir in the remaining maize meal a handful at a time with a firm spoon until the nsima is stiff, cover for 5 minutes, then mould into mounds and serve with the fish stew.

title: Zambian Ifisashi
instructions: Wash and chop the collard greens, then cook them in a pot with a splash of water until wilted and drain off the liquid.
Blend the raw peanuts with the chili pepper and 180 ml (3/4 cup) of water into a thick, paste-like sauce.
Return the drained greens to the pot and add the chopped tomatoes and onion first.
Stir in the peanut paste and the salt.
Simmer over low heat for 45 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes, until the greens are tender and the sauce is thick.
Taste for salt and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chakalaka and Pap

lines.text: 500 g maize meal, for the pap

instructions: Heat the oil, fry the chopped onion until translucent, then add the green pepper and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the turmeric and masala, then the grated tomatoes, and cook until the tomatoes break down.
Add the grated carrots and cook briefly. Drain the sauce from the baked beans and mix it with the crumbled stock cube.
Add the drained beans and the stock mixture, season with salt and keep stirring until the relish is thick.
For the pap, boil 750 ml of water with the margarine. Whisk the maize meal with 500 ml of cold water in a bowl until smooth.
Pour the maize meal mixture into the boiling pot and stir for about 10 minutes, with no lumps, until thick, adding salt to taste.
Serve the pap in bowls with the chakalaka spooned alongside.

title: Madagascar Chicken (Akoho sy Sakamalao)

lines.text: 4 whole chicken legs, thighs attached (about 1 kg with bone, about 790 g meat and skin)

instructions: Zest the lemon, grate the ginger and crush the garlic, then rub the mixture over the chicken legs with the salt and pepper.
Cover and refrigerate the chicken for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Heat the coconut oil in a large skillet over medium heat and brown the chicken on both sides for 10 to 15 minutes.
Lift the chicken out, then soften the sliced pepper and onion in the same pan.
Return the chicken to the pan, cover, reduce the heat and simmer for 45 minutes until it falls off the bone.
Check the seasoning and serve with the pan juices.

title: Gateaux Piments (Mauritian Chili Poppers)

lines.text: 1 cup yellow split peas, soaked for 4 to 8 hours
2 tablespoons canola oil taken up while deep frying

instructions: Soak the yellow split peas in water for 4 to 8 hours, then drain them well.
Blend half the peas with the cumin seeds in a blender or food processor into a fine paste, scraping down the sides often.
Add the rest of the peas, the green onion, cilantro, chili pepper, turmeric and salt and pulse until just combined and still a little chunky.
Shape the mixture into 12 small balls, dipping one hand in water so the mixture does not stick.
Heat oil to about 350 F in a pot and fry the balls in batches for 4 to 5 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
