title: Muamba de Galinha

lines.text: 1 whole chicken (about 1.4 kg), cut into quarters
1 lb pumpkin, cut into 1.5 inch cubes

instructions: Mix the lemon juice, half the garlic, salt and chili powder, rub the mixture over the chicken quarters and marinate for 1 hour.
Heat the palm oil in a large pot and brown the chicken on all sides in batches so the pot is not crowded.
Add the onions, the rest of the garlic, the whole chili pepper and the tomatoes, bring to a simmer and cover.
Cook on low heat for about 1 hour, until the chicken is tender.
Add the pumpkin, broth and okra and cook for 15 minutes, until everything is tender.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Pondu (Saka-Saka Cassava Leaves)

lines.text: 3 small tilapia, about 300 g of flesh

instructions: Wash the cassava leaves and chop the onion, green onions, green pepper and garlic; cut the eggplant and zucchini into chunks and cut up the tilapia.
Heat the palm oil in a large pot and saute the onion, green onions, green pepper and garlic until soft.
Add the cassava leaves with a splash of water, cover and simmer until they are tender.
Stir in the eggplant, zucchini, salt and pepper and simmer until the vegetables are soft.
Lay the tilapia on top, cover and simmer until the fish is cooked through, then serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Libyan Bazeen
instructions: Brown the lamb with the diced onion in a large pot, then stir in the tomato paste, fenugreek, cayenne, turmeric and salt.
Add enough water to cover, bring to a boil, add the halved potatoes and simmer until the lamb and potatoes are tender.
Hard-boil the eggs, cool and peel them.
Bring the dough water to a boil, add the barley flour with a pinch of salt and beat vigorously with a wooden spoon until it forms a firm, smooth dough.
Shape the dough into a dome on a large platter and make a well around it.
Pour the sauce around the dough, arrange the potatoes and lamb, and top with the halved eggs.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Oha Soup (Ofe Oha)

lines.text: 120 g oha leaves, shredded and washed
1 1/2 tablespoons corn starch (in place of ground ofo)

instructions: Bring the stock or water to a boil, then stir in the ground crayfish and pepper.
Add the precooked beef, stockfish and dried fish and turn the heat to low; the meats are already cooked, so only warm them through.
Stir in the palm oil and the salt.
Dissolve the cornstarch in a spoonful of the hot liquid, pour it into the pot and stir until the soup thickens.
Stir in the shredded oha leaves, switch off the heat and let the residual heat wilt them so they stay green.
Taste and adjust the salt, then serve hot with a swallow of your choice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Ewa Agoyin

lines.text: 1 lb dried brown beans (cowpeas), picked over and rinsed
3/4 cup dried chilies, rehydrated in hot water
1 medium onion, half blended and half sliced

instructions: Pick over the beans, rinse them and boil in 6 to 8 cups of water for about 2 to 2.5 hours, until very tender.
Mash the cooked beans coarsely with a potato masher or wooden spoon and keep them warm.
While the beans cook, soak the dried chilies in boiling water for about 2 hours, then blend them with the red bell peppers, half the onion, the ginger and a quarter cup of water.
Heat the palm oil until very hot, add the remaining sliced onion and cook 10 to 15 minutes until browned but not burnt.
Stir in the blended peppers and cook about 10 minutes.
Add the crayfish and salt and cook another 5 to 10 minutes until the sauce turns from bright red to dark red.
Spoon the sauce over the mashed beans and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Edikang Ikong Soup

lines.text: 1.2 kg meat (beef or goat), cut into pieces
100 g ponmo (cow skin), washed and cut
200 g ugwu (fluted pumpkin) leaves, washed and sliced

instructions: Wash the meat, ponmo, stockfish and dried fish. Put them in a pot with the chopped onion, salt and very little water and cook about 45 minutes until tender.
Wash and slice the waterleaf and ugwu leaves, and chop the scotch bonnets.
Stir in the palm oil, scotch bonnets, ground crayfish and periwinkles and cook about 5 minutes.
Add the waterleaf, stir and cook 2 to 3 minutes, then add the ugwu and cook 3 minutes more without overcooking.
Taste, adjust the salt and serve hot with a swallow such as pounded yam or eba.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Hausa Koko
instructions: Wash the millet and soak it in water for a few hours.
Blend the ginger, cloves, peppercorns, negro pepper and dried chilies with a little water.
Drain the millet and grind it with the spice blend into a smooth wet mix.
Pass the mix through a fine sieve, then let the starch settle and pour off the clear water.
Whisk a little of the starch with cold water, pour it into boiling water and stir for about 15 minutes until the porridge thickens.
Serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Attieke with Oven-Grilled Mackerel

lines.text: 3 to 4 whole mackerel, cleaned (about 700 g edible fish)
5 medium tomatoes for the sauce and 4 for the salad
1 small, 1 medium and 1 large onion, in the brine, salad and sauce
7 cloves garlic, in the brine and the green seasoning
15 ml olive oil for the sauce

instructions: Blend the onion, garlic, ginger, chilies and spring onions with a little water to make a brine, and soak the cleaned mackerel in it.
Dice the tomatoes, onion, bell peppers and cucumber for the salad.
Grill the mackerel in a hot oven, turning once, until the skin is crisp and the flesh cooked through.
Cook the remaining tomatoes and onion with the green seasoning of garlic, ginger, bell pepper and chili in a little oil until reduced to a sauce.
Sprinkle the attieke with a little water and steam or microwave it until hot and fluffy.
Plate the attieke with the fish, sauce and salad.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Koki Beans

lines.text: 4 cups koki (black-eyed) beans, soaked and peeled

instructions: Soak the beans in water and rub off the skins, then rinse until the water runs clear.
Blend the peeled beans with the warm water and scotch bonnet peppers into a smooth thick paste.
Stir in the palm oil, chopped spinach and salt until evenly mixed.
Spoon portions into banana leaves, plantain leaves or foil and fold into tight parcels.
Steam the parcels in a covered pot with a little water at the bottom for about an hour until firm.
Unwrap and serve warm with plantain, yam or cassava.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Tiguadege Na (Malian Peanut Stew)
instructions: Cut the chicken into pieces and cube the potato and eggplant, slice the carrots, and chop the onion and garlic.
Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion and garlic over medium heat for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the chicken and brown it lightly for 6 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste and cook 1 minute.
Add the diced tomatoes, broth and herbes de Provence and bring to a simmer.
Stir in the peanut butter until smooth, then add the potato, carrot and eggplant.
Simmer partly covered for 25 minutes until the chicken and vegetables are tender and the stew thickens, then season with salt and pepper and serve over rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Mukimo (Kenyan Mashed Potatoes with Pumpkin Leaves)

lines.text: 1 kg Irish potatoes, peeled and cut up

instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut them into chunks, slice the onions, and wash and chop the pumpkin leaves and coriander.
Boil the potatoes with the maize kernels in salted water for 20 minutes until the potatoes are soft, then drain, keeping a little of the water.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the onions for 8 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the pumpkin leaves and the crumbled seasoning cubes to the onions and cook 4 minutes until the leaves wilt.
Mash the potatoes and maize together, adding a splash of the cooking water if too stiff.
Fold in the leaf and onion mixture and the coriander until evenly green and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Matooke Katogo (Ugandan Green Banana Curry)

lines.text: 1/2 cup green beans, cut into 1 inch lengths

instructions: Peel the green bananas, cut them in half and keep them in water; slice the onion, mince the garlic and chop the tomatoes.
Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion and garlic for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes, curry powder and salt and cook 8 minutes until the tomatoes break down into a sauce.
Add the green bananas with about 1 cup of water, cover and simmer 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until tender.
Stir in the green beans and cilantro and cook 4 minutes more, then adjust the salt and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Samp and Beans with Beef (Umngqusho)
instructions: Rinse the samp and beans and soak them in plenty of water overnight, then drain.
Cover the samp and beans with fresh water in a large pot, bring to a boil and simmer for about 90 minutes until soft, adding water as needed.
Heat the oil in a second pot and cook the onion, garlic and chilli for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the cinnamon stick, curry powder and curry leaf, stir for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes and cook 6 minutes.
Add the beef and salt, cover with a little water and simmer 60 minutes until the beef is tender and the sauce is thick.
Drain off most of the water from the samp and beans, stir in some of the beef curry and serve the rest on top.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Tunisian Swordfish Couscous

lines.text: 4 onions, 1 diced and 3 cut in wedges
8 tbsp extra virgin olive oil in total

instructions: Peel and cut the potatoes and carrots, dice one onion, cut the other onions into wedges, grate the garlic and cut the swordfish into pieces.
Rub the swordfish with half the garlic, half the paprika, a little oil and some of the salt and leave it aside.
Heat some oil in the bottom of a couscous steamer, soften the diced onion for 5 minutes, then add the blended tomatoes and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the harissa, the remaining paprika and garlic, then add the onion wedges, carrots, potatoes and boiling water to cover, and bring to a simmer.
Toss the couscous with olive oil, turmeric and salt, set it in the steamer top and steam over the sauce for 20 minutes.
Lay the swordfish in the sauce for the last 15 minutes of cooking.
Tip the couscous onto a large plate, sprinkle it with hot water, work it loose and steam it again for 8 minutes.
Mix the couscous with some of the sauce until evenly colored, then serve with the fish and vegetables on top.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Beef Plov

lines.text: 1 1/2 lbs beef chuck, cut into 1/2 to 3/4 inch pieces
2 1/2 teaspoons salt (1 tsp for the meat and vegetables, 1 1/2 tsp for the rice)
3 cups long grain rice such as basmati or jasmine, rinsed

instructions: Trim the beef, pat it dry and cut it into small pieces. Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then drain it.
Heat a Dutch oven until very hot, add the oil, then brown the beef without crowding, stirring now and then.
Lower the heat and soften the onion, then add the carrot, 1 teaspoon of the salt, pepper, paprika, cumin and bay leaves and cook until the carrot softens.
Add hot water, cover and simmer on medium-low until the beef is tender.
Spread the rice over the beef without stirring, add hot water and the remaining salt, and boil until most of the water is absorbed.
Nestle the halved garlic head cut side down in the centre, sprinkle on the coriander, poke steam holes through the rice, then cover and cook on low until the rice is tender.
Remove the garlic and bay leaves and fold the plov gently so the beef and carrot mix through the rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Laghman (Noodles with Lamb Sauce)

lines.text: 1 lb lamb leg, cut into 1/2 inch cubes
1 1/2 teaspoons salt (1 teaspoon for the lamb, 1/2 teaspoon for the sauce)

instructions: Cut the lamb into small cubes and toss it with a little of the oil and 1 teaspoon of the salt.
Boil the noodles until tender, drain and rinse under cold water, then set aside.
Sear the lamb in a hot skillet for about 2 minutes until the outside browns but the middle is still pink, then move it to a plate.
Soften the onion in the remaining oil, then add the garlic and chili flakes until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, soy sauce, tomato paste, cumin and the rest of the salt and cook until the tomato breaks down into a sauce.
Stir in the bell pepper for a minute, then return the lamb and warm it through without overcooking.
Fluff the noodles onto plates and spoon the lamb sauce over the top.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Uyghur Lamb Pilaf

lines.text: 1.2 lb (600 g) lamb spare ribs, cut into 1 or 2 segments
2 teaspoons salt (1 teaspoon at the start, 1 teaspoon after an hour)

instructions: Cut the lamb ribs into one or two pieces each, soak the rice and prepare the onion and carrot.
Heat the oil in a wok, fry the garlic and ginger briefly, then brown the lamb with 1 teaspoon of the salt.
Add the onion, then the carrot, and cook until they start to soften.
Pour in 3 cups of water, skim the foam, add the sugar, cumin and dried chili, hang the Sichuan peppercorn in an infuser, then cover and simmer on low.
After an hour add the rest of the salt. When the lamb is tender, push it to the edges and add the drained rice in the middle with enough hot water to cover.
Move everything to a heavy pot, cover and cook on the lowest heat until the rice is tender.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Khachapuri

lines.text: 5 large eggs (1 for egg wash, 4 for the tops)

instructions: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the water and butter, and knead with a dough hook until smooth.
Let the dough rise covered in a warm spot until doubled.
Divide the dough into four balls and chill them on a lined tray for at least an hour.
Stir the four cheeses together and heat the oven to 400 F.
Roll each ball into an oval, spoon the cheese down the middle, then fold and twist the ends up into a boat.
Brush the rims with beaten egg and bake until golden and the cheese has melted.
Press the cheese down, crack an egg into each boat, raise the oven to 450 F and bake until the whites are set and the yolks still runny.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Beef Shashlik

lines.text: 2 lbs top sirloin, cut into 1 1/2 inch pieces
2 bell peppers, cut into 1 1/2 inch pieces
1 large purple onion, cut into 1 1/2 inch pieces

instructions: Stir the oil, lemon juice, salt, pepper, garlic, dill and bay leaves together in a glass or plastic bowl.
Add the beef pieces, coat well and marinate in the refrigerator for 4 to 6 hours, stirring a few times.
Soak wooden skewers for at least 30 minutes while the beef finishes marinating.
Slice the bell peppers and onion, then thread them onto the skewers alternating with the beef and brush with leftover marinade.
Grill over medium-high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning every 2 to 3 minutes.
Rest the kebabs for at least 5 minutes before serving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chashushuli (Georgian Beef and Tomato Stew)

lines.text: 1 pound boneless chuck roast, cut into 1 1/4-inch pieces
1 pound boneless beef short ribs, cut into 1 1/4-inch pieces
2 tablespoons finely chopped garlic (about 6 garlic cloves), divided
1 (28-ounce) can whole peeled tomatoes (undrained), crushed by hand
1 to 2 jalapeño chiles, seeded and finely chopped (1 used)
6 cilantro sprigs plus 1/2 cup chopped fresh cilantro, divided

instructions: Melt the butter in a large Dutch oven over medium-low heat, soften the onions for 6 to 8 minutes, then move them to a bowl.
Heat the sunflower oil over medium-high heat and brown the chuck and short rib in two batches, turning, until browned all over.

Return the meat and onions to the pot with half the garlic, the crushed tomatoes with their juice, 3 cups water and the salt. Bring to a boil, stir in the jalapeño and add the cilantro sprigs tied together with twine.
Cover and roast in a 350°F oven, stirring now and then, until the meat is fork-tender, about 2 hours.
Skim the fat from the top and discard the cilantro sprigs. Stir in the chopped cilantro, basil, parsley and the remaining garlic, rest for 5 minutes and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Beef Soup (Kharcho)
instructions: Salt the beef, then brown it in two batches in 2 tablespoons of the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Set it aside; it does not need to cook through.
Add the onion with more oil as needed and cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Add the tomatoes with their juice, the broth, 4 cups water and the browned beef. Bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat, cover and simmer 1 1/2 to 2 hours until the beef is tender.
Stir in the rice, lemon juice, garlic and coriander, cover and simmer 20 minutes until the rice is tender.
Take the pot off the heat, stir in the parsley and dill, cover and let stand 10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Balyg Kyukyusu (Smoked Fish and Herb Omelet)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Mix the smoked fish, celery, dill, parsley, scallions, lemon zest, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt in a second bowl until frothy.
Heat the olive oil in an ovenproof skillet over medium-low heat and cook the fish and herb mixture for about 1 minute, until the herbs turn bright green.
Pour the eggs over the top and use a fork to spread the fish and herbs evenly through them.
Bake about 20 minutes, until the top springs back lightly.
Let the omelet cool to room temperature, loosen the sides, turn it out and slice it into 10 pieces.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegetable Thukpa
instructions: Boil the egg noodles in salted water for 7 to 9 minutes until tender but firm, then drain, rinse and drain again.
Heat the mustard oil in a saucepan over medium-high heat and fry the onion for about 5 minutes until light brown.
Add the chiles, garlic and ginger and saute for 1 minute.
Add the bell pepper and mushrooms and stir-fry for 6 minutes.
Add the broth, yogurt and soy sauce and cook about 5 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Add the egg noodles and simmer 3 minutes, then stir in the spinach and cook 1 to 2 minutes until wilted.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Momos with Red Chile Chutney

lines.text: 4 garlic cloves for the chutney plus 3 garlic cloves for the filling
4 red Thai chiles, seeded and chopped
1/2 teaspoon kosher salt in the chutney plus 1 teaspoon in the filling
1 small white onion, finely chopped (about 1 1/4 cups)
3 spring onions, green and white parts chopped (about 1 1/2 cups)
1 small carrot, peeled and grated (about 1/4 cup)
20 to 25 frozen round dumpling wrappers, thawed (22 used)

instructions: Cook 4 garlic cloves in the sunflower oil for 1 minute, add the tomatoes, soy sauce, red chiles and half the salt, and cook 8 to 10 minutes until the tomatoes are mashed. Cool 30 minutes, then blend smooth.
Heat the canola oil, add the onion, 3 garlic cloves and the rest of the salt for 30 seconds, then add the spring onions, cabbage and carrot and cook 3 to 5 minutes until just soft. Cool slightly.
Put about 2 teaspoons of filling in the middle of each wrapper, gather and pleat the edges, and pinch the top shut like a small satchel.
Boil 2 inches of water, set a parchment-lined bamboo steamer on top and steam the momos in batches for 8 to 10 minutes until the wrappers turn transparent.
Serve the momos warm with the red chile chutney.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Dal Bhat Tarkari

lines.text: 2 onions, 1 minced for the dal and 1 chopped for the curry
1 cup chopped tomatoes for the dal plus 2 seeded tomatoes for the curry
4 tablespoons ghee (2 for the dal, 2 for the curry)
4 teaspoons ground cumin (2 for the dal, 2 for the curry)
2 teaspoons turmeric (1 for the dal, 1 for the curry)

instructions: Rinse the rice, then soak it in 4 cups of water for 30 minutes.

Toast half the cumin, coriander and turmeric in 2 tablespoons ghee for 30 seconds, then cook half the onion and half the garlic until translucent. Stir in half the tomatoes, the lentils and 4 cups of water, bring to a boil and simmer 45 minutes.
Bring the soaked rice and its water to a boil, cover tightly, cook on low for 20 minutes and rest covered for 10 minutes.
Toast the remaining spices in 2 tablespoons ghee for 30 seconds, then cook the remaining onion, garlic and the ginger until the onion is well cooked.
Add the remaining tomatoes, the potatoes, the cauliflower and 1 cup of water, bring to a boil and simmer 10 to 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Serve the dal, rice and vegetable curry together on a plate.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Paneer Jhol Momo

lines.text: 1 1/4 teaspoons salt across the dough, filling and jhol
6 teaspoons oil across the dough, filling and jhol
1 clove garlic in the filling plus 1 clove garlic in the jhol

instructions: Mix the flour with 1/2 teaspoon salt, 2 teaspoons oil and about 1/2 cup water into a dough and knead until smooth.
Cook the onion and garlic in 2 teaspoons oil, add the cabbage and paneer with a little salt and cook briefly for the filling, then cool.
Roll the dough into small rounds, fill each with a spoon of the filling and pleat the edges closed.
Steam the momos until the wrappers are cooked through.
Dry roast the sesame seeds and cumin until golden, then roast the dried chilies and garlic in 2 teaspoons oil, add the tomato and ginger and blend everything to a smooth paste.
Cook the paste with 2 cups of water and a little salt for about 5 minutes, then pour the hot jhol over the momos and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Nepali Aloo

lines.text: 3 cups peeled and sliced yellow potatoes
3 teaspoons oil, 1 for the potatoes and 2 for the tempering
1/2 teaspoon brown or black mustard seeds

instructions: Peel and cube the potatoes. Heat 1 teaspoon oil in a skillet over medium-high heat, spread the potatoes in one layer and let them sit for a minute or two, then stir.
Cover, reduce to medium-low and cook about 5 minutes, then flip and cook another 6 to 8 minutes until crisp at the edges and soft inside. Take the potatoes out.
Heat the remaining 2 teaspoons oil in the same skillet and cook the mustard and cumin seeds until the mustard seeds pop and the cumin darkens.
Lower the heat and stir in the ginger, garlic, green chili and a pinch of salt, cooking until the garlic turns golden.
Add the potatoes, turmeric, the rest of the salt and the vinegar, toss to coat and cook for a minute. Serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Ema Datshi
instructions: Cut the stalks off the jalapenos and quarter them lengthwise. Slit the green chilies, slice the onion, roughly chop the garlic and dice the tomato.
Put the peppers, onion, garlic, tomato, oil, salt and water in a pan.
Cover and boil on medium heat about 15 minutes until the peppers soften.
Turn off the heat, then stir in the butter and grated cheese until the cheese melts completely. Taste and adjust the salt.
Serve hot with boiled rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Lamb Dumplings
instructions: Mix the ground lamb with the Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce and dark soy sauce until it forms a sticky paste, then mix in the ginger, Sichuan peppercorn powder, salt and peanut oil. Cover and set aside.
Mince the zucchini and carrot, cook the carrot in a little oil for 2 to 3 minutes until done, and let it cool.
Just before wrapping, mix the green onion, zucchini and carrot into the lamb.
Place about 2 teaspoons of filling in the center of each wrapper, wet the edge, fold it into a half moon and seal it.
Wrap in batches of 20 to 25 and cook within 30 minutes. Boil the dumplings gently until they float and the dough turns transparent, about 2 minutes.
Serve with Chinese black vinegar and a few ginger slices.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Xinjiang Cumin Lamb Stir Fry

lines.text: 500 g boneless lamb leg, sliced 1/2 cm thick

instructions: Slice the lamb thinly and mix it with the soy sauce, cooking wine and cornstarch. Marinate for 30 minutes.
Mix the cumin and ground Sichuan pepper in a small bowl.
Heat 3 tablespoons of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the lamb in two batches in a single layer, about 90 seconds each, until lightly golden, and set aside.
Heat the remaining oil, add the dried chilies, ginger and garlic, and stir for 10 seconds.
Add the onion and cook about 2 minutes until it just begins to soften.
Return the lamb to the pan, sprinkle over the spice mix and toss until coated. Scatter with sesame seeds and serve; the whole chilies are for flavor, not for eating.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Nihari (Beef Shank Stew)

lines.text: 2 pounds beef shanks, cut in 3 inch pieces

instructions: Toast the coriander, fennel and cumin in a dry skillet until fragrant, cool and grind to a powder.
Brown the sliced onion in the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and set it aside.
Sear the shank pieces on all sides in the same oil, then stir in the ginger and garlic for a couple of minutes.
Add the paprika, chili powder, salt and the ground spices, return the onion, pour in about 6 cups of water and bring to a boil. Lower the heat and simmer for 2 to 3 hours.
When the meat is about 80 percent done, whisk the flour with a cup of cooled cooking liquid into a smooth paste and stir it slowly into the pot.
Simmer about 45 minutes more until the meat is falling apart and oil rises to the surface. Spoon off excess oil.
Serve hot with the saved oil, julienned ginger, cilantro, green chili and lemon, and naan on the side.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chapli Kabab
instructions: Combine the beef, crushed coriander, pomegranate seeds, chili, cumin, garlic, salt, egg and maize flour in a large bowl.
Add the chopped tomatoes and the squeezed chopped onion and mix thoroughly.
Add 2 to 3 tablespoons of water and knead well until the mixture holds together.
With wet hands, shape 150 g portions into balls, set them on parchment and press each flat to about 6 inches across.
Heat the oil on a griddle over medium heat and fry the kababs 4 to 5 minutes per side until deep golden brown.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chana for Halwa Puri
instructions: Soak the chickpeas overnight in hot water, then drain and rinse them.
Pressure cook the chickpeas in about 1.6 liters of water for 40 minutes, then keep them in their cooking liquid.
Heat the ghee, add the cumin, peppercorns and onion and cook about 15 minutes until the onion starts to brown.
Add the garlic, ginger and green chilies, then the yogurt, turmeric, chili powder and salt, and stir for 5 to 6 minutes until it forms a thick paste.
Add 1 liter of the chickpea liquid and the chickpeas and simmer, covered, for 15 minutes.
Blend about one ladle of the curry smooth, stir it back in and simmer 15 to 20 minutes until thick. Serve with puri and halwa.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Sri Lankan Fish Ambul Thiyal

lines.text: 1.5 lb tuna steaks, cut into thin flat pieces

instructions: Mix the goraka paste, black pepper, salt, chili powder, garlic powder and about half a cup of water into a thick paste.
Cut the tuna into thin flat pieces about 3 inches wide and 1 inch thick.
Dip each piece in the paste to coat it well and lay it in a single layer in a heavy-bottomed pot, wide side down.
Spread any remaining paste over the fish and add the curry leaves and cinnamon pieces.
Cover and cook on very low heat until the fish releases its liquid and is mostly cooked, then turn the pieces over.
Lower the heat and cook until all the moisture has evaporated. Let it cool in the pot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Ohn No Khau Swe

lines.text: 1 kilogram of chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
5 medium onions, blended to a smooth pulp
2 tablespoons salt (1 in the marinade, 1 in the curry)

instructions: Coat the chicken with the salt, garlic, ginger, chilli powder, turmeric and paprika and leave it to marinate while you make the broth.
Stir the chickpea flour into 5 cups of water over medium heat for 5 minutes until smooth, then add the coconut cream and stir until it melts.
Add 3 more cups of water and the remaining salt, then simmer on the lowest heat for 45 minutes, adding up to 5 more cups of water to keep it creamy.
Blend the onions with a little water, fry the paste in the oil for about 12 minutes until golden and the oil rises to the top.
Add the marinated chicken, brown it, then cover and cook on low heat for 30 minutes until tender.
Cook the spaghetti in salted water according to the packet and drain.
Put spaghetti in each bowl, ladle over the coconut broth and top with a scoop of the chicken curry.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Shan Noodle

lines.text: 14 garlic cloves (10 to 12 for the garlic oil, 3 to 4 for the sauce)
1 cup oil (1/2 cup for garlic oil, 1/2 cup for chilli oil)

instructions: Fry 10 to 12 chopped garlic cloves in half the oil until lightly browned, stir in the sesame seeds for a few seconds and set the garlic oil aside.
Heat the other half of the oil until very hot, pour it over the chilli flakes and stir to make the chilli oil.

Sauté the shallots and remaining garlic, add the chicken, tomatoes, paprika, soy sauce, salt and half a cup of water, and simmer until the chicken is cooked and the tomatoes break down into a thick sauce.
Cook the rice noodles according to the packet, then drain.
Toss the noodles with some garlic oil and chilli oil, top with the chicken tomato sauce and crushed peanuts.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Lao Khao Soi

lines.text: 2 tsp salt for the broth and a pinch for the sauce
2 tbsp yellow soybean paste — use Healthy Boy Soy Bean Paste 810 g (Australian label)
1 tbsp fish sauce, to taste (amount estimated)

instructions: Blanch the pork bones in boiling water for 10 minutes and drain.
Put the bones, onion, garlic and salt in a pot with water and simmer with the lid on for 1 hour.
Fry the red curry paste in the oil for 1 to 2 minutes, add the diced tomatoes and cook until they break down.
Stir in the ground pork, soybean paste and a pinch of salt, break up the clumps and simmer on low for 10 minutes.
Cook the rice noodles according to the packet and divide them among bowls.
Ladle broth over the noodles, add a scoop of pork sauce, then season with the chili powder and fish sauce to taste.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Bak Kut Teh

lines.text: 1 tbsp dark soy sauce, to serve (amount estimated)
6 g chilli padi (about 3), chopped, to serve (amount estimated)
10 g coriander sprigs, to serve (amount estimated)

instructions: Blanch the pork ribs in boiling water for 10 to 15 minutes to remove impurities, then drain and set aside.
Toast the garlic bulbs and the white peppercorns separately in a dry pan until golden and fragrant, then put them in a spice bag.
Bring a large pot of water to the boil with the spice bag.
Add the ribs, salt and chicken powder, top up with water and simmer for 2 to 2.5 hours until the meat nearly falls off the bone.
Mix the chopped chilli padi with the dark soy sauce for dipping.
Ladle the soup and ribs into bowls and top with coriander.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Thunder Tea Rice (Hakka Lei Cha Rice)

lines.text: 600 g cooked white rice, enough for 4
300 g long beans, cut into 1/2-inch pieces
200 g extra firm tofu, pressed and cubed
100 g chopped preserved radish (chai po), rinsed
180 g roasted peanuts (100 g topping, 80 g for the tea paste)

instructions: Rinse the preserved radish, then press the tofu between towels for 30 minutes and cut it into half-inch cubes.
Pan-fry the tofu cubes in a little oil until golden on all sides and set aside.
Stir-fry the choy sum until soft, then the long beans, each in turn in a hot wok, and set aside.
Fry the preserved radish for about 5 minutes and set aside.
Blend the basil, mint, coriander, 80 g of the peanuts, the sesame seeds and the green tea leaves with a splash of water into a thick paste.
Stir 2 to 3 tablespoons of paste into 3 to 4 tablespoons of boiling water and let it steep for 15 minutes.
Spoon the rice into bowls, arrange the vegetables, tofu, radish and remaining peanuts on top and pour the tea soup over just before serving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Hakka Style Chinese Stuffed Tofu
instructions: Cut the tofu into 2-inch squares about three-quarters of an inch thick and scoop about a teaspoon from the centre of each piece.
Mix the ground pork with the minced ginger, then add the scooped tofu, wine, white pepper, salt and half the scallion.
Press the pork mixture into each tofu hollow, mounding it slightly.
Arrange the pieces on a plate and steam over boiling water for about 10 minutes until the pork is cooked through.
Pour the steaming liquid into a small pan, add the oyster sauce, dark soy sauce and a splash of water, and bring to a simmer.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry until glossy, pour the sauce over the tofu and garnish with the remaining scallion.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Biang Biang Noodles (Yu Po Mian)

lines.text: 2 bundles (150 g) dried knife shaved noodles
4 heads baby bok choy, cut into bite-size pieces
1 green onion, white part minced, green part sliced
3 tablespoons peanut oil or vegetable oil, heated

instructions: Stir the soy sauce, vinegar and sesame oil together in a large bowl.
Blanch the baby bok choy in boiling water for about 2 minutes until tender, then move it to a plate.
Boil the noodles in the same pot following the package timing, rinse them under cold water, drain well and toss them in the sauce bowl.
Pile the minced white scallion, garlic, chili flakes, sesame seeds, cumin and ground Sichuan peppercorn on top of the noodles.
Heat the oil in a small pan until hot and pour it over the seasonings so it sizzles.
Toss everything together while hot, top with the bok choy and green scallion, and serve right away.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Yunnan Rice Noodle Soup (Little Pot Rice Noodles)
instructions: Mix the ground pork with the wine, soy sauce and a splash of water and refrigerate while you prepare everything else.
If the noodles are dried, soak and cook them, then rinse and set them aside.
Heat the oil in a large pot and fry the ginger and garlic until fragrant.
Add the marinated pork and cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Pour in the stock and bring it to a boil, then add the bean sprouts, pea tips and garlic chives and return to a boil.
Stir in the noodles to heat through, ladle into bowls and serve with the pickled sour cabbage.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Da Pan Ji (Big Plate Chicken)

lines.text: 4 boneless chicken thighs, diced to 1-inch pieces
1 russet potato, roll cut into 1/2-inch pieces

instructions: Mix the wine and soy sauce in a small bowl, and put the garlic, chilies and sliced white scallion on a plate.
Boil the noodles according to the package, rinse under cold water and drain.
Heat the oil in a wok, add the chicken and cook, stirring now and then, until the surface is light golden.
Add the garlic and chili plate with the doubanjiang and cook for 30 seconds, then add the wine and soy mixture to deglaze.
Pour in the stock, add the potato, bring to a simmer, cover and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add the red pepper and simmer 5 minutes more, stir in the scallion, and reduce over high heat if the sauce is thin.
Spoon the chicken and sauce over the noodles and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Dongbei Guo Bao Rou

lines.text: 1 pound pork loin, sliced 1/4 inch thick
About 1/4 cup oil absorbed from deep frying

instructions: Marinate the sliced pork with the soy sauce and Shaoxing wine for about 15 minutes.
Stir the potato starch into water, let it settle for 15 minutes, then pour off the extra water so a thick paste remains.
Mix the sugar, rice vinegar and sesame oil for the sauce and set it aside.
Coat the pork in the starch paste, then fry in 250 to 300 F oil in batches for about 2 minutes and drain.
Fry the pork again in small batches for about 30 seconds each until crisp and golden.
Fry the ginger and garlic briefly, add the sauce and reduce for 2 to 3 minutes, then toss in the carrot, scallions and pork to coat in a thin layer of sauce and serve at once.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Shanghai-Style Braised Pork Belly

lines.text: 1 1/2 lbs lean, skin-on pork belly, cut into 3/4-inch pieces

instructions: Cut the pork belly into 3/4-inch pieces, blanch them in boiling water for about 1 minute until opaque, then rinse.
Warm the oil and sugar over low heat until the sugar starts to melt, add the pork and brown it lightly over medium heat.
Turn the heat to low, add the Shaoxing wine and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the soy sauce, dark soy sauce and enough water to almost cover the pork.
Cover and simmer over medium heat for 45 to 60 minutes until fork-tender, stirring every 5 to 10 minutes and adding water if the pan dries.
Uncover, raise the heat and stir until the sauce reduces to a glossy coating on the pork.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Hunan Steamed Fish with Salted Chilies

lines.text: 12 oz tilapia or flounder fillet (340 g)
1/4 cup jarred Hunan chili peppers (duo jiao)
1 tablespoon fermented black beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Set a shallow plate on a steaming rack in a wok, then rinse and dry the fish and slice the tofu 1/2 inch thick.
Lay the tofu in two rows on the plate and set the fish on top, tucking the thin tail end under.
Stir the soy sauce, salted chilies and sugar together and spread over the fish and tofu, then scatter on the rinsed black beans.
Boil 2 cups of water in the wok, turn off the heat, set the plate on the rack and bring back to a gentle simmer.
Cover and steam for about 12 minutes, until the fish is opaque and a knife slides in easily.
Spoon the cooking liquid over the top and garnish with cilantro and scallion.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Armenian White Bean Plaki

lines.text: 1 1/2 cups dried Great Northern beans, soaked overnight
2 to 3 medium carrots, peeled and diced

instructions: Put the soaked beans in a large pot, cover with water by 1 inch, add the salt and simmer until nearly tender.
Stir in the carrot, celery, onion, tomatoes, lemon juice, paprika, cayenne and parsley and cook another 30 minutes.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the crushed garlic.
Taste, adjust the seasoning and serve warm or cold.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Paya (Lamb Trotters)

lines.text: 1 1/2 tablespoons ginger from the ginger and garlic paste
1 1/2 tablespoons garlic from the ginger and garlic paste

instructions: Put the trotters, onions, ginger, garlic, 2 glasses of water, chilli powder, salt, turmeric and coriander in a pressure cooker and cook for 20 minutes at high pressure.
Let the steam release on its own before opening the lid.
Add the tomatoes and cook on high heat until they are soft and mushy.
Stir in the ghee and cook on high heat for 3 minutes.
Add 12 glasses of water, seal the cooker and cook for 30 minutes at high pressure, then release the steam.
Stir in the garam masala, top with green chillies and serve hot with naan.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Coloradito Chicken

lines.text: 2 teaspoons kosher or coarse sea salt, divided
1 3-ounce bar Mexican chocolate, broken into pieces

instructions: Slit the plantain skin in a few places, bake it at 400 F in a foil-lined dish until cooked through, then peel and slice it.
Toast the ancho and guajillo chiles on a hot comal for about 30 seconds a side, then simmer them with the whole tomatoes in water for 12 to 15 minutes until soft.
Char the unpeeled garlic on the comal until softened and peel it. Toast the cinnamon, almonds and sesame seeds until fragrant.
Blend the garlic, cinnamon, almonds, sesame, chiles, tomatoes, a cup of their cooking liquid, the plantain and 1 teaspoon salt until completely smooth.
Season the chicken with the remaining salt and brown it in a wide pot in batches, then set it aside.

Pour the sauce into the pot and cook 6 to 7 minutes until thick. Add the broth, chocolate and chicken and simmer 30 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce coats a spoon. Serve with tortillas or rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Amarillito Mole with Chicken

lines.text: 1 lb (8 to 10) tomatillos, husked and rinsed
8 chicken pieces with skin and bones

instructions: Toast the ancho and guajillo chiles on a hot comal or dry skillet for 10 to 15 seconds a side until pliable and fragrant.

Simmer the chiles with the tomatillos, tomato and garlic in water until everything is soft, then blend with the cinnamon, oregano, 1 teaspoon salt and a little of the cooking liquid into a smooth sauce.
Heat the oil in a large skillet and brown the chicken pieces for 3 to 4 minutes a side, skin side down first.
Add the onion and cook 2 to 3 minutes until soft and translucent.
Pour in the blended sauce, the broth and the remaining salt, and simmer steadily for 15 to 20 minutes.
Lower the heat and cook another 12 to 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the mole has thickened enough to coat a spoon.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Papadzules

lines.text: 1 small white onion, diced, plus 2 tablespoons chopped for the broth
2 1/2 teaspoons salt, divided between broth and tomato sauce

instructions: Hard-boil the eggs, cool and peel them, then chop them.
Roast the tomatoes on a foil-lined griddle or under a hot broiler until blistered and soft, then peel and coarsely puree them with their juices.
Sauté the diced onion in the oil until deep golden, add the tomatoes and habanero, and simmer about 15 minutes until spoonable. Season with a little salt.
Boil the water with the epazote, the 2 tablespoons onion and the remaining salt for 5 minutes, steep off the heat for 15 minutes, then strain.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry skillet until they puff and pop, then blend with the epazote broth until smooth and warm the sauce gently without boiling.
Fill each warm tortilla with chopped egg and roll it up. Ladle on the pumpkin seed sauce and top with the tomato sauce and extra egg.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Pepián de Pollo

lines.text: 5-6 skinless chicken thighs, bone in or out
4 dried guajillo, pasa or poblano chiles
3 Yukon gold potatoes, thinly sliced and halved

instructions: Simmer the chicken thighs in the broth with enough water to cover and a little of the salt for 20 minutes, until cooked through.
Brown the tomatoes, tomatillos, onion and guajillo chiles in a dry skillet for 15 to 20 minutes until nicely browned.
Toast the pumpkin seeds, sesame seeds and cinnamon in a small dry skillet for 2 minutes, then grind them to a smooth paste.
Blend the browned vegetables with the ground seed mix, the toasted bread, the remaining salt and some of the reduced broth until smooth and orange.
Pour the sauce into a deep skillet and bring it to a simmer, loosening it with broth if it is too thick.
Add the cooked chicken and the sliced potatoes and simmer 20 to 30 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the chicken pulls apart. Serve over rice or with tortillas.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Nicaraguan Vigorón and Tajadas

lines.text: 2 teaspoons salt, plus more to taste
canola oil, for frying (about 2 tablespoons absorbed)
4 unripe green plantains, thinly sliced lengthwise

instructions: Peel the yuca, cut it into quarters and boil it in salted water with the lime juice for about 25 minutes until tender. Cool slightly and remove the woody centre.
Blanch the cabbage in boiling water for 50 to 60 seconds, then drain and pat dry.
Toss the tomatoes and onion with a teaspoon of salt and the vinegar, then add the cabbage and set aside.
Heat the oil to about 325 F and fry the plantain slices in small batches for about 45 seconds, flipping once, until lightly golden. Drain and salt them.
Top the yuca with the cabbage salad and the pork rinds and serve with the tajadas alongside.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Llapingachos

lines.text: 1/4 cup thinly sliced onion for the sauce

instructions: Peel the potatoes and boil them in salted water until a knife slides in easily, then drain and let them steam dry for a few minutes.
Mash the potatoes smooth with the achiote powder and salt, shape into balls of about 1/3 cup and chill for at least 20 minutes.
Simmer the milk with the sliced onion for 10 minutes without boiling, strain out the onion, whisk in the peanut butter and simmer 4 to 5 minutes until thick like heavy cream.
Mix the cheese with the chopped scallions, press a tablespoon of the mixture into each potato ball and flatten into a patty.
Pan-fry the patties in hot oil over medium heat until browned on both sides, keeping them warm in the oven as you go.
Serve the patties topped with the warm peanut sauce.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Bolivian Salteñas

lines.text: 3/4 stick butter for the filling plus 1 stick melted butter for the dough
1/2 cup sugar in the filling plus 1/2 cup sugar in the dough

instructions: Boil the diced potatoes until cooked but still firm. Melt the butter with the turmeric, add the onion and potatoes, then stir in the peas, parsley and sugar and cook a couple of minutes.
Stir in the cooked ground beef and the beef broth, bring to a boil, add the gelatin, stir well and take off the heat.
Chill the filling in a large bowl for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Mix the flour, sugar and the beaten eggs, add the almost-boiling water and the melted butter and knead into a smooth ball. Rest 10 to 20 minutes, then roll thin and cut 6-inch rounds.
Heat the oven to 500 F. Put about 1/4 cup filling on each round, wet the edge, fold over and pinch and twist the edge into a braided seam.
Bake on a lined tray for about 15 minutes until browned, then rest at least 10 minutes before eating.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Sopa de Maní
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion and garlic with the oregano and cumin until the onion softens.
Add the beef, broth, potatoes and peanuts and bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer on very low heat, about 90 minutes, until the beef and potatoes are tender.
Stir in the rice, peas and milk and cook about 20 minutes more until the rice is tender.
Taste for salt and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Rocoto Relleno

lines.text: 10 rocotos, tops cut off and seeds removed
3 eggs for the topping plus 4 eggs for the gratin
1 can evaporated milk plus 1 1/2 cups for the gratin
2 lb waxy potatoes, boiled, peeled and sliced
8 oz queso fresco, in thick slices

instructions: Cut the tops off the rocotos, scrape out the seeds and ribs wearing gloves, then boil them three times in fresh water to calm the heat and set aside.
Heat the oil, then cook the diced beef with the aji panca paste until browned.
Add the onions, peanuts, raisins, hard-boiled eggs, salt and pepper and cook until the onions soften. Fill the rocotos and stand them in a baking pan.
Beat one egg with part of the evaporated milk and pour it around the peppers, then top each with beaten egg and the pepper cap and bake at 350 F for 15 minutes until set.
Layer the boiled potato slices and queso fresco in a buttered dish, pour over the remaining eggs beaten with evaporated milk and bake at 350 F for 25 to 30 minutes until golden.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chicken Cau Cau
instructions: Simmer the chicken in water to cover with the spearmint sprigs for about 25 minutes until tender, then dice it and strain and keep the stock.
Brown the onion and garlic in the oil, then stir in the aji amarillo, cumin, turmeric, salt and pepper and cook 5 minutes.
Add the diced chicken, 4 cups of the stock, the potatoes, the peas and half the chopped spearmint and simmer 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Taste for seasoning, scatter over the rest of the spearmint and serve with white rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Frango com Creme de Milho (Chicken with Creamed Corn)

lines.text: 2 pounds chicken cutlets or breasts, cut into strips
4 cloves garlic, minced (the source's alternative to Brazilian sofrito)
1/2 teaspoon salt (source says salt and pepper to taste)

instructions: Toss the chicken strips with a tablespoon of the oil and the salt, and set aside.
Blend one can of the drained corn with the milk until smooth.
Sear the chicken strips in a hot pan with the rest of the oil until golden, then lift them out.
Soften the onion in the same pan, add the garlic, oregano and thyme and cook until fragrant.
Add the remaining corn and the blended corn, and simmer 5 to 8 minutes until thickened.
Remove the thyme, stir in the butter and parmesan, return the chicken and its juices and simmer a few more minutes.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Haitian Soup Joumou

lines.text: 3 pounds calabaza pumpkin or butternut squash, skin removed and cut into large chunks
2 pounds beef neck bones or beef shanks, cut into cubes
1 small scotch bonnet pepper, left whole
2 large potatoes, peeled and cut in 4 to 6 pieces

instructions: Toss the beef cubes with half the onion, half the garlic, the thyme, the whole scotch bonnet and 1 teaspoon of the salt. Marinate in the fridge for at least 30 minutes.
Cook the beef in a pot over medium-high heat with a little water, adding more as needed, until tender. Set it aside with its liquid.
Boil the squash in water until soft, let it cool for 10 minutes, then puree until smooth.
Soften the remaining onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the carrots, cabbage and remaining garlic and cook uncovered 5 minutes.
Stir in the squash puree and bring to a boil, thinning with water if needed. Add the potatoes and pasta and simmer 20 to 30 minutes until tender.
Return the beef with its liquid for the last 10 minutes, season with the remaining salt and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Guyanese Pholourie

lines.text: canola oil for deep frying, about 3 inches (about 2 tablespoons absorbed)

instructions: Grind the scallions, hot pepper and garlic to a fine paste in a mortar or food processor.
Mix the flour, split pea flour, cumin, turmeric and salt. In a separate bowl, stir the yeast into 1 cup of warm water and leave for 10 minutes.
Stir the yeast water and the paste into the dry mix and let the batter rise 40 minutes.
Heat about 3 inches of oil in a pan for deep frying.
Drop tablespoons of batter into the hot oil and fry 2 to 3 minutes, turning once the edges brown.
Drain the pholourie and serve with mango sour or apple chutney.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Guyanese Cook-up Rice

lines.text: 1 cup black eyed peas, soaked overnight
1 pound corned beef brisket, cut into bite-sized pieces

instructions: Soak the black eyed peas overnight, drain, cover with fresh water and boil 10 minutes until they soften. Set aside.
Cook the corned beef in a pressure cooker with 3 cups of water for 15 minutes, or about 30 minutes in a regular pot.
Heat the oil in a wide pot and brown the chicken pieces.
Add the onion, garlic, thyme and wiri wiri pepper and cook 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the corned beef and coconut milk, cook 5 minutes, then add about 2 cups of water and bring to a boil.
Stir in the rice, peas, scallions and bay leaf, cover and cook on low for 25 to 30 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is gone, adding water a little at a time if needed.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chipa 4 Quesos (Paraguayan 4 Cheese Bread)

lines.text: 1/4 cup butter at room temperature (the source also allows lard)

instructions: Heat the oven to 450 F and grease a baking tray.
Mix the four cheeses in a small bowl and set aside a third of a cup for topping.
In a big bowl combine the cassava flour, salt, anise, butter, egg, milk and the cheese mixture. It looks dry at first; bring it together with your hands into a uniform dough.
Knead the dough on a flat surface for about 5 minutes until it has a play dough texture.
Divide into 10 equal portions, roll each into a ball and flatten slightly. Set them on the tray and top with the reserved cheese.
Bake 25 minutes and let cool for 5 minutes. Eat hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Haitian Akra

lines.text: 1 lb malanga (yautia), peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces
1/2 tablespoon chopped Scotch bonnet pepper, seeds removed
2 cups vegetable oil for frying (about 3 tablespoons absorbed)

instructions: Peel the malanga and cut it into small cubes. Blend it in a food processor with the scallions, garlic, parsley, thyme, green pepper, black pepper, salt and Scotch bonnet until smooth but still slightly textured.
Scrape the batter into a bowl, cover it and chill for at least 30 minutes.
Let the batter come to room temperature for a few minutes, then stir in the flour.
Heat the oil in a deep pan over medium-high heat to about 350 to 375 F.
Drop small spoonfuls of batter into the oil and fry in batches for 3 to 5 minutes, until golden brown and crisp.
Lift the fritters out onto a rack or paper towels to drain and serve right away.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Salted Beef Callaloo

lines.text: 3/4 lb salted beef, cut into pieces
2 lb baby spinach, washed and chopped

instructions: Rinse the salted beef in cool water, cover it with water and boil for at least 1 hour until partly tender. Drain and set aside.
Warm the oil in a deep pot on low heat. Cook the onion, garlic, black pepper and thyme for 3 minutes, then add the beef and cook 2 to 3 minutes more.
Stir in the okra and pumpkin and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the chopped spinach and stir until it starts to wilt, about 2 minutes.
Add the salt, 3 1/2 cups water and the coconut milk. Bring to a boil, tuck in the whole Scotch bonnet, then lower to a gentle simmer for about 90 minutes.
Take out the beef and, if you want less heat, the pepper. Blend the soup to the thickness you like, return the beef, and taste for salt.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Oaxacan Tetelas
instructions: Blend the beans until smooth. Cook the onion and jalapeno in the lard until soft, add the bean puree and stir until it is dry but still creamy and spreadable. Season with salt and set aside.
Mix the masa harina, salt and lukewarm water into a soft dough that feels like play dough. Divide it into 8 balls and keep them under a damp towel.
Press each ball between two sheets of plastic into a 6-inch round. Spread beans in the middle and add a little cheese.
Fold in one side, then the other, then fold up the bottom to make a triangle. Pat it flat gently.
Heat a cast-iron pan until very hot and cook each tetela 3 to 4 minutes per side until lightly browned. Keep the cooked ones warm wrapped in a napkin.
sourceName: Mexican Recipes by Maricruz Avalos Flores
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Oaxacan Mushroom and Cheese Quesadillas

lines.text: 1 lb white or baby bello mushrooms, thinly sliced

instructions: Heat the oil and butter in a large saute pan over medium-high heat. When the butter sizzles, cook the onion until soft and translucent, 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the serrano and garlic and cook for about 1 minute, until fragrant.
Stir in the sliced mushrooms and cook about 5 minutes, stirring often, until their juices come out and begin to dry. Add the salt and cook 1 minute more. The mix should be moist, not wet.
Warm each tortilla on a hot comal or dry skillet for about 20 seconds. Put a spoonful or two of the mushroom mix and of the cheese in the center and fold it over like a turnover.
Cook the folded quesadillas about 2 minutes per side, until the cheese melts and the tortillas begin to crisp.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Poc Chuc

lines.text: 1/2 cup orange juice, stand-in for bitter orange juice
1/2 cup fresh lime juice, stand-in for bitter orange juice
1 cup cooked black beans, mashed for the side puree

instructions: Blend the orange juice, lime juice, garlic, salt and pepper until smooth.
Lay the thin pork slices in a dish, pour the marinade over, cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Warm the black beans and mash them to a rough puree while the grill heats to high.
Lift the pork out of the marinade and let the extra drip off.
Grill the pork 2 to 3 minutes per side until cooked through.
Warm the tortillas and serve the pork with the bean puree and tortillas.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Yucatecan Pork and Beans

lines.text: 4 pounds pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch chunks
4 fresh epazote sprigs, tied with twine
1 cup coarsely chopped cilantro leaves and upper stems

instructions: Rinse the beans, add them to a large pot with 6 liters of water, bring to a simmer and cook with the lid slightly ajar for 45 minutes.
Add the pork chunks, halved onion, tied epazote and the salt, and stir.
Keep simmering partly covered for about 1 hour 30 minutes until the pork is tender, adding about 4 cups of boiling water so the broth does not dry out.
Turn off the heat and taste the broth, adding more salt if needed.
Slice the radishes and chop the cilantro and avocado while the pot finishes.
Ladle the pork and beans into bowls and let everyone add radish, cilantro, avocado and a squeeze of lime.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Mole Verde with Pork and White Beans

lines.text: 4 pounds boneless country-style pork ribs, cut into 2-inch chunks
1 head of garlic plus 3 more cloves
1 white onion, halved, plus 1/2 cup chopped white onion
10 black peppercorns plus 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper
1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon kosher or coarse salt

instructions: Cover the pork, half the garlic head, the halved onion, peppercorns and part of the salt with water, boil, skim and simmer about 1 hour until tender, then lift out the pork.
Strain the broth, keep 4 cups, return the rest to the pot with the beans and cook about 1 hour until tender.
Broil the tomatillos and chiles until charred and soft, about 10 minutes, then blend with the remaining garlic, chopped onion, cloves, ground pepper, salt and 1 cup of the reserved broth.
Cook the puree in the oil in a covered casserole for 10 minutes until thick and darker.
Blend the epazote and parsley with the remaining 3 cups of broth and stir into the sauce.
Add the pork and beans and simmer about 25 minutes until the sauce thickens, then serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Arroz con Mariscos

lines.text: 1 whole mild white-fleshed fish (about 3 pounds), filleted, about 600 g fillets
1 pound cleaned squid, sliced into rings

instructions: Simmer the tomatoes, jalapenos and 3 whole garlic cloves for 10 minutes, then blend with the onion and part of the salt until smooth.
Cook the puree in 2 tablespoons of the oil for 6 to 7 minutes until thick, and set aside.
Cook the squid, then the shrimp, each with garlic and salt in hot oil for 2 minutes, and set them aside together.
Toast the rice in the remaining oil for 3 to 4 minutes, then pour in the tomato puree and cook 2 to 3 minutes until most is absorbed.
Add the broth and epazote, lay the shrimp, squid and seasoned fish fillets on top, cover and simmer on medium-low for 10 to 12 minutes until the fish flakes.
Serve at once in soup plates; the rice should be tender and soupy.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Jocon

lines.text: 2 1/2 to 3 pounds chicken, cut into serving pieces

instructions: Simmer the chicken with 4 cups of water and the salt for 30 minutes to 1 hour, then lift it out and strain the broth.
Shred the cooled chicken off the bones.
Toast the pumpkin and sesame seeds in a dry skillet until lightly browned and grind them fine.
Blend the ground seeds with the soaked tortillas, tomatillos, cilantro, scallions, jalapenos and 1 cup of the broth until smooth.
Return the chicken to the pot with the sauce and 1 to 1 1/2 cups more broth and simmer 15 to 25 minutes.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Mediterranean Chickpea Salad

lines.text: 2 cans (15 oz each) chickpeas, rinsed and thoroughly drained
1/2 cup fresh flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped

instructions: Rinse and drain chickpeas thoroughly, patting dry with a kitchen towel to help the vinaigrette coat evenly.
Chop the cucumber, halve cherry tomatoes, slice olives, and finely chop fresh parsley.
Whisk together extra virgin olive oil, fresh lemon juice, minced garlic, a pinch of sea salt, and black pepper.
Toss the chickpeas, vegetables, and olives with dressing, then gently fold in diced avocado before serving.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: White Bean Soup with Spinach and Fresh Herbs

lines.text: 3 cans (15 oz each) cannellini beans, rinsed and drained
5 oz fresh baby spinach, roughly chopped

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat; sauté onion, carrots, and celery until softened and fragrant.
Add minced garlic, chopped rosemary, and thyme; stir continuously for 1 minute until highly aromatic.
Stir in cannellini beans and low-sodium vegetable broth; bring to a rolling boil, then reduce heat and simmer gently.
Use an immersion blender to partially blend one-third of the soup to create a rich, creamy rustic broth.
Fold in fresh baby spinach and simmer for 2 minutes until just wilted, then season with black pepper and lemon zest.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Tuscan White Bean Ribollita

lines.text: 2 cans (15 oz each) cannellini beans, rinsed and drained
1 bunch Lacinato (Tuscan) kale, stemmed and chopped
1 can (14.5 oz) diced San Marzano tomatoes
2 thick slices day-old sourdough or whole-grain bread, torn

instructions: Warm extra virgin olive oil in a heavy soup pot; cook diced onion, carrots, and celery for 8 to 10 minutes until golden.
Add chopped Tuscan kale, Savoy cabbage, and canned diced tomatoes; cook down for 5 minutes.
Pour in vegetable broth and half the cannellini beans; purée the remaining beans with a splash of water and stir in.
Simmer covered over low heat for 20 minutes until the greens and root vegetables are meltingly tender.
Stir in torn stale whole-grain bread, allowing it to soak up the savory broth for 10 minutes, creating a hearty stew.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Mediterranean Three Bean Soup with Tomato Pesto

lines.text: 1 can (15 oz) cannellini beans, rinsed and drained
1 can (15 oz) red kidney beans, rinsed and drained
1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, rinsed and drained

instructions: Sauté onion and garlic in olive oil in a soup pot over medium heat until translucent and fragrant.
Stir in the sun-dried tomato pesto and diced zucchini, cooking for 3 minutes to bloom the concentrated tomato flavors.
Add cannellini beans, kidney beans, chickpeas, and vegetable broth; bring to a simmer.
Simmer gently for 20 minutes to allow the beans to absorb the rich sun-dried tomato essence.
Ladle into warm bowls and top generously with fresh torn basil leaves and freshly ground black pepper.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Mediterranean Shakshuka with Poached Eggs

lines.text: 1 can (28 oz) whole peeled plum tomatoes, crushed by hand
1 large red bell pepper, thinly sliced
2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro or parsley

instructions: Heat olive oil in a heavy 10-inch skillet over medium heat; sauté sliced onion and red bell pepper until soft and sweet.
Stir in sliced garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, and a pinch of chili flakes; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed plum tomatoes with their juices, reduce heat, and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until sauce thickens.
Make four wells in the simmering tomato sauce and crack an egg into each well.
Cover skillet and cook gently on low heat for 5 to 7 minutes until egg whites are set but yolks remain runny.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Tabouli Salad

lines.text: 3 large bunches flat-leaf parsley, washed, dried thoroughly, and finely minced
1/2 cup fresh mint leaves, finely minced
3 firm Roma tomatoes, seeded and finely diced
1/3 cup high-phenolic extra virgin olive oil

instructions: Soak fine bulgur in cold water for 15 minutes until tender, then press thoroughly in a fine mesh sieve to remove moisture.
Ensure parsley and mint are completely bone-dry before finely mincing with a sharp chef's knife.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the minced herbs, drained bulgur, finely diced tomatoes, and sliced scallions.
Whisk extra virgin olive oil, fresh lemon juice, and sea salt, then pour over the salad and toss gently to combine.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Vegetarian Stuffed Eggplant

lines.text: 1.5 cups canned diced tomatoes with juice

instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C); score eggplant flesh in a diamond pattern, brush with 1 tbsp olive oil, and roast cut-side down for 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a skillet; slowly caramelize sliced onions and garlic until deeply golden and sweet.
Add crushed tomatoes, lightly crushed chickpeas, cinnamon, salt, and pepper to the skillet; simmer for 8 minutes.
Scoop out some roasted eggplant flesh, stir into the tomato-chickpea mixture, and spoon filling back into the eggplant shells.
Bake stuffed eggplants for 10 minutes until bubbling; garnish with toasted pine nuts and fresh parsley.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Italian Lentil Soup
instructions: Sauté onion, carrots, and celery in extra virgin olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat for 8 minutes until tender.
Stir in garlic, rosemary sprig, and bay leaf; cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rinsed brown lentils, crushed tomatoes, and low-sodium vegetable broth; bring to a lively boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover partially, and simmer for 25 minutes until lentils are tender and earthy.
Remove herb sprig and bay leaf; season with black pepper and serve with a final drizzle of fresh olive oil.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Mediterranean Lentil Salad

lines.text: 1 cup French green lentils (lentilles du Puy), rinsed

instructions: Simmer green lentils in salted water for 20 minutes until tender but retaining a firm, toothsome bite; drain well and cool.
In a salad bowl, whisk olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper.
Add diced cucumber, quartered cherry tomatoes, minced red onion, olives, and fresh chopped herbs.
Add the cooled lentils to the bowl and toss thoroughly so the warm lentils absorb the bright vinaigrette.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Garlic Dijon Baked Salmon

lines.text: 4 wild Alaskan salmon fillets (5-6 oz each)

instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with unbleached parchment paper.
In a small bowl, whisk together Dijon mustard, minced garlic, fresh lemon juice, olive oil, and black pepper.
Arrange salmon fillets on the baking sheet skin-side down; spoon the garlic-Dijon glaze evenly over each fillet.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until salmon is tender, moist, and easily flakes with a fork.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: One-Pan Mediterranean Cod

lines.text: 1 fresh lemon, cut into thin wheels

instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
On a large rimmed baking sheet, toss cherry tomatoes, olives, capers, sliced garlic, and oregano with 1 tbsp olive oil.
Roast vegetables for 8 minutes until cherry tomatoes begin to blister and soften.
Nestle cod fillets into the pan amongst vegetables, drizzle remaining olive oil, top with lemon wheels, and bake 10 minutes until fish is opaque.
Garnish with fresh torn basil or parsley and spoon pan juices over each serving.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Chickpeas in Tomato Sauce

lines.text: 2 cans (15 oz each) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
3 tbsp Greek extra virgin olive oil

instructions: Warm extra virgin olive oil in a deep skillet over medium heat; cook chopped onion for 7 minutes until sweet and translucent.
Add minced garlic, cumin, and cinnamon; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes, 1/2 cup water, and the rinsed chickpeas; season with salt and freshly cracked black pepper.
Simmer gently over low heat for 20 minutes until the sauce reduces into a thick, savory, comforting gravy.
Stir in chopped parsley and drizzle with a spoonful of extra virgin olive oil before serving.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Lemon Garlic Salmon with Mediterranean Flavors
instructions: Pat salmon fillets dry and season lightly with sea salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large stainless skillet over medium-high heat; sear salmon fillets skin-side up for 4 minutes until golden.
Flip salmon; reduce heat to medium and add minced garlic, capers, lemon juice, lemon zest, and broth.
Simmer in the pan juices for 5 to 6 minutes, spooning the pan sauce continuously over the salmon until cooked through.
Sprinkle with chopped fresh parsley and serve immediately with the glossy lemon pan sauce.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Loaded Chickpea Salad

lines.text: 2 cans (15 oz each) chickpeas, rinsed and drained
1/3 cup sheep's milk feta cheese, crumbled

instructions: Drain and rinse chickpeas; spread onto paper towels and gently dry.
Dice yellow bell pepper, cucumbers, and quarter cherry tomatoes into bite-sized uniform pieces.

Cook the onions, leeks and thyme in about 3 tablespoons of the oil over medium heat for 10 minutes, then add the garlic for 2 minutes.
Add the lentils, celery, carrots, broth and tomato paste, cover and simmer on low about 20 minutes until the lentils are tender, then stir in the vinegar.
Heat the oven to 450 degrees F. Rub the salmon with a little oil and heat a dry oven-safe pan on high for 4 minutes.
Sear the salmon over medium heat for 2 minutes without moving it, turn it, and roast in the oven 5 to 7 minutes.
Spoon the lentils onto plates and set a salmon fillet on top.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Red Kidney Beans with Herbs (Tsiteli Lobio)

lines.text: 1 pound dried red kidney beans, soaked
2 cups chopped cilantro, plus a little for garnish

instructions: Drain the soaked beans, cover with fresh water in a large pot and add the summer savory, bay leaves and dried chili.
Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered about 60 minutes until the beans are tender, topping up the water if needed.
Cook the onion in the sunflower oil in a pan over medium heat for about 12 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, cilantro and celery leaves to the onion and cook 3 minutes until wilted.
Stir the onion and herb mixture into the beans and simmer 15 minutes so the flavors meet and the broth thickens.
Stir in the vinegar and the salt, rest 5 minutes, and serve with a little fresh cilantro on top.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Nikujaga (Meat and Potato Stew)

lines.text: 10 snow peas, cooked and cut in 2-3 pieces
4 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into 4-8 pieces

instructions: Boil the snow peas for a minute, cool them and cut each into two or three pieces. Cut the potatoes, onions and carrot, and the beef into 2-inch pieces.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and cook the beef until it changes color.
Add the potatoes, onions and carrot and cook for a minute.
Add 1 cup of water, cover and cook at medium heat about 20 minutes until the potatoes are nearly tender.
Season with the sugar, soy sauce and mirin and cook 15 minutes longer.
Take off the heat and let the stew sit 30 minutes, then add the snow peas and reheat to serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Calabacitas con Pollo y Elote

lines.text: 2 bone-in chicken thighs and 3 chicken legs, skin off
2 pounds Mexican squash or zucchini, cut in chunks
1 can no-salt-added sweet corn, with half its liquid

instructions: Grind the cumin and garlic with a splash of water in a mortar or blender and set aside.
Heat the oil in a wide pot and sear the chicken on all sides until well browned.
Add the onion, celery and bell pepper and cook 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in the tomatoes, the cumin and garlic mixture and the broth, cover and simmer about 20 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Add the zucchini and corn with its liquid and simmer 10 minutes until the squash is tender.
Scatter chopped cilantro over the pot and serve in bowls.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Finnish Salmon Soup (Lohikeitto)

lines.text: 1 large leek, white part only, finely chopped
5 medium potatoes, scrubbed and cut into 1/2-inch cubes
450 g (15.8 oz) salmon fillets, skinned and cut into 1-inch cubes
1 bunch fresh dill, roughly chopped (about 75 g)

instructions: Melt the butter in a large heavy pot over medium heat and soften the chopped leek for 7 to 8 minutes without browning it.
Add the carrot and potato cubes, pour in the fish stock and 2 cups of water, and bring to a simmer.
Cook, partly covered, for about 10 minutes until the potatoes are almost fork-tender.
Stir in the cream and slip in the salmon cubes. Simmer gently for 3 to 4 minutes until the fish is just cooked through.
Fold in the chopped dill and a little black pepper and simmer one more minute.
Ladle into bowls and add a splash of lemon juice if you like.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Adai Dosa

lines.text: 2 tablespoons ghee, for roasting the dosas

instructions: Rinse the rice and all four dals with the fennel, cumin and dried chillies, then soak in plenty of water for 4 hours and drain.
Grind in batches with the ginger, salt and a little water to a coarse paste, then pour into a large bowl and adjust the thickness.
Rest the batter for 2 hours.
Take the amount of batter you need and stir in the chopped onion.
Heat a dosa pan, pour a ladle of batter and spread it gently into a slightly thick round.
Spoon ghee over the top, roast on medium heat until golden underneath, then flip and cook through.
Serve the dosas hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Greek Fasolakia (Braised Green Beans in Tomato Sauce)

lines.text: 3 medium Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into wedges

instructions: Warm the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 8 to 10 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the pureed tomatoes, potato wedges, green beans, salt, pepper, red pepper flakes, dill and 1 1/2 cups of water.
Bring to a boil, lower the heat and simmer covered for about 30 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the beans nearly done.
Uncover, raise the heat to medium and cook 15 to 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens and clings to the vegetables.
Taste, adjust the seasoning, stir in the parsley and let it rest 10 minutes before serving warm.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Pasta con le Sarde

lines.text: 1 can (4.25 oz) sardines in oil, drained
3 slices dried bread, pulsed to breadcrumbs

instructions: Pulse the dried bread to crumbs. Toast the pine nuts in a dry skillet until browned and set aside, then toast the crumbs in a little of the oil until golden.
In a large saute pan, soften the sliced onion, fennel and garlic in the remaining oil over medium heat for about 5 minutes.
Add the anchovy fillets and stir until they melt into the oil, then lower the heat and fry the tomato paste for 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine, add the saffron and let the sauce simmer gently on low heat.
Meanwhile boil the spaghetti in unsalted water until just short of al dente, saving 1/2 cup of the pasta water.
Add the sardines to the sauce for the last 3 minutes, then toss in the drained pasta, loosening with pasta water if needed.
Serve topped with the toasted pine nuts and breadcrumbs.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Turkish Haricot Bean Casserole (Etsiz Kuru Fasulye)

lines.text: 700 g pre-soaked dry haricot beans (soaked overnight)

instructions: Boil the pre-soaked beans in plenty of water for about 40 minutes until a knife goes through but they still hold some firmness, then drain.
Soften the onion and garlic in the olive oil, add the chopped cayenne pepper, then the carrot and celery.
Stir in the tomato puree and crumbled stock cube and cook a few minutes more.
Add the drained beans, pour in 2 litres of boiling water with the lemon juice and the salt, cover and cook for about 45 minutes.
Add the diced potatoes and cook 30 minutes more until tender.
Serve hot with an onion salad and Turkish bread.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Lahanorizo: Greek Cabbage with Rice
instructions: Cook the onion and leek in the olive oil over medium heat for about 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the grated garlic until fragrant, then add the pureed tomatoes.
Add the carrot and chopped cabbage with a little pepper and cook for about 15 minutes until the cabbage wilts.
Stir in the rice, the salt and 1 cup of water. Bring to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes.
Fluff the rice with a fork, fold in the lemon juice and chopped parsley, and scatter the toasted almonds on top if you like.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Soy Milk Hot Pot with Chicken

lines.text: 200 g chicken thigh fillets, cut into large bite-size pieces
300 g Chinese cabbage, cut into 3 cm strips
70 g green onion, cut into pieces

instructions: Cut the chicken into large bite-size pieces. Slice the cabbage into 3 cm strips and the carrot into thin planks. Trim the shiitake and shimeji and cut the green onion, tofu and aburaage.
Bring the dashi, mirin and soy sauce to a boil in a wide pot.
Add the chicken, carrot and cabbage stems, cover and simmer for about 5 minutes.
Add the cabbage leaves, mushrooms, tofu and aburaage and simmer for 5 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Pour in the soy milk, add the green onion and warm over gentle heat for 2 minutes without boiling hard.
Ladle into bowls with the hot soy milk broth.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: White Bean Chile Relleno

lines.text: 2 tablespoons olive oil (1 to brush the peppers, 1 for the filling)
3 cloves garlic (2 minced for the filling, 1 for the cream)

instructions: Cover the cashews with hot water and leave them to soak while you prepare the peppers.
Brush the poblanos with oil and broil on high for 2 to 3 minutes per side until blistered. Cover them for a few minutes, then set the oven to 400 F.
Soften the onion and minced garlic in oil, then add the beans, corn, ¼ cup enchilada sauce and spinach and cook for 4 to 5 minutes.
Blend the drained cashews with ¾ cup water and 1 garlic clove until smooth, and stir about ⅓ cup into the filling.
Peel the skins off the peppers, slit them and remove the seeds. Spread ¼ cup sauce in a baking dish and stuff the peppers.
Pour ½ cup sauce over the peppers, drizzle with cashew cream and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until bubbling.
