license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Salmon Hot Pot

lines.text: 200 g salmon fillet, cut into large bite-size pieces
10 x 10 cm piece dried kombu, cut into 4 strips

instructions: Slice the potato, daikon and carrot. Rinse the shirataki with boiling water, halve the shiitake, trim the chrysanthemum leaves and cut the scallions.
Soften the miso with the mirin in a large pot, then stir in the dashi and add the kombu strips.
Bring to a boil, add the potato, daikon and carrot and cook for a few minutes.
Add the salmon and cook for about a minute.
Add the shirataki, shiitake, chrysanthemum leaves and scallions and cook until the shiitake are done.
Serve in small bowls with the miso broth.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: White Beans with Farro, Kale and Tomatoes

lines.text: 1 cup canned white beans, rinsed and drained
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper

instructions: Put the farro and low-sodium broth in a medium pot and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat and simmer for about 30 minutes until the farro is soft and chewy.
Stir in the drained white beans, halved tomatoes, baby kale and tomato sauce.
Add the Parmesan and heat for a few minutes until the kale wilts and everything is hot.
Season with black pepper and serve in bowls.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Greek Chickpea Soup (Revithosoupa)

lines.text: 14 oz (400 g) dry chickpeas, soaked overnight

instructions: Soak the dry chickpeas in plenty of water overnight, then drain.
Soften the onion, carrot, celery and potato in the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the grated garlic for 30 seconds, then add the chickpeas, bay leaves, oregano, salt and 8 cups of water and bring to a boil.
Reduce to low and skim off the foam that rises in the first 20 to 30 minutes.
Cover and simmer for 1 1/2 to 2 hours until the chickpeas are tender.
Mash a few chickpeas and potato against the pot to thicken the soup, then stir in the lemon juice and parsley and adjust the salt.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chicken Youvetsi with Orzo

lines.text: 2 pounds (900 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs
1 1/2 quarts (1.4 L) low-sodium chicken broth, kept hot
1 pound (454 g) uncooked whole wheat orzo

instructions: Heat the oven to 400 F (200 C) and keep the low-sodium chicken broth hot in a saucepan.
Soften the chopped onion in the olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven for 5 to 6 minutes, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken, crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, cinnamon stick, oregano and salt, stir well and cook uncovered for 20 minutes.
Move everything to a large roasting pan, stir in the whole wheat orzo and pour the hot broth over it, spreading it evenly.
Bake uncovered for 30 minutes.
Let the pan rest for 10 minutes while the orzo absorbs the liquid, then sprinkle with parsley and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chikuzenni (Simmered Chicken and Vegetables)

lines.text: 3/4 lb (340 g) boneless, skinless chicken thighs

instructions: Soak the dried shiitake in 1 cup of water for 20 to 30 minutes, squeeze them out, cut off the stems and slice the caps. Keep the soaking liquid.
Cut the chicken into slanted 1 1/2-inch pieces. Peel and halve the taro, then slice the carrot, lotus root and burdock, soaking the lotus root and burdock in water for 15 minutes.
Brown the chicken in 1 Tbsp of the sesame oil in a large pot until it turns white, then set it aside.
Add the remaining sesame oil, then stir the shiitake, taro, burdock, lotus root and carrot in the pot until coated.
Pour in the dashi and the strained shiitake liquid, bring to a simmer and skim off any scum. Stir in the mirin, soy sauce and sugar and return the chicken.
Cover with a drop lid and simmer for 10 minutes, then remove the lid and cook 10 more minutes until the taro and lotus root are tender.
Take the pot off the heat, cover it and let it cool for 10 minutes so the vegetables absorb the sauce.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Amaranth Porridge with Roasted Pears

lines.text: 1 cup plain 0% Greek yogurt, for serving

instructions: Heat the oven to 400 F (200 C). Rinse and drain the amaranth, then combine it with the milk, water and salt in a pot and bring to a boil.
Turn the heat to low, cover and simmer for 25 minutes until the amaranth is soft with a little liquid left, then let it sit 5 to 10 minutes to thicken.
Toss the pecans with 1 teaspoon of the maple syrup and roast for 10 to 15 minutes until toasted.
Dice the pear, toss it with the remaining maple syrup, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg and clove, and roast it alongside the pecans for 15 minutes until tender.
Stir three quarters of the roasted pears into the porridge, then spoon it over the yogurt and top with the remaining pear and the pecans.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Ground Turkey Sweet Potato Skillet

lines.text: 2 cups peeled and diced sweet potatoes
1/2 cup jarred salsa — use Pace Chunky Salsa Mild (US)

instructions: Microwave the diced sweet potatoes in a covered bowl with 1 tablespoon of water for 4 minutes, stir, then microwave 3 to 4 minutes more until tender.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the turkey and onion, crumbling the meat, until cooked through.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, sweet potato, corn, green chiles and half the cilantro.
Add the salsa and cook 2 to 3 minutes until warmed through, then squeeze in the lime juice.
Garnish with the remaining cilantro and serve right away.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Spanish Lentil and Cod Stew

lines.text: 2 carrots, peeled and cut into small pieces
1 cup dried green lentils (130 g), rinsed
1 cup vegetable broth plus 3 cups water
1/4 teaspoon sea salt and black pepper

instructions: Chop the onion, 4 cloves of garlic, the pepper and the carrots, grate the tomatoes and rinse the lentils.
Warm 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a stock pot and saute the onion, garlic, pepper and carrots for 3 to 4 minutes, then stir in the paprika and the grated tomato and let it thicken a little.
Add the lentils, broth and water, bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low for about 20 minutes until the lentils are tender.
Meanwhile pound the remaining 2 cloves of garlic with the parsley and the salt into a paste and stir in 1 tablespoon of oil.
Pat the cod dry, rub it with the last tablespoon of oil and some pepper, and sear it in a hot nonstick pan for about 3 minutes on each side, then rest it under foil.
Ladle the stew into shallow bowls, set a cod fillet on each and spoon the garlic and parsley sauce over the top.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Barley, Kale and Butternut Squash Risotto

lines.text: 1 medium bunch kale (about 1 pound), stemmed and coarsely chopped

instructions: Simmer the pearled barley in a large pot of salted water until it is about halfway cooked, tender outside and still hard in the center, then drain well.
Warm the broth in a saucepan and keep it at a bare simmer on low heat.
Heat the olive oil in a Dutch oven, cook the onion with a little hot broth until the liquid reduces away, then add the carrot and celery and cook until slightly soft.
Stir in the drained barley, let it dry for a minute, pour in the wine and simmer until it is absorbed.
Add enough broth to just cover the barley, stir in the kale and butternut squash and simmer until the first broth is absorbed.
Keep adding broth to cover and simmering until the barley is creamy and the vegetables are tender, then take the pot off the heat, stir in the butter and Grana Padano, and season to taste.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegetarian Yemista

lines.text: 3 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces

instructions: Heat the oven to 375 F. Cut the tops off the peppers and tomatoes and keep them, seed the peppers, and scoop the flesh out of the tomatoes into a bowl.
Finely chop the onion, garlic and zucchini, and blend the tomato flesh with 1 tablespoon of the tomato paste until smooth.
Soften the onion and garlic in the olive oil, add the zucchini and salt, then stir in the rice for a few minutes and pour in the blended tomato.
Off the heat, stir the parsley and mint into the filling, then pack it into the peppers and tomatoes and set the tops back on.
Stand the vegetables in a large baking dish with the potatoes between them, then pour in the rest of the tomato paste stirred into 3 cups of water.
Bake uncovered for about 90 minutes, checking the rice and adding 15-minute rounds until it is tender, then serve hot or at room temperature.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Revithada: Baked Chickpea Stew

lines.text: 1 pound (500 g) dried chickpeas, soaked in water overnight

instructions: Cover the chickpeas with plenty of cold water and soak them overnight, or for 6 to 8 hours.
Heat the oven to 375 F (190 C). Drain the chickpeas, cover them with water by 2 inches, add the bay leaves and boil until tender.
Toss the onion and carrot with the olive oil in a 9 by 13-inch baking dish and bake until soft and golden.
Stir in the garlic, pureed tomatoes, oregano, sugar, pepper and a pinch of the salt, and roast until the sauce thickens.
Drain the chickpeas, fold them into the sauce with the rest of the salt and 2 cups of water, and taste for seasoning.
Bake uncovered until the sauce is rich and thick, then top with the crumbled feta and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Bruinebonensoep

lines.text: 1 kg lean stewing beef, trimmed and cubed
500 g canned red kidney beans, drained

instructions: Put the beef, onions, garlic, ginger, lime leaves and 3 liters of water in a large pot, bring to a boil and skim any foam.
Lower the heat and simmer, partly covered, until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the potatoes and carrots and simmer until they begin to soften.
Stir in the drained red kidney beans, tomatoes, white pepper and salt and simmer until the vegetables are tender.
Add the spring onions, taste for seasoning and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Baked Cod with Tomatoes and Chickpeas

lines.text: 1 pint cherry or grape tomatoes, halved
1 1/2 pounds cod, cut into serving-sized pieces

instructions: Heat the oven to 400 F. Soften the shallots in the olive oil in an ovenproof skillet, then add the garlic for 30 seconds without browning.
Add the tomatoes and sugar and cook 3 to 4 minutes, pressing the tomatoes as they burst into a chunky sauce.
Stir in the chickpeas, capers, vinegar and thyme, then take the pan off the heat.
Nestle the cod into the sauce, folding any thin pieces in half, and dust the fish with paprika.
Bake about 15 minutes until the cod flakes easily, then serve straight from the pan.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Mediterranean Bulgur Salad

lines.text: 1 small English cucumber, seeded and diced

instructions: Cover the bulgur with 1 1/4 cups boiling water in a bowl, seal the bowl and leave 15 to 30 minutes until the water is absorbed, then cool and fluff.
Soak the diced red onion in cold water for 10 minutes to soften its bite, then drain.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, cumin and sugar together in a large bowl.
Add the bulgur, onion, red pepper, cucumber, dill, parsley and chickpeas and toss well.
Chill until ready to serve; it keeps up to two days.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Japanese Fried Rice with Edamame, Tofu and Hijiki
instructions: Spread the cooked brown rice on a lined tray to cool and let the steam escape.
Soak the hijiki in 1 cup of water for 20 minutes, then drain.
Blanch the aburaage in boiling water to remove excess oil, cool it, squeeze out the water and cut it into thin strips. Cut the carrot into matchsticks.
Heat the sesame oil in a large frying pan and saute the hijiki, aburaage and carrot until coated.
Add the sake, sugar and mirin, then the soy sauce, and stir to combine.
Add the edamame and cooled rice, breaking up any clumps, and stir until every grain is coated and heated through.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Steak Bowls

lines.text: 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil in total
Zest and juice of 2 limes plus 1 tablespoon juice
1 (15-ounce) can reduced sodium black beans, rinsed and drained
1 pint cherry or grape tomatoes, quartered
1/3 cup plus 1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro

instructions: Heat the oven to 425 F. Coat the sirloin steaks with 1 tbsp olive oil, lime zest and juice, chipotle powder and cumin and let them marinate 15 minutes.
Rinse the brown rice and cook it in water until tender, then stir in lime zest, lime juice and half the cilantro while it is still warm.
Sear the steaks in a hot oven-safe skillet with 1 tbsp olive oil, 2 to 3 minutes a side, then bake 5 to 7 minutes until medium-rare to medium.
Rest the steaks 10 minutes while you toss the black beans, corn, tomatoes, avocado, feta and remaining cilantro with 1 tbsp olive oil and a squeeze of lime.
Slice the steak thinly and serve over the lime rice with the salsa beside it.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Roasted Chicken with Okra: Kota me Bamies

lines.text: 1 whole chicken (4-5 pounds), cut up (about 1.24 kg edible meat and skin)
2 pounds fresh or frozen baby okra

instructions: Heat the oven to 375 F. Soak the okra in cold water with a splash of vinegar for 30 minutes, then pat dry and snip off the tops.
Pan-fry the okra in some of the olive oil until some pieces are golden but not cooked through, and move it to a large baking pan.
Brown the chicken pieces 3 to 4 minutes a side in the same pan and set them in or around the okra.
Soften the sliced onions in the pan, add the garlic for a few seconds, then add the crushed tomatoes and a cup of water and bring to a boil.
Pour the onions and sauce over the okra and chicken, season with red pepper flakes and mix to coat everything.
Roast on the center rack for 1 hour 15 minutes, then sprinkle with oregano and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Mediterranean Fish en Papillote

lines.text: 1 1/2 cups cooked no-salt-added white beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat the oven to 375 F. Let the cod sit uncovered at room temperature while you prepare the topping.
Toss the beans, olives, artichokes, tomatoes, lemon zest and juice and olive oil in a bowl.
Cut four large sheets of parchment, each about twice as long as a fillet.
Set a fillet in the center of each sheet, spoon a heaping 3/4 cup of the bean mixture over it, and fold the parchment shut tightly so no steam escapes.
Place the parcels in a baking dish and bake about 30 minutes, until the fish is cooked through.
Open each parcel and top with the chopped parsley and dill.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Bulgur Pilaf
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large stockpot over medium heat, add the onion and cook 5 to 7 minutes until soft and translucent.
Stir in the tomato paste and chopped green pepper and cook 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add the bulgur, cumin, salt and black pepper and stir 2 to 3 minutes until every grain is coated in the paste.
Lay the chickpeas on top, pour in the hot chicken broth and stir once to combine.
Take the pot off the heat, close the lid and let the bulgur absorb the liquid for 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and serve with the parsley.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Savory Teff Crepes with Miso Squash Filling

lines.text: 2 tablespoons avocado oil plus a little for greasing the pan
4 cups butternut squash, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch cubes
1/4 cup chickpea miso paste — use Miso Master Organic Chickpea Miso

instructions: Blend the teff flour, flaxseed meal and 1 1/2 cups of water until smooth, thick and pourable, and set the batter aside.
Heat the oven to 400 F. Toss the squash, red cabbage and onion with half of the miso, oil and water mixture on lined baking sheets.
Roast 25 to 30 minutes until the vegetables are tender with golden edges. Toss the kale in half of the remaining miso mixture.

Meanwhile, grease a skillet over medium heat and pour in 1/4 to 1/3 cup of batter, swirling to coat. Cook 3 minutes until the edges lift, flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more. Repeat with the rest of the batter.
Add the kale to the roasting vegetables and cook 3 to 5 minutes until wilted.
Fill half of each crepe with the vegetables, fold, and drizzle with the reserved miso mixture.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Arakas Laderos: Greek Peas and Potato Stew
instructions: Cook the chopped onion in the olive oil in a pot over medium heat until soft and golden.
Stir in the garlic, then add the potatoes, carrots, tomato puree, 1 cup of water, the salt and the red pepper flakes.
Bring to a boil, lower the heat to medium, add the peas and cook 25 to 30 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Taste the sauce and adjust the seasoning, then stir in the dill and mint.
Let the stew sit at least 45 minutes before serving so the flavors come together and the potatoes thicken the sauce.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Veg Thukpa

lines.text: 2 tablespoons oil (1 tablespoon for the noodles, 1 for the soup)
1 cup julienned red, green and yellow bell pepper (1/3 cup each)

instructions: Boil the whole wheat noodles in salt-free water until soft, drain well, and toss with 1 tablespoon of the oil so they stay loose.
Heat the remaining oil in a wok, then cook the ginger and garlic over high heat for a few minutes.
Add the sliced onion and cook until translucent, then add the tomato and cook for a minute.
Pour in 1 litre of hot water and bring to a boil. Add the carrots, bell peppers, mushrooms, cabbage and soy sauce.
Cook only 2 to 3 minutes so the vegetables stay crunchy, then stir in the spring onion greens.
Put the noodles in bowls and ladle the hot soup and vegetables over them.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Tsukune (Japanese Chicken Meatball Skewers)

lines.text: 5 cups cooked brown rice, for serving

instructions: Soak 8 bamboo skewers in water for 30 minutes. Simmer the reduced-salt soy sauce, mirin, brown sugar and 2 tablespoons of water in a small pan until reduced by about half and syrupy.
Cook one third of the ground chicken in a dry pan over medium heat without browning, breaking it up until no longer pink. Tip it into a bowl and let it cool fully.
Add the raw chicken, miso, sesame oil and sliced scallions to the cooled chicken. Knead by hand, about 30 turns each direction, until pale and sticky.
Divide into 8 portions, oil your hands lightly and shape each into a long oval patty around the top of a skewer, sealing the edges.
Broil on a rack over a foil-lined tray about 8 inches from the heat for 6 minutes, flip and broil 4 minutes more until the chicken reaches 165 F (74 C).
Brush with the glaze and broil 45 to 60 seconds a side until sizzling. Serve 2 skewers per person over the brown rice with extra glaze.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Crockpot BBQ Chicken
instructions: Whisk the tomato sauce, tomato paste, cider vinegar, maple syrup, molasses, Worcestershire, smoked paprika and garlic powder in a saucepan and simmer 10 to 15 minutes until thickened.
Lay the chicken in a single layer in a lightly oiled slow cooker and spoon about three quarters of the sauce over the top, keeping the rest for serving.
Cover and cook on low for 4 to 5 hours, until the chicken reaches 165 F (74 C).
Move the chicken to a board and shred it with two forks.
Stir the cornstarch with 1 tablespoon of water, add it to the sauce in the cooker, cover and cook on high until thickened, about 30 minutes.
Return the shredded chicken to the sauce, toss to coat and serve on the whole wheat buns with the extra sauce.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Goan Fish Curry

lines.text: 600 g firm white fish (cod), cut into cubes
3 cups cooked brown basmati rice, for serving

instructions: Blend half the red onion with the garlic, ginger, tamarind, chilli powder, coriander, cumin, turmeric and 6 tablespoons of water into a smooth paste.
Cook the remaining sliced onion in a dry non-stick pot over medium heat for 3 minutes until the edges turn golden.
Add the spice paste and cook 3 minutes, stirring, until the water cooks off and the spices smell toasted.
Stir in the tomato paste, then add the coconut milk and 2/3 cup of water and bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens.
Add the cod, stir gently and cook 3 to 4 minutes until the fish flakes easily. Serve over the brown basmati rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Diri Kole Ak Pwa Rouj

lines.text: 2 cups dry large red kidney beans

instructions: Rinse the red kidney beans, cover with 8 cups of water in a large pot and simmer until tender. Drain, keeping 3 1/2 cups of the liquid.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clearer.
Warm the olive oil in a pot over medium-high heat and cook the onion and garlic about 1 minute.
Stir in the drained beans for 1 to 2 minutes, then the rice, garlic powder, black pepper and salt.
Pour in the reserved bean liquid, tuck in the thyme and parsley, stir twice and lower the heat to medium-low with the lid half on until the liquid is absorbed.
Cover fully on low until the rice is cooked, then fluff with a fork and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chicken Kapama: Greek-Braised Cinnamon Chicken

lines.text: 1 chicken, 3-4 pounds, cut into about 10 pieces
1 pound whole wheat pasta, cooked al dente
1/4 cup grated Parmesan or Kefalotyri cheese

instructions: Cut the chicken into about 10 pieces, pat dry and season both sides with the ground cinnamon and black pepper.
Brown the chicken in the olive oil in a large pot in 2 or 3 batches, about 4 minutes a side, then set it aside.
Lower the heat and cook the onion about 10 minutes until very soft, then stir in the garlic for a minute.
Return the chicken and its juices to the pot with the pureed tomatoes, tomato paste, cinnamon sticks and oregano and bring to a boil.
Reduce to a simmer, cover and cook 1 hour, then uncover and cook on medium for 30 minutes more until the sauce thickens.
Cook the whole wheat pasta al dente while the sauce thickens. Serve the chicken and sauce over the pasta with the parsley and cheese.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Artichoke and Fava Bean Stew with Lemon Sauce

lines.text: 2 pounds fresh fava beans in the pod, shelled (about 2 cups, 225 g beans)
Juice of 2 lemons and the finely grated zest of 1 lemon

instructions: Warm the olive oil in a wide pot over medium heat, add the scallions, leek, fennel and garlic, coat them in the oil, then lower the heat and cook covered for 5 minutes.
Add the shelled fava beans, pour in water to cover them by 1 inch, bring to a boil, then simmer over medium-low heat for 10 minutes.
Stand the artichoke hearts top-down in the pot, add water to come about halfway up them, cover and simmer on low until very tender, about 15 minutes.
Whisk the flour into the lemon juice, then whisk in a ladleful of the pan juices in a slow stream and pour the mixture into the pot, tilting the pot to spread it.
Add the lemon zest and dill, simmer 3 to 4 minutes until the sauce thickens, and serve warm.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Spice-Rubbed Grilled Salmon with Black Beans and Corn Salsa

lines.text: 4 wild Alaskan salmon fillets, 6 ounces each
1 lime for the rub plus 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice for the salsa
1 can (15.5 ounces) low-sodium black beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Mix the smoked paprika, cumin, chipotle powder, brown sugar and pepper, squeeze 1 lime over the salmon, rub the spices over every side and let it rest for 5 minutes.
Warm the olive oil in a large pan over medium heat, cook the red onion for 2 minutes, then add the beans and corn and heat through for 6 to 8 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the cilantro and the 2 tablespoons of lime juice.
Heat a lightly oiled grill or grill pan over high heat, then grill the salmon covered for 8 to 10 minutes until opaque throughout.
Serve each fillet over a spoonful of the black bean and corn salsa with lime wedges.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Curried Lentils (Dhal) and Kale Mallung

lines.text: 2 onions, chopped (1 for the dhal, 1 for the mallung)
2 tablespoons chopped garlic (1 for each dish)
6 tablespoons coconut oil (3 for the dhal, 3 for the mallung)
2 1/2 teaspoons roasted ground cumin, split between the two dishes
2 1/2 teaspoons ground coriander, split between the two dishes

instructions: Heat a dry pan and toast the mustard seeds until they pop.
Add 3 tablespoons of the coconut oil, the curry leaves, half the onion and half the garlic, and brown for about 2 minutes, then toss in the turmeric and half the cumin and coriander for 1 minute.
Add the red lentils, coconut milk and 2 to 3 cups of water and cook 7 to 10 minutes, removing the pan before the lentils turn mushy.
For the mallung, heat the remaining oil in a wok, add the remaining onion, garlic, cumin and coriander and toss for about 2 minutes.
Add the chopped kale and the shredded coconut and toss until the kale wilts slightly.
Serve the dhal with the mallung, warm or cold.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Buddha's Delight

lines.text: 10 g (2 tablespoons) dried wood ear mushrooms
40 g (1 small bundle) mung bean vermicelli noodles
10 pieces deep fried tofu puffs, halved

instructions: Cover the dried lily flowers, shiitake and wood ear mushrooms in separate bowls of boiling water and soak 20 minutes, trim any tough lily flower ends, slice the shiitake, cut the wood ear small, and keep 1 cup of the soaking water.
Soak the vermicelli in boiling water for 3 to 5 minutes until al dente, then drain.
Heat the peanut oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and stir the green onions until fragrant, then cook the carrot, lily flowers, shiitake and wood ear for 2 minutes.
Add the tofu puffs, soy sauce, reserved soaking water, napa cabbage and bok choy, cover and cook on medium heat 3 to 5 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the vermicelli and sesame oil and cook 1 minute more, then serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Acorn Squash with Chickpeas and Chimichurri

lines.text: 2 acorn squashes, seeded and quartered lengthwise
1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, for the squash, chimichurri, chickpeas and yogurt
1 small garlic clove for the chimichurri and 2 garlic cloves for the chickpeas, minced
1/2 cup finely chopped cilantro for the chimichurri plus 1/4 cup for the chickpeas
2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice for the chimichurri, 2 teaspoons for the chickpeas and 1 teaspoon for the yogurt
1 can (14 ounces) chickpeas, drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat the oven to 450 degrees F, drizzle the squash quarters with olive oil and roast them cut side up for 35 to 40 minutes until tender and browned at the edges.
Grind the pepitas fine in a food processor, then stir in the red pepper flakes, the small garlic clove, half a cup of cilantro, lemon juice, olive oil and a few grinds of pepper.
Cook the onion in olive oil over medium heat until soft and browned, then lower the heat and stir in the 2 garlic cloves, cumin and chickpeas.
Pour in the broth and simmer the chickpeas for 5 minutes, take them off the heat, stir in lemon juice and the remaining cilantro and let them thicken a few minutes.
Stir the yogurt with lemon juice and a little olive oil.
Set the squash on a platter, top with the chickpeas and the chimichurri, and spoon the lemon yogurt over.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Dango-jiru

lines.text: 120 g skinless chicken thigh, cut into bite-size pieces
70 g shimeji mushrooms (or shiitake or maitake)
20 g niboshi (dried baby sardines), heads and guts removed

instructions: Knead the flour with 60 ml of water into a smooth dough, wrap it and rest it for 30 minutes.
Simmer the niboshi in 700 ml of water for about 5 minutes, then lift the niboshi out and keep the dashi.
Add the chicken, daikon, carrot and taro to the dashi and simmer, skimming off any foam, until the roots start to soften.
Add the mushrooms and napa cabbage, then pinch off flat pieces of dough and drop them in. Simmer until the dumplings float and are cooked through.
Stir in the miso until dissolved, add the green onion and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Eggs in Purgatory

lines.text: 1 can (15 ounces) reduced-sodium chickpeas, rinsed and drained
2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil, to finish

instructions: Heat the oven to 375 F. Cook the onion in the olive oil in a large ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat until translucent, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the chickpeas, crushed tomatoes, oregano and red pepper flakes and simmer until slightly thickened.
Stir in the spinach a handful at a time and let it wilt.
Make 4 wells in the sauce with the back of a spoon, crack an egg into each and scatter the Parmesan over the top.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks are still soft, then top with basil.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Pasta e Ceci

lines.text: 1 can (15 ounces) reduced-sodium chickpeas, with their liquid
2 tablespoons olive oil, plus a drizzle to serve
1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, for serving
2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil, for serving

instructions: Drain the chickpeas over a measuring cup and add water to their liquid until you have 2 cups.
Heat the olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat, add the chickpeas and cook, stirring, until they start to pop.
Add the black pepper and garlic for 30 seconds, then stir in the crushed tomatoes and the chickpea liquid and bring to a simmer.
Add the ditalini, lower the heat and simmer gently, stirring often, until the pasta is al dente and most of the liquid is absorbed.
Ladle into bowls and top with Parmesan, basil and a drizzle of olive oil.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Nepali Dal Bhat

lines.text: 2 cups cooked white rice, to serve

instructions: Cook the onion in the oil in a large frying pan until translucent but not browned.
Turn the heat low and stir in the garlic, ginger, crushed coriander seed, chili powder and turmeric for about 3 minutes.
Add the washed red lentils and stir to coat them in the onion mixture.
Pour in 3 cups of water, bring to a boil, add the salt and simmer about 15 minutes until the lentils are tender.
Stir in the cilantro, take the dal off the heat and serve over steamed rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Rapini and Cannellini Bean Pasta

lines.text: 1 can (15 oz) cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Boil the whole wheat spaghetti in a large pot of salted water until just short of al dente, and keep a mug of the pasta water.
Warm the olive oil and butter in a large frying pan, add the garlic and beans, and saute until the beans soften and brown.
Mash about half the beans with a fork or wooden spoon so the sauce turns creamy.
Add a ladle of pasta water and the chopped rapini, and cook until the greens wilt down; squeeze in the lemon juice.
Move the spaghetti into the pan with another ladle of pasta water and toss until glossy, adding more water if it looks dry.
Off the heat, toss in the Parmigiano-Reggiano a handful at a time and serve right away.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chicken with Mixed Vegetables

lines.text: 12 oz boneless skinless chicken breast, sliced
3 tbsp plus 1 tsp neutral oil, divided
4 cups cooked brown rice, to serve

instructions: Toss the sliced chicken with a spoonful of cornstarch, some of the oil and 2 teaspoons of the oyster sauce, and set it aside.
Stir the broth, the rest of the oyster sauce, the low-sodium soy sauce and the sesame oil together in a bowl.
Blanch the broccoli and carrots in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain.
Stir-fry the chicken in a hot wok with part of the oil until it turns opaque, and move it to a plate.
Stir-fry the mushrooms and red pepper in the remaining oil for 30 seconds, then pour in the sauce and simmer for 1 minute.
Stir the remaining cornstarch with 2 tablespoons water, drizzle it in and simmer 30 seconds until the sauce thickens.
Return the chicken and blanched vegetables to the wok, toss to coat and serve over brown rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Cowboy Chicken

lines.text: 3 medium boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 1 1/2 lb)
1 can (15 oz) reduced-sodium black beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Heat the oven to 375 F. Pound the chicken to an even thickness and pat it dry.
Mix the smoked paprika, cumin and garlic powder, and rub half of it over the chicken.
Sear the chicken in an oven-safe skillet with the olive oil, about 3 minutes on the first side and 30 seconds on the second, then move it to a plate.
Add the diced tomatoes to the skillet and scrape up the browned bits. Stir in the black beans, corn, green chiles and the rest of the spice mix.
Nestle the chicken back in, spoon sauce over it and bake until it reaches 160 F, 7 to 10 minutes.
Sprinkle the Monterey Jack on top and broil 1 to 2 minutes until melted, then finish with lime juice and cilantro.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Whole Roasted Fish with White Wine, Tomatoes and Fennel

lines.text: 800 g whole sea bass (about 400 g edible meat)

instructions: Heat the oven to 430 F. Crush the garlic and rub the fish with olive oil, pepper flakes and rosemary, tucking some garlic and rosemary into the belly.
Toss the fennel batons with olive oil on a foil-lined tray, and set the fish on top so it does not touch the tray.
Roast the fish for about 10 minutes, flip it, and roast about 10 minutes more, until cooked through.
For the salsa, brown the sliced onion in olive oil in a hot pan, then add the halved cherry tomatoes and cook until they color.
Pour in the white wine and reduce it over high heat until the tomatoes turn saucy, then cool slightly.
Stir the lemon juice and chopped parsley into the salsa. Spoon it onto plates, then top with the fennel and the fish.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Buckwheat Cabbage Rolls with Mushrooms

lines.text: 3 medium heads of cabbage (about 1.8 kg of leaves used)

instructions: Cook the buckwheat in water until the grains are tender and the water is absorbed.
Core the cabbage heads, boil them until the leaves loosen, then peel off the leaves and shave down the thick center ribs.
Saute the chopped onions, grated carrots and sliced mushrooms in the oil until soft, then stir in the garlic powder, coriander and smoked paprika.
Mix the cooked buckwheat with the vegetables and chopped dill to make the filling.
Roll a spoonful of filling in each cabbage leaf, folding in the sides, and pack the rolls into a pot with the allspice berries and a little water.
Simmer the rolls covered until the cabbage is tender, then stir the sour cream with chopped dill into a sauce and spoon it over the rolls.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Doenjang Jjigae

lines.text: 3 ounces lean pork loin, thinly sliced
2 ounces Korean radish, cut into thin small squares
1 green or red chili pepper, sliced
2 cups cooked brown rice, for serving

instructions: Cut the tofu and zucchini into 1-inch cubes, cut the radish into thin small squares, slice the onion and chili, chop the scallion and slice the pork into thin strips.
Heat the oil in a small pot over medium heat and saute the pork, doenjang and gochugaru for 3 to 4 minutes.
Pour in 2 cups of water, stir to dissolve the doenjang and add the radish. Boil over medium-high heat for 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the onion, garlic, tofu, zucchini and chili and boil for 5 to 6 minutes more.
Stir in the scallion and serve while still bubbling, over the brown rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Pasta alla Norma

lines.text: 1/4 cup fresh basil leaves, for garnish

instructions: Heat the oven to 425 F and line two baking sheets with parchment. Crush the canned tomatoes with their juices in a bowl by hand.
Cut the eggplants into half-moons, divide between the sheets, toss with 3 tablespoons of the olive oil and the salt, and roast 25 to 35 minutes until tender and browned.
Boil the rigatoni in a large pot of water until al dente, saving a cup of the pasta water.

Warm the remaining oil in a large skillet, sizzle the garlic, oregano and red pepper flakes for 30 seconds, then stir in the tomato paste and the crushed tomatoes. Simmer 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Move the pasta into the sauce with a slotted spoon, add the roasted eggplant and the cheese, and toss, adding pasta water as needed until the sauce coats everything.
Serve topped with torn basil.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Shrimp with Lobster Sauce

lines.text: 2 tablespoons cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons water
4 cups cooked brown rice, for serving

instructions: Stir the cornstarch into 2 tablespoons of water until smooth and set the slurry aside.
Heat the oil in a dutch oven or wok over medium-high heat, cook the shrimp until lightly browned, then move them to a plate.
Cook the garlic, ginger and ground pork in the same pan until the pork is almost cooked through.
Pour in the broth and wine and bring to a boil, add the frozen peas and carrots and cook about 2 minutes until thawed, then return the shrimp.
Stir the slurry again, pour it in and simmer until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Take the pan off the heat, drizzle in the beaten egg, let it sit 30 seconds, then stir gently into thin threads. Add the green onion and serve over brown rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Huevos a la Mexicana

lines.text: 2 green onions, chopped, including the green parts

instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and brown the green onions for a minute or two.
Add the chopped tomato and cook a few minutes until somewhat mushy and some of the moisture has cooked off, letting it brown a little.
Stir in the oregano and the sliced jalapeno.
Crack the eggs into the pan, add the salt and stir with a spatula to mix in the sauce and lightly scramble. Take off the heat while still soft.
Warm the corn tortillas, sprinkle the eggs with cilantro and serve with the tortillas.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Sudado de Pollo

lines.text: 8 small potatoes, peeled and cut in half
3 cups cooked brown rice, for serving

instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and saute the onion and red pepper until the onion turns translucent, about 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and garlic and saute for 5 minutes more.
Add the chicken, 3 cups of water, the sazon and the cumin. Cover and cook for 25 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the potatoes and cilantro and cook for another 30 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Serve the chicken, potatoes and sauce over the brown rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Quick Mussels Fra Diavolo

lines.text: 3 lbs live mussels (about 48), scrubbed and debearded
6 slices whole wheat crusty bread, for serving

instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat, then cook the shallot, garlic and crushed red pepper for about 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the white wine and boil until reduced by half, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the marinara sauce and bring to a simmer.
Add the scrubbed mussels, cover and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until the shells open. Throw away any that stay closed.
Move the mussels and sauce to a wide platter or bowls, scatter with parsley and serve with the whole wheat bread.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Tuscan White Bean Tomato Toasts

lines.text: 3 tbsp plus 4 tsp extra virgin olive oil, divided
1 can (15 oz) reduced-sodium cannellini beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Heat the oven to 400 F (200 C). Brush both sides of the bread with 4 teaspoons of the olive oil and toast on a lined baking sheet, flipping once, about 10 minutes.

Warm the remaining olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the shallot, tomatoes, salt and pepper and cook, stirring now and then, until the tomatoes break down and caramelize, 10 to 12 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, red wine vinegar and honey and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the beans and warm them through for 1 to 2 minutes, lightly smashing some if you like a creamier topping.
Spoon the tomato and bean mixture over the toasts and finish with Parmesan and thyme.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Italian Panzanella and White Cannellini Bean Salad

lines.text: 1/2 cup plus 1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, for the tomatoes and the dressing
1 can (15 oz) reduced-sodium cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat the oven to 425 F (220 C). Toss the tomatoes with 1 tablespoon of the olive oil, half of the salt and the pepper and roast on a baking sheet until blistered and juicy, about 25 minutes.
Cut the day-old bread into cubes and the onion into thin slices, and shred the basil.
Whisk the remaining olive oil with the red wine vinegar and the rest of the salt.
Tip the roasted tomatoes and their juices into a large bowl and add the bread, beans and onion.
Pour over the dressing, add the basil and toss. Let the salad sit for 5 minutes so the bread soaks up the juices, then serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Fava Bean Puree and Wild Chicory

lines.text: 400 g dried split peeled fava beans
400 g wild chicory, or any broad leaf greens
4 slices crusty bread, toasted, for serving

instructions: Rinse the split fava beans and soak them in cold water for at least 1 hour.
Drain the beans and put them in a pot with the onion, celery, tomatoes and enough fresh water to cover by about 2 cm (1 in).
Bring to a boil, then simmer, skimming and stirring often and adding water when needed, until the beans fall apart, about 50 minutes. Stir in the salt near the end.
Mash the beans with a wooden spoon or an immersion blender, beat in the olive oil and keep stirring over low heat to a thick puree.
While the puree cooks, boil the chicory in salted water until tender, drain it and squeeze out the extra water.
Spoon the puree onto plates, top with the chicory and serve with the bread.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Shanghai-Style Red Vegetable Soup

lines.text: 2 pounds bone-in beef shank, in place of oxtails
2 large carrots (about 12 ounces), cut into large chunks
1 pound potatoes (about 2 large), peeled and cut into large chunks

instructions: Pat the beef shank dry. Heat the oil in a heavy soup pot over medium heat and brown the beef lightly on both sides.
Slice the onions, add them to the pot with the smashed garlic and cook until the onions soften.
Add the chopped tomatoes, push them aside, fry the tomato paste in the middle for a minute and stir until the tomatoes break down and the oil turns red.
Pour in 10 cups of water, turn the heat to high and add the carrots, cabbage, bay leaves, salt and pepper. Cover, bring to a boil, then simmer for 60 minutes.
Peel and cut the potatoes, add them to the pot, bring back to a boil and simmer 30 more minutes until tender.
Taste, adjust the seasoning and serve; the soup is even better the next day.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Steamed Red Snapper
instructions: Clean the snapper, cut a slash across the thickest part of each side, then stuff the cavity of each fish with half the thyme and one scallion.
Warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat and cook the onion and the rest of the thyme for about 3 minutes.
Stir in the pumpkin, carrot and chayote and cook for 3 minutes, stirring.
Pour in 2 cups of water, bring to a boil, then simmer for about 7 minutes. Add the remaining scallions, garlic and the coconut cream.
Tuck the fish, tomato and okra into the pot, spoon some liquid over the fish, cover and cook for about 10 minutes until the fish is cooked through.
Spoon more of the liquid over each fish before serving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Barbunya Pilaki

lines.text: 350 g (12 oz) dried borlotti beans, soaked overnight
1 medium to large onion, finely chopped
2 medium carrots, quartered and diced small
1/4 cup flat leaf parsley, finely chopped

instructions: Soak the dried beans overnight, then drain and rinse them.
Cover the beans with cold water, bring to a boil, partly cover and simmer for 30 to 35 minutes until tender but not mushy. Drain and rinse.
Warm the olive oil in a pot and cook the chopped onion for 2 to 3 minutes, then add the carrots and cook 2 minutes more.
Stir in the tomatoes, sugar and pepper, then add the beans and 2 cups of water.
Bring to a boil, lower the heat, partly cover and simmer for 30 to 35 minutes until the beans are cooked through but not mushy.
Serve warm or at room temperature with chopped parsley and lemon wedges.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chicken Chop Suey

lines.text: 12 oz boneless skinless chicken breast, sliced
6 oz bok choy, cut into pieces
1 1/2 tablespoons cornstarch plus 2 teaspoons for the chicken
4 cups cooked brown rice, for serving

instructions: Slice the chicken and mix with the cornstarch, a splash of water and half of the oyster sauce, then set aside while you prep.
Stir together the soy sauce, remaining oyster sauce, sesame oil and chicken broth in a bowl. Mix the remaining cornstarch with 2 tablespoons of water for a slurry.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok until very hot, spread the chicken in a single layer and stir-fry until golden and about 80 percent cooked, then remove.
Add the rest of the oil, then the mushrooms and bok choy, and stir-fry for about a minute.
Pour in the sauce, return the chicken, add the bean sprouts and snow peas and bring to a strong simmer.
Stir in the slurry until thickened, about 10 seconds. Serve over the brown rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Peruvian Chicken Stew

lines.text: 4 bone-in skinless chicken thighs (about 520 g meat)

instructions: Brown the chicken thighs in the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat, then set them aside.
Cook the chopped onion and garlic in the same pot until soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, panca pepper paste, cumin, black pepper and bay leaves and cook for a minute or two.
Return the chicken and add 3 cups of water, bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the potatoes and carrot, cover and cook for about 15 minutes until tender.
Stir in the peas and cook for a few minutes more, then remove the bay leaves and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Escarole and Beans

lines.text: 2 heads escarole, base removed, trimmed and washed
4 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, plus 1 whole clove for the beans

instructions: Simmer the cannellini beans in water with the whole garlic clove until tender, then drain and remove the garlic clove.
Cut the escarole into thirds, wash it several times and boil it in a large pot of water for about 10 minutes, stirring now and then. Drain.
Warm the olive oil in a second pot over medium-high heat and cook the sliced garlic and onion for about 3 minutes.
Add the whole peeled tomatoes, squeezing them as you stir, and cook for another 3 minutes.
Add the drained escarole and cook over low heat for about 5 minutes.
Add the beans and the chicken broth, bring to a boil, then simmer for about 7 minutes. Season with black pepper and serve in bowls.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Paksiw na Bangus

lines.text: 3 1/2 lb milkfish, cleaned and sliced crosswise into serving pieces

instructions: Scatter the sliced ginger, crushed garlic, onions and peppercorns across the bottom of a wide pot.
Lay the milkfish slices over the aromatics, then arrange the long green peppers, eggplant and bitter melon on top.
Pour in the vinegar, cover the pot and bring it to a boil. Boil for 2 minutes without stirring.
Add 2 cups of water, let it return to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes until the fish is cooked and the vegetables are tender.
Season with the fish sauce, then transfer to a deep serving plate and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Tavce Gravce

lines.text: 2 to 3 dried Rezha Macedonian peppers (or any dried or fresh sweet pepper)

instructions: Soak the lima beans in plenty of water overnight, then rinse and drain them.
Put the beans in a pot with fresh water, all but two thick slices of the onion, the garlic, the dried peppers and the bay leaves. Simmer on medium heat for 1 to 1 1/2 hours until soft.
Drain the beans. Pull out the onion and garlic and mash them with a fork; set the dried peppers aside.
Warm the olive oil on low heat and fry the paprika in it for 1 to 2 minutes to make a roux.
Move the beans to an earthenware pot and mix in the mashed onion and garlic, the paprika roux, salt, pepper and parsley. Add just enough water to cover the beans.
Lay the dried peppers and the reserved onion slices on top and bake at 200 C (390 F) for 45 to 60 minutes.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Buckwheat Porridge with Fruits

lines.text: 1/2 cup raisins (the dried fruit of your choice)

instructions: Rinse the buckwheat in a fine sieve under hot water.
Put the buckwheat, 2 cups of water, the raisins, cinnamon sticks, cardamom seeds and a pinch of salt in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer gently, stirring now and then, until the water is absorbed and the buckwheat is tender.
Take out the cinnamon sticks and serve the porridge topped with the sliced pears.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Pasta e Cavolfiore alla Siciliana

lines.text: 1 small cauliflower, cut into small pieces
a handful of raisins (about 40 g), soaked in warm water until soft
a handful of pine nuts (about 30 g)
1/2 tsp saffron, dissolved in warm water
1/3 cup dry breadcrumbs, toasted in olive oil

instructions: Cut the cauliflower into small florets and boil in lightly salted water for about 5 minutes until just tender. Lift it out and keep the water.

Saute the onion and garlic in the olive oil until soft, add the anchovy fillets until they melt in, then stir in the drained raisins and the pine nuts, plus the saffron, tomato paste and pepper flakes if using.
Add the cauliflower and a ladle of its cooking water and simmer, breaking the florets up with a spoon, until the liquid has nearly gone.
Cook the bucatini in the cauliflower water until slightly underdone.
Toss the pasta in the pan with another ladle of pasta water until it is al dente and the cauliflower sauce clings to it.
Toast the breadcrumbs gently in a little olive oil until golden and scatter them over each serving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chicknigang

lines.text: 2 lb chicken pieces, cut into serving pieces
1/4 cup tamarind pulp, simmered in the broth

instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and saute the garlic, onion and ginger until the onion softens.
Add the chicken and brown it for 2 minutes on each side.
Pour in about 1 quart (4 cups) of water and bring to a boil.
Add the daikon and tamarind pulp, cover and simmer on low to medium heat for 35 minutes, mashing the tamarind into the broth and discarding any seeds.
Add the tomatoes, okra and string beans and cook for 8 to 12 minutes until tender.
Season with the fish sauce, stir in the spinach for 1 minute and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Pad Pak Ruam
instructions: Cut the carrot, broccoli, cauliflower, mushrooms and baby corn into bite-size pieces and trim the sugar snap peas.
Mix the low-sodium soy sauce, sugar, white pepper and cornstarch with a splash of water to make the sauce.
Heat a wok over high heat, then fry the garlic and the hardest vegetables, carrot, broccoli and cauliflower, for a few minutes.
Add the baby corn, sugar snap peas and mushrooms and toss until everything is crisp-tender.
Pour in the sauce and toss for a minute until it coats the vegetables, then serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Ajiaco

lines.text: 1 large onion, halved, plus 1 small onion, diced
2 lb russet potatoes, peeled and cut in chunks
2 lb Yukon Gold potatoes (for papas criollas), peeled
1 lb red potatoes, peeled and sliced
2 ears corn, each broken in 3 pieces

instructions: Bring the stock, chicken breast, halved onion, guascas and the potatoes to a boil, then simmer for about 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked, and lift the chicken out to cool.
Keep simmering until the russet and Yukon Gold potatoes are completely tender and falling apart.
Mash some of the potato against the side of the pot with a whisk and stir hard to thicken, then add the corn and cook until the soup is as thick as heavy cream.
Dice the small onion and cover it with water in a small bowl with the cilantro and jalapeno to make the fresh aji.
Discard the chicken skin and bones, shred the meat, and set it out in a serving bowl.
Ladle the soup into bowls and pass the chicken, sour cream, aji and avocado slices at the table.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Grilled Fish and Yam

lines.text: 2 medium tilapia, cleaned (about 300 g edible fish)
2 tbsp oil for the pepper sauce, plus 1 tbsp to pan-fry the yam

instructions: Blend the onion, bell pepper, scotch bonnet, garlic and ginger with 2 tbsp of the oil and the salt into a smooth pepper sauce.
Rub the cleaned tilapia with the lemon juice and the pepper sauce and let it sit while the oven heats to 440 F.
Peel the yam and cut it into 4 pieces, then boil or steam it until nearly tender.
Bake the fish for 15 minutes, then broil it for 5 minutes until the skin crisps at the edges.
Pan-fry the yam in the remaining 1 tbsp of oil, turning, until golden on all sides.
Serve the fish with the yam and any leftover pepper sauce on the side.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Githeri

lines.text: 2 cans low-sodium red kidney beans, drained and rinsed
1 tbsp garlic, chopped, and 1 tbsp ginger, minced
2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cut in bite-size pieces

instructions: Boil the corn in 4 cups of water until tender, then keep the corn and its cooking water.
Heat the oil in a large pot and saute the onion until soft, then add the garlic, ginger and cumin and cook until fragrant.
Stir in the tomatoes, carrot, sweet potatoes and Worcestershire sauce and cook for a few minutes until the tomatoes break down.
Add the corn with its water and the beans, and simmer until the sweet potato is tender and the stew thickens.
Stir in the kale and half the cilantro until the kale wilts, then serve topped with the rest of the cilantro.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vignarola

lines.text: 7 oz shelled fresh fava beans (1.1 lb in the pod)
7 oz shelled fresh peas (1.1 lb in the pod)
1 head romaine lettuce, cut in strips
2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, 1 to cook and 1 to finish

instructions: Shell the peas and fava beans, trim and thinly slice the artichokes, cut the romaine into strips, and slice the scallions and chili.
Warm 1 tbsp of the oil in a wide pan and soften the scallions and chili until the scallions turn golden.
Add the artichokes for 3 to 4 minutes, then the fava beans for 3 minutes, then the peas for 3 to 4 minutes, and stir in the romaine.
Pour in the wine, let the alcohol cook off, then cover and cook for at least 10 minutes.
Uncover, season with the salt and cook 5 more minutes, then take off the heat and drizzle with the remaining oil.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Beans and Greens

lines.text: 2 cans (15.5 oz each) cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
1 teaspoon lemon zest and 1 tablespoon lemon juice
2 cups Tuscan kale, stems removed and chopped

instructions: Warm the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and cook the shallot, garlic and chili flakes for about 2 minutes, until they begin to soften.
Add the beans, broth, 1/2 cup water, lemon zest and pepper, and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, partly cover and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, until the beans are very soft.
Blend about a third of the beans in the pot with an immersion blender so the broth turns creamy.
Stir in the spinach and kale in batches and cook, stirring, until they wilt into the beans.
Take the pot off the heat, stir in the lemon juice and serve warm.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Baked Cod with Spring Vegetables

lines.text: 1 tablespoon lemon zest and 1/2 medium lemon, thinly sliced
1 bunch asparagus, trimmed and cut into 1-inch pieces
1 medium yellow or orange bell pepper, thinly sliced
1/2 medium red onion, halved and thinly sliced

instructions: Heat the oven to 400 F (204 C) and set out a large baking sheet.
Zest the lemon and thinly slice half of it.
Put the asparagus, tomatoes, pepper, onion, olives, oil, salt, lemon zest and slices, garlic and parsley on the sheet, toss, and spread in a single layer with room for the fish.
Pat the cod dry, set it on the sheet, and spoon some of the vegetables over the fillets.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until the cod flakes easily and reaches 145 F (63 C).
Serve the fish with the vegetables and a little more parsley.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Ecuadorian Lentil Stew (Menestra)

lines.text: 1/2 bunch cilantro for the pot plus 1/4 cup chopped cilantro

instructions: Warm the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the garlic until fragrant.
Add the tomato, pepper, onion, salt, black pepper and cumin and cook until the onion turns translucent.
Stir in the lentils, 4 cups of water and the half bunch of cilantro, and simmer for about 20 minutes.
Add the diced plantain and cook until it is soft and has changed color.
Remove the cilantro bunch, stir in the chopped cilantro and let the stew reduce.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Eggplant Tofu Stir-Fry in Spicy Basil Sauce

lines.text: 1 cup red and green bell pepper, square cut
1 tbsp vegetable oil for frying the tofu

instructions: Warm the oil in a large pan and fry the tofu cubes until golden outside, then set them aside.
Cook the garlic and chilies for 30 seconds, then add the eggplant with about 1/3 cup of water.
Cover and simmer the eggplant until it is soft, adding the mushrooms and broccoli for the last few minutes.
Stir in the bell peppers, oyster sauce, soy sauce and sugar and cook until the sauce coats the vegetables.
Return the tofu to the pan, toss in the Thai basil and take the pan off the heat.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Ground Turkey Baked Pasta
instructions: Heat the oven to 375 F and boil the whole wheat penne until just short of tender, then drain.
Warm the oil in an oven-safe skillet, add the onion and turkey and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and Italian seasoning and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the marinara, basil and spinach, let the spinach wilt, then fold in the cooked penne.
Cover with the mozzarella and bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbling.
Garnish with a little more basil and serve right away.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Mulligatawny Soup

lines.text: 1 tart-yet-sweet apple, peeled and finely chopped
1/2 cup chopped fresh cilantro, for serving

instructions: Heat the oil in a large soup pot over medium heat, stir in the garam masala for 30 seconds, then cook the carrot, onion, celery and apple for 7 to 8 minutes until softened.
Add the broth, coconut milk and red lentils, bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered for about 15 minutes until the lentils are tender and breaking down.
Purée the soup with an immersion blender until slightly thickened, or blend 2 to 3 cups in a blender and stir it back into the pot.
Stir in the shredded chicken and lime juice and heat through, then serve topped with cilantro.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Sweet Potato Hash

lines.text: 1 poblano pepper, stemmed, seeded and chopped
1 large sweet potato, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
4 leaves lacinato kale, stemmed and torn
Lime wedges, about 1 lime, for squeezing
1 tablespoon fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

instructions: Heat half the avocado oil in a large lidded skillet over medium heat and cook the onion, poblano, garlic and half the salt for 3 to 5 minutes until soft, then move them to a plate.
Heat the remaining oil, add the sweet potato cubes with the rest of the salt and cook, stirring now and then, for 8 to 10 minutes until fork-tender.
Return the vegetables to the pan with the chili powder and kale and stir to combine.
Make 4 shallow wells in the hash, crack an egg into each, cover and cook over medium-low heat for 3 to 5 minutes until the whites are set.
Top with sliced avocado and cilantro and serve with lime wedges.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Lebanese Lentil Soup

lines.text: 1 large sweet potato, peeled and diced (10 ounces)
1 whole bulb garlic, peeled and minced

instructions: Put the lentils in a large pot with the broth and 9 cups of water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 30 minutes until tender.
Separate the kale leaves from the stems, cube the stems and tear the leaves into large pieces.
Warm the olive oil in a skillet, cook the garlic for under a minute, then add the cilantro until just softened and take the pan off the heat right away.
Add the carrot, celery, sweet potato, kale stems, ginger and salt to the lentils and simmer for about 15 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic and cilantro mix with the lemon juice and simmer 2 to 3 minutes, then take the pot off the heat, add the kale leaves, cover for 10 minutes, stir and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Greek Fish with Tomatoes and Onions (Psari Plaki)

lines.text: 1 large yellow onion, halved and thinly sliced
2 pounds white fish fillet, such as halibut or cod
2 lemons, one juiced over the fish and one cut into wedges

instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Cook the onion in the olive oil over medium-high heat for about 7 minutes until soft and lightly golden, then add the garlic.
Add the tomatoes with their juice, break them up with a spoon, stir in 2 teaspoons of the oregano and simmer the sauce for 10 to 15 minutes.
Pat the fish dry, season it with the salt, the remaining oregano, the paprika and cumin, and squeeze one lemon over it.
Nestle the fish in the sauce, spoon sauce over the top and bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until the fish flakes easily.
Cut the second lemon into wedges, sprinkle the dish with parsley and serve the wedges on the side.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Matki Chi Usal

lines.text: 1 cup moth beans (matki), soaked and sprouted
1 tablespoon goda masala or garam masala

instructions: Soak the moth beans overnight, drain them and leave them under a cloth for 1 to 2 days until sprouted.
Heat the oil in a pan, let the mustard seeds splutter, then add the turmeric and onion and cook until the onion is soft.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and tomato and cook until the tomato softens.
Add the sprouted beans, salt, masala and 1 cup of water, cover and cook over medium-low heat for about 10 minutes until the beans are soft.
Stir in the jaggery, coriander and the grated coconut if using, and check the salt before serving with chapati, bhakri or rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Lebanese Baked Garlic Chicken and Potatoes

lines.text: 5 medium potatoes (about 1.9 lb), scrubbed and left unpeeled

instructions: Rub the skinless chicken with 1 tbsp of the olive oil, the salt and the seven-spice.
Cut the scrubbed potatoes into 1/2-inch rounds.
Set the chicken in a metal baking tray, lay the potato rounds on top and bake at 400 F (200 C) for 40 to 50 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
While it bakes, blend the garlic with the remaining olive oil for 4 to 5 minutes, add the lemon juice and blend 4 to 5 minutes more into a smooth sauce.
Drain off the liquid in the tray, pour the garlic sauce over the chicken and potatoes and mix well.
Return the tray to the oven and broil for 5 to 10 minutes, until the potatoes turn reddish. Serve warm.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Thai Ginger Chicken (Gai Pad Khing)

lines.text: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breast, thinly sliced
1 piece fresh ginger (about 4 inches), peeled and cut into matchsticks
3 cups cooked brown rice, for serving

instructions: Toss the sliced chicken with 2 tsp of the soy sauce and set aside.
Cut the ginger into matchsticks, slice the onion, mushrooms and green onions, and mince the garlic, keeping the green tops of the green onions apart.
Stir the oyster sauce, fish sauce, the remaining soy sauce and 1/4 cup water together in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken until it is almost done.
Add the garlic, ginger, onion and the white parts of the green onions and cook 3 minutes, then add the mushrooms and cook 2 minutes more.
Pour in the sauce and toss to coat, then take off the heat and stir in the green onion tops. Serve over the brown rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Slow Cooker Chicken Curry

lines.text: 1 large sweet potato, scrubbed and diced into 1/2-inch pieces
2 red bell peppers, cored and thinly sliced
1/4 cup freshly squeezed lime juice (about 2 limes)
2 tbsp cornstarch, mixed with 3 tbsp water

instructions: Put the diced sweet potato and sliced red peppers in the slow cooker, then pour over the water and lime juice.
Stir the curry powder, smoked paprika, cumin, chili powder and salt together and rub about two-thirds of it on both sides of the chicken thighs.
Sear the chicken in the hot olive oil for about 2 minutes on one side and 1 minute on the other, then set it on top of the vegetables and sprinkle with the remaining spice mix.
Cover and cook on low for 4 hours, until the chicken reaches 165 F (74 C).
Lift the chicken out, let it cool a little, then cut or shred it into bite-size pieces.
Stir in the coconut milk and the cornstarch slurry, turn the cooker to high and cook, covered, for 15 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Return the chicken, stir to coat and cook covered 15 more minutes until everything is hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Italian Tuna Salad

lines.text: 1/3 cup finely chopped dry-packed sun-dried tomatoes
1 can (15 oz) cannellini beans, rinsed and drained, divided
3 tbsp lemon juice (from 1 small lemon, plus its zest)
12 oz canned wild-caught solid pack tuna in water, drained
6 slices whole grain bread, toasted, for serving

instructions: Cover the sun-dried tomatoes with hot water and leave them to soften while you prepare the rest.
Blend about 3/4 cup of the beans with the Greek yogurt, olive oil, lemon juice and onion powder until the beans break up and the dressing is creamy.
Flake the tuna into a large bowl, keeping it chunky, and add the celery, capers, parsley and the remaining beans.
Drain and pat dry the sun-dried tomatoes and add them to the bowl.
Pour the dressing over and fold gently with a fork until combined, then serve on toasted whole grain bread.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Kisir (Turkish Bulgur Salad)
instructions: Put the bulgur in a heatproof bowl, cover with about 3/4 cup boiling water and leave it for 10 minutes to absorb.
Whisk together the tomato paste, olive oil, pomegranate molasses and lemon juice.
Dice the tomato and cucumber small, chop the parsley and thinly slice the spring onion.
Drain any water left on the bulgur, stir in the dressing, then fold in the tomato, cucumber, parsley and spring onion. Serve at once or chilled.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chicken Pozole Verde

lines.text: 2 cans (15.5 oz) hominy, drained and rinsed

instructions: Put the chicken, a quarter of the onion, 2 garlic cloves, the broth and the salt in a large pot, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on medium-low for 30 minutes, skimming any foam.
Lift out the chicken and shred it. Move the cooked onion and garlic from the pot to a blender.
Meanwhile, toss the tomatillos, poblano, remaining onion and 3 garlic cloves with the olive oil on a foil-lined tray and broil 5 to 6 minutes per side, until charred and tender.
Add the broiled vegetables, cilantro, spinach, cumin and 1 cup of the hot broth to the blender and blend until smooth.
Pour the green sauce into the pot, add the hominy and shredded chicken, and simmer 5 to 10 minutes.
Ladle into bowls and top with extra cilantro.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Zucchini with Bulgur Wheat and Tomatoes
instructions: Saute the chopped onions in the olive oil over medium-high heat until golden.
Meanwhile, put the chopped tomatoes in a separate pot with the tomato concentrate and about a cup of boiling water.
Stir the 7 spice, black pepper and salt into the tomatoes, bring to a boil, then lower the heat to medium.
Add the zucchini to the golden onions and cook for 5 to 10 minutes until half done, then add them to the tomato sauce.
Stir in the bulgur and just enough boiling water to cover, then simmer on low for 20 to 30 minutes, checking the salt five minutes before the end.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chicken Stir Fry with Kale and Mushrooms
instructions: Stir the soy sauce, rice wine, sugar, garlic, ginger and sesame oil together until the sugar dissolves.
Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and toss with 3 tablespoons of the sauce while you prepare the vegetables.
Tear the kale off its stems into small pieces, rinse and drain well. Quarter the mushrooms.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over high heat until very hot, add the chicken in one layer and leave it for a minute or two to sear, then stir-fry until nearly cooked.
Add the kale and mushrooms, pour the remaining sauce over and stir-fry until the kale and mushrooms are tender.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Instant Apple, Banana and Strawberry Bircher Muesli
instructions: Peel the banana, put it in a large bowl and mash it with a fork.
Coarsely grate the apple with its skin on and stir it into the banana.
Add the oats, dried cranberries, cinnamon and almond milk and mix until well combined.
Taste and stir in the maple syrup if you want it sweeter.
Divide between bowls and top with the strawberries, pumpkin seeds and chia seeds.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Ground Turkey Skillet with Zucchini, Corn, Black Beans and Tomato

lines.text: 14 ounces zucchini, quartered and sliced 3/4 inch
3/4 cup canned black beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Brown the turkey in a large skillet over high heat with 1 teaspoon each of salt and cumin, breaking it up, until cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Push the turkey aside, add the onion and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the black beans, corn, tomato, jalapeno, garlic and cilantro.
Add the zucchini with the remaining salt and cumin, cover and cook on low for 4 to 5 minutes, until tender-crisp.
Serve topped with more cilantro.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Salmon with Dill Sauce and Roasted Baby Potatoes

lines.text: 4 lemon slices and 1 tablespoon lemon juice

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the baby potatoes with 2 tablespoons of the olive oil, the rosemary, oregano and parsley.
Set the salmon on a sprayed sheet pan, drizzle with the last tablespoon of oil and season with pepper. Put a lemon slice on each fillet.
Scatter the potatoes around the salmon and roast for 20 minutes.
While it roasts, whisk the yogurt, mayonnaise, horseradish, lemon juice, dill, shallot and pepper, then chill.
Take the lemon slices off the salmon, spoon a little dill sauce over each fillet and serve with the potatoes.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Wheat Berry Salad

lines.text: 1 small butternut squash, peeled and cubed
3 medium shallots, cut into 1/2-inch pieces (1 cup)
1 tablespoon plus 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, for drizzling and the dressing

instructions: Simmer the wheat berries in plenty of water until tender, then drain. This takes 25 to 90 minutes depending on the grain, so cook them ahead.
Heat the oven to 400°F, spread the squash cubes on a lined baking sheet and roast about 30 minutes.
Add the shallots to the pan and roast 20 minutes more, wrapping the sage in foil with a little olive oil for the last 2 minutes, then chop it.
Whisk the apple cider vinegar with the rest of the olive oil, pepper and a little of the thyme.
Massage the kale with some of the dressing in a large bowl.
Add the wheat berries, squash, shallots, sage, walnuts, cranberries, parsley and thyme and toss. Move to a platter, drizzle with more dressing and top with the pecorino.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Maqluba

lines.text: 4 pieces of chicken (bone-in thighs, skin removed)
1 head of cauliflower, cut into medium pieces
1 cinnamon stick plus 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon

instructions: Simmer the chicken in 4 to 5 cups of water with the ginger, seven spices, cinnamon stick, bay leaves, onion, garlic and salt until cooked through. Lift out the chicken and strain the stock.
Fry the cauliflower pieces in the oil until golden on the edges.
Rinse the basmati rice. Stir the turmeric and ground cinnamon into 3 cups of the stock.
Arrange the chicken in the bottom of a heavy pot, cover with the cauliflower, then the rice, and pour the spiced stock over everything.
Bring to a boil, cover and cook on low until the rice has absorbed the stock, then rest the pot off the heat.
Turn the pot upside down onto a large platter and lift it off.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Moroccan-Spiced Eggplant and Tomato Stew

lines.text: 1 large (about 1.2 lb) eggplant, unpeeled and cut into bite-size pieces
1 large white or yellow onion, thinly sliced
1 cup cooked chickpeas, rinsed and drained

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the eggplant pieces with 2 tablespoons of the olive oil and roast on a lined baking sheet for 30 to 35 minutes, turning once.
Meanwhile, soften the sliced onion in the remaining oil in a large pot over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, cumin and smoked paprika and cook 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes with their juice and 1/2 cup of water, cover and simmer 4 minutes.
Stir in the chickpeas, maple syrup and harissa paste and simmer covered over medium-low heat.
Fold in the roasted eggplant and simmer 10 minutes more. Serve with lemon and parsley.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Tomato and Onion Soup

lines.text: 2 pounds tomatoes, peeled, quartered and seeded
8 ounces tomato paste, no salt added
3 tablespoons roughly chopped parsley (or oregano or thyme)

instructions: Score an X in each tomato, blanch 30 to 60 seconds, cool in ice water and peel. Quarter them and scoop out most of the seeds.
Soften the diced onions in the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the garlic, half the herbs and the salt and cook 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, bay leaves, broth and tomato paste and simmer 30 minutes, then remove the bay.
Blend all or part of the soup with the remaining herbs to the thickness you like.
Ladle into bowls and top each with a poached egg and a slice of crusty bread.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Sardine Salad Sandwich

lines.text: 2 cans (3.75 oz each) boneless skinless sardines in oil, drained
1 tablespoon lemon juice and 1 teaspoon lemon zest

instructions: Drain the sardines into a large bowl and mash them with a fork.
Stir in the celery, red onion, mayonnaise, dill, lemon juice, lemon zest and Dijon until evenly mixed.
Toast the bread slices until golden.
Lay lettuce, tomato and cucumber on four slices of toast.
Spoon the sardine salad over the vegetables, top with the remaining toast and cut in half.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Barley Risotto

lines.text: 1 large fennel bulb, cored and diced

instructions: Heat the broth to just below a simmer. Brown the sliced mushrooms in 1 tablespoon of the olive oil with 1 clove of garlic, then set them aside and pour their liquid into the broth.
Cook 3 cloves of garlic in 1 tablespoon of olive oil for 15 seconds, add the spinach, cover for 2 minutes, then stir over high heat until wilted. Set the spinach aside and drain off any extra liquid.
Melt the butter with the remaining olive oil, then cook the fennel and onion for 3 to 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the barley for 2 minutes, then add the thyme and the last clove of garlic and cook 1 minute more.
Pour in the wine and cook for 2 minutes, then add two ladles of hot broth and simmer until it is absorbed.
Keep adding broth two ladles at a time for 25 to 30 minutes, until the barley is creamy but still slightly chewy, then serve topped with the spinach and mushrooms.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chicken Broccoli Ziti

lines.text: 1 pound boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1/2-inch strips
6 ounces dry whole-wheat ziti or penne
1 medium head broccoli, cut into florets
1 can (14 ounce) artichoke hearts in water, drained and quartered

instructions: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat and brown the chicken strips for about 5 minutes. Move them to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium and soften the onion for 3 minutes, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the broth and milk and bring to a boil.
Add the pasta and boil for 5 minutes, then add the broccoli and boil 5 to 7 minutes more, stirring often, until the pasta is al dente.
Stir in the artichoke hearts, lemon juice, Parmesan and the browned chicken, adjust with a splash of milk if dry, and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Marinated Gigante Beans

lines.text: 3 cups cooked gigante beans, drained and rinsed
1/4 cup lemon juice and 1 teaspoon lemon zest

instructions: Combine the cooked beans, olive oil, lemon juice, lemon zest, parsley, sun-dried tomatoes, garlic, salt and chili flakes in a large bowl.
Stir to coat the beans well, adding a little more olive oil if they look dry.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Taste, adjust the seasoning and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Salmon, Beet, and Arugula Salad with Pistachios and Pomegranates

lines.text: 1/2 pound wild salmon, cut into 2 fillets
1 cup cooked beets (8 ounces), cut into small wedges

instructions: Heat the oven to 450F. Whisk the olive oil, white wine vinegar and Dijon mustard in a large bowl and set it aside.
Heat an ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat until very hot and lightly coat it with oil.
Lay the salmon in the pan, skin side down if it has skin, and press it down gently. Cook without moving it for 1 to 2 minutes, until the edges turn opaque.
Flip the salmon and move the skillet to the oven for 2 to 4 minutes, depending on thickness, then set the fish aside.
Toss the arugula and beets in the dressing, then scatter over the radishes, goat cheese, pistachios, pomegranate seeds and capers.
Divide the salad between two plates and top each with a salmon fillet.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Roasted Chipotle Sweet Potato and Sorghum Salad

lines.text: 1 medium sweet potato, scrubbed and cut into 1/2-inch cubes

instructions: Toast the sorghum in a dry pot over medium-low heat for a few minutes until it smells nutty. Add 1 1/2 cups water and a pinch of the salt, bring to a boil, cover and simmer 45 to 60 minutes, until tender but still chewy.
