Heat the oven to 425F. Toss the sweet potato cubes on a sheet tray with 1 tablespoon of the olive oil, the chipotle powder, smoked paprika, cumin, coriander and the rest of the salt.
Roast the sweet potato for 30 to 40 minutes, until tender and browned at the edges.
Warm the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a small skillet over medium-low heat with the smashed garlic until the garlic is golden, then remove the pan from the heat.
Stir the cilantro and scallions into the cooked sorghum, then add the roasted sweet potato.
Discard the garlic, drizzle the oil over the bowl, squeeze in the lime juice and toss until coated.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Southwestern Butternut Squash and Black Bean Breakfast Bowl

lines.text: 3 cups butternut squash, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added black beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat the oven to 425F. Toss the squash with 1 tablespoon of the avocado oil and half the garlic powder on a lined tray and roast 25 to 30 minutes, stirring once at the 15-minute mark, until browned and tender.
Warm the black beans in a small saucepan over medium heat for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring often, then stir in 1/4 cup of the enchilada sauce.
Heat 1/2 tablespoon of the avocado oil with the red pepper flakes in a skillet until it sizzles, add the spinach and the rest of the garlic powder and toss until wilted.
Heat the last 1/2 tablespoon of avocado oil in the skillet, crack in the eggs and cook about 3 minutes.
Divide the squash, beans, spinach and eggs between two bowls and top with the remaining enchilada sauce, sliced avocado and cilantro.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Artichokes, Green Peas, and Potatoes

lines.text: 1 pound artichoke hearts, frozen and thawed
2 carrots, peeled and sliced into thin rounds
1/2 cup dill, stems removed and chopped

instructions: Warm the olive oil in a medium pot and saute the artichoke hearts, green onions and carrots for 5 minutes.
Add the dill, potatoes, lemon juice and 2 cups of water and bring to a simmer.
Simmer for 20 minutes, until the potatoes are nearly tender.
Add the peas and simmer for 10 more minutes.
Beat the cornstarch with 1/4 cup of water, stir it into the pot and boil for 2 minutes until the juices thicken.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chickpea Rice Pulao
instructions: Rinse the basmati and soak it in water for 15 minutes, then drain.
Soften the chopped red onion in the oil in a pot, then stir in the garlic, ginger and pulao masala until fragrant.
Add the tomato, carrot and green beans and cook until the tomato breaks down and the vegetables begin to soften.

1/4 red bell pepper, seeded and chopped

instructions: Remove the neck and innards from the chicken, then set it breast side up in a deep pot and cover with cold water. Bring to a boil and skim the foam until the water is clear.

Turn the heat to medium-low, add the sliced ginger, green onion and salt, flip the chicken and simmer 10 minutes. Flip it breast side up again and simmer until the thigh juices run clear and the joint reads 165 F, 15 to 20 minutes.
Move the chicken to a large ice bath for 3 to 4 minutes to tighten the skin and stop the cooking, then drain, pat dry and let it air dry on a board.
Blend the Thai chilies, red bell pepper, minced ginger, garlic, lime juice, soy sauce, Chinkiang vinegar and sugar into a coarse paste for the dipping sauce.
Rub the sesame oil over the chicken skin, then separate the legs, breasts and wings and slice the meat into bite-sized pieces.
Reheat a little of the strained poaching broth, then serve it alongside the sliced chicken and the chili sauce.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Taco Stuffed Zucchini Boats

lines.text: 4 medium zucchini (about 32 ounces), halved lengthwise and hollowed, about 700 g after the extra scooped flesh is discarded
1/2 cup mild salsa — use Pace Chunky Salsa Mild (US)
1/2 cup reduced-fat Mexican blend shredded cheese

instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water and heat the oven to 400 F. Spread half the salsa in the bottom of a large baking dish.
Hollow out the zucchini halves, leaving a shell about 1/4 inch thick. Chop 3/4 cup of the scooped flesh, squeeze out the water and set it aside.
Boil the zucchini shells for 1 minute, then lift them out and drain.

Brown the turkey in a skillet, breaking it up. Stir in the garlic powder, cumin, chili powder, paprika and salt, then add the onion, chopped zucchini flesh and tomato sauce and simmer covered for about 20 minutes.
Press the turkey filling firmly into the zucchini shells, set them in the baking dish and top each with some of the cheese.
Cover with foil and bake about 35 minutes, until the cheese melts and the zucchini is tender, then top with the scallions and serve with the remaining salsa.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Pollo con Rajas en Crema

lines.text: 2 lbs boneless chicken breast, seasoned with salt and black pepper
6 poblano peppers (5 cut into strips, 1 for the crema), roasted and cleaned, about 480 g
1 cup media crema or crema mexicana (table cream)
1 teaspoon salt for seasoning the chicken

instructions: Roast the poblano peppers until the skins blister and blacken, steam them in a covered bowl, then peel, seed and cut five of them into strips.
Blend the crema, cream cheese, the remaining roasted poblano, jalapeno, garlic, chicken broth and half the black pepper until smooth.
Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces, season with the salt and the rest of the black pepper, and cook in a wide skillet until browned and cooked through.
Add the sliced onion and soften it for a few minutes, then stir in the poblano strips.
Pour in the blended crema and simmer gently until hot, then let the pan rest a few minutes so the sauce thickens before serving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Mouthwatering Sichuan Chicken in Red Oil Sauce

lines.text: 2 bone-in skin-on chicken legs (1 to 1.5 lbs in total), about 400 g edible meat and skin
1 thumb of ginger, sliced, plus 1 teaspoon grated ginger
1 green onion, white part minced, green part sliced for garnish
4 tablespoons chili oil (3 tablespoons oil plus 1 tablespoon chili flakes)

instructions: Lay the ginger slices over the chicken legs on a heatproof plate, skin side up, pour the Shaoxing wine over them and set the plate in a steamer over boiling water.
Steam covered over medium-high heat until the juices run clear, about 30 minutes, then cool the chicken and save the cooking juices.

Stir the soy sauce, Chinkiang vinegar, sesame paste, sesame oil, minced green onion, garlic, grated ginger and Sichuan pepper together in a serving bowl, then thin with 3 tablespoons of the cooking juices and a spoonful of chili flakes from the chili oil.
Bone the cooled chicken and slice the meat into 1 cm pieces, then add it to the bowl of sauce.
Pour the chili oil over the chicken, scatter on the peanuts and green onion and toss gently before eating.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Lebanese Garlic Sauce Chicken Wings

lines.text: 1 kg chicken wings, tips removed, about 500 g edible meat and skin
About 1 teaspoon ground allspice, to taste
2 to 3 tablespoons Lebanese garlic sauce (about 2 1/2 tablespoons)

instructions: Trim the wing tips, pat the wings dry, and mix them with the salt, allspice and olive oil.
Heat the grill to low-medium and line the pan with foil. Thread the wings onto short metal or pre-soaked wooden skewers, spaced evenly.
Whisk the lemon juice and garlic sauce together in a bowl deep enough to hold the wings.
Grill the wings, turning the skewers often, until crisp and browned and cooked through at the bone, about 20 minutes.
Slide the hot wings off the skewers into the bowl, toss to coat, cover with foil to let the sauce soak in, then top with parsley and serve right away.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Spanish Chicken in Bravas Sauce

lines.text: 2 boneless chicken breasts (10 oz / 300 g each)

instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pan over medium heat while you pat the chicken dry, season it with salt and pepper and cut each breast into pieces about 4 cm thick.
Fry the chicken in a single layer for 3 minutes per side until browned but not fully cooked, then set it aside.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the same pan for 3 minutes.
Stir in the sweet and hot smoked paprika for a few seconds, then slowly pour in the broth, stirring, and let it simmer until lightly reduced.
Add the white wine vinegar and a little salt and pepper, return the chicken to the pan in a single layer and turn each piece in the sauce.
Cover on low-medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until the chicken reaches 165 F, then serve topped with the parsley.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Peruvian-Style Roast Chicken with Green Sauce

lines.text: 1 whole chicken, 4 lb (about 1.1 kg meat and skin)
5 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided between marinade and sauce
5 tbsp lime juice, divided between marinade and sauce
6 cloves garlic, divided between marinade and sauce
1 tbsp plus 1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided

instructions: Blend 3 tbsp of the olive oil with 1/4 cup of the lime juice, 4 cloves garlic, 1 tbsp salt, paprika, 1 tsp pepper and the cumin until smooth.
Remove the giblets, pat the chicken dry, loosen the skin over the breasts and legs, spoon about two thirds of the marinade under the skin and spread the rest over it.
Marinate the chicken in the refrigerator for at least 6 hours or overnight.
Heat the oven to 425 F, tie the legs together, set the chicken breast side up on a rack and roast 20 minutes until the skin is golden.
Lower the oven to 375 F and roast about 1 hour 10 minutes more until the juices run clear between leg and thigh, loosely covering with foil if it browns too fast.
Blend the jalapenos, cilantro, 2 cloves garlic, mayonnaise, sour cream, 1 tbsp lime juice, 1/2 tsp salt and 1/8 tsp pepper, then drizzle in the remaining 2 tbsp oil while blending and chill.
Rest the chicken under foil for 20 minutes, carve and serve with the green sauce.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Cock-a-Leekie Soup

lines.text: 1 medium chicken, jointed (about 900 g edible meat and skin)
2 leeks, cut into thick rounds (tops reserved)

instructions: Heat the oil in a large heavy saucepan and brown the chicken pieces in batches, then set them aside.
Fry the bacon, carrots, celery and leek tops for 5 minutes until browned, then pour off excess fat.
Add the wine and boil hard, scraping up the browned bits from the pan base.
Return the chicken with the bay leaves and thyme, cover with cold water, bring slowly to the boil and simmer for 40 minutes.
Lift out the chicken, strain the broth into a clean pan, skim off the fat and pull the chicken from the bones in large pieces.
Simmer the broth with the shredded chicken and sliced leeks for 20 to 30 minutes, season with salt and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Hunan Chicken

lines.text: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thigh, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 tbsp Shaoxing wine, divided between marinade and sauce
6 scallions, cut in 1-inch pieces, whites and greens separated
2 stalks celery, sliced on the bias

instructions: Toss the chicken with 1 tbsp of the Shaoxing wine and set aside.
Stir together the remaining Shaoxing wine, oyster sauce, soy sauce and dark soy sauce for the sauce.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over high heat and sear the chicken in one layer for 2 minutes, flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more, then move it to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, scallion whites, garlic, ginger and black beans and stir over medium heat for 1 minute.
Add the chili, celery and scallion greens and stir-fry for 2 minutes until just tender.
Return the chicken, pour in the sauce and cook, stirring, until it reduces and coats everything, then serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Ayam Kecap

lines.text: 2 1/2 lb chicken drumsticks (about 850 g edible meat and skin)

instructions: Pat the drumsticks dry and set them aside for 10 minutes while you prep the aromatics.
Sear the drumsticks in the hot oil in a medium pot until lightly browned on all sides, then move them to a plate.
Cook the garlic, shallot and dried chilies in the same pot until caramelized and fragrant.
Pour in the stock to lift the browned bits, then stir in the galangal, coriander, clove, lime leaves, kecap manis and soy sauce.
Return the drumsticks and simmer uncovered for 25 minutes, turning every 5 to 10 minutes and skimming any foam.
Raise the heat slightly and reduce until the sauce coats a spoon, then serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chinese Lemon Chicken

lines.text: 14 oz boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 tsp granulated erythritol sweetener (sugar-free), plus more to taste
3 tbsp cornstarch, divided (1 tbsp for the sauce, 2 tbsp for the coating)
3 tbsp vegetable oil, divided (1 tbsp for the marinade, 2 tbsp for frying)
1 tsp salt, divided between the sauce and the chicken

instructions: Whisk the lemon juice, broth, rice vinegar, erythritol, 1 tbsp cornstarch, lemon zest and half the salt into a sauce and set it aside.
Toss the chicken pieces with 1 tbsp oil and the remaining salt, then let them marinate for 15 minutes.
Stir the beaten egg into the chicken, then add 2 tbsp cornstarch and mix until the pieces have an uneven coat with a little dry starch left.

Heat the remaining oil in a large skillet until very hot, spread the chicken in a single layer and fry 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden. Move it to a plate and let the pan cool for 2 to 3 minutes off the heat.
Return the pan to medium heat, add the green onions and ginger and stir a few times until fragrant.
Stir the sauce again, pour it in and simmer until it thickens, then toss the chicken through the sauce and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chicken Chasseur

lines.text: 4 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (about 250 g each)
4 tbsp unsalted butter, divided (half to brown the chicken, half cold to finish the sauce)

instructions: Pat the chicken dry and season with salt and pepper. Brown the thighs skin-side down in the oil and half the butter for about 5 minutes, flip for 1 minute, then brown the drumsticks on 3 sides. Set the chicken aside.
In the same pan, cook the mushrooms and onions over high heat for about 5 minutes until the mushrooms wilt, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Pour in the brandy and let it bubble for 20 to 30 seconds, then add the white wine and boil until reduced by half, scraping up the browned bits.
Stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute, then add the beef stock and a pinch each of salt and pepper.
Return the chicken skin-side up, cover and simmer for 10 minutes, then uncover and simmer 20 minutes more until tender.
Lift out the chicken and simmer the sauce for 3 minutes to reduce slightly.
Off the heat, stir in the remaining cold butter in two additions until glossy, return the chicken and sprinkle with tarragon.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Turkey Burgers with Sun-Dried Tomatoes, Basil and Feta

lines.text: 1 tbsp avocado oil for the pan

instructions: Stir the basil, oregano, sun-dried tomatoes, green onions, garlic, feta, salt, red pepper flakes and black pepper together in a large bowl.
Add the ground turkey and mix gently with your hands for a couple of minutes until the flavorings are spread evenly.
Divide the mixture into 4 equal portions, shape into patties and press a dimple into the centre of each.
Chill the patties for at least 30 minutes so they hold their shape.
Heat the avocado oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the patties dimple-side up for 5 to 6 minutes per side, until they reach 165°F (74°C) inside.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chicken in Creamy Mustard Sauce

lines.text: 700 g (1.4 lb) skinless boneless chicken thigh fillets
3/4 tsp salt, divided between the chicken and the sauce

instructions: Season the chicken thighs with half the salt and pepper.

Heat the oil in a large pan that is not non-stick over medium-high heat and sear the thighs smooth-side down for 4 minutes, then flip and cook 3 minutes until cooked through (72°C / 162°F). Move them to a plate.
Scrape any loose black bits from the pan and discard them.
Return the pan to medium heat, add the cream and both mustards and stir until the mustard dissolves, scraping up the brown bits. Heat until hot but not simmering.
Stir in the remaining salt and pepper, the tarragon and the parsley, adding a splash of water if the sauce is too thick.
Return the chicken and its juices to the pan or plate it and spoon the sauce over the top.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Crispy Breaded Chicken Cutlets

lines.text: 4 medium boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 2 lbs total)
2 large eggs, beaten with 1 tbsp water
2 1/2 oz (70 g) pork rinds, finely crushed, in place of the panko
Extra light olive oil for shallow-frying (about 3 tbsp counted)

instructions: Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally into 8 cutlets, pound them to about 1/4 inch thick between plastic wrap or parchment, and season with 1 tsp of the salt and the pepper.
Whisk the eggs with the water in one dish. In another, mix the crushed pork rinds, Parmesan, garlic powder, Italian seasoning and the remaining salt.
Dip each cutlet in the egg wash, let the excess drip off, then press it firmly into the crumb mixture. Rest the coated cutlets on a tray for 5 to 10 minutes so the coating sets.
Heat enough oil in a large skillet to come about halfway up the cutlets, keeping it at 350 to 375°F (175 to 190°C).
Fry the cutlets in batches for about 2 minutes per side, until deep golden and 165°F (74°C) in the centre, then drain on a wire rack.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Paprika Chicken

lines.text: 3 large boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 680 g), cut into 1-inch cubes
2 red bell peppers, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 can (14.5 oz) chicken broth, simmered down to 3/4 cup

instructions: Simmer the chicken broth in a small pan until it reduces to 3/4 cup, and drain the canned tomatoes in a colander.
Cut the onion and red peppers into 1-inch pieces. Trim the chicken breasts and cut them into 1-inch cubes, then season with 1 teaspoon of the sweet paprika and the salt.
Brown the chicken in 1 tablespoon of the oil over medium-high heat for about 5 minutes, until barely cooked through, and move it to a plate.
Cook the onion in the remaining oil for 4 minutes, add the rest of the sweet paprika and the hot paprika, and cook 1 minute more.
Add the peppers until they begin to soften, then the tomatoes for 2 minutes, then the reduced broth for 2 to 3 minutes.
Return the chicken and its juices, simmer on low for 2 to 3 minutes, then turn off the heat and let the pot stop bubbling for a minute or two.
Stir a few spoonfuls of the hot liquid into the sour cream, then stir that mixture gently into the pot and serve hot in bowls.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Roasted Cornish Hens

lines.text: 2 whole Cornish hens (about 1 1/2 lb each), about 800 g edible meat and skin

instructions: Mix the Italian seasoning, smoked paprika, garlic powder, pepper flakes and salt in a small bowl.
Pat the hens dry, rub the seasoning generously over and inside each bird, and heat the oven to 425 F.
Scatter the rosemary, thyme, garlic, onion and half the lemon slices in a roasting pan and set the hens on top. Drizzle with the olive oil.
Roast for 50 to 60 minutes, until a thermometer in the thickest part of the breast reads 165 F.
Rest the hens for 20 minutes, then garnish with extra thyme, rosemary and lemon slices and serve half a hen per person.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Grilled Chicken Kebabs

lines.text: 1 pound boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 red and 1 yellow bell pepper, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 teaspoon granulated erythritol sweetener, in place of the honey

instructions: Soak wooden skewers in water for at least 30 minutes if using them.
Whisk the olive oil, garlic, parsley, dill, lemon juice, sweetener and salt in a large bowl.
Toss the chicken pieces in the marinade, cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes up to 2 hours.
Heat the grill to medium-high. Thread the chicken, onion, bell peppers and zucchini onto the skewers, alternating them.
Grill the skewers 5 to 7 minutes on each side until the chicken is cooked through, and serve with a little extra parsley.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Dak Bulgogi

lines.text: 1 pound boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 2-inch by 1-inch pieces
1 teaspoon granulated erythritol sweetener, in place of the brown sugar and honey

instructions: Trim the chicken thighs and cut them into pieces about 2 inches long and 1 inch wide.
Stir the soy sauce, lemon juice, sweetener, garlic, ginger, sesame oil and pepper in a bowl until the sweetener dissolves.
Coat the chicken in the marinade and refrigerate for about 30 minutes.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and add the chicken, keeping back the leftover marinade.
Cook about 2 minutes on each side until cooked through and lightly caramelized, then scatter with the sesame seeds.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Pan Seared Duck Breast with Cherry Sauce

lines.text: 2 duck breasts (6 to 8 ounces each), about 300 g cooked weight once the fat has rendered
1/2 cup fresh cherries, pitted and halved

instructions: Score a diamond pattern into the duck skin without cutting into the meat, and season both sides with the salt and pepper.
Set the duck skin side down in a cold heavy skillet over medium-low heat with no oil and cook 6 to 10 minutes, raising the heat to medium as the fat renders, until the skin is brown and crisp.
Flip and cook 2 to 4 minutes to 130 to 135 F for medium-rare, then rest the duck 5 to 10 minutes under foil.
Pour off all but 2 to 3 tablespoons of fat, cook the shallot over high heat for 30 seconds, add the wine and scrape up the browned bits for 1 minute.
Add the cherries, thyme and stock and boil 3 to 4 minutes until reduced to a sauce, then take off the heat and stir in the butter. Slice the duck across the grain and spoon the sauce over.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Low Carb Turkey Chili with No Beans

lines.text: 2 cups cooked butternut squash, roasted until soft

instructions: Halve and seed the butternut squash, roast it cut side down at 425 F until soft and golden, then let it cool and scoop out the flesh.
Heat the avocado oil in a large Dutch oven and cook the onion and bell pepper until softened.
Stir in the garlic for a minute, then add the ground turkey with half the salt and cook until browned.
Add the chili powder, smoked paprika and the remaining salt, then stir in the roasted squash.
Pour in the diced tomatoes, tomato sauce and beef broth and bring back to a low boil.
Lower the heat, cover and simmer for 30 to 40 minutes before serving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Ultimate Chicken Salad

lines.text: 2 pounds boneless skinless chicken breasts, poached

instructions: Cover the chicken breasts with salted water in a wide pan and bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce the heat to low, cover and poach 8 to 12 minutes until the center reaches 160 to 165 F, then chill in the fridge.
Dice the cooled chicken into half-inch pieces and put it in a large bowl.
Add the grapes, celery, green onion, mayonnaise, Dijon, almonds, parsley, tarragon and lemon juice.
Season with salt, stir until evenly coated and chill until ready to serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Keto Chicken Katsu

lines.text: 2 large boneless skinless chicken breasts, halved into 4 cutlets
1 cup pork panko (finely crushed pork rinds)
1/2 teaspoon salt for the crumb mixture
1 tablespoon soy sauce or liquid aminos

instructions: Cut each chicken breast in half through the middle and pound the four pieces to an even thickness.
Mix the pork panko and sesame seeds in a shallow dish with a generous pinch of salt.
Press both sides of each cutlet into the crumb mixture so it sticks.
Fry the cutlets in hot oil 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and the center reaches 150 to 155 F, then drain on paper towels.
Stir the ketchup, Worcestershire, soy sauce, sweetener and garlic powder together for the sauce.
Slice the cooled cutlets into strips and serve over cauliflower rice with the sauce drizzled on top.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Keto Malai Kebab

lines.text: 500 grams boneless chicken leg and thigh meat
50 grams processed block cheese such as Amul or Britannia
2 teaspoons ghee, plus more for cooking

instructions: Cut the chicken into kebab-size pieces.
Mix the cheese, cream, ginger garlic paste, salt, pepper, cardamom and lime juice into a creamy marinade.
Coat the chicken in the marinade and leave it for at least an hour, or overnight.
Thread the chicken on skewers.
Fry the skewers in ghee on a cast iron or non-stick pan, turning, until cooked through, or bake at the highest oven heat.
Char the kebabs briefly over a stove flame and serve with chutney and lime.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Galeto a Passarinho

lines.text: 3 chicken breasts, boneless and skinless (about 600 g), cut into small chunks
3 tablespoons oil for frying, the share the chicken takes up

instructions: Cut the chicken breasts into small chunks and put them in a bowl.
Season with salt, pepper, paprika, herbes de Provence and the chopped chili, then add the lemon juice and crushed garlic and mix well.
Cover and chill the chicken for 30 minutes.
Fry the chicken in hot oil in a pan, turning the pieces once they turn light brown, for about 10 minutes until browned.
Lift the chicken out, dry it very well on paper towels, and toss it with the chopped parsley.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Spanish Chicken Chilindrón

lines.text: 4 large chicken drumsticks, skin on (about 520 g edible meat and skin)
1 large red bell pepper, finely diced
3 ripe tomatoes, grated with the skins discarded
4 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil, divided

instructions: Heat half of the olive oil in a large pan, season the drumsticks with salt and brown them on all sides over medium-high heat, adding a little of the garlic in the last minute, then set them aside.
Add the sliced onion and the rest of the oil to the pan and cook over medium heat until golden, then stir in the diced red pepper and the remaining garlic.
Add the grated tomato and the diced Serrano ham and simmer for about 20 minutes until most of the liquid has cooked away.
Push the sauce aside, add a splash of oil and stir the paprika, garlic powder, white pepper and ñora pepper in it for 1 minute, then mix them into the sauce.
Pour in the white wine, add a little water if the sauce looks dry, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Nestle the browned drumsticks into the sauce, cover and simmer for 5 minutes, then uncover, spoon the juices over the chicken and cook 5 more minutes until tender.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Roasted Turkey Breast with Keto Gravy

lines.text: 2 cups chicken or turkey broth, unsalted

instructions: Heat the oven to 350 F (175 C). Rub the turkey breast with the thyme, rosemary, sage, salt, pepper and 1 tablespoon of the olive oil.
Heat the remaining oil in an ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat and sear the turkey 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Move the skillet to the oven and roast the turkey for 30 to 35 minutes, then rest it for 5 minutes.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, stir in the almond flour for 2 to 3 minutes until golden brown, then slowly whisk in the broth.
Whisk in the xanthan gum, bring the gravy to a simmer for 5 to 7 minutes until thick, then stir in the cream and cook 2 to 3 more minutes and season.
Slice the turkey and serve it with the gravy, straining the gravy first for a smoother sauce if you like.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chicken Zucchini Noodle Soup

lines.text: 1 1/2 lb (680 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs
about 30 g Creole seasoning (4 tablespoons for the chicken, 2 to 3 for the soup)

instructions: Toss the chicken thighs with about 4 tablespoons of the Creole seasoning.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a large pot, brown the chicken until its juices cook off, then remove it and shred it with two forks.
In the same pot, heat the remaining oil and soften the onion, garlic, celery and bell peppers.
Add the broccoli, kale and the rest of the Creole seasoning, pour in the broth, cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the tomato paste, shredded chicken and spiralised zucchini and simmer covered for 15 more minutes.
Taste and add salt and pepper if needed, then serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Silkie Chicken Soup

lines.text: 1 silkie chicken, 1.5 lb / 680 g, about 440 g of meat and skin once the bones are removed

instructions: Put the silkie chicken, dried shiitake, goji berries, corn and ginger in a small Dutch oven that just fits the chicken.
Add 6 cups of water so the chicken is covered, then bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Turn to medium-low and skim the surface with a fine sieve for about 10 minutes, until the broth looks clear.
Cover and simmer for at least 90 minutes, up to 2 to 2.5 hours, until the chicken is very tender and almost falling off the bones.
Serve the soup as is, or lift out the chicken and strain the broth for a clearer soup.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chicken Cordon Bleu Bake

lines.text: 4 large, thick boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut in half lengthwise into 8 cutlets
4 slices ham, cut in half lengthwise
4 slices Swiss cheese, cut in half lengthwise
8 oz cream cheese, cut into cubes and softened
1/2 cup freshly grated Parmesan in the sauce plus 1/2 cup for the top

instructions: Heat the oven to 375F and let the cream cheese soften in a bowl.
Cut each chicken breast in half lengthwise into two thin cutlets.
Sear the cutlets in the olive oil for 2 minutes per side, then blot them dry between paper towels.
Lay the cutlets in a large baking dish and top each with a half slice of ham and a half slice of Swiss.
Whisk the softened cream cheese with the chicken stock, sour cream, mayonnaise, Dijon and half of the Parmesan until thick.
Spread the sauce over the chicken and sprinkle with the remaining Parmesan.
Bake about 30 minutes, until bubbling hot and starting to brown on top.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Garlic Dijon Chicken and Brussels Sprouts

lines.text: 1 1/2 lbs Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
2 tablespoons olive oil in the marinade plus 2 teaspoons for the sprouts
1/2 tablespoon plus 1/2 teaspoon sea salt, divided between the marinade and the sprouts

instructions: Stir the olive oil, garlic, parsley, lemon juice, Dijon, salt and pepper together, coat the chicken thighs and marinate at least 6 hours, ideally overnight.
Heat the oven to 400F and halve the trimmed Brussels sprouts.
Toss the sprouts with salt, pepper and the olive oil on a parchment-lined sheet pan and spread them in a single layer at the edges.
Set the marinated thighs skin side up in the center of the pan, about 1/2 inch apart.
Bake uncovered 25 minutes, or 30 for bone-in thighs.
For crisper skin, broil on high for 2 to 4 minutes until browned.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Piri-Piri Chicken

lines.text: 1 chicken, about 2 kg, roughly 1.3 kg of meat and skin once the bones are removed

instructions: Boil the dried chillies with the vinegar, then leave them to soak until the vinegar is cold.
Blitz the red chillies, garlic, soaked chillies and vinegar in a food processor, add the paprika, oregano, thyme, a pinch of salt and the lemon juice, and blend to a paste.
Score the chicken all over, 1 cm deep, including the legs and underside, then massage the marinade into the cuts.
Cover and chill for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Roast at 180C (160C fan) for 1 hour, then raise to 220C (200C fan) for 30 to 35 minutes until a crust forms.
Rest the chicken for 30 minutes before carving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Salmon Burgers

lines.text: 1 pound skinless fresh salmon (about 1 1/4 pounds with skin)
1 tablespoon olive oil for the pan

instructions: Cut the skinless salmon into chunks, then chop it by hand with a chef's knife into a coarse mince with a few larger pieces left for texture.
Gently fold the salmon with the egg, almond flour, parsley, red onion, garlic, Dijon, lemon juice and salt until just combined. Do not overwork it.
Shape the mixture into 4 patties and refrigerate them for 20 to 30 minutes so they hold together.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the patties 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and just cooked through.
Serve each burger wrapped in butter lettuce leaves with sliced avocado.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Poached Salmon
instructions: Spread the lemon slices, shallot and sliced fennel over the bottom of a wide skillet that has a lid.
Season the salmon lightly with salt and pepper and set the fillets skin-side down on the vegetables.
Tuck the dill sprigs around and over the fish, then pour in the wine and 1 cup of water. The liquid does not need to cover the fish.
Bring the liquid to a vigorous simmer over medium-high heat.
Turn the heat to low, cover, and cook 5 to 12 minutes depending on thickness, until the flesh flakes easily or reads 125 to 130 F.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Swedish Shrimp Salad (Skagenröra)

lines.text: 1 handful finely diced red onion (about 1/4 cup)

instructions: Pat the cooked, peeled shrimp dry and cut any large ones into bite-size pieces.
Chop the dill and finely dice the red onion.
Fold the shrimp with the mayonnaise, dill, red onion, lemon zest and lemon juice.
Season with salt and white pepper to taste.
Cover and chill in the fridge for 1 hour so the flavors blend, then serve cold.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Moroccan Fish in Spicy Tomato Sauce (Chraime)

lines.text: 2 lb halibut or other firm white fish, cut in pieces

instructions: Warm the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat, add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the onions, and cook until lightly caramelized.
Stir in the smoked paprika, hot paprika and cumin and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chopped tomatoes, cover, and simmer 10 minutes, then mash the softened tomatoes with a masher.
Pour in 1 cup of water, then tuck the fish pieces into the sauce.
Cover and simmer 10 minutes, turn the fish, season with the salt and pepper, and cook 5 to 8 minutes more until done.
Taste for seasoning and finish with the chopped cilantro or parsley.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Goan Prawn Caldinho

lines.text: 400 g raw king prawns, deveined, with a pinch of salt
1 tablespoon Goan or white wine vinegar
3 garlic cloves and a 1-inch piece of ginger, pounded to a paste
1 teaspoon cumin seeds, 10 peppercorns and 1 tablespoon coriander seeds, ground

instructions: Toss the prawns with the turmeric, vinegar and a pinch of salt and leave them for 15 to 20 minutes.
Grind the cumin seeds, peppercorns and coriander seeds to a fine powder.
Fry the onion in the oil for 5 to 7 minutes until light brown, add the tomato for 3 to 4 minutes, then the garlic and ginger paste for 1 minute.
Stir in the ground spices and fry for 2 minutes, then add the prawns and coat them in the spice mixture.
Pour in the coconut milk, 80 ml of water and the tamarind paste and simmer 3 to 4 minutes until the prawns turn pink.
Add the green chillies, season with salt, and garnish with chopped coriander.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Fish Ambul Thiyal

lines.text: 500 g firm fish such as tuna, cut into chunks
1 tablespoon ginger paste and 1 tablespoon garlic paste

instructions: Cut the fish into chunks and rub them with the goraka paste, black pepper, ginger and garlic paste, turmeric, cinnamon and salt.
Put the fish in a wide pot with the curry leaves, pandan leaf and slit green chillies, then pour in the water.
Cover and simmer over low heat for about 20 minutes, turning the fish once.
Uncover and cook a few more minutes, stirring gently, until the liquid is gone and the spices cling to the fish.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Classic Shrimp Louie Salad

lines.text: 2 lb raw shrimp (16/20 count), peeled and deveined

instructions: Bring a pot of water to a rolling boil, add the shrimp and cook 3 to 5 minutes until pink and opaque.
Move the shrimp to an ice bath, then drain and pat dry.
Whisk the mayonnaise, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, lemon juice and salt into the dressing.
Dice the celery, onion and red pepper and chop the parsley.
Toss the shrimp, diced vegetables and parsley with the dressing and chill for at least 30 minutes.
Top with the sliced avocado and quartered eggs and serve cold.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Tuna Steak with Sauce Vierge

lines.text: 2 tuna steaks, about 190 g each, skinless and boneless
1 tablespoon olive oil for the tuna and the pan
3 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil for the sauce
6 black olives, pitted and cut into strips
1/2 teaspoon parsley, 1/4 teaspoon chives and 1/4 teaspoon tarragon, finely chopped
1/4 teaspoon salt split between the tuna and the sauce

instructions: Rub the tuna with the tablespoon of olive oil and season both sides with half the salt and the pepper.
Heat a skillet over high heat until smoking, then sear each steak 45 seconds, rotate a quarter turn and sear 45 seconds more.
Flip and cook the second side about 1 minute for a rare centre, then rest the tuna on a rack for 5 minutes.
Mix the extra virgin olive oil, lemon juice, tomato, olives, anchovy, garlic, herbs and remaining salt into the sauce.
Slice the tuna and spoon the sauce over the slices at room temperature.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Thai Fish Cakes

lines.text: 500 g white fish fillets, skinless and pin boned, cut into chunks
1/4 cup (25 g) almond flour in place of the rice flour

instructions: Blend the fish, red curry paste, cilantro, fish sauce, lime juice and egg in a food processor into a thick paste.
Stir the almond flour and sliced green beans into the paste until evenly mixed.
Scoop 1/4 cup portions and shape them into patties about 1 cm thick, making about 12.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and fry the patties 2 minutes per side until deep golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve with lime wedges and extra cilantro.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Pan Seared Scallops with Lemon Garlic Butter
instructions: Pat the scallops dry with paper towels and sprinkle them with kosher salt.
Heat the avocado oil in a saute pan over medium-high heat until shimmering, then sear the scallops about 1 1/2 to 2 minutes per side until golden, working in batches, and move them to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium and add the butter, garlic, lemon zest, lemon juice and parsley, whisking until the sauce is lightly simmering.
Return the scallops to the pan, spoon the sauce over them and serve with extra sauce drizzled on top.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Mediterranean-Style Steamed Clams

lines.text: 1/2 green pepper and 1/2 red pepper, chopped

instructions: Sort the clams, discard open ones that will not close, then soak and scrub them clean in cool water.
Heat the olive oil in a Dutch oven and cook the onion, peppers and garlic about 5 minutes without letting the garlic burn.
Stir in the tomatoes, cumin, smoked paprika and red pepper flakes, pour in the wine and water and boil gently 5 to 7 minutes until the tomatoes soften.
Lower the heat to medium, add the clams, cover and cook 7 to 10 minutes until most have opened, discarding any that stay shut.
Turn off the heat, stir in the parsley and serve in bowls.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Steamed Mussels with Thai Herbs

lines.text: 1 lb live mussels, rinsed and debearded
1 stalk lemongrass, thinly sliced on a bias
5 kaffir lime leaves, torn, center rib removed

instructions: Rinse the mussels twice, tap any open ones and discard those that do not close, then pull off the beards.
Saute the garlic in the vegetable oil in a large pot until it just turns golden.
Add the stock, lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, chilies, 1 cup of the tomatoes and the fish sauce and bring to a boil.
Add the mussels, cover and cook about 2 minutes, stirring halfway, until they open.
Turn off the heat, stir in the Thai basil and the remaining tomatoes, cover for 30 seconds, then add the lime juice and adjust the seasoning.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Zarzuela de Pescado y Mariscos

lines.text: 1/2 red bell pepper and 1/2 green bell pepper, roughly chopped
14 oz cod fillet, cut into 1 inch pieces
10 raw jumbo shrimp, peeled and deveined

instructions: Fry the almonds and garlic in the olive oil until golden, then pound them in a mortar into a paste.
In the same pan soften the onion and bell peppers, then add the wine and let it cook down a few minutes.
Stir in the tomato sauce and simmer about 10 minutes until it thickens.
Add the fish broth, saffron and the almond paste, bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low about 10 minutes.
Add the cod pieces and clams, cover and cook about 4 minutes until the clams open.
Add the shrimp and cook 1 to 2 minutes until pink, then ladle into shallow bowls.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Crispy Marinated Baby Octopus

lines.text: 1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil, 3 tablespoons left behind
1 tablespoon canola oil, for the grill or skillet

instructions: Simmer the octopus very gently in salted water with onion, garlic, peppercorns, lemon juice and bay for about 1 hour until a leg is tender.
Drain the octopus in a colander and pick out the bay leaves and onion.
Mix the olive oil, minced garlic, lemon zest, lemon juice, chilli flakes, salt and pepper and pour over the hot octopus.
Toss, let it cool, cover and marinate in the fridge overnight.
Lift the octopus from the marinade onto a hot oiled grill plate or skillet and cook 3 to 5 minutes, turning, until golden and crispy.
Pile onto a plate and scatter with parsley.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Spanish Tomato and Sardine Salad

lines.text: 3 medium tomatoes, sliced into 1/4 inch rounds
3 tablespoons of the olive oil from the sardine can

instructions: Slice the tomatoes into 1/4 inch rounds and lay them in overlapping circles on a serving dish.
Slice the onion thinly, separate the slices into strands and scatter them over the tomatoes.
Lift the sardines out of the can, halve each one lengthwise, remove the spines and lay them over the salad. Season with black pepper.
Pound the garlic, parsley and a pinch of sea salt to a paste in a mortar, then stir in 3 tablespoons of the sardine-can oil and the sherry vinegar.
Spoon the dressing over the salad and serve at room temperature or chilled.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Spicy Swordfish

lines.text: 3 swordfish steaks, about 1 inch thick (about 200 g each)

instructions: Halve the cherry tomatoes lengthwise, crush the garlic and finely chop the chili and parsley.
Warm the olive oil with a splash of water in a large pan over low heat, add the garlic, then the tomatoes and half the chili, stirring.
Press the tomatoes gently with a potato masher to release their juice, crush the olives by hand and add them with the capers, half the parsley, the salt and the pepper.
Lay the swordfish in the pan, season the top, cover and cook for about 3 and a half minutes.
Turn the steaks, spoon the sauce, olives and tomatoes over them, add the remaining parsley and chili and cook covered for another 3 and a half minutes.
Take the pan off the heat right away so the swordfish stays moist, and serve with the sauce.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Rainbow Trout Almondine

lines.text: 2 rainbow trout fillets, about 5.5 ounces each
2 tablespoons almond flour (low-carb swap for cornstarch)

instructions: Pat the trout dry, season with the salt and pepper and dust both sides lightly with the almond flour.
Heat the olive oil and 1 tablespoon of the butter in a large pan over medium heat and lay the trout in skin side down.
Cook undisturbed for 3 to 4 minutes, flip and cook 2 to 3 minutes more until lightly golden, then move the fish to a plate.
Wipe the pan clean, return it to medium heat and melt the remaining 3 tablespoons of butter.
Add the sliced almonds and cook, stirring, until the butter browns and the almonds toast.
Turn off the heat, stir in the lemon juice, parsley and capers and spoon the sauce over the trout.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Roasted Branzino with Citrus Pesto

lines.text: 2 tablespoons olive oil for the fillets plus 1/4 cup olive oil for the pesto
1 cup fresh basil leaves, moderately packed
3 oranges: 1 zested and juiced for the pesto, 2 sliced for topping
2 lemons: 1 zested and juiced for the pesto, 1 sliced for topping

instructions: Heat the oven to 350 F and line a baking tray with parchment.
Lay the fillets on the tray, brush with 2 tablespoons of the olive oil and season with part of the salt and pepper.
Roast for 12 minutes, until the fish is cooked through.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan while the fish cooks.
Blend the toasted pine nuts, basil, remaining olive oil, the zest and juice of 1 orange and 1 lemon, the garlic and the remaining salt and pepper into a pesto.
Slice the remaining orange and lemon thinly. Set the fillets on a platter and top each with pesto and a few citrus slices.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Cioppino (Fisherman's Stew)

lines.text: 1/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, divided
7 sprigs fresh thyme plus 1 teaspoon chopped
1 1/2 pounds halibut fillets, cut into 2 inch pieces
1 1/2 pounds extra large raw shrimp, peeled and deveined

instructions: Heat the oven to 400 F. Cook the shallots in 1/4 cup of the olive oil until soft, then stir in the garlic for 1 minute without browning.
Add the wine, turn the heat to high and boil until reduced by about half.
Add the crushed tomatoes, clam juice, 1 teaspoon of the salt, the thyme sprigs and 1 cup of water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 25 minutes.
Toss the halibut with the remaining 2 tablespoons of oil and 3/4 teaspoon of salt, spread it on a foil-lined sheet and bake for about 10 minutes. Cover to keep warm.
Remove the thyme sprigs, stir in the butter, add the clams and simmer covered for about 6 minutes until most open.
Add the shrimp, return to a simmer and cook covered for about 5 minutes until the shrimp are cooked and all clams are open. Discard any that stay shut, then stir in the chopped thyme.
Divide the halibut among bowls and ladle the stew with clams and shrimp over it.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Salt and Pepper Shrimp

lines.text: 1 pound large shrimp, shells on and deveined (about 340 g once peeled)
3 tablespoons potato starch or cornstarch, for dredging
1/4 cup oil, for shallow-frying the shrimp and garlic
2 teaspoons whole black peppercorns, dry-roasted and ground
1 long hot green or red pepper, thinly sliced

instructions: Dry-roast the peppercorns in a small pot over medium-low heat for about 15 minutes until fragrant, cool completely, and grind to a powder.
Dry-roast the salt in the same pot over medium heat until it turns slightly yellow, cool, and mix with the ground pepper.
Rinse the shrimp and pat them completely dry, then dredge them in the potato starch.
Heat most of the oil to about 375 F (190 C) and fry the shrimp in batches, 30 seconds per side, spacing them apart. Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with some of the pepper salt.
Fry the garlic in the remaining oil until golden, drain it, and leave about 1 tablespoon of oil in the wok.
Stir-fry the sliced hot pepper in the wok, turn off the heat, add the garlic and shrimp, toss for 10 seconds with more pepper salt, and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chinese Steamed Fish with Ginger Shallot Sauce

lines.text: 2 whole snapper or bream, 350 to 400 g each, gutted and scaled (about 375 g of edible fish)
2 stems of scallions, cut into thin 5 cm strips
4 pieces of ginger, 3 cm each, cut into thin strips
2 tablespoons Shaoxing wine, sprinkled over the fish
4 tablespoons vegetable oil, heated until smoking

instructions: Cut two slashes into each side of the fish, right down to the bone, and sprinkle each fish with the Shaoxing wine.
Set the fish on a plate in a steamer over boiling water, cover, and steam for about 10 minutes until the flesh flakes. A foil parcel baked at 350 F (180 C) for 15 minutes also works.
While the fish steams, heat the oil in a small pan until it is hot and nearly smoking.
Move the fish to serving plates and pile the scallion and ginger strips on top.
Sprinkle with the salt and drizzle over the soy sauce and sesame oil.
Pour the hot oil over the aromatics so it sizzles, scatter over the sliced chili if using, and serve straight away.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Pecan Crusted Tilapia

lines.text: 2 tablespoons yellow mustard (the source allows any mustard)
1/2 lemon, cut into wedges, for serving (optional)

instructions: Preheat the oven to 400 F (205 C) and pat the tilapia fillets dry with paper towels.
Whisk the mayonnaise, mustard, sugar-free maple syrup and garlic powder in a bowl and brush both sides of each fillet. Keep about half of the sauce aside.
Press the pecan meal onto both sides of each fillet so it coats evenly.
Set the fillets on a lined baking sheet, spritz with avocado oil if you like, and bake 8 to 10 minutes until the fish flakes.
Serve hot with lemon wedges and the leftover sauce for spooning.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Cajun Shrimp Boil Foil Packets

lines.text: 1 pound large shrimp, peeled and deveined
6 ounces fully cooked andouille sausage, sliced into 1/4-inch rounds
2 medium zucchini, sliced into 1/4-inch rounds (12 to 14 ounces)
1 pound green beans, trimmed and cut in half (in place of the potatoes and corn)
1 tablespoon Cajun seasoning plus 2 teaspoons seafood seasoning, about 5 teaspoons in all
2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley, for serving
1 lemon, cut into wedges, for serving

instructions: Preheat an outdoor grill to medium-high, or the oven to 400 F (200 C).
Toss the shrimp, andouille, zucchini and green beans in a large bowl with the melted butter and the seasonings.
Divide the mixture among four 16 by 12 inch pieces of heavy-duty foil, mounding it in the center.
Bring the shorter edges to the center, fold them over, then fold in the sides to seal each packet with some air space inside.
Grill covered for 10 minutes, flip, and grill 5 minutes more, or bake on a rimmed sheet for 15 to 20 minutes, until the shrimp are cooked through and the vegetables are tender.
Open the packets carefully and serve hot with parsley and lemon wedges.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Lobster Roll Lettuce Cups

lines.text: 8 ounces cooked lobster tail meat (2 tails)
6 large butter lettuce leaves for the cups, plus 3/4 cup shredded lettuce (in place of hot dog buns)

instructions: Chop the cooked lobster tail meat into small bite-size pieces.
Fold the lobster with the chives, shallot, celery, mayonnaise, Greek yogurt, black pepper and lemon zest.
Arrange the butter lettuce leaves on a platter, two per serving, and add a little shredded lettuce and a tomato slice to each pair.
Spoon one third of the lobster salad into each pair of lettuce cups and serve right away.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Potted Crab

lines.text: 1 cucumber, sliced into rounds, to serve with the crab (low-carb swap for sourdough)

instructions: Tip the crabmeat into a bowl and mix with the mayonnaise, shallot, chives, orange zest and a little seasoning.
Spoon the mixture into a shallow serving dish, smooth the top and put it in the fridge.
Gently melt the butter with the smoked paprika, then let it cool a little without letting it set.
Pour the clear butter fat over the crab, leaving the milky residue behind in the pan.
Return the dish to the fridge for 20 to 25 minutes, or up to a day, until the butter is firm.
Slice the cucumber into rounds and serve them alongside for spreading.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Smoked Mackerel Pate

lines.text: 3 smoked mackerel fillets, skinned and boned
4 celery sticks, to serve (low-carb swap for griddled sourdough)

instructions: Skin the mackerel fillets and check carefully that every bone is out.
Break two of the fillets into a food processor and add the cream cheese, lemon zest and juice, and the parsley.
Pulse for 20 to 30 seconds until smooth.
Scrape the pate into a bowl, flake the third fillet through it, and season to taste, going easy on salt as the fish is already salty.
Toss the watercress with the olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Serve the pate with the dressed watercress and celery sticks.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Nicoise Salad

lines.text: 275 g canned chunk tuna in oil, drained and broken into large chunks
2 tomatoes, each cut into 8 to 10 wedges
1/2 baby cos lettuce, cut or torn into large bite-size pieces
100 g unpitted black olives (about 85 g pitted)

instructions: Shake the lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, Dijon mustard, salt and pepper together in a jar for the dressing.
Hard boil the eggs, then cool, peel and quarter them.
Boil the green beans until tender, then refresh them under cold running water, drain and pat dry.
Spread the lettuce over a large wide plate.
Scatter the tomatoes and green beans over the lettuce, then finish with the eggs, olives and large chunks of tuna.
Drizzle the dressing over the top and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Thai Lime & Garlic Steamed Fish

lines.text: 2 coriander roots, roughly chopped (stems used if no roots)
1/2 tsp sea salt, plus more for the fish

instructions: Pound the chillies, coriander roots, garlic and salt to a rough paste, then stir in the stock, fish sauce and lime juice.
Lay the lemongrass on a heatproof plate that fits your wok, set the fish on top and season it with salt.
Fill the wok about a quarter full of water, bring it to a simmer and set the plate on a foil ring trivet.
Cover and steam for 5 minutes.
Lift the lid, pour the sauce over the fish, cover again and steam 6 to 7 minutes more until the fish is cooked through.
Carefully lift out the plate and serve the fish with the sauce from the plate.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Shrimp Mozambique

lines.text: 2 lb medium shrimp, shells on (about 600 g edible weight)
1 cup white wine or Vinho Verde
1/2 tbsp piri piri or other hot sauce
1 tbsp finely minced parsley, for garnish

instructions: Heat the olive oil in a medium skillet over medium heat, add the onion and cook about 2 minutes until translucent.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, then add the shrimp and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the butter, bouillon cube and paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine, stir and bring to a boil on medium heat.
Add the salt and simmer until the shrimp turn pink, then stir in the piri piri.
Cook a few minutes longer until the wine has reduced, then scatter with parsley and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Coconut Stewed Haddock

lines.text: 1 pound haddock, cut into 2 to 3 inch pieces

instructions: Rinse the haddock pieces with the juice of half the lemon and cool water, drain and set aside.
Heat the coconut oil in a large pan, then cook the garlic, seasoning peppers and Scotch bonnet over lowered heat for 1 minute.
Add the thyme, scallions and black pepper and saute for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the haddock and stir gently to coat it with the aromatics.
Pour in the coconut milk, salt and the rest of the lemon juice, bring to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for 5 to 7 minutes until the fish is cooked through.
Taste, adjust the seasoning and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Smoked Haddock and Leek Chowder

lines.text: 300 g cauliflower florets, diced small (instead of potatoes)

instructions: Lay the haddock in a deep frying pan, pour over the milk, cover and bring to the boil, then take off the heat and leave for about 5 minutes until just cooked.
Lift out the haddock, remove the skin and bones and flake it onto a plate, keeping the milk.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan and fry the bacon until it starts to brown.
Add the celery, leeks, bay leaves and cauliflower and cook for a couple of minutes.
Pour in the stock and the reserved milk, bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the flaked haddock and single cream, season with pepper, stir in the parsley and heat through gently.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Smoked Salmon Deviled Eggs

lines.text: 1 teaspoon finely chopped dill, plus extra to garnish

instructions: Bring a pot of water to the boil, turn the heat low, lower in the eggs, then bring it back to high and boil for 14 minutes.
Chill the eggs in an ice water bath, then peel them and halve lengthwise.
Scoop the yolks into a bowl and set the whites on a serving plate.
Stir the yolks with the mayonnaise, mustard, lemon juice, shallot, dill and salt until smooth.
Spoon the filling into the whites, then top each half with a piece of smoked salmon, a few capers and a little dill.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vietnamese Lettuce Wraps with Peanut Sauce

lines.text: 300 g peeled whole cooked prawns, halved horizontally

instructions: Stir the peanut butter, hoisin, coconut milk, garlic and sambal oelek together, adding lime juice a little at a time to taste, and set aside to let the flavours blend.
Cut the prawns in half horizontally and remove the vein.
Julienne the carrots and cucumbers and pick the mint and cilantro.
Lay the lettuce, vegetables, herbs and prawns out on a big platter with the sauce in a bowl.
Build each wrap with a lettuce leaf, vegetables, prawns and herbs, drizzle with the sauce, then fold and eat.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Parmesan-Herb Baked Salmon

lines.text: 1 whole wild salmon filet with skin, 1 1/2 inches thick (2 lbs)

instructions: Heat the oven to 425 F and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper or foil.
Stir the mayonnaise, Parmesan, garlic, dill, parsley, basil and chives together in a small bowl.
Set the salmon skin side down on the sheet, cover it with another piece of parchment and bake for 8 minutes.
Take off the top parchment and spread the Parmesan-herb mixture over the salmon.
Bake uncovered for 15 to 18 minutes, until the top has browned and the salmon flakes easily or reads 135 F.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Steak au Poivre
instructions: Pat the filets dry, flatten them slightly to about 1 1/2 inches thick and salt both sides.
Crush the peppercorns in a small bag with a pan or mallet and press them onto both sides of each steak.
Sear the steaks in the hot oil for about 4 minutes per side for medium-rare, then rest them on a plate under foil.
Pour off the excess fat, then cook the shallots in the butter over medium-low heat until golden and soft.
Add the Cognac carefully, scraping up the browned bits, and boil it down to a glaze.
Stir in the cream, Dijon and any resting juices, simmer until thickened and spoon the sauce over the steaks.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Keto Salisbury Steak
instructions: Mix the ground beef with the cream, parmesan, half the salt and the pepper, then shape four patties.
Brown the patties in 2 tablespoons of butter for about 5 minutes per side and set them aside.
Melt the remaining butter in the skillet and cook the onion until soft.
Add the mushrooms and the rest of the salt and cook until their liquid has evaporated.
Stir in the tomato paste and arrowroot for a minute or two, then whisk in the broth and wine and bring to a simmer.
Return the patties to the skillet, cover on low heat and cook for 10 to 15 minutes.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Carne Asada

lines.text: 1/4 cup plus 1 1/2 teaspoons olive oil, divided

instructions: Mix the garlic, orange juice, lime juice, cilantro, salt, most of the olive oil, jalapeno and vinegar in a zip bag.
Add the steak, coat it well and marinate in the fridge for 1 to 8 hours.
Let the steak sit at room temperature for 20 to 30 minutes, then heat a grill or skillet with the remaining oil until smoking.
Cook the steak 3 to 4 minutes per side, no further than medium, then rest it under foil for 5 minutes.
Slice thinly against the grain and serve with sliced avocado and diced tomato.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Texas Chili

lines.text: 4 pounds beef chuck roast, trimmed and cut into 1/2-inch chunks

instructions: Season the chuck chunks with the salt, then brown half in 2 tablespoons of oil in a large pot and set aside; repeat with the rest.
Add the remaining oil, then cook the jalapenos and onion for about 10 minutes until soft without browning.
Stir in the garlic, chili powder, smoked paprika, cumin and oregano for 30 seconds.
Return the beef with the crushed tomatoes and beef broth and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer uncovered for 3 to 3 1/2 hours, stirring now and then and adding broth if it gets too thick.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Pan-Fried Greek Lamb Chops

lines.text: 1/2 lemon, cut into wedges, to serve
2 tablespoons chopped fresh mint, to serve

instructions: Whisk the garlic, vinegar, olive oil, salt, pepper, cumin and oregano and pour it over the chops in a tray.
Cover and refrigerate the chops overnight.
Bring the chops to room temperature and heat a cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook the chops about 5 minutes per side, then 2 minutes on each thin edge, until the thickest part reaches your preferred temperature.
Plate with lemon wedges and chopped mint.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Lamb Vindaloo

lines.text: 1.25 lb (567 g) boneless lamb shoulder, cubed
1 large onion (1 cup), very finely chopped

instructions: Soak or blend the chilli powder, coriander, cumin, garlic, ginger and vinegar with a splash of water into a smooth vindaloo paste, adding half the salt.
Coat the lamb with the turmeric and paste, cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 6 hours or overnight.
Heat the mustard oil in a heavy pot and cook the onion over medium heat until golden.
Add the marinated lamb and saute over medium-high heat for 5 minutes until the paste smells fragrant and leaves the sides of the pan.
Pour in 1 cup of boiling water, cover and cook on low for about 1 1/2 hours, stirring every 15 minutes and adding hot water in small batches after 40 minutes.
Season with the remaining salt, then cook uncovered until the lamb is fork tender and the sauce is thick and semi-dry.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Samgyupsal Gui with Lettuce Ssam

lines.text: 9 cloves garlic (8 thinly sliced, 1 minced for the sauce)

instructions: Wash and dry the lettuce, slice the scallions, garlic and green chilies and cut the pork belly into bite-size pieces.
Stir the doenjang, gochujang, minced garlic, 2 teaspoons of the sesame oil and the sesame seeds into a thick ssamjang, thinning with a little water if needed.
Heat a flat pan or grill pan over medium heat and lay in the pork belly with the sliced garlic and green chilies.
Grill the pork, flipping once, until it is browned and cooked through.
Toss the scallions with the remaining sesame oil, the salt and a little pepper.
Serve the pork right away with the lettuce, scallions and ssamjang so each person wraps their own bites.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Sausages and Garlic Buttered Broccoli
instructions: Boil the broccoli florets for 3 minutes, then drain and chill them in ice water to stop the cooking.
Put the sausages in a skillet with a little water, cover and cook over medium-high heat for about 10 minutes, turning now and then.
Once the water has evaporated, add half the butter and half the garlic and cook the sausages a couple of minutes more, then set them aside.
Melt the remaining butter in the same skillet over lower heat, add the broccoli and remaining garlic and stir for about 5 minutes.
Add the lemon juice, vegetable broth and hot sauce and cook a few minutes, stirring.
Return the sausages to the pan to take up the sauce, then serve with parsley.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Porchetta

lines.text: 5 teaspoons kosher salt, divided (halve for table salt)

instructions: Toast the fennel seeds and peppercorns in a dry pan for about 2 minutes, crush them, then mix with half the salt, the rosemary, chilli flakes, garlic and 1 tablespoon of the oil into a paste.
Trim a strip of meat from one long edge of the belly, score the flesh in diamonds and rub the paste into the cuts, placing the trimmed piece in the middle.
Roll the belly firmly and tie it with string at 1 inch intervals, then refrigerate uncovered on a rack for 24 to 48 hours before roasting.
Heat the oven to 265 F, rub the skin with the remaining oil and the rest of the salt, and slow roast for 3 1/2 hours.
Raise the oven to 465 F, drizzle with oil and roast for 30 to 40 minutes until the skin is puffed and crisp.
Rest for at least 30 minutes, then cut the strings and slice with a serrated knife.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Slow Cooker Pulled Pork
instructions: Stir the paprika, oregano, salt, pepper and cumin together and rub the blend all over the pork shoulder.
Set the pork in the slow cooker and scatter the diced onion and chopped garlic over the top, then pour in the orange juice.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours, until the pork pulls apart easily with two forks.
Lift the pork onto a cutting board and shred it with two forks, discarding any large pieces of fat.
Return the shredded pork to the juices in the slow cooker and toss to coat before serving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Parmesan Crusted Pork Chops

lines.text: 1/2 cup crushed pork rinds (a low-carb stand-in for breadcrumbs)

instructions: Let the chops sit at room temperature for 20 minutes, then pat them dry and season both sides with the salt and pepper.
Beat the egg with the water in a shallow bowl, and on a plate mix the Parmesan, crushed pork rinds, parsley, garlic and lemon zest.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Turn each chop in the egg, let the excess run off, then press it into the coating until covered on every side.
Swirl the avocado oil into the hot pan, add the chops and cook for 3 minutes, then flip them one at a time, a minute apart.
Cook another 3 minutes until the chops feel firm and read 140 F in the thickest part.
Move the chops to a plate, tent loosely with foil and rest for 10 minutes before serving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Cumin Beef

lines.text: 8 dried Chinese chili peppers, halved, seeds removed
1 small red onion, cut into 1/2-inch pieces

instructions: Slice the flank steak along the grain into two pieces, then against the grain into 1/4-inch slices. Toss with a quarter teaspoon of the salt, the baking soda and 1 tablespoon of oil and marinate for 30 minutes.
Stir the cumin, chili flakes, black pepper and remaining salt together in a small bowl.

Drain any liquid from the beef. Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over medium-high heat and cook the slices in batches in a single layer until golden on both sides, 3 to 5 minutes per batch, then set aside.
Add the last tablespoon of oil to the wok with the dried chilies, ginger and garlic and stir for a few seconds until fragrant.
Add the red onion and cook 1 minute, then return the beef, scatter the spice mix over it and stir at once to coat.
Take the wok off the heat, taste for salt, stir in the sesame seeds and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Bistec a la Criolla

lines.text: 2 pounds sirloin steak, trimmed and cut into 4 equal portions

instructions: Cut the steak into 4 equal portions and pound each one between sheets of wax paper to about 1/2 inch thick.
Put the steaks in a zip-top bag with the mustard, cumin, garlic, cilantro, salt and pepper, turn to coat and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the sliced onion for about 3 minutes.
Lay the steaks in the skillet and cook for 3 minutes on each side.
Add the diced tomatoes, cover the pan and cook for 7 minutes more, then serve the steaks with the onion and tomato from the pan.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Garlic Butter Steak Bites

lines.text: 1 1/2 pounds sirloin steak, cut into bite-sized pieces

instructions: Pat the steak cubes dry and season them with the salt, black pepper and red pepper flakes.
Heat a large cast-iron pan over medium-high heat, add the olive oil, and when it shimmers lay in the steak in a single layer.
Sear the steak for 1 to 2 minutes on each side until browned, then move it to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium-low, add the butter, shallot and garlic to the pan and cook for 1 minute.
Return the steak to the pan and stir it through the garlic butter to coat.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the parsley and serve right away.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Cuban Vaca Frita

lines.text: 1 white onion, cubed, plus 2 large white onions, sliced
5 garlic cloves, roughly chopped, plus 6 garlic cloves, minced

instructions: Chop one onion and five garlic cloves. Pat the flank steak dry, season with the salt and pepper, then coat with the oregano, cumin, one tablespoon of olive oil, the lime juice and the orange juice and marinate for at least 20 minutes.
Put the marinated steak in a pressure cooker with the chopped onion, garlic and bay leaves and seal the lid.
Cook on high pressure for 1 hour, then release the pressure carefully and lift out the steak.
Shred the steak on a board with two forks.
Heat the remaining 3 tablespoons of olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat and fry the shredded steak in batches, 2 minutes at a time, turning gently, until crisp all over.
Make a gap in the centre of the pan, cook the minced garlic and the two sliced onions there, then fold them into the beef, switch off the heat and finish with lime juice and a little extra salt.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Kalops

lines.text: 1 kg (2.4 lbs) chuck roast, cut into 1 inch cubes
3 large carrots, cut into bite-sized pieces

instructions: Season the beef cubes with salt, then sear them in the hot oil in a single layer, in batches, until browned on all sides.
Add the onion, celery and garlic to the pot and cook until just softened.
Stir in the butter until melted, then add the allspice, pepper and bay leaves.
Pour in the beef stock, bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes, adding the carrots partway if you want them to keep some bite.
Uncover and simmer for another 45 minutes, adding water if the pot runs low, until the beef is very tender and the sauce has reduced.
Remove the bay leaves, taste for salt and serve in bowls.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Pork Souvlaki

lines.text: 1 1/2 pounds pork tenderloin, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 medium red onion, quartered and separated

instructions: Trim the silver skin from the pork tenderloin and cut it into 1-inch cubes.
Whisk the vinegar, olive oil, garlic, mustard, oregano, rosemary, paprika and pepper, add the pork, toss and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Take the bowl out of the fridge 30 minutes before grilling, and soak wooden skewers in water if you use them.
Quarter the red onion, pull it into layers and thread the pork and onion onto the skewers.
Season with the sea salt, brush with the leftover marinade and grill over high heat for about 4 minutes per side until marked and 145 F inside.
Rest the skewers loosely covered for 4 to 5 minutes, then squeeze the lemon over them.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Instant Pot Caldo de Res

lines.text: 3 lbs beef shank, bone-in (about 950 g meat)
2 lbs beef chuck short ribs, bone-in (about 500 g meat)
1 calabacita (Mexican zucchini), cut into large pieces
1/4 small head cabbage, cut into large pieces

instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper, then brown both sides of each piece in the hot avocado oil on Sauté, in batches, and set it aside.
Lower the heat, cook the diced tomatoes until juicy and scrape up the browned bits, then stir in the tomato paste and oregano for 1 minute.
Pour in 8 cups of water, return the beef and add the garlic head, onion and a bay leaf if you have one.
Cook on high pressure for 35 minutes, then let the pressure fall naturally for 10 minutes before releasing the rest.
Lift out the excess fat, loose bones, onion and garlic, season the broth with salt, and add the chayote, carrots, calabacita and cabbage.
Cook on high pressure for 3 minutes, let the pressure fall naturally for 5 minutes, release the rest and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Mexican Picadillo

lines.text: 1/2 onion, diced, plus 1/4 white onion for the sauce
1 dried ancho chile, deveined and deseeded

instructions: Saute the tomatoes, a quarter of the onion, the ancho chile, garlic and oregano in the oil in a large pan, then lift them out and blend with the beef stock and chipotle until smooth.
In the same pan, cook the ground beef with the diced onion, cilantro and cumin and season with salt and pepper.
Once the beef is browned, add the carrots and cook for about 5 minutes over medium heat.
Pour in the blended sauce and bring it to a boil for 10 minutes.
Taste, add more salt if needed and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Osso Buco

lines.text: 5 thick veal osso buco (300 g / 10 oz each, bone in)
4 garlic cloves, minced (3 for the sauce, 1 for the gremolata)
1 cup flat-leaf parsley leaves, lightly packed
2 to 3 tsp finely grated lemon zest

instructions: Season the veal shanks generously with salt and pepper, then sear them in hot olive oil in a heavy pot until browned on both sides and set them on a plate.
Lower the heat and cook the garlic and onion for 1 minute, then add the carrot and celery and cook gently about 8 minutes until soft and sweet.
Stir in the crushed tomato, wine, broth and tomato paste, return the veal to the pot, cover and simmer gently on medium-low.
Braise for about 1 1/2 hours, checking every 15 minutes after that, until the meat pulls apart easily with a fork.
Lift the veal into a bowl, then simmer the sauce for 5 to 15 minutes until thickened and adjust the salt and pepper.
Chop the parsley with the remaining garlic clove and the lemon zest for the gremolata, then serve each shank with sauce and gremolata on top.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Greek-Style Lamb Burgers

lines.text: 1 small head iceberg lettuce, leaves used as the wrap and shredded for topping

instructions: Preheat the grill to high heat.
Mix the shallots, garlic, mint, oregano, salt and pepper in a large bowl, add the lamb and mix by hand until combined.
Shape the mixture into 6 oval patties about 1/2 inch thick.
Oil the grill grates and grill the patties covered for 2 to 4 minutes until browned, then flip and cook a few minutes more to your doneness.
Rest the burgers on a tray under foil, then set each in a lettuce leaf and top with shredded lettuce, tomato, red onion and crumbled feta.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Slow Roasted Crispy Pork Belly (Siu Yuk)

lines.text: 3 1/2 lbs whole slab of skin-on pork belly
1 teaspoon salt, spread over the skin

instructions: Stir the soy sauce, oyster sauce, Shaoxing wine, garlic, pepper and five-spice in a shallow dish.
Pat the skin dry, score it in a crosshatch without cutting into the fat, and set the belly in the marinade with the skin above the liquid.
Marinate uncovered in the fridge overnight or up to a day, then set the belly on a rack over a lined baking sheet and spread salt over the skin.
Roast at 400 F for 30 minutes, then lower the oven to 300 F and roast 2 more hours.
Raise the oven to 450 F and roast 30 to 45 minutes more until the skin puffs and crisps.
Rest the pork 10 to 15 minutes under foil with a cross slashed in it to let steam out, then slice and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Rack of Lamb with Dijon Herb Crust

lines.text: 2 racks of lamb, frenched (8 ribs per rack)
2 tablespoons finely chopped fresh thyme leaves

instructions: Stir the Dijon mustard, garlic, rosemary, thyme, parsley and lemon zest together for the herb paste.
Take the racks out of the fridge 30 minutes ahead, pat them dry, heat the oven to 425 F and season them all over with the salt and pepper.
Sear the racks in an ovenproof skillet with the olive oil over medium-high heat, 2 to 3 minutes fat side down and 1 to 2 minutes on the meat side.
Brush the herb paste over the meat side of both racks, avoiding the bones.
Roast fat side up for 18 to 22 minutes until a thermometer reads 125 to 130 F for medium-rare.
Rest the racks for 5 minutes, then slice between the bones into chops.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Thai Garlic Pepper Pork
instructions: Pound the white peppercorns in a mortar until fine.
Add the garlic and pound it roughly while the pepper is still in the mortar.
Season the pork pieces with the salt, add the pepper and garlic mixture and massage it in for about a minute.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat and fry the marinated pork.
Add the oyster sauce and soy sauce and keep frying for another few minutes until the pork is cooked through.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Beef Tataki
instructions: Rub the steak with the vegetable oil and sprinkle it with the salt.
Simmer the sake and mirin in a small pan for 1 minute, pour into a bowl to cool, then stir in the rice vinegar, soy sauce, lemon juice and lime juice.
Warm the garlic slices in the light olive oil over low heat for about 5 minutes until light golden, then cool and strain the oil.
Sear the steak in a smoking-hot cast iron skillet for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes a side for rare.
Cool the steak, then slice it as thinly as you can.
Lay the slices on a plate, drizzle with the dressing and the garlic oil and scatter the green onion over the top.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Asado de Tira (Argentinian Short Ribs)
instructions: Season the short ribs on all sides with the coarse salt and let them come to room temperature.
Peel and seed the roasted red peppers, then blend or chop them with the garlic, parsley, oregano, chilli flakes, red wine vinegar, canola oil and both paprikas into a loose chimichurri rojo.
Build a bed of hardwood embers and set the grill rack high so the heat stays low.
Grill the ribs over the low embers, turning now and then, until deeply browned and tender, about 1 hour 15 minutes.
Rest the ribs for 10 minutes, then serve with the chimichurri rojo spooned over or alongside.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Andalusian Pork Kebabs (Pinchos Morunos)
instructions: Pound the garlic, saffron and a pinch of salt in a mortar, then work in the oregano, both paprikas, cumin, turmeric and cinnamon.
