Stir the lemon juice and olive oil into the spice paste.
Pat the tenderloin dry, halve it lengthwise, cut it into 1-inch pieces and season with salt and pepper.
Coat the pork in the marinade, cover and refrigerate for 2 hours.
Thread 4 pieces of pork on each of 6 soaked skewers.
Cook the skewers in a hot nonstick pan over medium heat, 3 at a time, 1 1/2 to 2 minutes a side until the pork reaches 145 F, then serve with parsley and lemon wedges.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Mediterranean Baked Feta

lines.text: 1 cup pitted olives, drained and halved
1/2 cup sun-dried tomatoes, drained and roughly chopped
1 tablespoon roughly chopped fresh parsley, for garnish

instructions: Heat the oven to 350F (175C) and set the block of feta in a small baking dish.
Stir the olives, sun-dried tomatoes, olive oil, garlic, oregano, thyme, basil, red pepper flakes, salt and pepper together in a bowl.
Pour the topping over the feta so it is fully coated in oil, then push most of the olives and tomatoes to one side.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the feta softens, then broil for 1 to 2 minutes if you want a lightly browned top, watching the olives.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve with sliced cucumber.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Kadai Paneer

lines.text: 1 teaspoon kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed

instructions: Grind the coriander seeds and dried red chilies to a fine powder and set it aside.
Saute the onions and cashews in 1 tablespoon of oil until the onions turn pink, add the tomatoes and cook until mushy, then cool and blend to a smooth puree.
In the same pan, saute the capsicum on high heat until half done, toss in the paneer for 1 to 2 minutes and set both aside.
Heat the remaining oil, cook the ginger garlic paste until the raw smell goes, then stir in the ground masala for 2 to 3 minutes and the puree for 2 minutes before adding the garam masala.
Pour in 1 cup of water and the salt and boil until the gravy thickens and oil shows on top, then crush in the kasuri methi.
Fold in the paneer and capsicum, cover and let it rest for 2 minutes, then leave it to stand so the paneer takes on the flavor.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Thai Basil Eggplant

lines.text: 1/2 large red pepper and 1/2 large green pepper, sliced
2 1/2 tablespoons sugar-free maple syrup (low-carb swap for maple syrup)

instructions: Slice the eggplant and peppers, then blend the syrup, tamari, rice vinegar, peanut butter, sesame oil and 1/3 cup of water into a sauce.
Cook the peppers in 1 tablespoon of oil over high heat for 1 to 2 minutes until still crunchy, then lift them out.
Cook the eggplant in 2 tablespoons of oil over medium heat, stirring and sprinkling in a little water, for 7 to 8 minutes until soft but intact, then set it aside.
Heat the last tablespoon of oil and cook the garlic, ginger and chili for 1 to 2 minutes until they change color.
Pour in the sauce and simmer over high heat for a few minutes until it thickens.
Return the eggplant and peppers, add the basil, toss to coat and simmer on low for 2 minutes.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Veggie Lasagna Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms
instructions: Heat the oven to 400F, remove the portobello stems, scoop out the gills and set the caps on an oiled baking sheet.
Cook the onion, garlic and red pepper in the olive oil for 3 to 4 minutes until soft, then wilt the spinach in it for about 1 minute.
Mix the ricotta, parmesan and egg in a bowl, then stir in the cooked vegetables and chopped basil.
Fill each cap with the ricotta mixture and top with marinara and mozzarella.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the filling is hot and the cheese has melted.
Garnish with a little more basil and serve warm.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Roasted Cauliflower Steaks

lines.text: 2 one-inch thick cauliflower steaks from 1 medium cauliflower
3 tablespoons olive oil, divided (1 for searing, 2 for the romesco)
1 roasted red bell pepper, from a jar

instructions: Blend the roasted pepper, tomato paste, vinegar, hazelnuts, almonds, garlic, paprika, 2 tablespoons of the oil, a pinch of salt and about 1 1/2 tablespoons of water until smooth, then season.
Heat the oven to 400F and cut two 1-inch slices from the cauliflower, keeping the core intact.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a cast iron pan, press the steaks in, season and sear for 2 minutes per side until golden.
Move the pan to the oven and roast for 15 minutes until the cauliflower is tender but still firm.
Spread the romesco on two plates and set a steak on each.
Top with the parsley and toasted pine nuts and season with salt and pepper.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Keto Eggplant Parmesan

lines.text: 2 medium eggplants, cut into 1/2 inch slices
3/4 teaspoon salt, for salting the eggplant

instructions: Lay the eggplant slices on paper towels, salt both sides and leave them for 30 minutes, then pat dry.
Sear the slices in a hot, lightly sprayed skillet for a few minutes on each side and set aside.
Heat the oven to 400F. Spread 1/2 cup marinara in a sprayed casserole dish, add a layer of eggplant, then 1/2 cup marinara, 1/2 cup parmesan and a sprinkle of italian seasoning.
Repeat for a second layer. Finish with eggplant, the last 1/2 cup marinara, all the mozzarella and more italian seasoning.
Bake for 30 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Tofu Bhurji

lines.text: 1/2 red or yellow onion, finely chopped
14 oz firm tofu, lightly squeezed and crumbled

instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat, add the onion and cook for 3 minutes until it starts to turn golden.
Add the garlic, green chilli and a pinch of salt and cook for 2 minutes until golden.
Stir in the turmeric, cumin and black pepper, then add the tomato with 1/4 teaspoon salt and cook for a minute to soften.
Add the cilantro, the crumbled tofu and the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt, mix well, cover and cook for 2 minutes.
Sprinkle in the kala namak, stir for a few seconds, take off the heat and let it sit for a minute before serving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Dubu Jorim

lines.text: 1 pack (about 18 oz) firm tofu, cut into 1/2-inch slices

instructions: Cut the tofu into 1/2-inch rectangles and pat them dry with a paper towel.
Mix the soy sauce, water, sesame oil, gochugaru, sesame seeds, garlic and scallions into a sauce.
Heat the oil in a large non-stick skillet and sear the tofu over medium to medium-high heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side until lightly golden.
Spoon the sauce over the tofu, lifting the edges so it runs underneath, and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes.
Flip the pieces, simmer another minute or two while spooning the sauce over, and serve warm.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Stracciatella Soup

lines.text: 1/2 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste

instructions: Bring the chicken broth and thyme to a gentle simmer in a large pot, then season with salt and white pepper.
Stir in the spinach and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until just wilted.
Whisk the eggs with the parmesan, parsley, a pinch of salt, white pepper and the nutmeg until smooth.
Lower the heat, stir the broth in a circle and drizzle in the egg mixture in a thin stream. Cook 1 to 2 minutes until just set.
Ladle into bowls and top with a little more parmesan and parsley.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Lebanese Cabbage Salad
instructions: Whisk the olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, garlic and salt in a large bowl.
Shred the cabbage and dice the tomatoes. Slice the radishes and green onions thinly.
Chop the parsley, mint and dill.
Add the cabbage, tomatoes, radishes, green onions and herbs to the dressing and toss gently.
Taste and add more lemon juice or salt, then serve right away or chill for up to 4 hours.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Greek Zucchini Tots

lines.text: 1 lb / 500 g zucchini, grated and sweated with 1/4 tsp salt
3/4 cup almond flour (low-carb swap for the plain flour and panko)
3/4 cup finely sliced green onion, white and pale green parts
3/4 cup plain Greek yogurt, for the minted yogurt
1 tbsp olive oil (1/2 tbsp stirred into the yogurt, the rest sprayed on the tots)

instructions: Grate the zucchini, toss it with a little salt in a colander and leave it to sweat for 30 minutes.
Squeeze the zucchini a handful at a time to remove as much water as you can.
Mix the zucchini with the almond flour, eggs, green onion, parmesan, oregano and garlic, then gently fold in the feta.
Dollop heaped tablespoons onto two lined trays and shape each into a short cylinder.
Spray with olive oil and bake at 200C / 390F for 30 minutes, swapping the trays at about 20 minutes, until golden and crusty.
Stir the yogurt with the mint, lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper and let it rest while the tots bake, then serve alongside.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Japanese Marinated Mushrooms

lines.text: 500 g mushrooms (a mix of maitake, shimeji and nameko in the source)
Red chili flakes, 1/4 teaspoon to taste
5 g fresh basil, cut into ribbons
1 tablespoon soy sauce (the source uses dashi soy sauce and says regular soy sauce works)

instructions: Trim any tough stems from the mushrooms and cut large ones into bite-sized pieces.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over high heat, add the mushrooms, chili flakes and salt and stir-fry for 5 to 6 minutes until browned at the edges.
Mix in the basil until it turns bright green.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the rice vinegar and soy sauce.
Transfer to a lidded container and marinate for at least a day, up to three days.
Plate the mushrooms and garnish with the chopped scallion.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Eggplant Rollatini

lines.text: 2 medium Italian eggplants, cut lengthwise into 10 slices 1/4 inch thick (21 oz sliced)
3/4 teaspoon kosher salt, for the eggplant and the filling
8 oz frozen spinach, heated through and squeezed well

instructions: Slice the eggplants lengthwise into 10 slices, sprinkle with salt and leave for 15 minutes, then pat dry.
Arrange the slices on two lined baking sheets, season, cover tightly with foil and bake at 400F until pliable but not fully cooked.
Beat the egg and mix in the ricotta, pecorino, spinach, garlic, a little salt and pepper.
Spread a little marinara over the bottom of a baking dish, spoon filling onto each slice, roll up and set seam side down in the dish.
Top with the rest of the marinara and the mozzarella, cover tightly with foil and bake about 60 minutes until the eggplant is very tender.
Let the dish stand for 5 minutes and serve with extra pecorino if you like.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Low Carb Green Gazpacho

lines.text: 2 medium cucumbers, cut into 1 inch pieces
1 small white onion (about 70 g), cut into 1 inch pieces
1 medium avocado, cut into 1 inch pieces
2 large celery stalks with leaves, cut into 1 inch pieces
1 cup fresh cilantro, thick stems removed
Extra virgin olive oil for drizzling, 1 tbsp per serving
Sour cream for topping, about 1/2 cup

instructions: Roast the green pepper and jalapeno until charred, then peel, seed and stem them, or use them raw with stems, seeds and membranes removed.
Cut the cucumbers, onion, avocado and celery into 1 inch pieces and pick the parsley and cilantro leaves.
Puree everything except the olive oil and sour cream in batches with the vinegar, salt, black pepper and about a cup of water, scraping down the sides.
Taste and add more salt or pepper if needed.
Pour into a tightly lidded container and chill for 1 to 2 hours.
Serve in bowls drizzled with olive oil and topped with a dollop of sour cream.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Cream of Mushroom Soup

lines.text: 1/2 cup dry wine (the source uses Marsala)
1/2 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley, to serve

instructions: Melt the butter with the oil in a large pot, soften the onion for a few minutes and cook the garlic until fragrant.
Add the mushrooms and half of the thyme and cook for 5 minutes, then pour in the wine and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the broth, salt and pepper, bring to a boil, then simmer on low to medium for 10 to 15 minutes.
Blend about half of the soup with an immersion blender or in a blender until smooth, then return it to the pot.
Reduce the heat to low, stir in the cream and warm gently without boiling, then adjust the salt and pepper.
Stir in the parsley and the remaining thyme and serve warm.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Tomatoes and Burrata with Zucchini Noodles

lines.text: 3 large cloves garlic, halved to flavor the oil
3 balls burrata cheese, cut into quarters
2 tablespoons thinly sliced fresh basil, for garnish

instructions: Trim the zucchini and spiralize it into noodles; halve the cherry tomatoes, quarter the burrata balls and slice the basil.
Warm the olive oil in a large heavy pan over medium heat, add the halved garlic cloves and cook about 1 minute until fragrant without browning, then lift them out.
Add the cherry tomatoes and Italian herb blend and cook about 2 minutes, stirring a few times.
Add the zucchini noodles and cook about 4 minutes, turning them gently, until barely tender and heated through.
Move the noodles and tomatoes to a serving dish, top with the burrata quarters and basil, and serve right away.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Spicy Hunan Steamed Tofu and Mushrooms

lines.text: 3 tablespoons vegetable oil (1 tablespoon for the mushrooms, 2 for the sauce)
salt, to taste (about 1/2 teaspoon in all)
2 tablespoons duo jiao salted chopped chili peppers
2 scallions, finely chopped, white and green parts separated

instructions: Cut the silken tofu in half lengthwise, slice it crosswise into 1/2-inch pieces, fan them out on a heatproof rimmed plate and salt lightly.
Steam the tofu over boiling water for about 10 minutes.
While the tofu steams, brown the oyster mushrooms in 1 tablespoon of the oil in a hot skillet, turning them once, and season with salt.
Pour the liquid off the steamed tofu, lay the mushrooms on top and dust with the white pepper.

Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons oil over low heat, cook the ginger 1 minute, then the garlic 1 minute, then the duo jiao chilies 1 to 2 minutes until the oil turns red; stir in the scallion whites for 10 seconds.
Add 2/3 cup hot water and the soy sauce, bring to a boil and simmer briefly, stir in the scallion greens, pour the sauce over the tofu and mushrooms and serve at once.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Caprese Stuffed Avocado

lines.text: 2 ripe avocados, peeled, seeded and halved
1/2 cup grape or cherry tomatoes, halved
2 tablespoons basil pesto, homemade or store bought
salt and pepper, to season (about 1/4 teaspoon salt)

instructions: Toss the halved tomatoes, mozzarella balls, pesto, garlic, olive oil and a pinch of salt and pepper together in a bowl.
Set the avocado halves on a plate.
Spoon the caprese filling into each avocado half.
Drizzle with the balsamic vinegar, scatter over the chopped basil and serve right away.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Muhammara Dip

lines.text: 3 large red bell peppers, roasted, peeled and seeded
1 cucumber, sliced, for dipping (the source's veggies of choice)

instructions: Heat the oven to 450 F, set the whole red peppers on a baking sheet and roast 20 to 25 minutes until blackened.
Cover the peppers with foil to steam for 10 minutes, then peel off the skins and remove the cores and seeds.
Pulse the pomegranate molasses, cumin, salt, Aleppo flakes, garlic, walnuts, olive oil and lemon juice in a food processor.
Add the peeled peppers and pulse a few more times, leaving some texture.
Taste and adjust with more lemon, garlic, chili, salt or cumin.
Serve with sliced cucumber; it is best fresh and keeps covered in the fridge up to 3 days.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Cauliflower Hash Browns

lines.text: 3 cups riced cauliflower (about 1 1/4 pounds of head, or 1/2 medium head)

instructions: Heat the oven to 400 F with racks in the center and upper third, and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment.
Microwave the riced cauliflower for 2 minutes, spread it on a clean towel to cool 5 minutes, then twist the towel and squeeze out as much moisture as you can.
Beat the egg in a large bowl and stir in the cheddar, Parmesan, salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder and smoked paprika, then mix in the cauliflower.
Divide the mixture into 8 portions, squeeze each into a ball and flatten it into a patty about 1/2 inch thick, spacing them 1 inch apart on the sheet.
Bake on the center rack about 15 minutes, turning the pan halfway, until lightly browned and set.
Move the pan to the upper rack under a low broiler for about 5 minutes until crisp on top, watching closely, then cool 5 minutes to set.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Spicy Asian Cucumber Salad

lines.text: 1 eschalot (French shallot), halved and very thinly sliced
1 cup green onion, green part only, finely sliced

instructions: Smash each cucumber with a rolling pin or meat mallet until the sides split, then halve lengthwise and cut into 2.5 cm (1 inch) pieces.
Toss the cucumber pieces with the salt in a bowl and leave them for 30 minutes to draw out water.
Tip the bowl into a strainer and discard the salty liquid, then return the cucumbers to the bowl.
Whisk the rice vinegar, soy sauce and toasted sesame oil in a small bowl, and taste a little of the chilli crisp to judge how hot it is.
Add the green onion, shallot, sesame seeds, dressing and chilli crisp to the cucumbers and toss for about 30 seconds until the shallot softens.
Serve with a few extra sesame seeds and a spoonful of chilli crisp on top, with plenty of the dressing from the bowl.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Baked Spicy Cabbage
instructions: Heat the oven to 450 F (230 C) and oil a baking sheet.
Quarter the cabbage, discard any wilted outer leaves, then halve each piece with the core still attached to make 8 wedges.
Lay the wedges on the sheet with space between them.
Whisk the oil, lime juice, Sriracha and salt, then brush the glaze over the top of each wedge, turn them and brush the other side, saving a little glaze.
Roast for 15 to 17 minutes until the edges start to brown, then turn the wedges and brush them with the remaining glaze.
Roast for 15 to 17 minutes more until the second side browns, then sprinkle the sesame seeds over the top.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Sichuan Napa Cabbage Stir-fry

lines.text: 1 pound napa cabbage stems, sliced at an angle
4 dried red chilies, deseeded and chopped

instructions: Stir the soy sauce, black vinegar and oyster sauce in a bowl, and mix the cornstarch with 1 tablespoon of water in another.
Heat the canola oil in a wok over medium-low heat and cook the garlic, dried chilies and scallion for 1 minute.
Add the napa cabbage stems, turn the heat to high and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in the sauce and cook for 1 minute, then season with the salt.
Stir the cornstarch slurry, add it to the wok and stir-fry for 1 more minute until the sauce thickens, then serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Zucchini Frittata

lines.text: 2 tablespoons plus 1/4 cup coarsely grated Parmesan
1/4 teaspoon salt and fresh ground pepper

instructions: Scrape the seeds from a large zucchini, dice the flesh to about 1/2 inch pieces and measure 2 cups.
Brown the zucchini in the olive oil in an oven-safe non-stick pan over high heat for about 6 minutes, seasoning with the herb blend, salt and pepper.
Beat the eggs and measure the mozzarella, feta and the 2 tablespoons of Parmesan while the zucchini cooks.
Turn the heat to low, sprinkle the three cheeses over the zucchini for a minute or two, then pour in the eggs and stir gently once.
Cover the pan and cook on low for 10 to 12 minutes until the frittata is barely firm but still slightly wet on top.
Heat the broiler, scatter the 1/4 cup Parmesan on top and broil about 6 inches from the heat for 2 to 3 minutes until browned.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chinese Broccoli with Oyster Sauce

lines.text: 1 bunch Chinese broccoli (gai lan), ends trimmed

instructions: Trim the ends of the Chinese broccoli and halve any very thick stems lengthwise so they cook evenly.
Steam the broccoli, for example in a covered microwave steamer on high for 4 minutes, until the stems are just cooked.
Stack the cooked stalks, cut them into 10 cm (4 inch) lengths and arrange them on a plate.
Stir the corn starch with 6 tablespoons of water in a small saucepan, then add the oyster sauce, dark soy sauce, cooking wine, sesame oil, vegetable oil, garlic and ginger.
Bring the sauce to a boil over medium heat, boil for 30 seconds until it thickens, then drizzle it over the broccoli and serve warm.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Low-Carb Cauliflower Mac and Cheese

lines.text: 1 large head cauliflower, cut into small florets
1 cup shredded mozzarella or Italian blend

instructions: Cut the cauliflower into small florets, cover them in a microwave-safe bowl and steam for 8 to 10 minutes until tender, or boil them for 5 minutes.
Heat the olive oil and butter in a large pan over medium-high heat and cook the diced onion for 3 to 5 minutes until it starts to brown.
Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds, then pour in the milk and add the cheddar, mozzarella, parmesan and cream cheese.
Stir until the cheeses are fully melted and the sauce is smooth, then season with the salt and pepper.
Add the steamed cauliflower, mix well and simmer for 3 to 5 minutes until the florets are as soft as you like.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Crustless Quiche Lorraine

lines.text: 6 strips center-cut bacon, cooked and chopped

instructions: Heat the oven to 350 F and grease a pie dish with a little oil.
Cook the bacon in a frying pan over medium heat, turning now and then, until browned, then drain it and chop it into 1/2-inch pieces.
Spread the bacon in the dish and top it with the grated Gruyere.
Whisk the milk, half and half, eggs, salt, pepper and nutmeg together and pour the custard over the bacon.
Scatter the chives on top and bake for 35 minutes until the center is set.
Cut the quiche into 6 pieces and serve warm.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Low-Carb Pepperoni Pizza with Fathead Crust

lines.text: 3 cups shredded mozzarella (1 1/2 cups for the dough, 1 1/2 cups for the topping)
2 ounces full-fat cream cheese, cut into chunks
1 tablespoon olive oil, for handling the dough
20 slices pepperoni — use HORMEL Original Pepperoni Slices (US)
1 small garlic clove, to rub on the crust

instructions: Heat the oven to 425 F with one rack at the bottom and one in the upper third.
Microwave 1 1/2 cups of the mozzarella with the cream cheese for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, stirring halfway, until molten.
Scrape the cheese into a food processor, add the egg and process, then add the almond flour and process until a sticky dough forms.
With oiled hands or a rolling pin between parchment sheets, shape the dough on a lined sheet pan and prick it all over with a fork.
Bake the crust for 8 to 10 minutes until golden brown, then rub it with the cut garlic clove.
Spread on the pizza sauce, add the remaining mozzarella and the pepperoni, and bake until the cheese melts. Cut into 6 pieces.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Meatball Parm and Kale Casserole

lines.text: 1 cup shredded mozzarella for the meatballs plus 6 ounces for the topping

instructions: Grate the zucchini, press it in a strainer to remove as much moisture as you can, and heat the oven to 400 F.
Mix the turkey, sausage, 1 cup mozzarella, parmesan, zucchini, egg, garlic powder, onion powder, basil, salt and pepper until just combined.
Roll the mixture into golf-ball-sized meatballs and set them in a casserole dish.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until almost cooked through, then drain off any excess moisture.
Tuck the kale around the meatballs, pour the tomato sauce over them and cover with the remaining mozzarella.
Bake again for 10 to 12 minutes until the cheese melts, then broil for 2 to 3 minutes to crisp the top if you like.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Keto Shepherd's Pie
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat, add the lamb, garlic, Italian seasoning and salt, and cook, stirring, until the meat is browned.
Stir in the tomatoes, zucchini and celery and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring now and then.
Steam the cauliflower florets over boiling water in a covered pot for 8 to 10 minutes until tender.
Blend the cauliflower in a food processor with the cream cheese, cheddar and cream until smooth.
Heat the oven to 350 F, spread the meat mixture in a baking dish and cover it with the cauliflower mash.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the topping starts to brown.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Keto Cheeseburger Casserole with Bacon

lines.text: 1 pound no-sugar bacon, cooked and chopped (about 5 oz cooked)

instructions: Cook the chopped bacon in a cast-iron skillet until crisp, drain off the fat and set the bacon aside.
Brown the ground beef with the garlic and onion powder over medium-high heat, then drain off the excess fat.
Spread the beef over the bottom of an oven-safe skillet and stir the bacon pieces into it.
Whisk the eggs, tomato paste, cream, salt and pepper until smooth, then stir in 8 ounces of the cheddar.
Pour the egg mixture over the beef and bacon and sprinkle the remaining 4 ounces of cheddar on top.
Bake at 350 F for 30 to 35 minutes, until golden brown on top and set in the middle.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Keto Taco Casserole

lines.text: 1 can (10 ounces) diced tomatoes with green chilies (Rotel)

instructions: Heat the oven to 375 F. Brown the ground beef in the avocado oil over medium-high heat until almost cooked.
Add the onion, garlic and chili powder and cook until the beef is done and the onion has softened.
Lower the heat to medium, add the tomatoes with green chilies, zucchini, olives and riced cauliflower, cover and simmer until the zucchini and cauliflower soften.
Spoon the beef mixture into a casserole dish with a slotted spoon, leaving most of the liquid behind, and top with the shredded cheese.
Bake for 10 minutes, until the cheese has melted.
Dollop the sour cream over the top and scatter with cilantro before serving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Keto Sloppy Joes

lines.text: 1/2 cup tomato puree or tomato sauce
8 large butter lettuce leaves, for serving as cups (the source also offers keto buns)

instructions: Heat the avocado oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat, add the onion and salt and cook about 5 minutes until softened.
Add the ground beef and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, just until it loses its raw pink color.
Stir in the garlic, chili powder, monk fruit sweetener, ketchup, tomato sauce, water and hot sauce.
Simmer about 8 minutes, until the sauce has slightly thickened.
Spoon the meat into the butter lettuce leaves and serve right away.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Keto Chicken Pot Pie Casserole

lines.text: 1 1/4 cups heavy whipping cream (1/4 cup in the topping, 1 cup in the sauce)
1 teaspoon garlic powder, divided between topping and sauce
1 cup frozen green beans, partially thawed
2 pounds boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces

instructions: Heat the oven to 350 F. Boil the broccoli and cauliflower in a little water for 5 minutes, then rinse and drain.
Toss the broccoli, cauliflower and green beans together in a 9 by 13 inch casserole dish.
Mix the almond flour, egg, 1/4 cup of the cream, half the garlic powder, baking powder and a pinch of salt into a thick biscuit topping.
Cook the chicken pieces in the olive oil in a high-sided skillet with salt and pepper until no longer pink in the center.
Stir in the broth, remaining cream and remaining garlic powder and cook the sauce down until it thickens, then take it off the heat and stir in the Parmesan.
Pour the chicken and sauce over the vegetables and toss, then spread the biscuit topping thinly over the top.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until the topping is browned and the filling is bubbling.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Loaded Cauliflower Casserole
instructions: Heat the oven to 425 F. Put the cauliflower in an 8 by 8 inch baking dish and toss with the melted butter, salt, onion powder, garlic powder and pepper.
Roast for 20 minutes, until the cauliflower is fork tender.
Stir the cream, sour cream, cheddar, bacon, cream cheese and green onion together in a bowl.
Spread the cheese mixture over the roasted cauliflower.
Return to the oven for 8 to 10 minutes, until the cheese has melted.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Keto Reuben Skillet Meal

lines.text: 2 ounces dill pickle, served on the side

instructions: Drain the sauerkraut and squeeze out as much liquid as you can.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium-low heat and fry the corned beef 1 to 2 minutes per side until slightly crisp.
Stir the sour cream, mayonnaise and Dijon mustard together in a small bowl.
Spread the sauerkraut over the corned beef, dollop the sauce on top and lay the Swiss cheese over it.
Cover the pan if needed and let the cheese melt, then spoon out portions and serve with the dill pickle on the side.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Keto Ham and Cheese Stromboli
instructions: Heat the oven to 400F and melt the mozzarella in the microwave or a toaster oven, stirring until smooth.
Mix the almond flour, coconut flour, Italian seasoning, salt and pepper in a bowl and work in the melted mozzarella.
Once the cheese has cooled slightly, stir in the egg to make a moist dough.
Flatten the dough between two sheets of parchment, then cut diagonal strips from the edges toward a 4 inch uncut centre.
Lay the ham and cheddar down the centre, then fold the strips over the filling one at a time.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes until golden, then slice and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Almond and Parmesan Baked Fish

lines.text: 4 cod fillets, about 6 ounces each and at least 1/2 inch thick
1 teaspoon OLD BAY Classic Seasoning (US 6 oz) instead of unspecified fish rub

instructions: Heat the oven to 425F and spray a baking dish with non-stick spray.
Melt the butter over low heat and let it cool slightly.
Mix the almond flour, Parmesan, garlic powder, pepper and fish rub in a flat bowl wide enough to hold a fillet.
Dip each fillet in the butter, turning to coat both sides, then press it into the almond mixture so the crumb sticks.
Lay the fillets in the dish and bake about 20 minutes, until the fish feels firm and the coating turns golden brown.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Easy Jalapeño Poppers
instructions: Heat the oven to 400F, halve the jalapeños, scoop out the seeds and membranes and set them on a baking sheet.
Crisp the bacon if it is not cooked already, then crumble it.
Stir the cream cheese, cheddar, 4 strips of crumbled bacon, chives, garlic, salt and pepper together until combined.
Spoon the filling into the pepper halves.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes until lightly golden, then top with the remaining bacon and extra chives and serve warm.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Loaded Cauliflower Potato Salad

lines.text: 2 pounds cauliflower, cut into small pieces
7 slices bacon, fried crisp and cut into strips

instructions: Steam the small cauliflower pieces 5 to 6 minutes until soft, then drain them in a colander without rinsing and let them cool and dry.
Cut the bacon into short strips, fry until very crisp and drain on paper towels.
Hard-boil the eggs, cool them and chop them coarsely.
Whisk the mayonnaise, yellow mustard, 1 teaspoon of the onion powder, salt and pepper into a dressing.
Put the dry cauliflower in a bowl, top with the eggs, season with the remaining onion powder, salt and pepper, then add the dressing and fold gently.
Stir in the bacon, cheddar and green onion, saving a little to garnish, and serve now or chill for a few hours.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Keto Chicken Broccoli Casserole with Cream Cheese
instructions: Slice the chicken into bite-sized pieces, season with the salt and heat the oven to 350 F.
Cook the chicken with the garlic in the olive oil and butter over medium heat until no longer pink.
Stir in the mushrooms, lemon juice, cream cheese, sour cream, broth and broccoli.
Cook and stir over medium heat for about 8 minutes until the cream cheese melts into a sauce.
Pour into a 9x13 inch casserole dish and sprinkle the parmesan over the top.
Bake for 20 minutes, until bubbling and lightly browned.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Ground Turkey Cauliflower Casserole
instructions: Heat the oven to 400 F and rice the cauliflower; it does not need cooking first.
Brown the turkey in a skillet and season with the garlic powder and onion powder.
Stir in the cauliflower, cream cheese, butter, cream, and half of the cheddar and mozzarella until combined.
Pour into a casserole dish and sprinkle the remaining cheddar and mozzarella on top.
Bake for 30 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbling.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Instant Pot Easy Keto Lasagna Soup
instructions: Brown the beef with the onion and garlic in the olive oil on the Instant Pot saute setting until no longer pink.
Stir in the tomatoes, tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce and Italian seasoning.
Add the chicken broth and cauliflower rice and stir.
Seal the lid and pressure cook on high for 5 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then vent the rest.
Ladle into bowls and top with the ricotta and mozzarella.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Keto Pot Roast (Instant Pot, Slow Cooker)
instructions: Drizzle the olive oil over the chuck roast and rub the salt and pepper over every side.
Brown the roast on all sides in a very hot skillet, then set it aside to rest.
Brown the onion, celery and turnips in the same skillet, scraping up the browned juices.
Put the vegetables in the bottom of the slow cooker and set the roast on top.
Pour in the beef broth, add the rosemary and thyme, and cook on low for 6 hours until the meat is very tender.
Whisk the xanthan gum into a cup of the cooking liquid, let it thicken, and serve over the sliced roast.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Zuppa Toscana

lines.text: 3 thick slices bacon, cut into short strips
1 package (19.5 ounces) hot or mild Italian sausage

instructions: Cook the bacon in a large soup pot over medium-high heat until crisp, lift it out and pour off some of the fat.
Cook the onion in the pot until starting to brown, then add the garlic for 1 to 2 minutes.
Squeeze the sausage out of its casings into the pot and brown it, breaking it up, for 10 to 15 minutes.
Add the cauliflower, broth, red pepper flakes and bacon, bring to a low boil and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes.
Add the kale and cook on medium for 5 to 10 minutes until it is as soft as you like.
Let the soup cool a few minutes off the boil, then stir in the cream and heat it through gently without boiling.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Keto Cheeseburger Soup

lines.text: 1 cup diced daikon radish (the low-carb stand-in for potato)

instructions: Brown the ground beef in a large stock pot over medium heat, then move it to a plate.
Melt the butter in the same pot and cook the onion, red pepper and celery for 3 to 5 minutes until softened.
Return the beef to the pot with the daikon and stir to combine.
Pour in the chicken broth, bring to a boil, then turn down and simmer on low for 10 to 12 minutes.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the cream, cheddar and salt until the cheese melts.
Ladle into bowls and top with the crumbled bacon.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Low-Carb Keto Meatloaf

lines.text: 3/4 cup crushed pork rinds (the low-carb stand-in for breadcrumbs)

instructions: Heat the oven to 350 F and lightly oil a 5 by 9 inch loaf pan or line it with foil.
Combine the beef, dried onion, crushed pork rinds, tomato paste, vinegar, eggs, Worcestershire sauce, basil, olive oil, salt and pepper in a large bowl and mix until blended.
Pat the mixture into a loaf shape in the pan.
Bake until a thermometer in the center reads 165 F, about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes.
Drain the fat from the pan and let the meatloaf rest for 10 minutes before slicing.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Keto Cheddar Biscuits

lines.text: 1 cup almond flour (the low-carb stand-in for wheat flour)

instructions: Heat the oven to 350 F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Microwave the mozzarella and cream cheese in 30-second bursts, stirring, until melted and smooth.
Beat the cheese with the almond flour, baking powder, garlic powder, egg, cheddar, oregano, basil, parsley and a pinch of salt on high until well combined.
Wet your hands, shape the dough into 8 even balls and flatten them slightly on the baking sheet.
Bake for 15 minutes until lightly browned.
Let the biscuits cool a few minutes before serving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Low Carb Keto Fried Chicken in an Air Fryer or Oven

lines.text: 2 cups crushed pork rinds (the low-carb stand-in for flour)

instructions: Put the chicken in a large bowl, pour over the almond milk mixed with the vinegar and soak it in the refrigerator for 2 hours.
Mix the crushed pork rinds with the thyme, oregano, basil, celery salt, pepper, paprika, mustard and garlic salt in a wide shallow dish.
Heat the oven to 350 F and set a rack in a baking pan.
Dip each piece of chicken in the pork rind mixture until coated and arrange it on the rack.
Bake for about 50 minutes until a thermometer in the thickest part reads 165 F.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Keto Chicken Fried Steak

lines.text: 1/2 cup almond flour (the low-carb stand-in for wheat flour)
1 cup ground pork rinds (the low-carb stand-in for breadcrumbs)
1/2 cup low-sodium chicken broth, up to 1 cup for a thinner gravy

instructions: Season both sides of each cubed steak with salt and pepper.
Set out three shallow bowls: almond flour, eggs whisked with 2 tablespoons water, and ground pork rinds mixed with the garlic powder.
Coat each steak in almond flour, then egg, then the pork rind mixture, pressing it on both sides.

Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a skillet over medium heat and fry 2 steaks about 3 minutes per side until they reach 145 F inside, then rest them on a clean plate for 3 minutes. Repeat with the rest of the butter and steaks.
Whisk the cream and 1/2 cup broth into the skillet and simmer until reduced, adding more broth to thin it, then serve over the steaks.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Jeyuk Bokkeum

lines.text: 2 pounds thinly sliced pork shoulder or butt

instructions: Slice the pork thinly if it is not already sliced, and slice the onion and cut the scallions into 2-inch pieces.
Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, rice wine, sesame oil, garlic and ginger in a large bowl until smooth.
Add the pork, onion and scallions and toss until every slice is coated, then leave to marinate for about 30 minutes.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and fry the pork in 2 batches so it browns rather than steams.
Cook until the edges are slightly caramelized and the pork is cooked through, adjusting the heat if the marinade starts to scorch, then serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Steamed Eggs with Crispy Pork

lines.text: 150 ml chicken stock (equal volume to the eggs)
150 ml water (equal volume to the eggs)

instructions: Mix the ground pork with the Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, dark soy sauce, ginger and cornstarch and marinate for 15 to 20 minutes.
Beat the eggs, then stir in the water, stock and sesame oil until evenly mixed.
Pour the egg mixture into a heatproof dish and steam over high heat for 3 minutes.
Turn off the heat and leave the dish covered for about 14 minutes so the custard finishes setting gently.
Fry the marinated pork in the vegetable oil until crisp and browned, then stir in the scallion.
Spoon the crispy pork over the steamed eggs and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Pork Lettuce Wrap

lines.text: 1 can (3.5 ounces) water chestnuts, small diced
10 to 12 lettuce leaves (iceberg, Bibb, butterhead or romaine)

instructions: Stir the oyster sauce, hoisin sauce, and Shaoxing wine together in a small bowl.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the peanut oil in a large skillet, spread the ground pork in an even layer and cook without touching for 2 to 3 minutes until browned on the bottom.
Flip the pork and chop it into smaller pieces, cook until golden, then push it to one side of the pan.
Add the remaining oil, onion, garlic and ginger to the empty side, cook for 2 minutes, then mix everything together.
Add the water chestnuts, red pepper and the sauce, and cook for about 2 minutes until the vegetables soften.
Spoon the filling into the lettuce leaves, top with the peanuts and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: West Lake Beef Soup

lines.text: 2 teaspoons cornstarch for the beef plus 1/4 cup cornstarch for the slurry

instructions: Mix the ground beef with 1/2 teaspoon salt, the Shaoxing wine and 1 teaspoon cornstarch and set it aside to marinate.
Bring a small pot of water to a boil, add the beef, turn the heat to low and break it apart until it just turns pale, then drain.
Bring the stock and ginger to a boil, add the mushrooms and tofu and simmer for 3 minutes.
Stir 1/4 cup cornstarch into 1/4 cup water until dissolved, pour it in and stir at once until the soup thickens.
Reduce to low heat and pour in the beaten egg white in a very thin stream, then stir gently to break it into ribbons.
Stir in the beef, scallion, remaining salt and white pepper, turn off the heat and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Shrimp Curry

lines.text: 1 pound large shrimp, peeled and deveined
2 tablespoons freshly squeezed lemon juice in total
1 tablespoon plus 2 teaspoons curry powder in total
2 red bell peppers, cored and thinly sliced

instructions: Toss the shrimp with 1 tablespoon of the lemon juice and 2 teaspoons of the curry powder and leave for 15 minutes.
Sear the shrimp in 1 tablespoon of the olive oil for about 3 minutes until just opaque, then move them to a plate.
Cook the onion in the remaining oil for about 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, turmeric and remaining curry powder and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the red peppers, crushed tomatoes and coconut milk and simmer partly covered for 15 to 20 minutes until thickened.
Stir in the remaining lemon juice, the cilantro and the shrimp with their juices and heat through before serving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Winter Melon Soup with Meatballs

lines.text: 1/2 teaspoon salt, split between the meatballs and the soup
1 1/2 to 2 lbs winter melon, peeled and seeded

instructions: Mix the ground pork with the Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, ginger, half the salt, egg white and 2 tablespoons water, then stir in the cornstarch until the meat turns pasty and sticky.
Cut the winter melon into pieces, slice off the rind, remove the soft seedy centre and cut the flesh into even 1 cm bite-size slices.
Bring the chicken stock to a boil, lower to medium-low and drop in the pork mixture a tablespoon at a time as meatballs, then cook for 1 minute after the last one.
Lift the meatballs onto a plate, they will still be raw inside, then add the winter melon, bring the stock to a boil and cook on medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes until the edges turn translucent.
Return the meatballs, bring the soup back to a boil for 1 minute, turn off the heat, cover and leave it for 5 minutes so they finish gently.
Stir in the remaining salt, taste, and serve hot topped with the cilantro.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chakhokhbili Georgian Chicken with Tomatoes and Herbs

lines.text: 4 chicken leg quarters, legs separated from thighs, skin and bones on
1 tablespoon prepared red adjika: red bell pepper, red chili, garlic, cilantro, purple basil, parsley, salt, blue fenugreek, marigold, coriander and sunflower oil only
1 can (400 g) whole peeled tomatoes, lightly crushed
1/2 teaspoon salt, to season the chicken

instructions: Pat the chicken dry and season with the salt and pepper.
Brown the chicken in the oil in a large pot over medium heat in two batches, 4 to 6 minutes per side, then set it aside.
Pour off all but 2 tablespoons of fat, then soften the onion in the pot for 5 to 7 minutes, scraping up the browned bits.
Stir in the adjika and tomato paste for 2 minutes until the paste darkens, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the crushed tomatoes and their juice, return the chicken with its juices, cover and cook on medium-low for about 45 minutes until tender.
Lift out the chicken, stir the cilantro into the sauce for 5 minutes, season to taste and spoon the sauce over the chicken.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Tandoori Salmon
instructions: Heat the oven to 200 C (390 F) and line a baking tray with foil.
Mix the salt, turmeric, chili powder, garam masala, cumin, coriander, garlic powder and crushed kasuri methi on the tray and make a well in the middle.
Pour the oil and lemon juice into the well and stir, adding a splash of water, until you have a thick smooth paste.
Pat the salmon dry, lay it on the tray and smear the paste over both sides.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, then broil for 3 to 4 minutes until the salmon flakes easily with a fork, and serve with a squeeze of extra lemon.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Larb Gai Thai Chicken Lettuce Wraps

lines.text: 1 lemongrass stalk, white and pale green part finely chopped
2 Thai bird's eye chilies, deseeded and chopped
7 small romaine lettuce leaves, for wrapping

instructions: Stir the lime juice and fish sauce with 3 tablespoons water in a small bowl and set aside.
Heat the peanut oil in a wok over medium-high heat and saute the ginger, garlic, lemongrass and chilies for about 1 minute without letting the garlic burn.
Add the ground chicken, turn the heat to high and break it into small pieces, cooking 3 to 4 minutes until almost cooked through.
Pour in the lime and fish sauce and cook for 1 minute, coating the chicken.
Take the wok off the heat and stir in the red onion, cilantro and mint.
Spoon the chicken into the lettuce leaves and serve with extra herbs.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Sri Lankan Devilled Prawns

lines.text: 1/2 teaspoon plus 1 teaspoon crushed black pepper
2 small capsicum (bell peppers), cut into chunks

instructions: Toss the prawns with the 1/2 teaspoon pepper, lemon juice and a pinch of salt and leave them for 10 minutes.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the prawns for 2 minutes until just cooked, then set them aside.
Heat the remaining oil, add the garlic, ginger, green chilies and curry leaves and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in the chili flakes and the 1 teaspoon pepper for 15 seconds.
Add the onions and capsicum and stir-fry for 2 minutes so they stay crisp.
Return the prawns, add the tomato, toss for 1 minute, season with salt and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Fish a la Talla

lines.text: 4 skin-on red snapper fillets, about 6 ounces each
6 medium dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded

instructions: Roast the unpeeled garlic in a dry skillet over medium heat until soft with blackened spots, then cool and peel it.
Toast the guajillo and arbol chiles for a few seconds on each side against the hot skillet until fragrant.
Soak the chiles in hot water for 30 minutes under a weighted plate, and light the charcoal fire about 20 minutes before grilling.
Drain the chiles, keeping 1/2 cup of the water, then blend them with the garlic, oregano and pepper, strain the adobo and season it with salt.
Oil a hinged grill basket and the fish, salt the fillets and grill them skin side up for 4 to 5 minutes.
Flip the basket, spread the adobo over the fish and dot it with mayonnaise thinned with the milk, then grill until the skin is crisp.
Move the fish to a platter and serve at once with lime wedges.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Rolled Stuffed Flank Steak with Garlicky Herb Sauce

lines.text: 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus 1/2 cup for the herb sauce
2 links (about 6 ounces) fresh chorizo, removed from casings
2 1/2 cups loosely packed fresh cilantro leaves, split between the paste and the sauce
2 1/2 cups loosely packed fresh Italian parsley leaves, split between the paste and the sauce
1 small red bell pepper, cut into 1/4-inch strips

instructions: Crumble the chorizo into a skillet with 1 tablespoon of the oil and cook it through, then drain and cool it.
Butterfly the flank steak by scoring it down the middle and cutting flaps out to the edges, pound it to about 1/2 inch, then season with salt and brush with 2 tablespoons oil.
Chop half of the cilantro and parsley with the garlic into a chunky herb paste.
Brush the steak with mustard, spread the paste leaving a 1-inch border, then line up the egg, chorizo, carrot and pepper, roll it up and tie it with twine.
Grill the roll over direct heat for about 2 minutes per side to brown it on all four sides.
Move the roll to indirect heat, cover and turn occasionally for 25 to 30 minutes, until the centre reads 115 degrees F.
Chop the rest of the cilantro and parsley with the garlic, and stir in the vinegar, salt and 1/2 cup oil for the sauce.
Rest the steak, untie it and slice it on a slight bias, then drizzle with the herb sauce.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Mille-Feuille Nabe
instructions: Mix the dashi, sake, soy sauce and salt in a bowl for the broth.
Slice the ginger and the scallion thinly.
Quarter the cabbage lengthwise, wash the leaves and tuck a pork belly slice between each pair, keeping the core attached.
Cut off the cores and cut each wedge into stacks 2 to 2 1/2 inches long.
Pack the stacks on their sides into a pot in tight circles, tuck in the ginger and pour in the broth.

Cover and bring to a boil over medium-high heat, skim the scum, then simmer on medium-low for 8 to 10 minutes until the cabbage is tender and the pork is cooked, and scatter the scallion over the top.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Beef Negimaki

lines.text: 2 teaspoons granular monk fruit sweetener, in place of the sugar

instructions: Trim the scallions and cut them a little wider than the beef slices, splitting any thicker than 1/4 inch.
Lay out a beef slice, put scallions along one side and roll tightly, then repeat with the remaining beef and scallions.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium-high heat and brown the rolls seam side down, turning them until every side is browned.
Blot the excess oil from the pan with a paper towel.
Add the sake, soy sauce and sweetener and roll the beef in the pan until the sauce thickens into a glaze, then top with sesame seeds.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Karniyarik

lines.text: 300 g double-ground beef, rib or brisket cut
1 1/2 teaspoons salt, including extra for the eggplants

instructions: Peel the eggplants in stripes, prick them with a knife, salt them lightly and shallow-fry in sunflower oil until browned and soft. Drain on a sieve.
Brown the beef in a pan, add the diced onions with half the salt and pepper and cook until the onions are soft and golden.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and vinegar and cook 1 to 2 minutes. Take off the heat and mix in most of the parsley.
Set the fried eggplants in a baking dish, cut a slit down each without cutting through, press them open and salt the insides lightly.
Spoon the beef filling into each eggplant and set the quartered tomatoes and green peppers alongside.
Bake at 220C (430F) for 15 to 20 minutes until bubbling and lightly roasted, then scatter with the remaining parsley.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Sizzling Liempo Sisig

lines.text: 1 1/2 tablespoons soy sauce (in place of liquid seasoning)
1 tablespoon butter, for the sizzling plate

instructions: Boil the pork belly in 4 cups of water over medium heat for 25 minutes, drain and let it cool.
Grill the pork belly 4 to 5 minutes per side, then cut it into cubes.
Mince the onions and the grilled pork in a food processor.
Pan-fry the chicken liver 3 to 5 minutes per side in some of the oil, then mince it.
Soften the onion in the remaining oil, add the pork and cook 3 minutes, then add the liver and cook 5 to 7 minutes more.
Stir in the soy sauce, pepper, garlic powder and chili, cook 2 to 3 minutes, then mix in the mayonnaise over high heat for 3 minutes.
Heat a sizzling plate, melt the butter on it, pile on the sisig and serve with lemon.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Sate Lilit

lines.text: 1 teaspoon sea salt (1/2 in the paste, 1/2 in the fish)

instructions: Pound the turmeric, ginger, shallots, garlic, chili, shrimp paste and candlenut to a fine paste in a mortar or pulse in a food processor.
Fry the paste in a little oil over medium heat, stirring constantly, with a few lime leaves and a pounded lemongrass stalk, for a few minutes. Cool and remove the leaves and lemongrass.
Mix the minced fish with 2 tablespoons of the cooled paste, the chopped lime leaves, the salt and the coconut milk until thoroughly combined.
Wrap the fish mixture around the root end of each cleaned lemongrass stalk.
Grill over a hot, lightly oiled grill about 6 minutes, turning only once the first side releases, until golden on all sides.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Beef Tomato Stir-fry

lines.text: 1 pound flank steak, sliced 1/4 inch thick
3 1/2 teaspoons cornstarch (2 for the marinade, 1 1/2 for the slurry)
3 scallions, whites and greens, cut in 2-inch pieces
2 pounds ripe tomatoes, in bite-size wedges

instructions: Toss the beef with water, 2 teaspoons of the cornstarch, 1 teaspoon of the oil and the oyster sauce and marinate 30 minutes to 1 hour. Stir the soy sauce and sesame oil together as the sauce.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok until smoking, sear the beef about 1 minute until 80 percent cooked and set it aside.
Add the rest of the oil over medium heat, frizzle the ginger 10 seconds, then add the garlic and scallion whites for 10 seconds and fry the ketchup 30 seconds.
Add the tomato wedges in one layer and sear 15 seconds, pour in the Shaoxing wine and stir-fry 10 seconds, then push the tomatoes to one side.
Pour the sauce into the cleared space and stir until bubbling.
Return the beef and stir-fry 20 seconds on high heat.
Add the scallion greens and the remaining cornstarch mixed with a tablespoon of water a little at a time, cook 15 seconds and serve at once.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Basque-Style Scrambled Eggs
instructions: Dice the onion, chop the pepper and garlic, cube the zucchini, grate the tomatoes, and whisk the eggs with the parsley, salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil over low-medium heat, add the onion, green pepper and garlic and cook about 5 minutes until the onion is translucent.
Add the zucchini and cook another 5 minutes until translucent.
Stir in the grated tomato, season with salt and pepper and simmer about 4 minutes until thickened.
Turn the heat to medium, pour in the whisked eggs and stir constantly for about 3 minutes until cooked through, then serve at once.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Rump Cap Roast (Picanha)

lines.text: 2 kg / 4 lb beef rump cap (picanha), silver skin trimmed off
3/4 tsp kosher salt for the butter
3 tsp finely minced garlic (3 to 4 cloves)
1 tsp deseeded, finely minced large red chilli

instructions: Heat the oven to 140C / 285F. Pat the rump cap dry and score the fat cap in 2.5 cm diamonds, cutting into the fat but not the meat.
Rub the meat with 2 teaspoons of the salt and half the pepper, then rub the remaining salt and pepper into the fat cap.
Set the beef on a rack over a tray and roast until the middle reads 48C, 70 to 90 minutes.
While it roasts, melt the butter with the kosher salt, cook the garlic and chilli for 30 seconds, then take it off the heat and cool 5 minutes. Stir in the parsley and lemon juice.
Rest the roast uncovered for 30 to 40 minutes. Halfway through, heat the broiler as high as it goes and brown the fat cap 2 to 3 minutes, watching closely.
Slice the beef 8 mm thick and serve with the warm chimichurri butter spooned over.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Steamed Red Curry Fish (Haw Mok Plaa)

lines.text: 500 g / 1 lb cod fillets, cut into small pieces

instructions: Soften the banana leaves over a flame, cut 12 rounds of 18 cm, stack them in pairs and fold each pair into a square cup held with toothpicks.
Whisk the curry paste, coconut milk, fish sauce and eggs in a bowl, add the cod and stir hard for 5 minutes until the mixture thickens.
Warm the coconut cream with the sea salt in a small pan on low heat, whisking until it thickens.
Layer cabbage and Thai basil in each cup, spoon in the fish mixture, and top with the coconut cream.
Scatter lime leaves and red chilli over the cups and steam over boiling water for 25 to 30 minutes until the fish is cooked through.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chicken Tikka Kebab

lines.text: 2 pounds boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 large red onion, cut into 1-inch pieces

instructions: Whisk the yogurt, tomato paste, olive oil, garlic and ginger in a large bowl, then whisk in the turmeric, garam masala, cumin and salt.
Stir the chicken into the marinade, cover and refrigerate for 1 to 4 hours.
Thread the chicken and red onion onto metal skewers, with a piece of onion between each chicken cube.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium and lightly oil the grates.
Grill the kebabs, turning, until charred all over and the chicken reaches 165F, 22 to 25 minutes in total.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Turkish Eggs
instructions: Stir the Greek yogurt with the grated garlic and salt, then set it aside.
Melt the butter in a small pan over medium-low heat, stir in the Aleppo pepper and paprika for a minute, then turn off the heat.
Crack each egg into a small strainer over a bowl to drain off the thin white, then tip each one into its own ramekin.
Bring a wide pot of water to a simmer, stir in the vinegar and turn the heat down so only a few bubbles rise. Slide in the eggs, spaced well apart, and poach for 3 minutes.
Lift the eggs out with a slotted spoon onto a paper towel.
Spread the yogurt on two plates, set the eggs on top, drizzle with the spiced butter and scatter the dill.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Egg Bhurji
instructions: Whisk the eggs with a fork in a bowl and set aside.
Heat the ghee in a pan over medium heat and fry the ginger and green chili for a minute until the ginger turns light golden.
Add the onion and cook for 2 minutes, then the red pepper for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato and cook for 2 minutes, then add the garam masala and salt and cook for 1 minute more.
Add the peas and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the eggs and keep stirring for about 5 minutes until they are fully set, then fold in the coriander.
Serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Baked Eggs with Mushrooms
instructions: Heat the oven to 200C (390F) and lightly grease four 300 ml ramekins.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the mushrooms for 3 minutes until golden at the edges.
Add the garlic, thyme and salt and cook for 1 more minute.
Stir in the spinach for 30 seconds until just wilted, then divide the mixture among the ramekins.
Make a small dent in each, crack in an egg, drizzle with cream and top with Parmesan.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until the whites are just set, taking them out slightly underdone, then scatter with chives and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Egg Muffins

lines.text: 1 cup lightly packed baby spinach, chopped
3/4 cup finely diced red bell pepper
3/4 cup finely diced green bell pepper

instructions: Heat the oven to 350F (175C) with a rack in the center and coat a 12-cup muffin tin with nonstick spray.
Divide the spinach, red pepper, green pepper and tomatoes among the cups until they are about two-thirds full.
Whisk the eggs, egg whites, salt, basil and oregano in a large measuring cup until well combined.
Pour the egg mixture into each cup until it is three-quarters full and sprinkle the feta over the tops.
Bake for 24 to 28 minutes until the muffins are set.
Let them cool for a few minutes, then run a butter knife around each one to loosen it and lift it out.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Almond Flour Pancakes

lines.text: 1 1/3 cups super fine blanched almond flour

instructions: Whisk the almond flour, baking powder and salt together in a large bowl.
Stir in the cream, eggs, almond milk, melted butter, sweetener and vanilla until the batter is smooth.
Heat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat.
Pour 2 to 3 heaping tablespoons of batter per pancake and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the underside is golden.
Flip each pancake and cook for 1 to 2 minutes more, then repeat with the remaining batter.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Zucchini and Feta Omelette from Crete
instructions: Cook the scallions in the olive oil in a 10 to 11 inch non-stick skillet over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until soft.
Add the zucchini rounds with a little salt and cook until softened.
Add the diced tomatoes and cook for 2 to 3 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with the feta, mint and the rest of the salt, pour them into the pan and swirl to mix lightly.
Cover the pan and cook over medium heat for about 10 minutes until the eggs set.
Take the pan off the heat, rest the omelette for 5 minutes, then slide it out and cut into wedges.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Sausage, Kale, and Mozzarella Egg Bake
instructions: Heat the oven to 375F and spray a 9 by 12 inch casserole dish with nonstick spray.
Cut the sausage in half lengthwise, then slice it into half-moons about 3/8 inch thick.
Brown the sausage in 1 teaspoon of the olive oil in a large pan and put it in the bottom of the dish.
Wilt the baby kale in the other teaspoon of oil for about 2 minutes and spread it over the sausage.
Sprinkle the green onions and mozzarella over the kale, season with pepper, pour the beaten eggs over and stir gently with a fork so everything is coated.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, depending on how brown you like it, and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Keto Low Carb Cloud Bread Loaf

lines.text: 3/4 cup whey protein powder (a low-carb flour stand-in) — use NOW Sports Whey Protein Isolate Unflavored

instructions: Heat the oven to 300F and grease a loaf pan.
Whip the egg whites with the cream of tartar until stiff peaks form, which takes 10 to 15 minutes. Set aside.
Whisk the yolks with the sour cream, baking powder, salt, whey protein powder, garlic powder and onion powder until smooth.
Fold a little of the egg whites at a time into the yolk mixture until everything is combined.
Pour the batter into the pan and bake on the middle shelf for 50 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Turn the oven off and leave the loaf inside with the door shut for 10 minutes, then cool it completely and toast the slices.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chicharrones con Huevos

lines.text: 2 medium jalapeno peppers, deseeded and finely diced

instructions: Finely dice the tomato, jalapeno and onion.
Fry the bacon in a pan, set it on paper towels and keep as much of the fat in the pan as you can.
Fry the pork rinds in the bacon fat until crisp, then add the vegetables and salt and cook until the onion is nearly translucent.
Stir in the cilantro, then pour in the whisked eggs and cook like an omelet, stirring once so the raw egg reaches the pan.
Fold in the cubed avocado, crumble the bacon over the top and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Zucchini and Prosciutto Egg Muffins
instructions: Heat the oven to 350 F.
Heat the olive oil in a pan over medium heat and saute the onion and garlic for 1 minute.
Add the bell pepper, spinach and parsley and saute 2 more minutes, until the spinach wilts.
Whisk the eggs, coconut milk, salt and pepper in a large bowl, then stir in the cooked vegetables and the sliced zucchini.
Grease a 12-cup muffin tin with olive oil and line each cup with a slice of prosciutto.
Ladle the egg mixture into the cups and bake for about 20 minutes, until cooked through.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Gluten Free Dutch Baby Pancake
instructions: Heat the oven to 425 F.
Blend the almond flour, coconut flour, eggs, cream, vanilla, almond milk, salt and stevia in a food processor until you have a thin crepe-like batter.
Melt the ghee in a 7 inch skillet over medium-high heat.
Pour in the batter so the ghee runs up to the edges and cook on the stove for 1 minute.
Move the skillet straight into the oven and bake for about 24 minutes, until the top and centre are set but still custardy.
Brush with melted butter, dust with cinnamon and cut into slices.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Keto Breakfast Egg Wrap
instructions: Cook the chicken sausages in a frying pan, then cover them with foil to keep warm.
Whisk the eggs in a large bowl with the salt and pepper.
Melt a teaspoon of butter in a nonstick pan over medium heat, pour in a quarter of the eggs and cook 2 to 3 minutes.
Flip the egg carefully, cook another 1 to 2 minutes, and slide it onto a plate. Repeat for the other wraps.
Spread each wrap with mashed avocado, then cream cheese, and top with the diced jalapeno.
Lay a chicken sausage on each wrap, fold in the sides and roll it up.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Thai Stuffed Omelette (Kai Yat Sai)

lines.text: 4 tablespoons vegetable oil (2 for the filling, 2 for the omelette)

instructions: Stir the fish sauce, white pepper and ketchup together in a small bowl.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the garlic and onion until soft.
Add the pork and cook until nearly done, pour in the seasoning mix and stir for 1 minute.
Stir in the diced tomato, combine well and take the filling off the heat.
Whisk the eggs with 4 tablespoons of water. Heat a 22 cm non-stick pan, add the remaining oil, pour in half the eggs and spread until firm.
Spoon half the filling into the centre, fold the edges over and slide it onto a plate. Make the second omelette the same way.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Heirloom Tomato and Swiss Chard Eggs Benedict
instructions: Blend the egg yolks in a blender. Melt the butter in a frying pan until it stops foaming, then pour it slowly into the running blender until the sauce emulsifies.
Add the lemon juice and cayenne, blend until thick and leave the hollandaise in the blender to stay warm.
Saute the sliced garlic in the buttered pan until fragrant, add the chard cut into 2 inch pieces and cook until wilted. Season with salt and pepper and cover to keep warm.
Simmer a wide pan of water with a splash of vinegar and some salt, slide in the eggs one at a time, and poach them gently for about 4 minutes.
Lay the tomato slices on plates, season them, and top with the chard and a poached egg each.
Pour the hollandaise over the eggs and scatter with chives.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Turkey Breakfast Sausage
instructions: Cook the minced onion with the olive oil and a pinch of the salt over medium low heat for 4 to 5 minutes, add the garlic, and stir until soft.
Add the fennel seeds and toss for about 1 minute until fragrant, then move the mixture to a bowl to cool a little.
Add the turkey, vinegar, thyme, sage, paprika and the rest of the salt and mix with a fork until evenly combined.
Shape the mixture into 8 even patties and set them on parchment.
Brown the patties in a hot nonstick skillet in two batches, 3 minutes per side.
Turn the heat to low, cover, and cook each batch until the center reaches 165 F.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Ham and Asparagus Quiche

lines.text: 6 ounces Applegate Naturals Slow Cooked Ham, chopped (about 1 cup)

instructions: Heat the oven to 375 F with racks in the middle and lowest positions and grease a 10 inch pie plate.
Peel the asparagus lightly, trim 8 spears to fit across the plate and slice the rest. Saute the sliced asparagus, onion and ham in the butter until the onion softens, then cool.
Beat the eggs, cream, water, salt and white pepper with a hand mixer until frothy.
Layer a third of the gruyere and a third of the ham mixture in the plate, repeating twice more.
Pour the custard over, arrange the asparagus spears on top, and bake on the lowest rack for 30 minutes.
Move to the middle rack for about 10 minutes more until just set, then broil briefly to brown the top and let it rest.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Buffalo Chicken Rice Bowls
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice thoroughly, then cook with 350ml water and a pinch of salt until tender, about 15 minutes.

Toss cubed chicken breast with olive oil, garlic powder, and half the ranch seasoning. Sear in a hot non-stick skillet over medium-high heat until golden and fully cooked to 165°F (74°C), about 8 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk together the buffalo hot sauce, non-fat Greek yogurt, and remaining ranch seasoning to create a creamy high-protein buffalo drizzle.
Divide the cooked rice into four meal prep containers, top evenly with seared chicken breast, sliced celery, and drizzle with the creamy buffalo sauce.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Curried Chicken Fried Rice

lines.text: 600g chicken breast, diced into bite-sized pieces

instructions: Heat half the sesame oil in a large wok over medium-high heat. Add diced chicken seasoned with curry powder and minced garlic; sear until cooked through, about 6 minutes, then set aside.
Pour beaten whole eggs and egg whites into the wok, scramble quickly until soft curds form, then remove with the chicken.
Add remaining oil and toss in day-old rice and frozen peas and carrots; stir-fry vigorously for 4 minutes until rice grains are slightly toasted and fragrant.
Return chicken and scrambled eggs to the wok, pour over low-sodium soy sauce, toss everything together over high heat for 2 minutes, and portion into four servings.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Honey Sriracha Chicken Rice Bowls

lines.text: 650g chicken breast, cut into bite-sized cubes
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water

instructions: Cook white rice in lightly salted boiling water for 15 minutes until tender and fluffy.
In a small bowl, whisk honey, sriracha, low-sodium soy sauce, and cornstarch slurry until smooth.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over high heat. Sear chicken pieces for 6-8 minutes until golden browned on all sides.
Pour the honey sriracha sauce into the pan; simmer for 2 minutes while tossing constantly until the sauce thickens into a glossy glaze coating the chicken.
Assemble containers with fluffy white rice, steamed broccoli florets, and glazed chicken; finish with toasted sesame seeds.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Slow Cooker Enchilada Chicken

lines.text: 1 can (400g) black beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Place raw chicken breasts, enchilada sauce, black beans, sweet corn, green chiles, and ground cumin into the slow cooker bowl.
Cover and cook on LOW for 4 hours (or HIGH for 2.5 hours) until chicken is fork-tender and registers at least 165°F (74°C).
Using two forks, shred the chicken directly in the slow cooker and stir well to absorb the rich enchilada sauce.
Serve generous portions over warm cooked brown rice and sprinkle each serving with 20g of shredded Monterey Jack cheese to melt.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Sriracha Lime Chicken Bowls

lines.text: 1 large red bell pepper, sliced into strips
1 large yellow bell pepper, sliced into strips

instructions: Whisk lime juice, lime zest, sriracha, minced garlic, and salt in a bowl; toss with chicken strips and marinate for 15 minutes.
Simmer quinoa in 400ml water with a pinch of salt for 15 minutes until tender and water is fully absorbed.
Heat olive oil in a cast-iron skillet over high heat. Sear marinated chicken strips and sliced bell peppers for 7-9 minutes until charred and cooked through.
Divide cooked quinoa among meal containers, top with sizzling chicken and peppers, and spoon remaining pan juices on top.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Halal Cart Style Chicken & Turmeric Rice
instructions: Marinate trimmed chicken thighs in cumin, coriander, half the turmeric, lemon juice, garlic, and salt for 20 minutes.
Melt 1 tbsp butter in a pot; toast rinsed basmati rice with remaining turmeric and a dash of cumin for 2 minutes, then add 380ml broth and simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Sear marinated chicken thighs in a smoking-hot skillet for 5 minutes per side until deeply caramelized and fully cooked; rest 5 minutes then chop into bite-sized pieces.
Whisk Greek yogurt, white vinegar, garlic powder, black pepper, and lemon juice into a tangy high-protein white sauce.
Plate bright yellow turmeric rice alongside chopped chicken, crisp iceberg lettuce, and fresh diced tomatoes, drizzled generously with the white sauce.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Mediterranean Lemon Garlic Chicken Rice Bowls
instructions: Cook brown basmati rice in 420ml water with a pinch of sea salt for 22 minutes until tender.
Toss cubed chicken breast with olive oil, lemon juice, pressed garlic, oregano, salt, and black pepper.
Sear seasoned chicken in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 8 minutes until golden browned and juicy.
Assemble meal bowls by layering warm brown rice, seared lemon oregano chicken, diced cucumbers, sweet cherry tomatoes, and sliced kalamata olives.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Sweet Chili Crispy Chicken Bowls

lines.text: 650g chicken breast, cut into bite-sized chunks

instructions: Cook jasmine rice according to package instructions until light and fluffy.

Toss chicken chunks with cornstarch, salt, and garlic powder. Spread onto a parchment-lined baking sheet, spray lightly with olive oil, and bake at 400°F (200°C) or air fry for 14 minutes until crisp.
Blanch green beans in boiling salted water for 4 minutes until vibrant green and tender-crisp.
Warm sweet chili sauce with light soy sauce in a skillet, add crispy chicken chunks, toss to coat evenly, and divide into four bowls over rice and green beans.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Tex-Mex Fajita Chicken Rice Bowls

lines.text: 700g chicken breast, sliced into fajita strips
2 tbsp fajita spice mix (cumin, paprika, chili, garlic)
2 large bell peppers (red and green), sliced

instructions: Toss chicken strips with 1 tbsp fajita seasoning and a drizzle of olive oil.
Sear chicken strips in a smoking hot skillet for 6 minutes until charred on the edges and cooked through; transfer to a plate.
In the same skillet, sauté sliced onions and bell peppers with remaining fajita seasoning for 5 minutes until tender-crisp with blistered edges.
Layer cooked brown rice, black beans, charred chicken strips, and fajita peppers into four meal containers; squeeze fresh lime over top before sealing.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Filipino-Style Sawsawan Chicken Rice Bowls

lines.text: 650g boneless skinless chicken, cut into cubes
60ml Filipino cane vinegar or apple cider vinegar

instructions: Cook jasmine rice with water according to package directions.
In a pot, combine chicken, vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, peppercorns, and bay leaves; bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 15 minutes.

lines.text: 720g chicken breast cut into bite-sized nuggets

instructions: Boil penne pasta in salted water for 8 minutes until al dente; drain.
Sear chicken breast nuggets in a hot skillet with Italian seasoning and salt for 6 minutes until golden browned.
In a baking casserole dish, combine drained penne, seared chicken, and marinara sauce; mix until well combined.
Top with shredded mozzarella, parmesan, and breadcrumbs; bake at 375°F (190°C) for 14 minutes until cheese is melted and crust is crunchy and golden.

title: Creamy Cajun Chicken & Turkey Bacon Penne

lines.text: 2 bell peppers, sliced into thin strips
90g light cream cheese or Greek yogurt

instructions: Cook high-protein penne in salted water for 8 minutes; drain and keep warm.
Crisp chopped turkey bacon in a large skillet; remove bacon and sear Cajun-rubbed chicken strips in the pan for 6 minutes until browned; transfer out.
Sauté sliced bell peppers in the pan for 3 minutes; deglaze with chicken broth and stir in light cream cheese until smooth and creamy.

lines.text: 200g dry high-protein pasta shells or rotini

Add dry pasta shells, red enchilada sauce, chicken broth, and black beans; bring to a vigorous boil.
Cover with a tight-fitting lid, reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer for 11 minutes until pasta is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Sprinkle Mexican cheese blend over the top; cover for 2 minutes to let cheese melt into a gooey layer, then portion into meal containers.

title: Crispy Red Lentil Tofu Peanut Stir-Fry

60g powdered peanut butter whisked with 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp maple syrup, 1 tsp sriracha

Assemble meal bowls with brown rice, steamed greens, crispy tofu cubes, and drizzle with peanut sauce.

title: High-Protein Paneer & Chickpea Tikka Masala

1.5 tbsp garam masala, 1 tbsp cumin, 1 tbsp coriander, 1 tsp turmeric

title: Mediterranean Falafel & Spiced Chickpea Hummus Power Bowl

200g chickpeas tossed with cumin and paprika, roasted crunchy
150g garlic hummus or whipped tahini dip

title: Bacon Mushroom Stuffed Chicken

lines.text: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 8 oz each)
8 oz bacon (about 85 g once cooked and drained)

instructions: Stir the mayonnaise, sour cream, honey, Dijon mustard and paprika into a smooth honey mustard sauce.
Chop the bacon and cook it in a large skillet, then lift it out, keeping 1 tsp of the grease. Saute the mushrooms in that grease until browned, season lightly and let them cool.
Cut a pocket in each chicken breast, season with salt and pepper, and fill with cheese, mushrooms and bacon, saving some of each for the top. Close with a toothpick and heat the oven to 350F.
Heat 1 tsp oil in the skillet over medium-high heat and sear the chicken 4 to 5 minutes per side.
Top with the saved bacon, mushrooms and cheese, drizzle with the sauce, cover with foil and bake 15 minutes, then uncover and bake 2 to 3 minutes more.
