title: Sheet Pan Chicken Scarpariello

lines.text: 4 boneless skinless chicken thighs (about 450 g), cut in 1 inch pieces
12 oz sweet Italian chicken sausage, cut in 1 inch pieces
1 cup red onion, sliced 1/4 inch thick
1 red bell pepper, sliced in 1/4 inch strips
1 1/2 cups potato gnocchi (about 210 g) — use DeLallo Mini Potato Gnocchi (US 1 lb)
1 cup jarred cherry peppers (or banana pepper rings) with 1/4 cup of their brine

instructions: Heat the oven to 425F and lightly oil a large sheet pan.
Cut the chicken thighs and sausage into 1 inch pieces and slice the onion and bell pepper into quarter-inch strips.
In a large bowl toss the chicken, sausage, onion, pepper, gnocchi, cherry peppers and brine with the olive oil, garlic, Italian seasoning and salt until evenly coated.
Spread everything over the sheet pan in one layer and roast for about 18 minutes.
Turn everything over and roast another 12 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the gnocchi and edges are browned.

title: Kadai Chicken

lines.text: 700 g boneless chicken thighs in 1 inch pieces
1 1/2 tbsp coriander seeds, dry roasted and ground

instructions: Dry roast the coriander seeds in a pan on medium heat for 2 minutes until fragrant, cool them and grind to a fine powder.
Heat the oil, saute the onions until golden, then stir in the ginger garlic paste for 30 to 60 seconds.
Add the chicken and stir fry 3 to 4 minutes until it turns pale, then lower the heat and stir in the turmeric, chili powder, salt and the ground coriander.
Pour in the tomato puree and cook on medium heat 3 to 4 minutes until it thickens and loses its raw smell.
Partly cover and cook until the chicken is tender and the gravy is thick, then add the garam masala.
Mix the cream with a spoonful of the gravy, stir it back in, simmer 2 minutes and garnish with coriander leaves.

title: Chicken Manchurian

lines.text: 2 tbsp corn starch for the batter plus 3 tsp for the sauce
1 tsp soy sauce in the marinade and 1 tbsp in the sauce
Oil for deep frying, about 3 tbsp absorbed plus 1/2 tbsp for the sauce

instructions: Mix the chicken with the soy sauce, salt, pepper, a little ginger, garlic and chili powder, then stir in the egg white, flour and 2 tbsp corn starch and marinate for at least an hour.
Heat oil to a medium fry temperature, deep fry the chicken until golden and crisp, then drain it on a towel, making sure it is cooked through.
Stir the remaining corn starch into 3 tbsp water, and mix the soy sauce, red chili sauce and a splash of vinegar in a small bowl.
Keep half a tablespoon of the frying oil, fry the garlic and ginger until fragrant, then cook the onion until it turns translucent.
Add the bell pepper for 2 minutes, pour in the sauces, and when it bubbles add the corn starch mixture with 1 cup water and stir until thickened.
Season to taste with salt and a little sugar, fold in the fried chicken and scallions and serve hot.

title: Samgyetang

lines.text: 1 Cornish hen (about 1.5 lb), edible meat and skin about 400 g
1 scallion white part and 2 scallions, finely chopped for garnish
1/4 tsp salt and pepper to season at the table

instructions: Rinse the hen and pat the cavity dry, then fill it with the sweet rice and two cloves of garlic, leaving room for the rice to swell.
Cross the legs and tie them with twine, or tuck one leg through a small slit in the skin, so the rice stays inside.
Set the hen in a medium pot with the remaining garlic, ginger, jujubes, ginseng and the scallion white, and pour in 5 to 6 cups of water.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, skim the foam, cover and boil 15 minutes.
Lower to medium-low and cook covered about 25 minutes more, until the hen is tender and the rice is soft, then turn off the heat and rest 10 minutes.
Serve the hen in its broth with chopped scallions, with salt and pepper on the side.

title: Korean Air Fryer Chicken Wings

lines.text: 1 1/2 pounds chicken wings, split into flats and drumettes
2 tablespoons chopped green onions, for serving

instructions: Split the wings into flats and drumettes, discarding the tips if still attached. Pat them dry and season all over with the kosher salt.
Spray the air fryer basket, lay the wings in a single layer so they do not touch, and cook at 360 degrees F for 12 minutes. Flip and cook 12 minutes more.
Flip the wings again, raise the heat to 390 degrees F and cook about 6 minutes until the skin is crisp.
While the wings cook, simmer the soy sauce, rice vinegar, maple syrup, garlic, ginger and gochujang in a saucepan for about 1 minute, whisking, until slightly reduced.
Pour the glaze into a large bowl and stir in the sesame oil.
Toss the hot wings in the glaze, then serve sprinkled with green onions and sesame seeds.

title: Chicken Nanban

lines.text: 1 boneless, skinless chicken breast (10.5 oz, 300 g)
2 large eggs, one for the coating and one hard-boiled for the tartar sauce
Neutral oil for frying (about 2 tablespoons absorbed from 2 cups)

instructions: Boil one egg for 12 minutes, cool it in ice water, peel and mince it. Mix it with the minced onion (soaked and squeezed dry), minced cucumber, mayonnaise and a little rice vinegar and chill.
Simmer the soy sauce, remaining rice vinegar, mirin and sugar until the sugar dissolves, then take it off the heat.
Butterfly the chicken breast, cut it in half into two cutlets and pound to an even thickness. Season with salt and dust with flour.
Heat oil to 340 degrees F. Dip each floured cutlet in the beaten egg and fry one at a time for about 4 minutes, turning halfway, then rest on a rack.
Raise the oil to 350 degrees F and refry each cutlet for 30 seconds per side until deep golden, then drain.
Turn the hot cutlets in the nanban sauce, slice into pieces and top with the tartar sauce.

title: Thai Grilled Chicken (Gai Yang)

lines.text: 2 lb / 1 kg skinless, boneless chicken thigh fillets
1 large lemongrass stalk, white part only, sliced

instructions: Blend the lemongrass, garlic, fish sauce, both soy sauces and brown sugar into a smooth puree, then stir in the oil.
Toss the chicken thighs in the marinade, cover and chill overnight, or at least 3 hours.
Heat a grill on high or a non-stick pan over high heat.
Lift the chicken from the marinade, discarding the leftover marinade, and cook it over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes per side until golden brown, flipping early if it darkens.
Rest the chicken for 3 minutes before serving.

title: Chicken Vesuvio

lines.text: 3 1/2 pounds bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks
2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley, for garnish

instructions: Heat the oven to 425 degrees F. Pat the chicken dry and season with salt and pepper. Toss the halved potatoes with a pinch of salt, a little oil and pepper.
Sear the chicken skin-side down in hot olive oil in an oven-safe skillet for about 5 minutes, flip and brown 3 to 4 minutes more, then set aside.
Soften the onion in the same pan for about 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic and oregano for 30 seconds.
Pour in the white wine and simmer for 1 minute, scraping up the browned bits. Add the broth and lemon juice, then the potatoes.
Nestle the chicken back among the potatoes and roast for 40 to 45 minutes until the chicken reaches 165 degrees F and the potatoes are tender, broiling 2 to 3 minutes for crisper skin.
Rest for a few minutes, then spoon over the pan sauce and finish with parsley and extra lemon.

title: Opor Ayam

lines.text: 550 g boneless skinless chicken thigh fillets

instructions: Blend the shallots, garlic, candlenuts, coriander seeds and cumin with a splash of water into a smooth paste.
Fry the paste in the oil with the bruised lemongrass and galangal until fragrant and no longer raw-smelling.
Add the chicken and turn it in the paste until coated.
Pour in the stock, cover and simmer until the chicken is tender.
Stir in the coconut milk and sugar and simmer gently, stirring now and then so the sauce does not split.
Taste, adjust the seasoning and serve hot.

title: Pineapple Chicken Afritada

lines.text: 800 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into serving pieces

1 red bell pepper and 1 green bell pepper, cut into squares

instructions: Heat the oil, fry the garlic until golden, then add the onion and cook until soft.

Pour in the tomato sauce, pineapple juice and broth, cover and bring to a boil.
Add the bay leaves, cover and cook over low heat.
Turn the chicken pieces over and cook the other side.
Add the pineapple, potato and carrot and cook until the potato is tender.
Season with fish sauce and pepper, add the bell peppers and cook a few minutes more.

title: Aji de Gallina

lines.text: 1/2 cup mild yellow chilli paste (aji amarillo)

instructions: Poach the chicken breasts in the stock until cooked through, then shred them and keep the stock.
Soak the bread in the evaporated milk until it falls apart.
Fry the onion and garlic in the oil until soft, then stir in the yellow chilli paste.
Blend the soaked bread with a ladle of the poaching stock until smooth and stir it into the pan.

Serve over sliced boiled potatoes with the halved eggs.

title: Chicken Stew
instructions: Season the chicken with the salt, a little paprika, thyme and ginger garlic paste, then cook it with a splash of water until just done and keep the stock.

Fry the blend in the oil over medium heat until it reduces and the oil rises to the top.

Add the chicken with a little of its stock and simmer until the stew coats the meat.

title: Durban Chicken Curry

lines.text: 900 g boneless skinless chicken thighs (deboned pieces)

instructions: Heat the oil and fry the cinnamon stick, bay leaves and cumin seeds until fragrant.
Add the onion and cook until golden brown.
Stir in the ginger garlic paste, chili powder, garam masala and turmeric with a splash of water and fry the masala.
Add the chicken and turn it in the masala until coated and lightly seared.
Add the tomato, cover and cook until it breaks down into the sauce.
Add the potatoes with enough water to just cover and simmer until the potatoes and chicken are tender.

title: Chicken and Cauliflower Maklouba

lines.text: 1 kg bone-in chicken pieces (about 780 g edible meat and skin)

instructions: Sear the chicken pieces in 2 tbsp oil until golden, toast the cardamom, then soften the diced onions and garlic in the same pot.
Cover the chicken with water and the salt, skim, and simmer with the lid ajar for 40 to 50 minutes. Lift out the chicken and strain the stock.
Fry the cauliflower florets and a few garlic cloves in 2 tbsp oil until browned on all sides, then drain and salt them.
Wash and drain the rice, then mix it with the cardamom, black pepper, turmeric, remaining salt and 1 tbsp oil.
Line a pot with a little rice and sliced tomato, add the chicken skin side down, then a thin rice layer, the cauliflower and the rest of the rice.
Pour in stock to the level of the rice, boil on high for 5 minutes, then cover and cook on low for 20 minutes and steam off the heat for 10.
Rest the pot for 15 minutes, set a plate on top, flip it, and rest another 10 minutes before lifting the pot away.

title: Chicken Stew with Tomatoes and Fresh Herbs (Chakhokhbili)

lines.text: 1 chicken (4 lb), cut into serving pieces (about 1.1 kg edible meat and skin)

instructions: Brown the chicken pieces in the oil and butter in a wide pot, a few at a time, then set them aside.
Cook the onions and red pepper in the same pot until soft, then stir in the garlic.
Add the diced tomatoes and return the chicken to the pot with the salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer gently for about 40 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce is thick.
Stir in the cilantro, parsley and basil, simmer 3 minutes more, and serve with bread for dipping.

title: Pollo alla Diavola

lines.text: 1 whole chicken, 2.4 kg, spatchcocked (about 1.46 kg edible meat and skin)
4 tbsp olive oil in total (1 in the marinade, about 3 in the pan)

instructions: Cut out the backbone, flatten the chicken, pat it dry, and whisk the paprika, vinegar, 1 tbsp oil, honey, chopped rosemary, chilli flakes, salt and pepper into a marinade.
Brush the marinade over both sides and chill the chicken for at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Warm the rest of the oil in a wide cast-iron pan over medium heat with the garlic, sliced chilli and whole rosemary until fragrant.
Lay the chicken in the pan, set a flat weight on top, and cook 10 minutes, then turn it skin side down and cook 10 minutes more under the weight.
Turn the chicken bone side down, cover with a lid and cook about 20 minutes, until the breast reaches 75 C, then uncover and re-crisp skin side down for 5 to 10 minutes.
Rest the chicken 10 minutes on a bed of rosemary, squeeze over the lemon, spoon over the pan juices and carve.

title: Chicken Parmo

lines.text: 30 g plain flour for dredging plus 25 g plain flour for the sauce
1 tsp oil, sprayed over the chicken

instructions: Heat the oven to 200C and bash the chicken breasts between baking parchment to about 1 cm thick.
Dredge each breast in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, set on an oiled lined tray, spray with a little more oil and bake 40 minutes until crisp and cooked through.
Melt the butter, cook in the remaining flour for 2 to 3 minutes, then whisk in the milk a little at a time and simmer 5 minutes until thick.
Season the sauce, grate in the nutmeg and melt in three quarters of the cheese off the heat.
Spoon the sauce over the chicken, scatter on the remaining cheese and grill 1 to 2 minutes until bubbling.

title: Coronation Chicken

Stir the mayonnaise, Greek yogurt, curry powder, cinnamon, salt, white pepper and mango chutney together.
Mix in the sultanas and chopped apricots until combined.
Fold in the chicken to coat it, spoon into a bowl and top with the toasted almonds.

title: Huli Huli Chicken

lines.text: 3/4 cup pineapple juice, canned or bottled, unsweetened

instructions: Whisk the pineapple juice, ginger, garlic, ketchup, soy sauce, sherry, brown sugar, Sriracha, rice vinegar and sesame oil together and set aside 3/4 cup for basting.
Pour the rest of the marinade over the chicken in a glass or ceramic dish, coat well, cover and refrigerate for 24 to 48 hours.
Heat a grill or skillet over medium-high heat and brush it with the oil, then lift the chicken out of the marinade, let the excess drip off and lay it on the heat.
Cook the first side for 2 to 3 minutes until golden, flip and cook 2 minutes more, then baste generously with the reserved marinade.

title: Chicken Fricassée

lines.text: 4 chicken thighs, skin-on and bone-in (about 250 g each)

instructions: Pat the chicken dry and season with part of the salt.

title: Pollo al Ajillo

lines.text: 4 cloves garlic, chopped, plus 1 full head of garlic, trimmed

instructions: Heat the oven to 200 C / 400 F.
Brown the drumsticks in half the oil over high heat, seasoning with salt, and add the chopped garlic halfway through, about 5 to 6 minutes in all.

title: Chicken Do Pyaza

lines.text: 2.6 lb chicken, cut into 12 to 14 pieces, bone-in, skinless (about 700 g edible meat)

instructions: Toast the coriander and cumin seeds in a dry pan until fragrant, cool them and grind coarsely.
Heat the oil in a large pan or karahi and sizzle the green cardamom, cloves and dry red chillies.
Add the sliced onions and fry on medium-high for 5 to 8 minutes until the edges wilt, then add the ginger and garlic and cook 5 minutes more.

title: Creamy Sri Lankan Chicken Curry

lines.text: 800 g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 4 cm pieces
2 long green chillies, deseeded and cut into strips

instructions: Heat the oil in a large deep pan, add the onion and salt, lower the heat and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger and green chilli for 1 minute, then stir in the curry leaves and curry powder.
Add the chopped tomato and stir, then add the chicken, vinegar and 1/4 cup water.
Cover and cook, stirring now and then, for 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.

title: Chicken Kathi Roll

lines.text: 1 tablespoon oil for the marinade plus 1 1/2 tablespoons oil for cooking, and a little to fry the eggs
3/4 cup very thinly sliced onions to saute, plus 1/3 cup sliced onions for topping
1 cup very thinly sliced bell peppers

instructions: Stir the yogurt, Kashmiri chili powder, garam masala, salt, lemon juice and 1 tablespoon of the oil into a marinade, coat the chicken and let it rest while you prepare the rest, or refrigerate up to 2 days.
Slice the onions and bell pepper very thin. Saute the pepper and the 3/4 cup of onions in half of the remaining oil over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, then move them to a plate.
Add the rest of the oil to the pan, cook the chicken 3 minutes per side until cooked through, then stir the onions and peppers back in, taste, and cool the filling completely so the rolls stay crisp.
Cook the parathas as the pack directs. For each roll, pour a beaten egg into a lightly oiled non-stick pan, press a paratha onto it once the egg begins to set, and cook until the egg is done.
Fill each egg paratha with the chicken mixture and the remaining sliced onions, fold in the sides and roll up tightly. Wrap in parchment if you like.

title: Greek Chicken Gyros

lines.text: 1 tablespoon sweet paprika for the marinade plus 2 teaspoons for the sauce
1 1/2 teaspoons salt for the marinade plus 1/2 teaspoon for the sauce
3 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil in the marinade plus 2 tablespoons in the sauce

instructions: Mix 3 tablespoons of the olive oil with 1 tablespoon paprika, the mustard powder, oregano and 1 1/2 teaspoons of the salt, coat the chicken thighs and marinate in the fridge for at least 3 hours, or overnight.
Stir the yogurt, the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil, garlic powder, remaining 2 teaspoons paprika and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt into a sauce and set aside.
Cook the chicken in batches on a hot grill or a large non-stick pan, 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden and cooked through.
Rest the chicken under loose foil for 3 minutes, then slice it into 1 cm pieces.
Warm the pitas, spread sauce down the middle, pile on chicken, lettuce, tomato and red onion, drizzle with more sauce and fold.

title: Chicken Doner Kebab

lines.text: 2 pounds chicken breasts, boneless and skinless
1/4 cup plain yogurt in the marinade plus 1 cup plain yogurt for the sauce
1/2 cup olive oil in the marinade plus 1 tablespoon extra virgin olive oil in the sauce and 1 tablespoon to cook

instructions: Stir 1/4 cup of the yogurt, the tomato paste, soy sauce, 1/2 cup of the olive oil, curry powder, cumin, paprika and coriander together, add the chicken and mix until fully coated.
Lay the chicken on a large sheet of plastic wrap and roll it tightly into an even log, then freeze for at least 3 to 4 hours until firm.
Whisk the remaining 1 cup yogurt with the garlic, lemon juice and 1 tablespoon olive oil and refrigerate until needed.
Unwrap the log and slice off thin slices of chicken; if it is too hard, let it sit a few minutes at room temperature first.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the slices in batches for 3 to 5 minutes, until cooked through and almost charred.
Warm the pitas, spread each with yogurt sauce, add the chicken and drizzle with olive oil, then fold.

title: Chicken Stroganoff

lines.text: 2 large chicken breasts, cut in half horizontally to make 4 fillets
3 tablespoons flour to dredge the chicken plus 1 tablespoon flour for the sauce
2 tablespoons butter to sear plus 3 tablespoons butter for the sauce
1/2 teaspoon paprika to season the chicken plus 1 teaspoon paprika in the sauce
2 cups low sodium chicken stock plus 1/2 cup stock in place of the white wine

instructions: Season the chicken fillets with half the paprika and dredge them in 3 tablespoons of the flour. Sear in 2 tablespoons butter and the olive oil, 4 minutes per side, then set aside.
Melt the remaining butter in the pan, saute the onion until soft, stir in the garlic for 30 seconds, then cook the mushrooms until golden, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the mustard and remaining paprika, pour in 1/2 cup of the stock to deglaze and let it reduce for about 3 minutes.
Stir in the last tablespoon of flour for 1 minute, then add the rest of the stock and the Worcestershire sauce and simmer 2 to 4 minutes until slightly thickened.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, stir in the sour cream and simmer 3 to 4 minutes until smooth. Return the chicken with its juices and simmer 2 minutes until cooked through.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chicken and Buckwheat Patties

lines.text: 1/4 cup plain bread crumbs in the mix plus 1 cup Italian bread crumbs to coat the patties
3 tablespoons extra light olive oil to saute the spinach and cook the patties

instructions: Cut the broccoli into florets and pulse in a food processor until finely chopped, then tip into a large bowl.
Chop the spinach and saute it in 1 tablespoon of the oil for a few minutes until soft, then add it to the bowl.
Grind the cooked buckwheat and chicken breasts together in the food processor and add them to the bowl with the minced onion, plain bread crumbs, egg, sour cream and salt. Mix well.
Shape the mixture into oval patties and coat both sides in Italian bread crumbs.
Cook the patties on a well-oiled skillet over medium heat, flipping 4 to 5 times, until cooked through.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chicken Giouvetsi with Orzo

lines.text: 575 g boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into bites

instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a large frying pan, soften the chopped onion, then season the chicken pieces and fry them until lightly colored.
Move the chicken and onion to a plate. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of oil to the same pan and saute the orzo with the tomato paste for a couple of minutes.
Pour in the chopped tomatoes, tomato juice and a cup of warm water, then return the chicken and onion with a pinch of sugar and cinnamon and a little salt and pepper.
Cover and cook over medium heat for about 15 minutes, stirring now and then, adding another cup of hot water halfway if the liquid is absorbed, until the orzo is tender.
Take the pan off the heat, drizzle with olive oil and stir in the crumbled feta. Rest for 5 minutes and serve warm.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chicken Shashlik

lines.text: 650 grams skinless boneless chicken thighs, cut to 1 1/2 inch
1 large red onion, diced to the size of the chicken

instructions: Mix the tomato paste, paprika, cumin, garam masala, salt, garlic, soya sauce, lemon juice and olive oil in a bowl and adjust the salt and heat to taste.
Stir in the chicken, cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or up to 12 hours.
Soak wooden skewers for 30 minutes if using them. Line a tray with foil, set a greased wire rack on it and heat the oven to 240 C (460 F).
Mix the diced onion and bell peppers into the marinade, then thread the chicken, onion and peppers alternately onto the skewers.
Bake on the rack for 16 minutes, turning at 10 minutes, then broil on the top rack for 3 to 4 minutes until lightly charred and the chicken reads 74 C (165 F).
Brush the hot skewers with lemon juice and a little olive oil and serve with rice and a yogurt or garlic dip.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: One Pot Mexican Chicken and Rice

lines.text: 5 chicken thighs, bone-in, skin on (about 1 kg, about 750 g meat and skin)
1 can (400 g) black beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat the oven to 180 C (350 F). Mix the cumin, paprika and salt, then toss the chicken with half the oil and some of the spice mix.
Sear the chicken skin side down in a deep ovenproof skillet in the remaining oil for 4 minutes until golden, flip for 1 1/2 minutes, then remove to a plate.
Saute the onion and bell pepper in the same skillet for 3 minutes until softened.
Stir in the rice, broth, passata, corn, black beans and the remaining spice mix, then set the chicken on top, skin side up.
Bring to a simmer, cover and bake for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake 15 minutes more until only small puddles of liquid remain.
Rest uncovered for 10 minutes, then fluff the rice and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Slow Cooker Honey Garlic Chicken

lines.text: 2 teaspoons chili paste (sambal oelek or sriracha)
2 cups prepared brown rice, to serve

instructions: Put the chicken thighs in a 6-quart slow cooker. Whisk the soy sauce, honey, tomato paste, chili paste, garlic and rice vinegar together and pour over the chicken.
Cover and cook on low for 4 to 5 hours or on high for 2 to 3 hours, until the chicken reads 165 F, flipping once halfway if you can.
Move the chicken to a plate to cool slightly, then whisk the cornstarch into the cooking liquid.
Cook the sauce on high for 15 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then, or simmer it in a saucepan for 5 to 10 minutes until it thickens.
Shred the chicken with two forks, return it to the sauce and toss to coat.
Serve over brown rice with sesame seeds and green onion.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Turkey Bolognese

lines.text: 10 ounces uncooked mezze rigatoni or fusilli

instructions: Brown the turkey with the salt in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it into small pieces, until no longer pink. Set it aside.
Add the oil, onion, carrot and celery to the pot and cook, stirring, until the vegetables start to soften.
Stir in the tomato paste and garlic and cook a few minutes until coated.
Add the pasta, cooked turkey, crushed tomatoes and broth, stir and bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until the pasta is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 15 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the parmesan and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Turkey Tetrazzini

lines.text: 1 cup whole milk plain Greek yogurt

instructions: Heat the oven to 350F. Boil the spaghetti, broken in half, until just under al dente, then drain.
Melt the butter in a Dutch oven and cook the onion until soft. Add the mushrooms and cook until they give up their liquid.
Stir in the flour for 2 minutes, then slowly pour in 3 cups of the broth and simmer until reduced by about a third.
Off the heat, melt in the cream cheese with the Worcestershire sauce, then stir in the turkey, peas and Parmesan, followed by the Greek yogurt.
Toss in the spaghetti, loosening with more broth if it looks thick, and scoop into a greased 9x13 dish.
Bake for 25 minutes until hot and bubbly, then rest a few minutes before serving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Turkey Roulade

lines.text: 1 large boneless turkey breast half with skin (about 2 1/2 pounds)
5 ounces whole wheat French bread, cut into small cubes
3/4 cup broth for the stuffing plus 2 cups for the gravy
1/4 cup all-purpose flour for the gravy
1/2 tablespoon butter plus 1 teaspoon to rub on top
4 fresh sage leaves, minced, plus 2 leaves for the gravy
1 1/4 teaspoons kosher salt on the turkey plus 1/4 teaspoon in the stuffing

instructions: Cook the onion, celery, parsley and sage in the butter until soft, then stir in the cubed bread, cranberries, 3/4 cup of the broth and the egg.
Skin the turkey breast half, butterfly it, cover it with plastic wrap and pound it about 1/4 inch thick. Season both sides with salt.
Spread the stuffing over the turkey leaving a border, roll it up, lay the skin on top, tie it with twine and rub on the butter.
Cover the roulade tightly with foil and roast at 375F for 45 to 55 minutes until the stuffing reaches 165F, then uncover and broil 5 to 7 minutes until golden.
Whisk the remaining broth with the flour and sage in a pot with the pan drippings and simmer 8 to 10 minutes until thick.
Cut off the twine, slice the roulade into 12 slices and serve with the gravy.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Turkey Taco Skillet

lines.text: 12 ounces jarred salsa — use Pace Chunky Salsa Mild (US)
1 cup shredded reduced fat Mexican cheese blend

instructions: Warm the oil in a large skillet and cook the onion and jalapeno for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the turkey and cook, crumbling it, until browned.
Stir in the chili powder, paprika, cumin, beans, corn and salsa and cook for 3 minutes.
Crush the chips over the top, scatter on the cheese, cover and cook 1 to 2 minutes until melted, or broil 2 to 3 minutes.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chicken Marsala
instructions: Halve the chicken breasts into 4 cutlets, pound them 1/3 inch thick, season with 1/2 teaspoon of the salt and the pepper, and dredge in the flour.
Brown the cutlets in the oil and butter for 3 to 4 minutes per side until cooked through, then set aside under foil.
Cook the mushrooms in the same pan until golden, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the Marsala and reduce until mostly gone, then pour in the stock and cream and simmer 4 to 5 minutes until slightly thick.
Season with the remaining salt, return the chicken with the parsley and warm through for 2 minutes.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Sweet Potato Turkey Chili

lines.text: 3 sweet potatoes, chopped into small pieces

instructions: Heat the oil in a deep pot and brown the turkey and onion with half the chili powder and taco seasoning, adding splashes of water if it sticks. Set aside.
Add the sweet potatoes and the rest of the spices and brown them slightly, then stir in the garlic.
Pour in 2 cups of water and the broth, bring to a low boil and simmer about 10 minutes until the sweet potatoes are very soft.
Puree the sweet potato mixture with an immersion blender until it reaches a chili-like thickness.
Stir the browned turkey, black beans and cayenne back in and warm through, tasting for spice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Yakitori Don

lines.text: 2 pieces boneless, skinless chicken thighs (about 10 oz or 284 g)
3 thick green onions, whites cut in 1 1/2-inch lengths and greens sliced
2 servings cooked Japanese short-grain rice (about 2 cups)

instructions: Cook the rice if you have none ready. Cut the white parts of the green onions into 1 1/2-inch lengths and slice the greens into thin rounds.
Pat the chicken thighs dry, cut them into 1 1/2-inch pieces and coat them in the flour, shaking off the excess.
Stir the mirin, soy sauce and sugar together in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Heat a stainless steel pan over medium heat with 1 tablespoon of the oil and sear the green onion whites on both sides. Move them to a plate.
Add more oil if needed and lay the chicken in a single layer, in batches if the pan is crowded. Sear about 3 minutes until golden, flip, cover and cook over medium-low heat for 3 minutes.
Wipe excess fat from the pan, return the green onion whites, pour in the sauce and shake the pan until the chicken is glazed.
Spoon the rice into two bowls, scatter the nori, top with the chicken and green onion, and sprinkle with the sliced greens.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Sesame Chicken

lines.text: 1 1/2 pounds boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into small 1/2-inch cubes
1 teaspoon arrowroot or cornstarch for the chicken, plus 1 tablespoon for the slurry
1 1/2 tablespoons toasted sesame oil plus 1/2 tablespoon for the sauce
1 tablespoon sesame seeds, plus more for garnish

instructions: Toss the chicken cubes with 1 tablespoon of the sesame oil and the 1 teaspoon of cornstarch until evenly coated.

Stir the soy sauce, honey, tomato paste, rice vinegar, the remaining 1/2 tablespoon sesame oil and 1 tablespoon sesame seeds into a sauce. Whisk the remaining 1 tablespoon cornstarch with 1/4 cup water in a separate bowl.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat, add half the avocado oil, and brown half the chicken in a single layer for 5 to 6 minutes, flipping once. Remove, then repeat with the rest.
Add the last 1/2 tablespoon of sesame oil to the pan with the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in half the sauce and cook 1 minute, scraping the pan. Return the chicken, add the remaining sauce, then drizzle in the cornstarch slurry and stir about 2 minutes until glossy and thick.
Serve over the rice, topped with the scallions and extra sesame seeds.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chicken Saltimbocca

lines.text: 8 chicken breast cutlets (or 4 medium chicken breasts, about 2 pounds)

instructions: Heat the oven to 200F and set a wire rack on a baking sheet. Pat the chicken dry and season both sides with the salt and half the pepper.
Mix the flour with the remaining pepper in a shallow dish and dredge each cutlet lightly on both sides. Scatter the minced sage over the tops and press a slice of prosciutto onto each.

Heat the olive oil and 1/2 tablespoon of the butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the cutlets prosciutto-side down in two batches, 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Keep them warm on the rack in the oven.
Pour the wine into the skillet, scrape up the browned bits and simmer about 2 minutes until reduced by half.
Add the chicken broth and simmer about 4 minutes until reduced by nearly half. Stir in the remaining 2 1/2 tablespoons butter and the red pepper flakes and simmer 1 minute.
Plate the chicken and spoon the sauce over the top.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chinese Satay Chicken Stir Fry

lines.text: 8 oz / 250 g chicken breast, sliced thinly
2 cups cooked white rice to serve

instructions: Cut the chicken in half lengthwise, then slice it thinly. Rinse and pat dry if you tenderise it with baking soda first.
Stir the peanut butter, brown sugar, soy sauce, rice vinegar, Sriracha, coconut milk and the curry powder into a sauce, then whisk in 1/4 cup water.
Heat the peanut oil in a wok or skillet over high heat. Stir-fry the onion and garlic for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and stir-fry for 2 minutes until just cooked through and a little browned.
Lower the heat slightly, pour in the sauce and stir-fry for 1 to 1 1/2 minutes until it reduces and thickens. Serve straight away over the rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Mediterranean Meatball Bowl

lines.text: 1/4 cup chopped Italian parsley for the meatballs plus 3 tablespoons for the salad
1 1/2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil, divided between the couscous and the salad
2 cups Persian or English cucumber, diced

instructions: Heat the oven to 400F and line a sheet pan with parchment. Beat the egg in a bowl, then mix in the dill, 1/4 cup of the parsley, panko and garlic.
Add the turkey and mix gently with a fork without overworking it. Roll into 16 meatballs of about 1 ounce each and set them on the sheet pan.
Bake the meatballs for 20 minutes without turning.

Meanwhile warm 1/2 tablespoon of the oil in a small pot over medium heat, toast the couscous about 3 minutes, pour in the hot broth, bring to a boil, cover and simmer about 10 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
Toss the tomato, cucumber, the remaining 3 tablespoons parsley, 1 tablespoon oil and the lemon juice together.
Divide the couscous among four bowls and top each with some salad and 4 meatballs.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Crock Pot Pepper Steak

lines.text: 2 pounds sirloin, cut into 2-inch by 1/2-inch strips
2 green and 2 red, orange or yellow bell peppers, cut into 1/2-inch strips
1 can (15 ounces) fire roasted diced tomatoes in their juices

instructions: Toss the sirloin strips with the garlic powder and salt, then brown them on all sides in the canola oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Move the beef and its juices to a 6-quart slow cooker.
Soften the sliced onion in the same skillet with a splash of water, scraping up the browned bits, then add it to the slow cooker.
Add the bell pepper strips and fire roasted tomatoes to the slow cooker.
Whisk the soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce, honey, ginger and 3 tablespoons of the cornstarch together and pour the mixture over everything.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours until the beef is tender, or on high for 3 to 4 hours.

Stir the remaining 2 tablespoons of cornstarch with 2 tablespoons of water, stir it into the cooker and cook uncovered on high for 10 minutes until thick and glossy. Taste, adjust the soy sauce and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Bison Chili

lines.text: 5 medium sweet potatoes, one baked per serving as the page suggests

instructions: Warm the olive oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat and cook the garlic, onion and diced bell pepper until the onion is soft and translucent.
Add the ground bison and break it up as it cooks.
Stir in the chili powder, smoked paprika, thyme, cinnamon, salt and pepper and keep cooking until the meat is browned.
Pour in the beef stock and tomato paste and fold everything together.
Lower the heat to a gentle simmer, cover and cook at least 25 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and let the chili cool slightly so it thickens, then serve each portion with a baked sweet potato.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Bison Buffalo Burgers
instructions: Mix the ground bison, oat flour, buffalo sauce, buttermilk, egg and all the spices and salt in a large bowl until combined.
Shape the mixture into 4 patties.
Chill the patties in the fridge for 15 to 20 minutes so they firm up and hold together.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet or grill to medium-high, about 350 F.
Cook the patties 5 to 7 minutes per side until fully cooked to 165 F, without pressing down so the juices stay in.
Rest the burgers 3 to 5 minutes, then build them on the buns with lettuce.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Carne Asada Burrito Bowls

lines.text: Juice of 4 limes (2 for the steak, 1 for the rice, 1 for the beans)
1/2 cup chopped cilantro for the steak plus 1/3 cup for the rice
4 cloves garlic (2 grated into the steak marinade, 2 minced for the peppers)
600 grams red and green bell peppers, sliced
2 teaspoons salt, divided across the steak, peppers, rice and beans

instructions: Whisk the soy sauce, brown sugar, half the lime juice, 2 grated garlic cloves and half the cilantro, coat the flank steak and marinate at least 30 minutes.
Cook the rice, then stir in the remaining cilantro, 1 lime of juice and a little of the salt.
Warm the drained black beans with the remaining lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Sear the steak with the ancho chili powder, cumin and salt in a hot pan or on a grill, resting it before slicing across the grain.
Saute the sliced peppers with the remaining garlic, cumin, ancho chili powder and salt until just tender.
Divide the rice, beans, peppers and steak among 5 containers.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Swedish Meatballs
instructions: Melt 1 tablespoon of the butter in a large skillet and soften the diced onion, about 5 minutes. Move it to a bowl and keep the skillet for the gravy.
Add the panko, egg, milk, allspice and a pinch of salt to the onion, then mix in the beef and turkey until just combined.
Shape into 12 meatballs and chill at least 15 minutes.
Bake the meatballs on a sheet at 425 F for 20 minutes, then broil 2 to 3 minutes until golden.

Stir the Worcestershire sauce into the broth. Melt the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter in the skillet, whisk in the flour for 2 minutes, then slowly whisk in the broth and simmer until thick. Season with salt to taste.
Stir a little of the hot gravy into the sour cream, return it to the skillet, add the meatballs and toss to coat.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Et Sote

lines.text: 400 g beef sirloin, cut into small pieces

instructions: Slice the onions into strips and cook them in the butter over medium heat until soft.
Stir in the turmeric, then add the sirloin pieces and saute for 5 minutes. Add the salt.
Pour in 1 cup (250 ml) of water, cover and cook over low heat for 40 to 45 minutes until the beef is tender.
Meanwhile chop the green peppers and tomatoes.
Stir in the black pepper and pul biber, then add the tomato paste and chopped tomatoes and cook about 5 minutes until the liquid reduces.
Add the green peppers, cook 5 minutes more, and dust with sumac before serving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Baked Katsudon

lines.text: 2 boneless pork loin chops (about 4 oz / 113 g each)
1 Tbsp neutral oil, to toast the panko
3 large eggs (1 for the coating, 2 for the bowls)
About 1 1/2 cups cooked Japanese short-grain rice per bowl (200 g each)
1/4 tsp shichimi togarashi (Japanese seven spice), to serve

instructions: Heat the oven to 400 F (200 C). Toast the panko in the oil in a frying pan over medium heat until golden, then cool it in a shallow dish.
Trim the fat from the pork, slit the connective tissue, pound the chops flat, then coat in flour, one beaten egg and the toasted panko.
Bake the cutlets on a rack on a baking sheet for about 20 minutes until no longer pink, then cut into 1-inch pieces.
Mix the dashi, mirin, soy sauce and sugar. Beat the other two eggs.

Simmer half the onion in the sauce for 4 to 5 minutes until translucent, lay the cutlet pieces on top, drizzle in the beaten egg and cover for about 30 seconds until half set. Repeat for the second bowl.
Slide each cutlet and egg portion with its sauce over a bowl of hot rice and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Air Fryer Steak Bites and Potatoes

lines.text: 2 lb sirloin steak, cut into 1-inch bites
2 tbsp olive oil (1 tbsp for the potatoes, 1 tbsp for the steak)
1 tsp garlic powder (plus 1/2 tsp in the marinade)

instructions: Heat the air fryer to 400 F (200 C). Toss the potatoes with 1 tbsp oil, garlic powder, smoked paprika, pepper and salt.
Air fry the potatoes for 10 minutes.
Toss the steak bites with the remaining oil, soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce and a little garlic powder while the potatoes cook.
Push the potatoes aside, add the steak in one layer and air fry 6 to 8 minutes, checking at 6 for medium-rare to medium.
Move everything to a large bowl, mix the melted butter with the garlic and parsley, pour it over and toss right away.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Beef and Potato Curry

lines.text: 1 tsp ginger paste and 1 tsp garlic paste

instructions: Heat the oil in a pan, add the cinnamon and cardamom and fry 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the diced onion and saute until golden brown.
Add the beef and sear 5 to 7 minutes until browned, then stir in the ginger and garlic paste, tomatoes, turmeric, cumin and Kashmiri chili with salt to taste.
Add enough water to cover, put on a lid and simmer until the beef is tender.
Stir in the garam masala and potatoes for 3 to 4 minutes, add more water, cover and cook until the potatoes are soft.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Sukiyaki

lines.text: 1 Tokyo negi (long green onion), white part sliced
1/2 package broiled tofu (yaki dofu), about 127 g
1/4 cup soy sauce (half the sauce batch)

instructions: Mix the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar in a small pan, bring to a boil until the sugar dissolves, then turn off the heat.
Cut the napa cabbage into 2-inch pieces, slice the negi and onion, trim the shiitake and cut the tofu into pieces.
Heat a pot over medium heat, pour in enough sauce to cover the bottom and cook the beef slices on both sides.
Add the vegetables, shiitake and tofu with a little more sauce, bring to a gentle simmer and cook until tender, thinning with water if it gets too salty.
Beat the pasteurized eggs in two bowls and dip the beef and vegetables in the egg to eat.
When most of the food is gone, add the cooked udon to the broth, heat through and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Beef Kabob Koobideh

lines.text: 1 1/2 medium yellow onions, quartered, chopped fine and strained to a pulp
1/4 cup butter, melted, for brushing after grilling
1 large green bell pepper, deseeded and quartered

instructions: Chop the onions very fine in a food processor, strain out all the liquid and keep the pulp.
Knead the onion pulp with the beef, garlic, egg, salt, sumac, pepper and turmeric for several minutes until paste-like.
Divide the meat into 10 portions and press each onto a wide metal skewer in an even layer about 1/2 inch thick, then press shallow dents about an inch apart along it.
Thread the tomatoes and green pepper on narrower skewers and grill them over high heat first, then keep them warm.
Grill the kabobs, turning them often in the first few minutes so the meat holds, until cooked through but still juicy, about 10 to 15 minutes in all.
Brush the kabobs with the melted butter and serve with the grilled vegetables.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Cochinita Pibil

lines.text: 1 lb pork butt roast plus 1 lb pork shoulder (2 lb, boneless)
3/4 orange, juiced, plus 1/4 orange for the salsa
1 lime plus 1/4 lime, juiced, in place of bitter orange
1/2 purple onion, sliced, for the pickle
1 tablespoon white vinegar for the pickled onion

instructions: Blend the achiote paste, orange and lime juice, garlic, oregano, cumin seeds and salt into a smooth marinade.
Cut the pork into large chunks, coat it in the marinade and leave it covered in the fridge for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Roast the pork in a covered dish at a low oven temperature for about 3 hours, until it pulls apart easily.
Blend the habanero with a squeeze of orange and lime and a pinch of salt for the salsa, and soak the sliced red onion in the vinegar with a pinch of oregano and salt.
Shred the pork in its juices and serve with the salsa and pickled onion.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Steak Pizzaiola

lines.text: 500 g thin, lean beef (top sirloin), pounded flat and cut into strips

instructions: Pound the beef between two sheets of baking paper with a mallet until thin, then cut it into small pieces or strips.
Warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium-low heat, add a splash of water and the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Crush the peeled tomatoes by hand into the pan, stir in the passata, oregano and salt, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the beef a little at a time and cook for no more than 2 minutes, stirring gently.
Turn off the heat, add the pepper and tear in the basil.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Pork Tenderloin with Romesco Sauce

lines.text: 2 cups sweet potatoes, cut into cubes
2 tablespoons for searing, 1 tablespoon for the sweet potatoes and 1/4 cup for the romesco

instructions: Char the whole red pepper at 500 F or under the broiler, turning it until blackened, then cool it in a paper bag and peel and seed it.
Toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tablespoon of oil and some of the salt and bake at 375 F for 20 minutes, turning once halfway.
Pat the tenderloins dry, season with salt and pepper, sear in 2 tablespoons of oil for about 8 minutes in total, then roast at 425 F for 10 minutes and rest for 10 minutes.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 4 to 5 minutes, then blend them with the peeled pepper, garlic, tomato puree, parsley, vinegar and paprika, stream in the remaining oil and season.
Slice the pork and serve with the sweet potatoes and a generous spoonful of romesco.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Picanha with Egg Farofa

lines.text: 2 tablespoons prepared Brazilian sofrito made only from onion, garlic and olive oil

instructions: Preheat the grill to 350 F and mix the sofrito, mustard powder and dried parsley into a rub.
Cut the picanha with the grain into 4 steaks, season with salt and pepper, and rub with the sofrito mixture.
Grill the steaks on all sides to your preferred doneness, then rest them for 5 minutes.
Melt the butter in a skillet, soften the onion for 2 minutes, scramble in the eggs until just set, then stir in the cassava flour and cilantro and season.
Slice the steaks across the grain and serve with the farofa.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Carne Molida (Latin Ground Beef Skillet)

lines.text: 2 tbsp pitted green olives or alcaparrado, chopped

instructions: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet over high heat, season with salt and break it into small pieces.
Lower the heat to medium-low, add the onion, garlic and sofrito, and cook for 4 to 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato sauce, diced potato, olives with 2 tablespoons of their brine, water, cumin and achiote.
Add the cilantro and bay leaf, cover, and cook on low about 30 minutes until the meat and potato are tender and the sauce thickens.
Remove the bay leaf, taste for salt, and serve warm.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Italian Breaded Pork Chops
instructions: Beat the eggs with the milk, half the salt and half the pepper in a shallow bowl.
In a second bowl stir together the breadcrumbs, parmesan, Italian seasoning, garlic powder, parsley and the remaining salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat.
Dip each chop in the egg mixture, then press it into the crumb mixture to coat both sides.
Brown the chops 4 to 6 minutes per side, until they read 135F in the center.
Rest the chops 10 minutes so the temperature rises to 145F, then slice and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Soutzoukakia (Greek Baked Meatballs in Tomato Sauce)

lines.text: 6 cloves garlic, minced (4 for the meatballs, 2 for the sauce)
4 teaspoons ground cumin (2 for the meatballs, 2 for the sauce)

instructions: Knead the beef with the eggs, 4 cloves of garlic, 2 teaspoons cumin, cinnamon, olive oil, breadcrumbs, salt and pepper, then chill for 1 hour.
Shape the mix into oblong meatballs of about 70 g each and bake at 200C/390F until golden.
Saute the grated onion in a little olive oil, stir in the tomato paste and 2 teaspoons cumin for 2 minutes, then add the last 2 cloves of garlic for a few minutes.
Pour in the wine, passata and sugar, bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Slide the baked meatballs into the sauce, cover and simmer on low for 30 minutes, adding a splash of water if it thickens too fast.
Taste for salt and pepper and serve hot with plenty of sauce.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Giouvetsi (Greek Beef Stew with Orzo)

lines.text: 1 kg diced beef or veal shoulder (35 ounces)
100 g grated kefalotyri or feta cheese (5 ounces)

instructions: Pat the beef dry, then cook the onions and carrots in 1/2 cup olive oil for 5 minutes. Raise the heat and brown the beef on all sides.
Stir in the tomato paste for a minute, pour in the wine and let it cook off.
Add the tomatoes, sugar, cinnamon stick, salt, pepper and enough water to cover the meat, then simmer with the lid on about 45 minutes until the beef is tender.
Meanwhile, toast the orzo in 3 tbsp olive oil in another pan until golden.
Remove the cinnamon stick, tip the beef and sauce into an oven tray with the orzo, mix and add water so the pasta is just covered.
Cover with foil and bake at 180C for 30 minutes, uncover, add a splash of water if dry and bake 15 minutes more.
Sprinkle with grated cheese and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Albondigas Soup

lines.text: 1 1/2 onions for the soup plus 1/4 onion for the meatballs
4 to 5 garlic cloves for the soup plus 3 for the meatballs
1/2 cup uncooked rice in the soup plus 1/2 cup cooked rice in the meatballs, as dry rice

instructions: Roast the tomatoes at 400F for 20 to 30 minutes, until blistered and soft.
Mix the beef with the eggs, mint, grated 1/4 onion, 3 garlic cloves, the cooked rice, salt and pepper, and roll into 1-inch meatballs.
Brown 1 1/2 onions and 4 to 5 garlic cloves in oil, then blend them with the roasted tomatoes and the chipotle.
Sweat the potatoes, carrots and 1/2 cup raw rice in oil in a large pot for a few minutes.
Add the tomato puree, stock, oregano, salt and pepper and bring to a boil.
Lower in the meatballs, simmer 20 to 25 minutes until the vegetables and rice are tender, and adjust the seasoning.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Juicy Cuban Mojo Pork Roast

lines.text: 4 lb / 2 kg boneless skinless pork shoulder (pork butt)
1 cup fresh orange juice (3/4 cup for the marinade, 1/4 cup for the sauce)
10 tbsp lime juice (1/2 cup for the marinade, 2 tbsp for the sauce)

instructions: Blend the olive oil, cilantro, mint, garlic, oregano, cumin, orange zest, three-quarters of the orange juice, lime juice, salt and pepper until the herbs are finely chopped.
Coat the pork shoulder in the marinade in a bag set in a bowl and refrigerate overnight.
Lift the pork out, reserve the marinade, and leave the pork on the counter for 1 hour. Heat the oven to 425 F (220 C).
Roast uncovered for 30 minutes, then lower the oven to 375 F (190 C) and roast for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, basting with the pan juices every half hour, until the pork reaches 160 F (70 C).

Rest the pork loosely covered with foil for 20 minutes while you boil the reserved marinade with the remaining orange juice, 2 tbsp lime juice and 2 tbsp pan drippings for a minute to make the mojo sauce.
Slice the pork and serve with the mojo sauce on the side.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chinese Pork with Noodles

lines.text: 750 g fresh white flour noodles, cooked

instructions: Stir the chilli bean sauce, sweet bean sauce, dark soy sauce, black vinegar and stock together in a bowl.
Cook the noodles as the packet directs and keep them warm.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat, cook the onion for 1 minute, then add the garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute until the onion turns translucent.
Add the pork and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Pour in the sauce and cook 3 to 5 minutes until most of it has reduced.
Divide the noodles between bowls, top with the pork, add the cucumber batons on the side and mix everything together to eat.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Moo Ping Thai Grilled Pork Skewers with Sticky Rice

lines.text: 3 tsp Thai black soy sauce or kecap manis

instructions: Soak the sticky rice overnight, drain it and steam it for about 20 minutes until tender.
Pound the garlic, coriander roots and white pepper to a paste and stir in the palm sugar, fish sauce, kecap manis, oil, cornflour and coconut milk.
Slice the pork loin about 2 mm thick, coat it in the marinade and rest it for 1 hour.
Cut the pork fat into thin pieces and thread it onto skewers alternating with concertina-folded pork slices.
Grill the skewers 2 to 3 minutes per side, basting with a little extra coconut milk, until the pork is cooked through.
Serve the skewers hot with the sticky rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Pork Schnitzel

lines.text: 2 lb boneless pork chops, trimmed and sliced into 1/2 inch cutlets
about 3 tbsp extra light olive oil, for frying

instructions: Trim the pork chops, slice them into 1/2 inch cutlets and pound them between plastic wrap to 1/4 inch.
Mix the flour, salt, garlic powder, paprika and pepper in one dish, beat the eggs in a second and put the panko in a third.
Coat each cutlet in the seasoned flour, then the egg, then press it into the panko.
Heat about 1/8 inch of oil in a large skillet to about 350 F (175 C).
Fry the cutlets in a single layer 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and 145 F (63 C) inside.
Rest the cutlets on a wire rack for 3 minutes and serve with lemon wedges.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Thai Beef and Basil Stir-fry with Fried Egg

lines.text: 2 mild large red chillies, 4 spicy Thai chillies and 1 bird's eye chilli
1 1/2 cups holy or Thai basil leaves
2 cups steamed jasmine rice, to serve
2 tbsp vegetable oil, for frying the eggs

instructions: Crush the chillies and garlic together into a coarse paste and stir the oyster sauce, fish sauce, pepper and sugar together for the sauce.
Heat the oil in a wok until very hot and fry the eggs until the edges are crisp and the yolks are still runny. Set them aside.
Stir-fry the chilli and garlic paste for a few seconds until fragrant.
Add the beef mince and cook over high heat, breaking it up, until browned.
Pour in the sauce and toss, then add the basil and stir until just wilted.
Serve over steamed rice topped with a fried egg.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Bo Kho Vietnamese Beef Stew

lines.text: 1.3 kg (3 lb) beef brisket, cut into 1 by 2 inch cubes
1 kg (2 lb) carrots, cut into bite-sized pieces
4 stalks lemongrass, cut into 3-inch lengths and bruised

instructions: Mix the brisket cubes with the sugar, five-spice powder, grated ginger, half the garlic and the soy sauce and marinate for 1 hour.
In a large pot, saute the remaining garlic with the lemongrass and star anise until fragrant, then brown the marinated beef on all sides.
Stir in the tomato sauce, then pour in the coconut water and beef broth and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer gently until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the carrots and simmer until they are soft and the beef pulls apart easily, then remove the lemongrass and star anise.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Italian Meatballs

lines.text: 1 lightly packed cup diced white sandwich bread, crusts removed
1 small onion, grated, plus 3/4 cup finely chopped onion for the sauce
4 garlic cloves, minced (2 for the meatballs, 2 for the sauce)
1 3/4 teaspoons salt, divided between meatballs and sauce

instructions: Grate the onion into a large bowl, add the diced bread and mix until the bread softens in the onion juice.
Add the beef, pork, egg, parsley, half the garlic, parmesan and half the salt, mix with your hands and roll into heaped-tablespoon balls.
Brown the meatballs in half the olive oil in a large non-stick pan for 3 to 4 minutes, then set them aside, still raw in the middle.
Heat the remaining oil in the pan and soften the chopped onion and remaining garlic, then add the passata, Italian herbs and remaining salt and bring to a gentle simmer.
Return the meatballs and their juices to the sauce and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until cooked through.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Classic Pot Roast

lines.text: 4.5 lb beef chuck roast (4 to 5 lb)
5 to 6 whole carrots, peeled and cut into 2-inch pieces
2 tablespoons cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons cold water, to thicken the sauce (optional)

instructions: Rub the roast with 3 teaspoons of the salt and leave it uncovered at room temperature for 1 hour, and heat the oven to 325 F.
Sear the roast in the olive oil in a large Dutch oven for about 3 minutes per side, then set it on a plate.
Soften the onion in the pot, stir in the garlic, then the tomato paste for 2 minutes, and pour in the wine to scrape up the browned bits.
Add the beef stock, thyme, parsley and the remaining salt, return the roast with the carrots and bring to a simmer.
Cover and bake at 325 F until the roast pulls apart easily, about 3 hours.
Shred the meat, and if you want a thicker sauce, simmer the cornstarch slurry into the liquid before returning the meat to it.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Carne Asada Salad

lines.text: 1 boneless strip steak, 1 inch thick, trimmed (about 10 ounces)

instructions: Rub the steak all over with the garlic, then season with the cumin, salt and any black pepper you like.
Broil or grill the steak about 3 minutes per side for medium-rare to medium, or sear it in a very hot skillet.
Squeeze a lime wedge over each half of the steak, let it rest briefly, then slice it thin.
Divide the greens, pico de gallo, cheese and guacamole between two plates and top with the steak slices.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Slow-Cooker Hawaiian Pulled Pork Sandwiches

lines.text: 5 pounds boneless pork butt or shoulder
2 tablespoons rice vinegar for the sauce, plus 1/4 cup rice wine vinegar for the slaw
Hawaiian buns, for serving (one per serving, about 38 g each)

instructions: Mix the onion powder, salt and garlic powder and rub the mix all over the pork.
Put the pork in the slow cooker and cook on low for 8 hours.
Shred the pork with two forks, removing any large pieces of fat, and skim the fat from the cooking liquid.
Whisk 2 cups of the skimmed liquid with the pineapple, hoisin, honey, soy sauce and 2 tablespoons of the vinegar, stir it into the pork and cook on low for 1 hour.
Toss the cabbage with the remaining vinegar and the sugar and let it wilt for about 20 minutes, tossing often.
Pile the pork on the buns and top with the slaw.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Classic Spanish Lentils with Salmon

lines.text: 2 salmon fillets (7 oz / 200 g each), cut into bite-sized pieces

instructions: Warm the olive oil in a stock pot over medium heat. Finely chop the onion and both peppers and roughly chop the garlic.
Cook the vegetables for about 4 minutes, then stir in the smoked paprika and cumin and add the grated tomatoes. Simmer about 3 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add the rinsed lentils and the vegetable broth, bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low for 20 to 25 minutes until the lentils are fully cooked.
Pat the salmon dry, season with salt and pepper, and cut into bite-sized pieces while the lentils cook.
Season the lentils, stir in the salmon, cover and cook 1 to 2 minutes until the salmon is just cooked through.
Ladle into shallow bowls and scatter with chopped parsley.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Air Fryer Salmon Patties

lines.text: 1 tsp Old Bay seasoning — use OLD BAY Classic Seasoning (US 6 oz)
12 ounces cooked wild salmon, flaked (from 1 lb raw wild salmon)

instructions: Cook the salmon fillet (bake or pan-cook) until it flakes easily, then cool and flake it, discarding any skin. Line the air fryer basket with parchment or spray it with oil.
Mix the eggs, red onion, dill, mayonnaise, Dijon and Old Bay in a bowl.
Fold in the flaked salmon and the panko until combined.
Freeze the mixture for 10 minutes so it holds together. If it is too wet, add another tablespoon of panko.
Form 6 tight patties and set them in the basket, then air fry at 400F for 8 to 10 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden.
Serve over greens or in bowls with a squeeze of lemon, 2 patties per serving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Spanish Chickpea & Cod Stew

lines.text: 2 cans chickpeas (15.5 oz / 440 g each), drained and rinsed
2 cod fillets (8 oz / 250 g each), cut into bite-sized pieces
3 oz fresh spinach (100 g), roughly chopped

instructions: Cover the eggs with cold water, bring to a boil, turn off the heat, cover and leave 11 to 12 minutes, then cool and peel.
Meanwhile warm the olive oil in a stock pot and saute the chopped onion, garlic and green pepper for 3 to 4 minutes.
Stir in the smoked paprika and the grated tomatoes, season, and simmer about 4 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add the chickpeas, fish broth and bay leaf, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low-medium for 15 minutes.
Add the seasoned cod pieces, cover and cook 3 to 4 minutes until cooked through, then stir in the spinach until wilted.
Serve in shallow bowls topped with the halved eggs.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Lemon Tuna Steaks on Roasted Veggies

lines.text: 2 tbsp olive oil, for the tuna
1 tbsp olive oil for the vegetables, plus 2 tsp to finish
1 lemon, zest in strips for the tuna, plus 2 tsp juice to finish
Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste (about 1/2 tsp salt)

instructions: Coat the tuna steaks in 2 tbsp olive oil and black pepper and rub the cut side of the lemon zest over them. Do not salt yet.
Heat the oven to 400F. Cut the carrots and potatoes into even pieces, toss with the garlic, 1 tbsp of the olive oil, salt and pepper, and roast about 40 minutes until the potatoes are almost done.
Add the asparagus, toss with a little more oil if needed, and return to the oven.
Heat a heavy pan over medium heat until very hot. Discard the zest, salt the tuna on both sides and sear without moving until the bottom third is brown.
Flip and cook until the bottom third of the other side is brown and the middle stays pink.
Plate the vegetables, set the tuna on top right away, and finish each steak with 1 tsp lemon juice and 1 tsp olive oil.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Ahi Tuna Poke Bowl

lines.text: White and black sesame seeds, for garnish (about 2 tsp)

instructions: Rinse the sushi rice in a fine mesh colander until the water runs clear.
Cook the rice with 1 1/2 cups water: bring to a boil, reduce to low, cover and cook for 20 minutes.
While the rice cooks, cut the ahi tuna into bite-sized cubes.
Stir the tamari, sesame oil and rice vinegar together, add the tuna and stir gently to coat, then mix in the green onion.
Spoon the rice into bowls and top with the tuna, sliced cucumber and diced avocado.
Sprinkle with white and black sesame seeds and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Blackened Salmon
instructions: Stir the paprika, salt, garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, thyme, cayenne and black pepper together in a small bowl.
Pat the salmon dry, drizzle on 1 tablespoon of the olive oil and rub it in.
Sprinkle the spice mix over the fillets and rub it in so they are evenly coated.
Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Lay the salmon in the pan top side down and cook 2 to 3 minutes until the crust darkens.
Flip and cook another 2 to 3 minutes until cooked through, then serve or portion for meal prep.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Fish en Papillote (Fish in a Bag)

lines.text: 2 x 160 g (5.6 oz) snapper fillets, skin off
200 g (7 oz) fingerling potatoes, peeled and sliced 0.5 cm thick
1 red bell pepper, cored and sliced 0.5 cm thick
1/2 red onion, cut into thin wedges

instructions: Heat the oven to 190 C (375 F). Brown the sliced potatoes in 2 tablespoons of the oil for 4 minutes.
Add the zucchini, pepper, onion, garlic and half the salt and pepper, toss for about 1 minute, then set aside.
Set two sheets of foil topped with parchment on the counter and divide the vegetables between them.
Pat the snapper dry, season with the remaining salt and pepper and lay it on the vegetables.
Top each fish with 3 dill sprigs, drizzle with the last tablespoon of oil and 1 tablespoon of wine, then fold and seal each parcel.
Bake the parcels on a tray for 18 minutes, rest 3 minutes, then open carefully and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Acqua Pazza (Italian Poached Fish)

lines.text: 2 x 180 g (6 oz) snapper fillets, skin on
1/2 medium fennel bulb, sliced 1 cm thick
1/2 large red chilli, seeds removed and chopped
3 garlic cloves, 2 minced and 1 halved for rubbing
25 red and yellow cherry tomatoes, halved

instructions: Cook the fennel and onion in 2 tablespoons of the oil over medium heat for 4 minutes until softened.
Stir in the minced garlic and chilli for 1 minute, then add the cherry tomatoes and cook 4 minutes.
Turn the heat to high, pour in the wine and boil 2 to 3 minutes until reduced by half. Add 2 cups of water and half the salt.
Simmer 20 to 25 minutes until the broth has reduced by about two thirds, then salt the flesh side of the fish.
Lay the fish skin side down on the sauce, cover and cook about 6 minutes until just cooked through, then lift out and stir the basil and parsley into the broth.
Brush the baguette slices with the last tablespoon of oil and salt, bake at 180 C (350 F) for 10 minutes, rub with the halved garlic, and serve the fish and broth over the crostini.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Shrimp Etouffee

lines.text: 1 1/2 pounds medium shrimp, peeled and deveined

instructions: Toss the shrimp with the Cajun seasoning. Sear them in the oil over medium-high heat for about 2 minutes until just pink, then set aside.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat, stir in the flour and cook 6 to 8 minutes until it is the color of peanut butter.
Add the onion, pepper, celery and garlic and cook until slightly softened.
Stir in the stock a little at a time until the sauce is smooth.
Add the tomatoes and Worcestershire, bring to a boil, then simmer on low, uncovered, about 20 minutes.
Stir the shrimp and their juices back in and heat just until warmed through. Serve over rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Spanish Seafood Stew from Valencia

lines.text: 1 cleaned tube of squid, cut into 1/4 inch rings
1/2 lb raw jumbo shrimp, peeled and deveined

instructions: Heat the olive oil over medium heat and fry the baguette slice, garlic and almonds for 3 to 4 minutes until golden, then remove them.
Saute the squid rings in the same pan for 1 to 2 minutes and set them aside.
Cook the onion for 3 to 4 minutes, stir in the paprika, add the tomatoes and saute 5 to 10 minutes.
Pound the fried garlic, almonds and baguette with the saffron to a paste in a mortar.
Pour the fish broth into the pan and simmer 10 minutes, then stir a ladle of broth into the paste and mix it into the pan.
Add the seasoned cod pieces in one layer and simmer 2 to 3 minutes, flip them, add the squid and shrimp, and simmer 2 to 3 minutes more until just cooked. Serve from the pan.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Cajun Blackened Fish

lines.text: 4 catfish fillets, about 200 g / 7 oz each
1 cup corn kernels, frozen and thawed

instructions: Mix the paprika, cumin, onion powder, garlic powder, thyme, salt and cayenne in a shallow dish.
Pat the catfish dry and coat both sides in the spice mix, shaking off the excess.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat until hot.
Cook the fillets 4 to 5 minutes until the rub turns black, flip, and cook the other side until the fish flakes.
Meanwhile stir the corn and day-old rice into the melted butter in a second pan until hot.
Serve the fish at once over the corn rice salad.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Puttanesca Fish Tray Bake

lines.text: 4 cod fillets, about 170 g / 6 oz each
3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, divided

instructions: Heat the oven to 220 C (430 F). Toss the potatoes with half the oil and a pinch of salt, spread them on a rimmed tray and roast for 20 minutes.
Mix the fennel, cherry tomatoes, olives, garlic, capers, anchovy and crushed tomatoes in the same bowl.
Add the sauce to the tray, toss with the potatoes and return to the oven for 10 minutes.
Pat the cod dry and season both sides with the remaining salt.
Set the cod on the sauce, drizzle with the remaining oil and bake 15 minutes until it flakes easily.
Scatter the basil over the tray and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Maryland Crab Cakes

lines.text: 1 lb lump crab meat, picked over
2 1/2 tbsp mayonnaise in the cakes plus 1/2 cup in the tartar sauce
1 1/2 tsp Dijon in the cakes plus 1 tsp in the tartar sauce
1 tbsp minced red onion in the tartar sauce
1 tsp Old Bay seasoning — use OLD BAY Classic Seasoning (US 6 oz)
2 tbsp vegetable or canola oil for frying

instructions: Whisk the eggs, 2 1/2 tbsp mayonnaise, 1 1/2 tsp Dijon, the Worcestershire, Old Bay and celery in a large bowl.
Fold in the crab and panko gently so the lumps stay whole, then shape into 6 cakes of about 1/2 cup each.
Chill the cakes, covered, for at least 1 hour so they set.
Stir the remaining mayonnaise, the relish, red onion, 1 tsp Dijon and the lemon juice into a tartar sauce.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick pan over medium heat and cook the cakes 3 to 5 minutes a side until golden.
Serve the cakes warm with the tartar sauce.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Salmon Nicoise Salad

lines.text: 4 boneless skinless salmon fillets, 4 oz (113 g) each
8 cups bibb or butter lettuce, torn

instructions: Heat the oven to 325 F (165 C). Mix the onion powder, 2 tablespoons of the mustard and the salt, and spread about 1 tablespoon on each salmon fillet.
Bake the salmon for 15 to 20 minutes, then let it cool and flake it into large pieces.
Whisk the remaining mustard with the white wine vinegar and olive oil to make the dressing.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 to 25 minutes, adding the green beans for the last 5 minutes. Drain, rinse under cold water, cool and halve the potatoes.
Spread the lettuce over a large platter and arrange the salmon, potatoes, green beans, eggs, olives and artichoke hearts in groups on top.
Drizzle with the dressing and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Samkeh Harra

lines.text: 1 kg boneless white fish fillets, such as cod
1/2 cup plus 1 tbsp canola oil, for the fish, the sauce and frying the nuts
1 cup chopped fresh parsley, half for the sauce and half to garnish
1 tsp salt, plus more to taste
1/4 cup pine nuts, fried until light golden

instructions: Heat the oven to 200 C (400 F). Slice the onion into thin half-moons and crush the garlic with the salt.
Lay the fish in an oiled baking tray with the onion, ground coriander and chilli flakes, drizzle with the oil and bake 15 to 20 minutes until nearly cooked.
Whisk the tahini with the garlic paste, lemon juice and water until pourable, then stir in the juices from the tray.
Stir the cilantro and half the parsley into the sauce, pour it over the fish and bake 10 minutes more.
Fry the pine nuts in a little oil until pale gold; they keep colouring after leaving the oil.
Top with the remaining parsley and the nuts and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Thai Coconut Curry Mussels

lines.text: 400 g cooked frozen mussels, defrosted, beards removed
450 g hot cooked jasmine rice, for serving

instructions: Slice the onion and chilli, mince the garlic and chop the coriander. Defrost the cooked mussels and remove any beards.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and soften the onion, garlic and chilli for about 4 minutes.
Stir in the red curry paste and cook for a minute until fragrant, then pour in the coconut milk and simmer for 3 minutes.
Season with the sugar, fish sauce and lime juice, tasting and adjusting the sugar to suit the curry paste.
Add the mussels and warm them through in the sauce for 2 to 3 minutes, then scatter over the coriander.
Spoon the mussels and sauce over hot jasmine rice in three bowls.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Trinidad Curry Fish with Mango

lines.text: 3 lb fish steaks such as red snapper (about 1,150 g edible fish)
1 cup all-purpose flour, for dusting (about 1/3 cup, 40 g, counted as clinging to the fish)
2 cups vegetable oil for frying (1/4 cup, about 55 g, counted as absorbed)
1/2 green mango, cut into thin strips
1 1/2 tsp salt, split between the fish and the sauce

instructions: Rinse the fish with cold water, season it with half the salt and marinate in the fridge for at least an hour, then bring it to room temperature.
Dust the fish in flour and fry in the vegetable oil on both sides until golden but not cooked through, then set aside.
Cook half the onion in the olive oil in a wide pan until the edges brown, then stir in the curry powder with 1/2 cup water and cook until the water has evaporated and the curry is fragrant.
Add the mango, the rest of the onion and the garlic and stir-fry for a minute, then add 1 cup water and cook until the mango softens and the oil separates.
Add 2 to 3 cups water, the remaining salt and the thyme and bring to a boil.
Add the fried fish, okra and tomato, spooning the sauce over the fish without turning it. Simmer 7 to 10 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Serve over steamed rice, dumplings or boiled provisions.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Spanish Cod and Potato Stew

lines.text: 1 large 12 oz (340 g) cod fillet, cut in 1/2 inch cubes
1/2 tsp sea salt, plus black pepper to taste

instructions: Slice the leek and rinse it well, then pat dry. Mince the garlic, dice the onion, pepper and potato, and cut the cod into 1/2 inch cubes, seasoning it with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large stock pot over medium heat. Cook the garlic and onion 2 minutes, then add the leek for 3 minutes.
Add the red pepper, potato, thyme and rosemary, then pour in the wine and fish broth and bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer gently until the potato is very tender, about 25 minutes.
Stir in the cod, replace the lid and cook 10 minutes more until it flakes.
Ladle into two bowls and garnish each with a rosemary sprig.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Golden Turmeric Fish

lines.text: 4 white fish fillets (180 g each), skinless
1 tsp salt in total (fish, paste and sambal)
1 tsp ground turmeric (instead of 2 tsp fresh)
1 large red chilli, deseeded and diced
600 g hot cooked jasmine rice, for serving

instructions: Heat the oven to 200C and line a tray with baking paper. Season the fish with half the salt and the lime juice and chill it for 10 minutes.
Blend the shallot, garlic, turmeric, ginger, macadamia nuts, a little salt, 1 tbsp oil and 2 tbsp water into a smooth paste.
Smear the paste over the top of the fish and bake for 15 minutes until the centre reaches 55C.
Lift the fish off the tray and rest it for 3 minutes.
For the sambal, soften the quartered tomatoes and diced chilli in 2 tsp oil with a pinch of salt for 2 minutes.
Serve the fish over hot jasmine rice with the sambal spooned on top.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Hawaiian Garlic Shrimp

lines.text: 3 tbsp canola oil, to fry in

instructions: Peel and devein the shrimp if needed and pat them very dry. Mince the garlic.
Toss the shrimp with the cornstarch, paprika, cayenne, salt and pepper until evenly coated.
Melt the butter in a small pan and cook the garlic gently until fragrant, then take it off the heat and add the lemon juice.
Heat the canola oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and fry the shrimp in batches for about 2 minutes a side until golden and cooked through.
Toss the shrimp in the garlic butter and serve at once.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Spanish Cod and Shrimp Skillet

lines.text: 5 tbsp extra virgin olive oil (3 tbsp for the onions, 2 tbsp for the garlic sauce)
6 cloves garlic (4 for the base, 2 for the garlic sauce)
1 lb raw shrimp, peeled and deveined

instructions: Warm 3 tbsp of the olive oil in a large pan over medium heat, add the sliced onions and stir every minute or two until translucent.
Pat the cod and shrimp dry and season the cod on both sides and the shrimp on one side with salt and pepper.
Stir the chopped garlic into the onions for 1 minute, add the flour and stir for 1 minute, then pour in the wine with the thyme and crushed red pepper and cook until the alcohol smells gone.
Add the fish broth and stir gently for 4 to 5 minutes until the sauce is slightly creamy, then season with salt and pepper.
Lay the cod in a single layer, turn each fillet once, scatter the shrimp over, cover and simmer on low-medium for 5 to 6 minutes until both are just cooked through.
Pound the 2 remaining garlic cloves, the parsley and a pinch of salt to a paste in a mortar, then stir in the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil and the lemon juice.
Spoon the garlic sauce over the cod and serve at once.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Kung Pao Shrimp

lines.text: 1 pound jumbo raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
3 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce (1 tbsp for the marinade, 2 tbsp for the sauce)
2 tbsp + 2 tsp rice vinegar (2 tsp for the marinade, 2 tbsp for the sauce)
1 1/2 tsp sesame oil (1/2 tsp for the marinade, 1 tsp for the sauce)
3 tsp cornstarch (1 tsp for the marinade, 2 tsp for the sauce)
1 red bell pepper and 1 green bell pepper, diced into 1/4-inch pieces
