instructions: Whisk 1 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tsp rice vinegar, 1/2 tsp sesame oil and 1 tsp cornstarch in a bowl, toss in the patted-dry shrimp and marinate for at least 15 minutes.
Whisk the remaining 2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp sesame oil, the red pepper flakes and 2 tsp cornstarch into a smooth sauce, and dice the peppers and onion.
Heat 1 tbsp canola oil over medium-high heat, sear the shrimp and marinade for 1 to 2 minutes until golden underneath, turn and cook about 1 minute more, then move to a plate.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil, stir the red pepper, green pepper and onion for 1 to 2 minutes until crisp-tender, then add the peanuts.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook about 30 seconds until fragrant, then pour in the sauce.
Return the shrimp and its juices, stir for 1 minute until coated and hot, and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vietnamese Braised Caramelized Catfish (Ca Kho)

lines.text: 3 lb catfish steaks, 1 inch thick (weighed as about 80% edible, bone-in)
3 tbsp granulated sugar (1 tbsp for the marinade, 2 tbsp for the caramel)
1/2 can Coco Rico coconut soda (6 oz) — use Coco Rico Natural Coconut Flavored Soda (US)

instructions: Marinate the catfish steaks in the fish sauce and 1 tbsp of the sugar for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wide skillet or clay pot over medium-high heat and sprinkle the remaining 2 tbsp sugar in a thin layer.
Let the sugar melt and caramelize to a dark amber color.
Stir in the minced shallot and garlic for about 15 seconds until fragrant.
Add the catfish with all its marinade, turn the steaks to coat them in the caramel, then pour in the coconut soda.
Braise on a low simmer, partly covered, for 20 minutes, flipping the steaks at the halfway mark or spooning the liquid over them if they are too delicate to turn.
Top with the green onion and black pepper and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Seafood Pasta

lines.text: 1 pound mussels in the shell (weighed as about 136 g of meat)
8 ounces large shrimp, peeled and deveined
3 tbsp unsalted butter (2 tbsp for the seafood, 1 tbsp for the shallot)

instructions: Soak the mussels in cool water with a little flour for 30 minutes, drain, pull off any beards, scrub them and discard any that stay open.
Boil the linguine in well-salted water until al dente, reserve 1 cup of the pasta water, and drain.

Melt 2 tbsp of the butter with the oil in a wide deep skillet, sear the scallops for 1 1/2 minutes, move them aside, add the shrimp and cook about 2 minutes more until opaque, then take the seafood out.
Lower the heat, melt the remaining 1 tbsp butter, soften the shallot for 3 minutes, then cook the garlic and red pepper flakes for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine, bring to the boil, add the mussels, cover and steam for about 5 minutes until they open, discarding any that stay shut.
Add the linguine, lemon juice, scallops, shrimp and parsley, toss with some of the reserved pasta water, and serve right away.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Portuguese Seafood Stew

lines.text: 3 dozen littleneck clams, scrubbed (weighed as about 9 g of meat each)
1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
1/2 cup fresh parsley, finely chopped (1/4 cup in the pot, 1/4 cup to top)

instructions: Scrub the clams, mince the garlic, chop the onion and parsley, slice the chorizo and dice the tomato.
Soften the garlic and onion in the olive oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat for 4 minutes.
Add the chorizo, tomato, wine, a splash of water, the bay leaf, half the parsley and a little salt and pepper, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the clams, stir, cover and cook for about 5 minutes until they open, discarding any that stay closed.
Add the shrimp and scallops and cook 2 to 3 minutes until the shrimp turn opaque and the seafood is cooked through.
Ladle into bowls and top with the remaining parsley.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Salmon Teriyaki Donburi

lines.text: 10 ounces skinless, boneless salmon fillet, cut into bite-size pieces
2 cups cooked short grain Japanese rice

instructions: Sprinkle the salmon pieces with salt and let them rest on a plate for 10 minutes.
Dust the salmon pieces with flour on all sides, adding a little more if they still look wet.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium high heat and add the salmon.
Cook for 2 minutes, flip the pieces and cook 1 minute more.
Pour in the teriyaki sauce and cook 1 to 2 minutes until it bubbles, thickens and coats the fish, then turn off the heat.
Fill two bowls with rice, layer on the spinach and then the salmon, and top with scallions and sesame seeds.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Shrimp Fried Rice

lines.text: 1 pound medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
3 cups cold leftover cooked brown rice

instructions: Pat the shrimp dry and toss them with the cornstarch, salt and pepper.

Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wide skillet or wok over medium high heat and sear the shrimp 1 to 2 minutes on the first side and about 30 seconds on the second until pink. Move them to a large plate.
Melt half the butter in the pan, pour in the beaten eggs and scramble until barely set, then add them to the shrimp.
Add the remaining oil and the white parts of the green onions for 15 seconds, then add the cold rice, spread it flat and let it sizzle 1 to 2 minutes before stirring and crisping again for a minute.
Drizzle in the soy sauce and sesame oil, stir, then add the frozen peas and carrots and the remaining butter and cook 1 to 2 minutes.
Stir in the shrimp, eggs and green onion tops, breaking up the eggs, and heat for a minute before serving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Salmon in Coconut Lime Sauce

lines.text: 4 skinless salmon fillets, 180 g (6 oz) each
1 lemongrass stalk, peeled and finely grated
2 teaspoons lime zest plus lime juice to taste, from 1 lime

instructions: Season the salmon with salt and pepper, sear it in half the oil skin side up for 1 1/2 minutes, flip for 1 minute, then set it aside still raw inside.
Lower the heat, let the skillet cool a little, then warm the remaining oil and cook the garlic, ginger and lemongrass about 1 minute until the garlic is light golden.
Add the brown sugar and cook about 20 seconds until it caramelizes, then stir in the chilli paste.
Pour in the coconut milk, scraping up the browned bits, add the fish sauce and simmer 2 minutes over medium heat.
Slide the salmon back in, lower the heat and simmer gently for about 4 minutes until just cooked, then lift it out.
Stir the lime zest and lime juice into the sauce, adjust with fish sauce, and spoon it over the salmon, with rice or noodles if you like.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Shrimp Fajitas

lines.text: 1 1/2 pounds jumbo shrimp, peeled and deveined

instructions: Stir the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, paprika and oregano together to make the fajita seasoning.
Toss the shrimp with 2 tablespoons of the oil, the juice of half the lime and the seasoning, and leave them to marinate while the vegetables cook.
Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of oil in a large skillet over medium heat and saute the onion and peppers 4 to 5 minutes until softened and the onion starts to caramelize. Move them to a plate.
Cook the shrimp in the same skillet 2 to 3 minutes per side until pink and opaque.
Return the onion and peppers to the pan, toss, squeeze in the rest of the lime and serve in warm corn tortillas.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Sheet Pan Mediterranean Salmon

lines.text: 1 small red onion, cut into chunks
8 ounces white potato, cut into 1/2-inch rounds and halved
3 teaspoons extra virgin olive oil, divided

instructions: Heat the oven to 425 F and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Toss the zucchini, bell pepper, red onion and potato with 2 teaspoons of the oil, half the garlic powder, the parsley and the oregano, then spread them on the sheet.
Roast the vegetables for 20 minutes until partly tender.
Meanwhile rub the salmon with the last teaspoon of oil, the paprika and the remaining garlic powder.
Shift the vegetables over, set the salmon on the pan, top it with the olives and roast 15 minutes until it flakes easily.
Serve the salmon with the roasted vegetables.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Greek Tofu Bowls

lines.text: 2 14-ounce packages extra firm tofu, drained and pressed
2 teaspoons lemon zest and 4 tablespoons lemon juice
2 small red bell peppers, cut into 1-inch pieces

instructions: Heat the oven to 400 F, press the tofu between towels under a heavy pan, and whisk the olive oil, lemon juice and oregano into a dressing.
Stir the yogurt with the garlic, lemon zest, salt and pepper, and mix the panko with oregano, salt and pepper on a plate.
Slice each tofu block widthwise into 8 slices, coat every slice in the yogurt, then press it into the panko.
Set the slices on an oiled sheet pan and bake 20 minutes, flip, and bake 20 minutes more.
Dice the cucumber and pepper, halve the tomatoes and slice the onion while the tofu bakes.
Divide the vegetables among 4 bowls, top with tofu slices, drizzle with dressing and finish with feta.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Tofu Poke Bowl
instructions: Press the tofu between towels under a heavy pan, then cut it into 32 cubes.
Stir the soy sauce and crushed garlic together and pour half over the tofu. Marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Toss the cucumber and scallion whites with 2 teaspoons of the remaining marinade.
Sprinkle the cornstarch over the tofu and toss to coat.
Brown the tofu in hot sesame oil, 2 to 3 minutes per side, then toss with the rest of the marinade.
Divide greens, rice, edamame and the cucumber mix between 2 bowls, top with tofu and avocado, and finish with scallion greens and sesame seeds.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Baked Eggplant Parmesan

lines.text: 3 tablespoons olive oil, for the pans, drizzling and the sauce

instructions: Heat the oven to 375F and oil 2 baking sheets. Set up three dishes: flour with salt and pepper, beaten eggs, and panko mixed with Parmesan.
Dip each eggplant round in the flour, then the egg, then the crumb mix, and lay it on the sheets.
Drizzle the rounds with olive oil and bake for 30 to 35 minutes, turning them halfway through.
Warm the marinara in a saucepan with the garlic cooked briefly in a little oil, then stir in the basil.
Spread a little sauce in a 9x13 dish, add half the eggplant, half the remaining sauce and half the mozzarella, then repeat the layers.
Bake uncovered at 375F for 20 to 25 minutes until the cheese is melted and golden.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Tofu Stir Fry

lines.text: 1 small bunch green onions, finely chopped

instructions: Press the tofu dry in paper towels and cut it into 3/4-inch cubes.
Heat the canola oil in a large nonstick skillet or wok, add the tofu and drizzle with 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce.
Saute the tofu, stirring every minute or so, for 8 to 10 minutes until browned on all sides and the moisture has cooked off.
Add the garlic, two-thirds of the green onion, the ginger, chili paste and the remaining 2 tablespoons soy sauce and cook for 1 minute.
Add the spinach by handfuls, letting each batch wilt before the next.
Stir in the sesame seeds and sesame oil, take the pan off the heat and top with the reserved green onion.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Stir Fry Tofu with Scrambled Eggs

lines.text: 1 block (400 g) firm tofu, cut into cubes
2 stalks spring onion, cut into 1-inch lengths

instructions: Cut the firm tofu into cubes and the spring onions into 1-inch lengths. Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper.
Heat the garlic in oil in a non-stick pan and stir-fry the tofu cubes until they take on a little color and turn chewy.
Pour the eggs over the tofu and stir gently with a spatula until they set into soft curds around the cubes.
Stir in the oyster sauce, sesame oil and spring onion for a few seconds, then scatter the crispy fried shallots on top and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Paneer Lentil Curry
instructions: Cut the paneer into cubes and pan-fry it in the butter until lightly golden, then set it aside.
Chop the tomato and garlic. Toast the fennel, cumin and coriander seeds in the same pan until fragrant.
Cook the tomato and garlic with the toasted seeds, chili powder, salt and pepper until they break down into a thick masala.
Pour in the coconut milk, stir in the paneer and bring it to a gentle simmer.
Stir in the rinsed red lentils and simmer until they are soft and the curry has thickened.
Taste, adjust the salt and pepper, and serve with naan or white rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Stroganoff with Seitan and Mushrooms

lines.text: 250 g (8.8 oz) seitan, sliced lengthwise into strips about 1 1/2 inches long
3 tablespoons olive oil (1 for searing the seitan, 2 for the mushrooms, replacing the vegan butter)
1 tablespoon flour stirred into 1/2 cup water
1/2 cup vegetable broth, or more if you like
1/2 cup vegan sour cream, or more — use Tofutti Better Than Sour Cream Plain

instructions: Slice the seitan lengthwise into strips about 1 1/2 inches long and pat them dry.
Sear the seitan in 1 tablespoon of the oil for 7 to 8 minutes until golden brown, then move it to a paper-towel-lined plate.
Heat the remaining oil in a second pan and cook the onion and mushrooms with a pinch of salt over medium heat for about 12 minutes until golden.
Stir in the garlic for 40 seconds, then the paprika, then pour in the wine and cook until the alcohol smell is gone.
Add the broth, the flour stirred into water, the miso and the mustard, and simmer 5 minutes.
Turn off the heat, fold in the vegan sour cream and the seared seitan, and serve right away.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Tofu in Tomato Sauce
instructions: Drain, rinse and dry the tofu, then cut it into 1-inch cubes and let them dry on a plate. Slice the onion and green onion separately and cut the tomatoes into wedges.
Pan-fry the tofu in 1 tablespoon of the oil over medium-high heat, about 8 minutes per side, turning gently, until golden. Move it to a plate.
In the same pan, heat the rest of the oil over medium heat and stir-fry the garlic and tomato paste briefly, then add the onion and tomatoes for 2 minutes.
Add 1/2 cup water, the soy sauce, sugar and black pepper and bring it to a simmer.
Return the tofu, cover and simmer 10 minutes, then rotate the tofu, cover and simmer another 10 minutes.
Top with the green onion and serve with hot rice if you like.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms

lines.text: 1 1/2 cups cooked cannellini beans, rinsed and drained
3 tablespoons chopped oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, drained and patted dry
2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil, plus more for garnish

instructions: Heat the oven to 400 F. Scrape the gills out of the mushroom caps, whisk 2 tablespoons of the oil with the balsamic vinegar, a pinch of salt and pepper, and brush both sides of the caps.
Roast the caps stem-side down on a lined baking sheet for 15 minutes while you make the filling.
Soften the shallot in the remaining tablespoon of oil over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, then stir in the garlic over low heat for 30 seconds.
Add the spinach by handfuls and stir until fully wilted, about 2 minutes. Turn off the heat.
Stir in the beans, crumbled goat cheese, sun-dried tomatoes, half the Parmesan and the basil, and season to taste.
Turn the caps stem-side up and mound the filling inside. Mix the panko with the remaining Parmesan and sprinkle it over the top.
Bake 10 minutes until the mushrooms are tender, then broil 2 to 3 minutes to brown the tops, watching closely. Garnish with basil and serve warm.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Greek Mac and Cheese

lines.text: 10 ounces frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
1 1/2 cups extra-sharp white Cheddar, shredded (about 6 ounces)
1 large green and 1 large red bell pepper, thinly sliced
1/2 cup sundried tomatoes, rehydrated and drained

instructions: Cook the onion, then the peppers and garlic, in a large sauté pan until tender and set the mixture aside.
Preheat the oven to 400F, squeeze the thawed spinach dry and soak the sundried tomatoes in boiling water.
Heat most of the milk, whisk the flour into the rest, stir it in and cook until thickened, then melt in the Cheddar and stir in the cottage cheese.
Boil the macaroni for 6 minutes until not quite tender, drain and mix it into the cheese sauce.
Fold in the drained sundried tomatoes, sautéed vegetables, spinach, feta and olives and spoon into a baking dish.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes until bubbly and golden, then serve warm.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Ratatouille Lasagna

lines.text: 1 medium eggplant (9 ounces), sliced 1/4 inch thick lengthwise
1 small zucchini (7 ounces), sliced thin lengthwise
1 small yellow squash (7 ounces), sliced thin lengthwise
1 small red and 1 small yellow bell pepper, diced

instructions: Preheat the oven to 375F and drain the cottage cheese in a sieve while you prepare the vegetables.
Soften the onion and garlic in a skillet, add the crushed tomatoes, diced peppers and half the basil, and simmer partly covered until thickened.
Grill the eggplant, zucchini and yellow squash slices a few minutes per side in a hot grill pan, then blot them on paper towels.
Mix the drained cottage cheese with half the mozzarella, the Parmesan, the remaining basil and the egg.
Layer sauce, eggplant, half the cheese mixture, sauce and zucchini, then the rest of the cheese mixture, sauce and yellow squash in a casserole dish.
Top with the remaining sauce and mozzarella and bake until bubbling and golden, then rest 10 to 15 minutes and cut into four.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Air Fryer Peanut Curry Tofu with Gingery Cauliflower Rice

lines.text: 14-ounce package extra-firm tofu, pressed and cubed
2 tablespoons plus 1 teaspoon reduced sodium soy sauce

instructions: Press the tofu to drain it, then cut it into small cubes.
Toss the tofu with soy sauce, grated garlic and curry powder and marinate for at least 10 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter, a little soy sauce, sriracha and ginger with warm water into a pourable sauce.
Air fry the tofu at 370F in a single layer, shaking the basket halfway, until golden and crisp.
Meanwhile sauté the garlic, ginger and scallion whites in olive oil, then cook the cauliflower rice until tender.
Toss the crisp tofu in the peanut sauce and serve over the cauliflower rice with scallion greens and chopped peanuts.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Southwest Dense Bean Salad

lines.text: 15 oz canned black beans, drained and rinsed
15 oz canned pinto beans, drained and rinsed
15 oz canned cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
1.5 cups sweet corn kernels (fresh or thawed)
1 large red bell pepper, finely diced
1 medium poblano pepper, seeded and finely diced
1 canned chipotle pepper in adobo sauce, minced

instructions: Rinse and thoroughly drain the black beans, pinto beans, and cannellini beans, then transfer them to a large salad mixing bowl.
Add diced red bell pepper, seeded poblano pepper, sweet corn, shredded red cabbage, diced red onion, sliced scallions, chopped cilantro, and pepitas.

In a glass measuring cup or small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lime juice, apple cider vinegar, maple syrup, Dijon mustard, minced chipotle pepper, adobo sauce, grated garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, and salt until emulsified.
Pour the chipotle-lime dressing over the salad and toss thoroughly until every ingredient is coated; gently fold in the diced avocado right before serving.

title: Vegan Sweet Potato Stew

lines.text: 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch cubes (~4 cups)
two 15 oz cans diced fire-roasted tomatoes with juices
15 oz can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
15 oz can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat; add diced sweet onion and sauté for 4-5 minutes until softened and translucent.
Stir in minced garlic, chili powder, smoked paprika, cumin, and cinnamon, cooking for 60 seconds until fragrant.
Add cubed sweet potatoes, fire-roasted tomatoes with their juices, rinsed chickpeas, cannellini beans, and vegetable broth. Stir well and bring to a boil.
Lower heat to medium-low, cover with lid slightly ajar, and simmer for 15-18 minutes until sweet potatoes are fork-tender.
Remove from heat, stir in tahini until dissolved and rich, then fold in fresh baby spinach until just wilted.

title: Lentil Unstuffed Shells with Whipped Lemon Ricotta

lines.text: 14 oz firm tofu, drained and pressed
14 oz can brown lentils, drained and rinsed

instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil; cook jumbo shells according to package directions until al dente, reserving 1/2 cup pasta cooking water before draining.

In a food processor, combine pressed tofu, lemon zest, lemon juice, 2 tbsp olive oil, 2 tbsp nutritional yeast, 1 tsp garlic powder, and salt; process until ultra-smooth and whipped, then fold in chopped chives.

In a large skillet, sauté onion and minced garlic in 1 tbsp olive oil for 4 minutes; stir in tomato paste, remaining nutritional yeast, diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, vegetable broth, and rinsed brown lentils, simmering for 12 minutes.
In a small dry pan, toast panko breadcrumbs with a dash of garlic powder and olive oil for 3 minutes until golden crisp.

Assemble unstuffed-style: ladle rich lentil marinara sauce onto plates, arrange tender cooked shells on top, dollop generously with whipped lemon tofu ricotta, and garnish with toasted panko and fresh basil.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Vegan Egg Roll in a Bowl

lines.text: 14 oz extra-firm tofu, pressed and crumbled
1 medium red bell pepper, thinly sliced
1 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce or tamari

instructions: Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a wide nonstick skillet or wok over medium-high heat; add sliced mushrooms and onions, cooking for 5 minutes until browned.
Add remaining olive oil along with crumbled pressed tofu, grated ginger, and minced garlic; cook for 6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tofu edges turn lightly golden.
Toss in julienned carrots, shredded cabbage, sliced bell pepper, and thawed edamame; stir-fry briskly for 4-5 minutes until vegetables are crisp-tender.
Whisk hoisin sauce, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, maple syrup, and sriracha in a small ramekin; pour over skillet and toss for 2 minutes until glossy and glazed.
Garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds; serve immediately.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Vegan General Tso's Tofu

lines.text: 16 oz extra-firm tofu, pressed and cut into 1-inch cubes
3 tbsp reduced-sodium soy sauce or tamari

instructions: Toss pressed cubed tofu in a bowl with cornstarch until every piece is evenly coated in a light powdery layer.
Heat avocado oil in a wide skillet over medium-high; arrange tofu cubes in a single layer and pan-fry for 8-10 minutes, flipping until crisp and golden on all sides.
In a small bowl, whisk soy sauce, rice vinegar, hoisin, maple syrup, tomato paste, grated ginger, minced garlic, and vegetable broth.
Push crispy tofu to one side of pan; drop dried red chilis into center for 30 seconds, then pour in the sauce mixture and simmer for 2 minutes until bubbly and thickened into a glossy glaze.
Toss crispy tofu in the glaze until thoroughly coated; serve alongside steamed bright green broccoli florets and garnish with sesame seeds.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Vegan Spicy Curry Ramen

lines.text: 2 portions organic vegan ramen noodles (approx 6 oz)
10 oz extra-firm tofu, sliced into strips and pan-seared
1.5 tbsp Japanese S&B curry powder or mild yellow curry powder
2 heads baby bok choy, halved lengthwise

instructions: Heat toasted sesame oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat; sauté minced garlic, ginger, and sliced shiitake mushrooms for 3 minutes until tender.
Stir in Japanese curry powder and cook for 1 minute to bloom spices; slowly whisk in vegetable broth, coconut milk, and soy sauce, bringing to a gentle simmer for 8 minutes.
Whisk white miso paste with 2 tablespoons of warm broth in a small cup until dissolved, then stir into the simmering curry broth; turn off heat.
In a separate pot of boiling water, cook ramen noodles for 3 minutes and blanch halved baby bok choy for 1 minute; drain well.
Divide ramen noodles between two deep bowls, ladle steaming creamy curry broth over top, and arrange pan-seared tofu strips, halved baby bok choy, mushrooms, scallions, and a drizzle of chili oil.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Black Pepper Tofu

lines.text: 14 oz extra-firm tofu, pressed and cut into bite-sized cubes
1.5 tbsp whole black peppercorns, coarsely crushed

instructions: Toss pressed tofu cubes with cornstarch in a medium bowl until dusted evenly.
Heat oil in a wide wok or skillet over high heat; pan-fry tofu cubes for 7-8 minutes, turning frequently until all sides are crisp and golden brown; remove tofu to a plate.
In the same wok with remaining oil, add crushed black peppercorns, sliced shallots, minced garlic, ginger, and red chili, tossing vigorously for 2 minutes until intensely fragrant.
Add dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, and maple syrup, stirring quickly as it bubbles into a dark peppery glaze.
Return crispy tofu to wok along with scallion batons; toss continuously for 1-2 minutes until every tofu piece is lacquered in cracked black pepper glaze.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Tofu Vindaloo

lines.text: 14 oz firm tofu, pressed and cut into cubes
3 whole dried Kashmiri chilis, soaked in warm water

instructions: In a high-speed blender, combine soaked Kashmiri chilis, vinegar, garlic, ginger, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, black peppercorns, cinnamon, and cloves with 1/4 cup water; blend to a smooth, vibrant red vindaloo paste.
In a large skillet over medium heat, melt 1 tbsp coconut oil and lightly sear pressed tofu cubes for 6 minutes until edges are pale gold; transfer tofu to a plate.
Add remaining coconut oil to skillet and cook finely chopped red onions over medium heat for 10 minutes until deeply golden brown and caramelized.
Pour in the blended vindaloo paste and cook for 4-5 minutes until the oil starts separating from the aromatics.
Stir in tomato puree, water, salt, and seared tofu; cover and simmer gently for 12 minutes so tofu absorbs the sharp, spicy vinegar sauce. Garnish with fresh cilantro.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Vegan Samosa Pie

lines.text: 1 sheet vegan commercial puff pastry, thawed
3 cups peeled and diced russet potatoes (~2 medium)
0.5 tsp dried mango powder (amchur) or lemon juice

instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Boil diced potatoes in salted water for 8 minutes until barely fork tender; drain well.
Heat oil in a skillet; add cumin seeds, crushed coriander seeds, and chopped cashews, sizzling for 1 minute until fragrant and lightly golden.
Add chopped red onion, ginger, and green chili; cook for 4 minutes, then stir in turmeric, garam masala, amchur powder, and salt.
Add boiled potatoes, green peas, water, and chopped cilantro; cook for 4-5 minutes while coarsely mashing some potatoes so the mixture holds together, then spread into a 9-inch baking dish.
Unroll vegan puff pastry over the spiced filling, crimping edges along dish rim and cutting two steam slits on top; bake for 25-30 minutes until deeply golden and flaky.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Spicy Urad Dal

lines.text: 1 cup whole or split black urad dal, rinsed
2 medium ripe Roma tomatoes, finely chopped

instructions: In a medium heavy pot or pressure cooker, combine rinsed urad dal, 3 cups water, turmeric, and 1/2 tsp salt; bring to a boil and simmer covered for 25-30 minutes until soft and creamy.
In a separate skillet, heat vegetable oil over medium; add cumin seeds, bay leaves, and cloves, sizzling for 60 seconds until aromatic.
Add chopped onion, garlic, grated ginger, and slit green chili; sauté for 6-8 minutes until onions turn reddish-brown.
Stir in chopped tomatoes, ground coriander, and Kashmiri chili powder; cook for 4-5 minutes until tomatoes break down into a glossy, fragrant masala paste.
Pour the hot onion-tomato tempering (tadka) into the cooked urad dal; stir vigorously, simmer for 3 minutes, and finish with garam masala, fresh lemon juice, and chopped cilantro.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Punjabi Dal Fry

lines.text: 0.75 cup dry split red lentils (masoor dal)
1 tbsp dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi), crushed

instructions: Rinse red lentils and toor dal thoroughly; add to a saucepan with water, ground turmeric, and 1/2 tsp salt, simmering for 20 minutes until completely tender and soft.
In a heavy skillet, melt vegan butter and oil over medium heat; add cumin seeds and mustard seeds, allowing them to crackle for 30 seconds.
Add chopped red onion, garlic, ginger, and green chilies; sauté for 7 minutes until onions are golden brown and sweet.
Add chopped tomatoes, Kashmiri chili powder, and garam masala; cook for 4 minutes until tomatoes soften into a jammy gravy.
Pour cooked lentils into the aromatic skillet, bring to a gentle simmer for 3 minutes, then crush kasuri methi between palms and stir in with fresh lemon juice and abundant cilantro.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Kung Pao Lentils

lines.text: 2 cups vegetable broth for cooking lentils
1 medium red bell pepper, cut into 3/4-inch squares
1 medium green bell pepper, cut into 3/4-inch squares
3 tbsp tamari or low-sodium soy sauce
2 tbsp Chinese black vinegar or rice vinegar
1 tbsp cornstarch dissolved in 3 tbsp cold water

instructions: Cook brown lentils in vegetable broth for 18-20 minutes until tender yet retaining shape and bite; drain any excess liquid thoroughly.
In a small bowl, whisk together tamari, rice vinegar, maple syrup, half of sesame oil, and dissolved cornstarch slurry to create the Kung Pao sauce.
Heat avocado oil and remaining sesame oil in a large wok over high heat; add dried red chilis and crushed Sichuan peppercorns, stirring for 30 seconds until darkened and aromatic.
Add minced garlic, ginger, chopped bell peppers, and celery; stir-fry briskly for 3-4 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Add cooked brown lentils, roasted peanuts, and scallions to the wok; pour in sauce and toss over high heat for 2 minutes until sauce turns into a glossy clinging glaze.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Lentil Orzo Salad

lines.text: 1.5 cups cooked brown lentils (or one 15 oz can, rinsed)
1 cup dry whole-wheat or regular orzo pasta
0.75 cup drained and diced roasted red peppers

instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil; cook orzo pasta for 8-9 minutes until al dente, drain, rinse with cool water, and shake dry.
In a large salad bowl, whisk together extra-virgin olive oil, lemon juice, grated garlic, dried oregano, sea salt, and black pepper to form the dressing.
Add cooked orzo, cooked brown lentils, diced cucumber, roasted red peppers, halved cherry tomatoes, diced red onion, and sliced Kalamata olives to the bowl.
Gently toss all ingredients with the dressing until well distributed; fold in fresh chopped parsley and mint.
Serve at room temperature or chill for 30 minutes before serving to allow Mediterranean herbs and dressing to marry.
license: Recipe formulation from the pre-existing Aptiva catalog

title: Chickpea Cashew Broccoli with Garlic Sauce

lines.text: two 15 oz cans chickpeas, drained, rinsed, and patted dry
3 tbsp low-sodium tamari or soy sauce

instructions: Heat avocado oil in a wide skillet over medium; add raw cashews and toast for 3 minutes, stirring constantly until golden and fragrant; transfer to a plate.
In the same skillet, add patted-dry chickpeas and cook for 6 minutes over medium-high heat until lightly blistered and crisp.
Add broccoli florets and 3 tablespoons of water; cover pan with a lid for 3 minutes to steam broccoli until vibrant emerald green and tender-crisp.

title: Creamy Red Lentil Butternut Squash Dal

title: Creamy Tuscan White Bean & Sun-Dried Tomato Skillet

title: Spicy Garlic Sesame Udon Noodles with Bok Choy

title: Crispy Baked Panko Tofu Katsu with Japanese Curry Sauce

title: High-Protein Smoky Tempeh Bolognese with Rigatoni

title: Crispy Indonesian Sweet Soy & Black Pepper Tempeh Skillet

title: Creamy White Bean, Roasted Garlic & Kale Soup

4 cups stemmed and chopped Tuscan kale

title: Middle Eastern Crispy Baked Herb Falafel Bowl with Tahini

title: Lobia Masala

title: Kidney Bean Millet Beet Burgers

title: Ragda Patties

2 teaspoons grated ginger, half in the wadis and half in the curry
1 teaspoon cumin seeds for the wadis

instructions: Drain the soaked moong dal and pulse it to a fine paste with the cumin seeds, half of the ginger and a pinch of salt. Pipe or spoon small rounds onto a lined tray and sun-dry them for 3 to 4 days, or use store-bought wadis.
Heat the 2 tablespoons oil in a pan and fry the wadis until golden. Drain them on a kitchen towel and set aside.
Heat the mustard oil on low, add the panch phoran for a few seconds, then add the remaining ginger and the onion and stir until light brown.
Add the green chilies, tomato, turmeric and remaining salt and cook until the tomato turns soft and mushy.
Add the bottle gourd, cover and cook for about 10 minutes until tender.
Stir in the fried wadis, cook a few minutes more so they soak up the gravy, and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Bajra Matar Ki Khichdi

lines.text: 1 cup bajra (pearl millet), soaked 4 hours or overnight
1/2 cup yellow moong dal (split), soaked 1 hour

instructions: Soak the bajra for 4 hours or overnight, and soak the moong dal for 1 hour. Drain both.
Pressure cook the bajra and dal with the turmeric and 4 cups water for 4 to 5 whistles, adding extra water for a creamy texture.
Meanwhile, chop the onion, tomato, potato, carrot and peas.
Heat the oil in a kadai, add the cumin seeds and cook until light brown, then add the onion and cook until translucent.
Add the tomato and cook until mushy, then stir in the potato, carrot and peas with the coriander powder and salt. Cook until the vegetables are soft.
Combine the vegetable mixture with the cooked bajra and dal and cook on low heat for 3 to 4 minutes. Serve warm with pickle.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Mango Dal

lines.text: 2 tbsp plus 1 tsp oil (pressure cooker and tempering)
3/4 tsp turmeric (1/2 tsp for the dal, 1/4 tsp for the mango)

instructions: Pressure cook the toor dal with 1/2 tsp of the turmeric, 1 tsp of the oil and 3 cups of water for 5 whistles, until completely soft.
Mash the cooked dal lightly with a spoon until it is silky, and set it aside.
In a wide pan, boil the chopped raw mango with the slit green chilies, the remaining 1/4 tsp turmeric and 1 cup of water, covered, until the mango is tender.
Stir in the mashed dal and the salt and simmer until the flavors blend, thinning with water if it is too thick.
Heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil and let the cumin, mustard seeds, chana dal, dried red chili and curry leaves splutter, then pour it over the dal.
Fold in the chopped coriander and serve with steamed rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Green Pea Falafels
instructions: Drain the chickpeas and let the peas thaw if frozen, then pat both dry with a clean towel.
Pulse the chickpeas, peas, buckwheat flour, cumin seeds, oregano, sumac, chilli flakes and salt in a food processor until coarse and just holding together.
Scoop the mixture and shape it into 12 small patties or balls, then chill for 5 minutes so they firm up.
Warm the olive oil in a wide non-stick frying pan over medium heat and cook the falafels for 4 minutes on each side until crisp and golden.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: 1-Pot BBQ Baked Beans

lines.text: 3 cups dry pinto beans, soaked overnight
1 1/2 cups chopped white or yellow onion
2 tablespoons yellow or spicy brown mustard

instructions: Cover the pinto beans with plenty of cool water and soak for at least 6 hours or overnight, then drain.
Warm the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion and red bell pepper until soft and translucent.
Add the drained beans and vegetable broth, top with water to cover by an inch, and simmer gently, uncovered, until the beans are tender.
Stir in the mustard, tomato paste, coconut sugar, salt, chili powder and liquid smoke and cook on low so the sauce thickens and coats the beans.
Taste and adjust the salt, chili powder or sweetness, then serve warm.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Smoky Instant Pot Black Eyed Peas and Greens

lines.text: 1 small bundle collard greens, stems removed and leaves chopped

instructions: Set the Instant Pot to saute, warm the olive oil and cook the diced onion until tender and translucent.
Stir in the red bell pepper and garlic for a minute, then cancel the saute setting.
Add the black-eyed peas, vegetable broth, bay leaves, smoked paprika, coconut aminos, liquid smoke and salt, then pile the chopped collards on top without stirring.
Seal and pressure cook on high for 17 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for 15 minutes, then release the rest by hand.
Remove the bay leaves, stir the greens into the peas and adjust the salt and smoke to taste.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Bisi Bele Bath

lines.text: 1/3 cup split pigeon pea (toor dal), soaked for an hour
1/2 cup brown basmati rice, soaked for an hour
1 tablespoon prepared homemade sambar powder: coriander, cumin, dried chili, fenugreek, black pepper, chana dal, urad dal, curry leaves, mustard, pure asafoetida resin and turmeric only

instructions: Rinse the toor dal and brown rice and soak them together for an hour, then drain. Meanwhile toast the shredded coconut in a dry skillet for about 15 seconds and set it aside.
Heat the oil in a pressure cooker and let the mustard seeds pop, then cook the onion until translucent.
Stir in the tomato, toasted coconut and sambhar powder and cook until the tomato turns saucy.
Add the tamarind, green beans and peanuts, then the drained dal and rice with the salt and about 2 3/4 cups of water.
Close the lid and pressure cook for one whistle, then lower the heat and cook 15 minutes more.
Let the pressure release naturally, open the lid, stir well and thin with hot water if it is too thick.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Cachupa
instructions: Cook the diced onion and garlic in a large pot with a splash of water or oil until soft.
Add the tofu, carrot, cassava and tomatoes with the paprika and salt and stir for a few minutes.
Pour in enough water to cover, bring to a boil, then simmer until the cassava and carrot begin to soften.
Stir in the drained hominy, kidney beans and white beans along with the cabbage and simmer gently.
Taste, adjust the salt and paprika, and serve hot in bowls.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Sri Lankan Red Lentil Curry

lines.text: 3/4 cup red lentils (masoor dal), soaked and drained

instructions: Rinse the red lentils and soak them while you prepare the rest.
Grind the fenugreek seeds with the cayenne and turmeric to a fine powder.
Heat the oil in a saucepan, let the mustard seeds pop, add the curry leaves and then the spice powder for 5 to 10 seconds.
Add the onion, cinnamon stick and a pinch of salt and cook for about 3 minutes.
Drain the lentils and add them with 1 1/2 cups water, the remaining salt and the coconut milk. Partially cover and cook for 12 to 14 minutes.
Stir in the tomato, lower the heat, cover and cook for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring once, until the lentils are soft and saucy.
Taste and adjust the salt, then serve as a thick soup or over rice or flatbread.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chana Gassi

lines.text: 3/4 cup dried chickpeas, soaked at least 4 hours

instructions: Soak the chickpeas for at least 4 hours, then drain and rinse.
Toast the coriander seeds and dried chilies in a dry skillet until they change color, add the coconut and roast for half a minute until golden.
Blend the toasted mix with the onion, garlic and 1/2 cup water, pulsing briefly so the onion and garlic stay mild, into a coarse sauce.
Pour the sauce into a pressure cooker, add the turmeric and half the salt, then the chickpeas and 1 cup water, and cook on high pressure for 35 to 40 minutes. Release the pressure after 10 minutes.
Stir in the tamarind and the rest of the salt and adjust to taste.
Heat the oil in a small skillet, let the mustard seeds splutter, add the curry leaves, and stir the tempering into the chickpeas. Serve hot with rice or flatbread.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Kala Chana Masala

lines.text: 1 cup black chana (kala chana), dry, soaked overnight

instructions: Soak the black chana overnight in plenty of water, then drain.
Heat the oil in a pressure cooker and let the cumin seeds, cardamom pods and bay leaf sizzle.
Add the onion and saute until it is soft and golden.
Stir in the tomato and cook until it turns soft and mushy and the oil separates.
Add the chili powder, amchur, garam masala, kasuri methi and salt and saute briefly.
Add the drained chana and 3 cups water, cover, and pressure cook for 8 whistles, until the chana are completely tender. Serve with rice or roti.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Imli Chole

lines.text: 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat the oil in a pressure cooker or deep pan and cook the onion for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the cumin, coriander, cinnamon, chili flakes, ginger paste and garlic paste and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the chickpeas, salt, sugar, tamarind and 1 1/2 cups water and stir well.
Pressure cook for 10 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally.
Open the cooker, mash some of the chickpeas into the gravy and adjust the salt, sugar and tamarind to taste. Serve with naan or rotis.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Dhaba Rajma Masala

lines.text: 1 cup dry dark red kidney beans, soaked 8 hours

instructions: Soak the kidney beans for 8 hours or overnight, then drain and rinse.
Put the beans, onion, ginger, garlic, green chili, cloves, cumin, chili powder, coriander, garam masala and 2 cups water in the pressure cooker.
Pressure cook for 55 to 60 minutes until the beans are soft, then let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes.
Open the lid, switch to saute and stir in the tomato puree and salt.
Mash some of the beans against the side of the pot and cook until the gravy comes to a good boil and thickens.
Taste and adjust the salt and spice, then let it rest a few minutes and serve with rice or flatbread.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chickpea Tomato Peanut Stew

lines.text: 1 cup canned coconut milk, thinned with water

instructions: Warm the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion, red pepper, garlic and a pinch of salt for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring often, until softened.
Stir in the diced tomatoes with their juices, tomato paste, chili garlic sauce, peanut butter, coconut milk and rinsed chickpeas.
Add 3 cups of water, or less for a thicker stew, and stir until the peanut butter melts into the sauce.
Bring to a simmer, then lower the heat, cover and cook for 15 to 20 minutes until slightly thickened and fragrant. Keep it at a low simmer, not a boil.
Taste and adjust with salt, more peanut butter for depth, chili garlic sauce for heat or tomato paste for tomato flavor. Serve as a stew or over cooked rice or quinoa.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Creamy Italian White Bean Skillet

lines.text: 2 (15 oz) cans white beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Soak the cashews in hot water for about 15 minutes while you start the skillet.
Warm the olive oil in a large rimmed skillet over medium heat and cook the shallot for 2 to 3 minutes until translucent.

Add the whole cherry tomatoes, garlic, red pepper flakes and salt and cook 2 minutes. Pour in 1/2 cup water, cover and cook on medium-high 5 to 8 minutes until the skins blister, then smash the tomatoes with a spoon.
Add the drained white beans and cook uncovered about 5 minutes until most of the liquid has cooked off.
Blend the drained cashews with 1 1/4 cups water until smooth, stir the cream into the skillet and cook until thick and saucy.
Turn off the heat, stir in the spinach and basil until wilted, and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Edamame Kara Kuzhambu

lines.text: 1 1/2 cups shelled edamame, thawed if frozen

instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat, add the mustard seeds and cook about 30 seconds until they sizzle, then stir in the curry leaves.
Add the onion and garlic and cook about 4 minutes until translucent.
Stir in the tomato, coriander, tamarind and cayenne and cook 6 to 7 minutes until the tomatoes turn saucy.
Add the edamame, coconut milk, 1 cup of water and the salt. Cover and cook about 25 minutes until the edamame are tender.
Taste and adjust the salt, heat and tang with more cayenne or a squeeze of lemon, add water for a thinner curry, and serve hot over rice or with dosa.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Spanish Poor Man's Lentil Stew
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a stockpot over medium heat and cook the onion and garlic for about 4 minutes, stirring every minute, until lightly sauteed.
Stir in the smoked paprika and cumin for a few seconds.
Add the rinsed lentils, vegetable broth and bay leaf, raise the heat to high and bring to a boil.
Stir in the rice, cover, lower the heat and simmer about 20 minutes until the lentils and rice are just cooked through, adding more liquid if needed.
Remove the bay leaf, season with salt and pepper and serve in shallow bowls.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Cauliflower Steak With Creamy Bean Purée

lines.text: 3 tbsp olive oil (a drizzle for the cauliflower, 1 tbsp in the sauce, 1 tbsp in the purée)
1 lemon, zested and juiced (1 tsp zest, a splash for the sauce, a squeeze for the purée)
240 g cooked pinto beans plus 120 g of their bean broth
1/2 tsp salt, plus pepper to taste

instructions: Blend the basil, bell pepper, onion, walnuts, lemon zest, vinegar, 1 tbsp olive oil, a splash of lemon juice, salt and pepper into a smooth sauce.
Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 30 seconds, then shock it in cold water and squeeze it dry.
Blend the spinach with the pinto beans, bean broth, garlic, a squeeze of lemon, 1 tbsp olive oil, salt and pepper until creamy.
Cut the cauliflower into thick slabs, season with salt and pepper and drizzle with olive oil.
Sear each side of the steaks for about 5 minutes in a hot pan until golden, or roast at 180 C (350 F) for about 15 minutes.
Spread the bean purée on plates, set a cauliflower steak on top and spoon the basil-walnut sauce over it.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: BBQ Tempeh Sandwiches With Sweet & Spicy Slaw

lines.text: 8 slices whole-wheat sandwich bread — use Food for Life Ezekiel 4:9 Sprouted Whole Grain Bread

instructions: Toss the sliced cabbage with the vegan mayo, sriracha and maple syrup, then taste and adjust the heat and creaminess.
Slice the tempeh into 1/4-inch slices.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and lay the tempeh in a single layer with a pinch of salt. Cook undisturbed for 3 to 5 minutes until golden and crisp.
Flip the slices and cook another 3 to 5 minutes, adding the remaining oil if the pan is dry and working in batches if needed. Return all the tempeh to the pan.
Take the pan off the heat, add the BBQ sauce and let it bubble and thicken for 2 to 3 minutes, turning the tempeh to coat it.
Mash a quarter of the avocado onto a slice of bread, top with 6 to 8 tempeh slices and 1/2 to 3/4 cup of slaw, and close with a second slice. Repeat for the other sandwiches and serve right away.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: The Ultimate Vegan Burrito

lines.text: 1 (16 oz.) package super firm high protein tofu
4 burrito-size flour tortillas — use Mission Burrito Restaurant Style Flour Tortillas (US)
2/3 cup vegan queso (store-bought) — use Credo Oat Milk Queso Blanco

instructions: Crumble the tofu into a large nonstick skillet over medium heat, stir in the taco seasoning and 1/2 cup water, and cook about 5 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Set aside.
Mash the avocado with the lime juice and salt, leaving it smooth or chunky as you like.
Chop the lettuce and tomatoes and lightly crush the tortilla chips.
Warm each tortilla in a dry skillet for 10 to 15 seconds per side until pliable.
Spread 2 to 3 tbsp of queso in the center of a tortilla, then add about 1/2 cup of tofu, 2 tbsp of guacamole, tomato, crushed chips and lettuce.
Fold the bottom edge up over the filling, tuck it in, fold in the left and right sides like an envelope and roll. Repeat for the other burritos and eat right away.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Tofu Ghee Roast With Vegetables
instructions: Blend the Kashmiri chili powder, coriander, garlic, tamarind, black peppercorns and half the salt with about 3/4 cup of water into a smooth paste.
Heat the oven to 410 F (210 C). Tear the pressed tofu into bite-size pieces and cut the cauliflower, potato and carrot small so they cook at the same pace.
Toss the tofu and vegetables with half the paste, 2 teaspoons of oil and a little salt, spread on a parchment-lined baking sheet and bake 20 to 25 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the red onion with the rest of the salt, adding splashes of water, until golden brown.
Stir the remaining paste into the onions, rinse the blender with a little water and add that too, then bring to a boil and simmer for a few minutes. Adjust the salt and thin with water if needed.
Fold the roasted tofu and vegetables into the sauce, cover and simmer for a minute, then serve with rice, quinoa or flatbread.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Kashmiri Lal Tofu

lines.text: 1 teaspoon Kashmiri chili powder for the tofu plus 2 tablespoons for the sauce

instructions: Slice or tear the pressed tofu. Toss it in a bowl with 1 teaspoon Kashmiri chili powder, the cornstarch and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt until coated.
Brown the tofu in 2 teaspoons of hot oil in a large skillet, 2 to 3 minutes per side, then set it aside.
In the same skillet, cook the onion with the fennel seeds, peppercorns and a pinch of salt in 1 teaspoon of oil until golden, adding the garlic halfway and a splash of water as needed.
Blend the onion mixture with 2 tablespoons of Kashmiri chili powder and 1 cup of water until smooth.

Warm the last teaspoon of oil with the cinnamon stick for a few seconds, then add the blended sauce, tomato puree, cumin and the remaining salt, rinse the blender with 1/2 cup of water and pour it in.
Add the tofu, cover and simmer on low for 20 to 30 minutes until the sauce darkens and thickens, then taste and adjust the salt.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Sri Lankan Jackfruit Curry

lines.text: 500 g young green jackfruit, cut into small pieces
350 ml coconut milk, thinned with 350 ml water
1 tsp tamarind paste (in place of goraka)
1 tbsp roasted Sri Lankan curry powder
2 tbsp roasted red chili powder, mild

instructions: Heat the coconut oil in a wide pan over medium heat, add the garlic and onion, and cook until the onion turns light golden.
Add the curry leaves, pandan leaves and tamarind paste and stir for about 10 seconds.
Stir in the turmeric, curry powder and chili powder and cook for 30 seconds so the spices smell toasted.
Add the jackfruit and toss until every piece is coated with the spices.
Pour in the coconut milk and water, add the salt and stir well.
Cover and simmer for about 20 minutes, until a fork goes easily through the jackfruit, then check the salt.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Homemade Vegan Dumplings

lines.text: 1/2 pack dried rice vermicelli, cooked (1 cup)
4 tablespoons oil for the filling, plus 1 tablespoon to pan-fry

instructions: Soak the dried shiitake and wood ear in hot water until soft, then rinse, trim and mince them. Cook the vermicelli, drain and chop it into short lengths.
Cook the garlic and ginger in 2 tbsp oil, add the mushrooms and carrot, then the cabbage and 1 tbsp soy sauce, until the liquid is gone. Move to a plate to cool.
Fry the crumbled tofu in the remaining filling oil, add the vermicelli and remaining soy sauce, and cook until dry.
Combine the tofu mixture with the cabbage mixture and green onions in a large bowl.
Place a spoonful of filling in each wrapper, wet the edge, fold and press to seal. Freeze extras on a tray if you like.
Pan-fry the dumplings in 1 tbsp oil until the bottoms are golden, add 2 tbsp water, cover and steam for 2 to 3 minutes.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Ganmodoki (Tofu Patties)

lines.text: 1 tablespoon potato starch for the patties plus 1 teaspoon for the sauce
40 g carrot, cut into thin matchsticks
Oil for deep frying (about 2 tbsp absorbed)
2 teaspoons soy sauce for the sauce
1 teaspoon brown sugar (kokuto) for the sauce

instructions: Crumble the tofu into a clean cloth and twist hard to wring out as much water as you can.
Mash the tofu with 1 tbsp potato starch and the salt until it forms a smooth paste.
Microwave the shiitake and carrot covered for 2 minutes, then knead them into the tofu with the edamame and black sesame.
Shape into 6 patties, tossing each between your hands to press out air pockets and seal cracks.
Fry the patties in oil at 170 C (340 F) for 5 to 6 minutes, turning once, until golden, then drain on a rack.
Bring 1 cup water, soy sauce, brown sugar and 1 tsp potato starch to a boil, stirring, and cook for 30 seconds. Ladle over the patties and top with ginger.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Stir Fry Tofu with Ginger and Mushroom

lines.text: 45 g spring onions, cut into 1.5 inch lengths
60 g Chinese parsley (cilantro), cut into 1.5 inch lengths

instructions: Cut the tofu into cubes, and cut the ginger, spring onions and cilantro into strips or short lengths.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan and cook the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the wood ear and tofu and stir gently for 3 minutes.
Stir in the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine and 150 ml water, simmer for 3 minutes.
Mix the tapioca flour with a splash of water and stir it in until the gravy thickens.
Fold in the spring onions and cilantro, finish with the sesame oil and serve with rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Tempeh Shepherdess Pie

lines.text: 1/4 cup plus 2 tbsp and 1 tsp olive oil, divided
2 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch chunks

instructions: Simmer the tempeh in the soy sauce and 2 cups of water for 15 minutes until most of the liquid is absorbed, then cool and crumble it.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for about 15 minutes until tender, drain, and mash with the soy milk and 1/4 cup of the olive oil until smooth.
Heat the remaining oil in a large skillet and cook the onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and mushrooms and cook until their liquid has gone.
Stir in the crumbled tempeh, peas and corn, sprinkle over the flour and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the vegetable broth and simmer 5 minutes until thick, then spread the filling in a baking dish.
Top with the mashed potato, rough up the surface with a fork and bake at 400 F (200 C) for 20 to 25 minutes until golden.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Breakfast Tacos

lines.text: 1/2 cup plus 1 tbsp salsa, divided — use Pace Chunky Salsa Mild (US)

instructions: Wrap the tofu in a clean towel and press it under something heavy while you prepare the toppings.
Warm the black beans in a small saucepan, then keep them at a simmer with a pinch of the cumin, chili powder and garlic powder.
Mix the remaining spices with 1 tablespoon of salsa and a splash of water into a pourable sauce.
Crumble the tofu into a hot oiled skillet and stir-fry 4 to 5 minutes until browned, then add the sauce and cook 5 to 10 minutes more, stirring often.
Warm the corn tortillas, then fill them with tofu, black beans, red onion, avocado, cilantro and salsa and finish with lime juice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Soya Manchurian

lines.text: 1/4 cup corn flour for the coating plus 1 tbsp for the slurry
2 tbsp oil absorbed in frying plus 2 tsp oil for the sauce
1 inch ginger, chopped, plus 1 tsp ginger garlic paste
2 tsp soy sauce for the coating plus 2 tbsp for the sauce

instructions: Boil the soya chunks in well-salted water for 5 minutes, then drain and squeeze out the water.
Toss the soya chunks with the ginger garlic paste, half of the chilli paste, 2 tsp soy sauce, a little salt, the maida and 1/4 cup corn flour until evenly coated.
Deep fry the coated chunks in hot oil over medium heat, stirring now and then, until golden and crisp. Drain and set aside.
Heat 2 tsp oil in a pan and stir-fry the chopped ginger, onion and capsicum until the onion is crunchy-tender.
Add 2 tbsp soy sauce, the vinegar, tomato sauce, remaining chilli paste and salt and cook until combined.
Stir in the corn flour slurry and cook until it thickens and turns glossy, then fold in the fried soya chunks.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Tahu dan Tempe Bacem

lines.text: 400 g extra firm tofu, cut into 3-inch pieces

instructions: Grind the coriander, galangal, shallots and garlic to a paste with a little of the oil.
Put the tofu and tempeh in a large pot with the coconut water, spice paste, bay leaves, kecap manis, sugar and salt.
Bring to a boil, then simmer gently until the liquid has reduced by half.
Turn the tofu and tempeh over and simmer until almost all the liquid has been absorbed.
Lift them out and let them cool.
Pan-fry the pieces in the remaining oil on all sides until golden and serve with chilies if you like.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Kung Pao Tofu

lines.text: 14 oz firm tofu, drained and cut into 1/2-inch cubes
1/3 cup cornstarch for the tofu batter plus 2 tsp for the sauce
1 tbsp soy sauce plus 1/2 tsp dark soy sauce

instructions: Drain the tofu on a plate for 10 minutes, pat it dry and cut it into 1/2-inch cubes.
Whisk 1/3 cup cornstarch with water into a thin batter, coat the tofu, and stir the soy sauces, rice vinegar, sesame oil and 2 tsp cornstarch with warm water into the sauce.
Toast the peanuts in the oil over low heat for about 5 minutes until golden, then lift them out.
Raise the heat to medium and pan-fry the tofu cubes about 5 minutes per side until browned, then set aside.
Stir-fry the carrots in a spoonful of the oil for a minute, add the ginger and chilies for 20 seconds, then the garlic for 20 seconds.
Pour in the sauce on high heat and simmer until it thickens, then toss in the tofu and peanuts to coat.
Finish with the Sichuan pepper powder and serve with steamed rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Tofu and Broccoli Stir Fry

lines.text: 1 block firm tofu (14 oz / 400 g), cut into 3/4-inch cubes
1/4 cup vegetable stock — use Pacific Foods Organic Vegetable Broth (US)
1/2 tbsp cornstarch for the sauce plus 1/3 cup to coat the tofu
1 large head broccoli, cut into florets

instructions: Cut the tofu into 3/4-inch cubes and marinate them in a sealed bag with 1/4 cup of the soy sauce and the sugar.
Stir the vegetable stock, Shaoxing wine, hoisin, remaining soy sauce, sesame oil and 1/2 tbsp cornstarch together for the sauce.
Cut the broccoli into florets and bite-size stem sticks, then wash and drain.
Drain the tofu, discard the marinade and shake the cubes in the 1/3 cup cornstarch until coated.
Blanch the broccoli in a skillet with a little boiling water for 2 to 3 minutes, drain it and wipe the pan dry.
Fry the tofu in 2 tbsp oil, turning, until most sides are golden, then set it aside.
Add the last 1/2 tbsp oil with the ginger and garlic, pour in the sauce until it thickens, then fold the tofu and broccoli back in and serve over rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Thai Pumpkin Curry

lines.text: 1 tablespoon red curry paste — use Thai Kitchen Red Curry Paste (US retail 4 oz)
2 cups peeled, cubed butternut squash (the source also allows pumpkin, kabocha or acorn)

instructions: Warm the oil, then cook the garlic with the red curry paste, miso and soy sauce for a minute.
Pour in the coconut milk and stir until smooth.
Add the cubed squash with the sugar and simmer until it starts to soften.
Add the bell pepper and tofu and simmer a few more minutes until the squash is tender.
Finish with the lime juice and Thai basil, adjust to taste and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Gochujang Chickpea Lettuce Wraps

lines.text: 1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 1/4 cup water
6 large romaine leaves (the source gives no amount)

instructions: Heat the oil and cook the garlic, onion, bell pepper and celery for a minute or two.
Stir in the gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil and sugar until combined.
Add the cornstarch-water mixture and the chickpeas, cover and simmer about 5 minutes until thickened.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then wash and dry the romaine leaves.
Spoon the chickpea mixture into the lettuce leaves and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Shawarma Chickpea Sweet Potato Buddha Bowl

lines.text: 1 tsp oil plus 2 to 3 tsp oil for the sweet potatoes

instructions: Heat a skillet with a teaspoon of oil, add the shawarma spices, chickpeas and a pinch of salt, and cook covered for a minute.
Add a spoonful of water, cover and cook 3 to 4 minutes until dry, then set the chickpeas aside.
Toss the sweet potato slices with the remaining oil and salt, then cook them in the skillet or roast them at 400 F until tender.
Roast or sear the zucchini slices alongside until lightly browned.
Blend the tahini, garlic, lemon juice and salt with a few tablespoons of water until smooth.
Arrange the sweet potato, zucchini and chickpeas in bowls and drizzle with the dressing.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Chickpea Nuggets

lines.text: 1 cup (96 g) rolled oats, blended to a flour
1 1/2 tsp garlic powder (1 tsp for the coating, 1/2 tsp in the chickpeas)
1 tsp salt (3/4 tsp for the coating, 1/4 tsp in the chickpeas)
1 tsp spray oil, a light coating

instructions: Blend the rolled oats with 1 tsp garlic powder, the nutritional yeast, 3/4 tsp salt, paprika and onion powder into a fine flour and tip it onto a plate.
Mash or pulse the drained chickpeas with 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/4 tsp salt and the poultry seasoning until a thick, slightly chunky paste forms.
Shape the chickpea mixture into small nuggets with damp hands.
Press each nugget into the seasoned oat flour until coated all over.
Spray the nuggets lightly with oil and cook in an air fryer, or on a lined tray in a hot oven, turning once, until crisp and golden.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Celery Black Pepper Tofu

lines.text: 3 tablespoons soy sauce (1 to coat the tofu, 2 in the sauce)
1 1/2 teaspoons black pepper (1/2 tsp in the coating, 1 tsp crushed)

instructions: Toss the cubed tofu with 1 tbsp of the soy sauce, then mix 1/2 tsp black pepper into the cornstarch and toss the tofu until coated.
Spread the tofu on a parchment-lined tray and bake at 200 C (400 F) for 20 minutes or longer until crisp, or pan-fry it in a little oil, turning until golden.
Meanwhile warm the oil in a skillet, lower the heat and cook the garlic, ginger and dried chilies for 2 to 3 minutes until the garlic is golden.
Add the celery and green pepper, raise the heat to medium and cook for 2 minutes, stirring once.

Add the crisp tofu, the remaining 1 tsp crushed black pepper, 2 tbsp soy sauce, maple syrup, rice vinegar and a few spoonfuls of water, and cook for up to a minute until the sauce thickens. Serve hot with rice, quinoa or in lettuce wraps.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Ginger Sesame Noodles with Crispy Tofu

lines.text: 1 1/2 cups fresh green beans, ends trimmed, cut into thirds
2 cups red cabbage, sliced into 1/4-inch slices
3 Tbsp avocado oil (1 1/2 Tbsp in the sauce, 1 1/2 Tbsp on the vegetables)

instructions: Heat the oven to 425 F (218 C) and line a baking sheet with parchment. Wrap the tofu in a towel and press it under something heavy for 15 minutes.
Whisk 2 1/2 Tbsp tamari, 1 1/2 Tbsp avocado oil, the sesame oil, maple syrup, ginger and chili garlic sauce into a sauce.
Crumble the tofu into pieces under 1/2 inch on half of the tray and toss it with 1/4 cup of the sauce.
Put the green beans and cabbage on the other half, toss them with the remaining 1 1/2 Tbsp oil and 1 tsp tamari, and keep the two apart.
Pour the rest of the sauce into a serving bowl.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, tossing halfway, until the tofu and vegetables are crisp and browned at the edges.
While the tray bakes, boil the brown rice noodles to the package directions, then drain them.
Toss the noodles and roasted vegetables with the sauce in the bowl, top with the crispy tofu, and scatter over green onion and sesame seeds.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Kabocha Chickpea Miso Soup

lines.text: 1 cup diced white or yellow onion
4 heaping cups kabocha squash, peeled and cut into 1 1/2 inch pieces
2 Tbsp chickpea miso paste — use Miso Master Organic Chickpea Miso

instructions: Warm the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 3 to 4 minutes until it begins to soften. Add the garlic and cook for 30 to 60 seconds until fragrant.
Add the kabocha, chickpeas, vegetable broth and 2 cups of water and bring to a boil, then lower to a simmer for 5 to 7 minutes until the squash is just barely tender.
Stir in the kale and cook for 5 minutes to soften, then take the pot off the heat.
Whisk the miso paste with 2 to 3 tablespoons of warm water until dissolved, stir it into the soup, and taste, adding more miso for richness and salt if needed, then serve topped with sesame seeds.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Crispy Edamame Shiitake Bowls

lines.text: 4 teaspoons soy sauce for roasting plus 3 to 4 tablespoons for the sauce
1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed into 1 cup water

instructions: Heat the oven to 205 C. Toss the edamame and shiitake separately with soy sauce and half the oil, spread them on a lined tray and bake 15 minutes.
Take the mushrooms out if they start to scorch, stir the edamame and bake 25 minutes more until crisp.
Rinse the rice, cook it in 2 cups water until nearly tender, then stir in the broccoli, cover and steam 3 minutes.
Fry the garlic in the remaining oil, add the onion and cook until soft.
Stir in the soy sauce, Kashmiri chili powder, rice vinegar and maple syrup, then the cornstarch slurry, and bring it to a boil to thicken.
Fold the roasted mushrooms into the sauce, spoon it over the broccoli rice and top with the crisp edamame.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Rainbow Vegetable Edamame Bowls with Teriyaki Sauce
instructions: Bring the rice and 2 cups water to a boil, cover and cook on low for 30 to 45 minutes until the water is gone.
Saute the mushrooms in half the sesame oil until browned.
Cook the cabbage, red pepper and two thirds of the green onion in the remaining sesame oil, then add the edamame and teriyaki sauce and steam briefly.
Toss the grated carrot and remaining green onion with 3 teaspoons of the rice vinegar.
Fluff the rice with the remaining rice vinegar and fold the mushrooms into the vegetables.
Divide the rice between bowls and top with the edamame stir-fry and the carrot slaw.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: 20-Minute Tofu Stir-Fry

lines.text: 1 cup extra firm tofu, pressed and crumbled
1 tablespoon coconut aminos to marinate plus 2 to 3 tablespoons for the sauce
1 teaspoon chili garlic sauce for the tofu plus 1 to 2 teaspoons for the sauce
1 cup thinly sliced red bell pepper

instructions: Toss the crumbled tofu with 1 tablespoon of the coconut aminos and 1 teaspoon chili garlic sauce and let it marinate briefly.
Whisk the peanut butter, remaining coconut aminos, maple syrup and remaining chili garlic sauce into a sauce.
Brown the tofu in half the sesame oil in a hot skillet, turning gently, then set it aside.
Stir-fry the shiitake, cabbage and red pepper in the remaining oil, covered, for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook 1 to 2 minutes, then push the vegetables aside and brown the cauliflower rice for 2 minutes.
Return the tofu, pour in the sauce and toss until hot and coated.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Palak Paneer with Curried Tofu

lines.text: 1 15-ounce block firm tofu, drained and cubed
1 1/2 teaspoons curry powder to season the tofu plus 2 teaspoons for the sauce
1 tablespoon tamari to season the tofu
5 cups loosely packed fresh spinach (about 6 ounces)
3 tablespoons oil (1 1/2 for the onion base, 1 1/2 to bloom the spices)

instructions: Heat the oven to 218 C. Press the tofu dry, cube it and toss with 1 1/2 teaspoons curry powder and the tamari.
Brown the tofu in an oven-safe skillet for 3 to 4 minutes, then bake 15 minutes and leave it to rest in the pan.
Cook the cumin seed, ginger and onion in half the oil for 5 minutes, then add the tomatoes and garlic and cook 3 to 4 minutes.
Boil the spinach for 2 minutes, drain, rinse in cold water and squeeze dry.
Blend the tomato mixture with the spinach until smooth.
Bloom the remaining curry powder and garam masala in the remaining oil for 30 seconds, add the spinach sauce and simmer 3 to 4 minutes, stir in the coconut milk and serve over the tofu.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Jerk Tofu & Roasted Plantain Bowls

lines.text: 1/4 cup DIY Jamaican jerk seasoning (spice blend)
3/4 teaspoon sea salt, the salt in half a batch of that blend
2 tablespoons olive oil for the jerk sauce plus 2 tablespoons for the tahini sauce
2 tablespoons tamari for the jerk sauce plus 1/2 to 1 teaspoon for the tahini sauce
1 tablespoon maple syrup for the jerk sauce plus 1 teaspoon for the tahini sauce
1 (14 to 16 ounce) package super firm tofu
2 ripe plantains, peeled and sliced on an angle

instructions: Heat the oven to 218 C and line two baking sheets. Whisk the jerk blend with the salt, 2 tablespoons oil, 2 tablespoons tamari and 1 tablespoon maple syrup.
Crumble the tofu onto one sheet, coat it with half the jerk sauce and bake 10 minutes.
Peel and slice the plantains, coat them with the rest of the jerk sauce and spread them on the other sheet.
Stir the tofu, return it to the oven and bake the plantains alongside for 16 to 20 minutes, tossing them once.
Blend the parsley, tahini, lime juice, remaining oil, remaining tamari, remaining maple syrup and a little water until smooth.
Divide the tofu and plantains between bowls and drizzle with the parsley tahini sauce.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Sheet Pan Peri-Peri Tofu and Vegetables

lines.text: 15 ounce block firm or extra-firm tofu, pressed and sliced
2 cups Yukon gold potatoes, peeled and cubed
1 red bell pepper, chopped, plus 1/4 cup roasted red bell pepper for the marinade
1 small red onion in wedges, plus 2 tablespoons red onion for the marinade
1 ear sweet corn, cut into 1 inch pieces
1 bulb garlic to roast, plus 3 cloves for the marinade
3 tablespoons peri-peri sauce — use Nando's Medium PERi-PERi Sauce (Australian formula)
1 tablespoon oil plus 1 teaspoon for the garlic
1/2 cup non-dairy yogurt — use So Delicious Unsweetened Plain Coconutmilk Yogurt

instructions: Press the tofu, then slice it into half-inch slices. Cut the potatoes, bell pepper, onion and corn into bite-size pieces and trim the top off the garlic bulb.
Blend the roasted red pepper, red onion, garlic cloves, peri-peri sauce, paprika, lemon juice and part of the oil until smooth.
Toss the tofu in some of the marinade for 15 minutes and coat the vegetables with the rest, saving a spoonful for basting.

Spread the tofu and vegetables on an oiled sheet pan, set the garlic bulb on the edge under foil with a little oil, and bake at 415 F for 30 to 35 minutes, flipping and basting the tofu at 20 minutes.
Mix the yogurt with cilantro and lemon juice, then squeeze in the roasted garlic and mash it through.
Serve the tofu and vegetables with the garlic yogurt dip and extra peri-peri sauce.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Italian Herb Tofu and Winter Vegetable Sheet Pan Meal

lines.text: 6 cups butternut squash, peeled and cut into 1 inch cubes
3 cups red cabbage, cut into 1/2 inch strips
1 large red onion, cut into 8 to 10 wedges
2 tablespoons olive oil for the vegetables plus 1 1/2 tablespoons for the tofu
2 teaspoons tamari for the vegetables plus 1 1/2 tablespoons for the tofu
1 tablespoon Italian herb seasoning (basil, oregano and thyme)
1/4 cup Garlicky Hummus Sauce, for serving (optional)

instructions: Heat the oven to 425 F. Toss the squash, cabbage and onion with 2 tablespoons olive oil and 2 teaspoons tamari and spread them on a baking sheet.
Roast the vegetables for 15 to 20 minutes until they begin to soften.
Press the tofu in a towel under a heavy pan for 15 minutes.
Whisk the balsamic vinegar, remaining tamari, remaining olive oil, tomato paste, Italian seasoning and garlic in the emptied bowl.
Crumble the tofu into pieces under half an inch and stir them through the marinade.

Stir the vegetables, top them with the tofu and roast 25 to 30 minutes more, stirring now and then, until the tofu is crisp and the vegetables caramelize at the edges. Serve with the hummus sauce if you like.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Tofu Lettuce Wraps

lines.text: 8 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and minced
1 block (14 ounce) firm tofu, cut into 1/3 inch squares
1 can (8 ounce) water chestnuts, drained and cut into 1/3 inch pieces
2 green onions, whites and greens separated and sliced

instructions: Soak the dried shiitake in hot water for 15 minutes, squeeze out the liquid and mince them.
Stir the hoisin, peanut butter, sriracha, sesame oil and garlic together to make the sauce.
Fry the small tofu squares in the peanut oil, leaving them still for the first minute, then turn and separate them until golden and crisp, about 5 more minutes.
Push the tofu aside and stir-fry the water chestnuts, shiitake and green onion whites on the empty side for 1 minute.
Stir everything together, add half the sauce and cook 30 seconds, then add the green onion greens and move to a plate.
Thin the remaining sauce with 2 tablespoons water for drizzling.
Serve the filling with the lettuce leaves, crushed peanuts and extra sauce, and wrap at the table.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Tofu Gimbap

lines.text: 2 cups uncooked short grain brown rice
1 tablespoon sesame oil for the rice, 1 teaspoon for the spinach and a little to brush the rolls
1 teaspoon salt, divided across the rice, tofu and vegetables
10 ounces firm tofu, cut into 3/4 inch sticks
3 kirby cucumbers, seedy centers removed, cut into 1/2 inch sticks

instructions: Cook the brown rice with a little less water than usual so it stays slightly firm for rolling.
Pat the tofu sticks dry, salt them lightly and fry in oil until golden on all sides.
Blanch the spinach, chill it in an ice bath, squeeze out the water, cut it short and toss with sesame oil and salt.
Stir-fry the cucumber sticks and then the carrots in a little oil until softened, seasoning each with salt.
Fold sesame oil and salt into the hot rice until evenly seasoned.
Spread about 3/4 to 1 cup of rice over a nori sheet, leaving the far edge bare, and lay the tofu and vegetables in a row near the edge closest to you.
Roll the sheet tightly away from you, pressing firmly, brush the roll with sesame oil and cut it into 1/2 inch slices with an oiled knife.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Jjajangmyeon

lines.text: 5 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked in 1 cup hot water
1 large onion, cut into large chunks (about 10 ounces)
1/4 green cabbage, cut into large chunks (about 8 ounces)
1 large zucchini, cut into cubes (about 12 ounces)
1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 1 tablespoon cold water
12 ounces dried udon noodles (3 ounces per serving)

instructions: Soak the dried shiitake in 1 cup hot water for 15 to 20 minutes while you cut the onion, cabbage, zucchini and mushrooms.
Squeeze the shiitake dry, keep the liquid, chop the mushrooms and top the liquid up with water to 1 cup.
Heat the oil in a wok, stir-fry the garlic for under a minute, then add the black bean paste and fry for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the onion, cabbage, zucchini and mushrooms and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until softened.
Pour in the shiitake broth, sugar and vegetarian oyster sauce, bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered for 10 to 15 minutes.
Cook the udon to the package directions, rinse under cold water and drain well.
Stir the cornstarch and water into the sauce until thick, then pour it over the noodles and mix before eating.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Singapore Noodles

lines.text: 1/4 red bell pepper and 1/4 green bell pepper, thinly sliced
3 stalks green onion, cut into batons

instructions: Soak the rice vermicelli in a pot of just-boiled water, loosening the strands now and then with chopsticks, until pliable.
Slice the shallot and bell peppers, chop the garlic and ginger, crumble the tofu and cut the green onion into batons.
Heat the oil in a sauté pan over medium-high heat and cook the shallot, garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the tofu and peppers and sauté for 2 to 3 minutes.
Drain the noodles, add them to the pan with the curry powder and soy sauce, and pour in a splash of water if the pan is dry.
Add the green onion and toss for 2 to 3 minutes until the liquid is absorbed, then plate with a little green onion on top.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Ants Climbing a Tree

lines.text: 2 bundles mung bean glass noodles, soaked, drained and cut shorter
600 g tofu: 300 g firm tofu pressed and crumbled plus 300 g frozen tofu thawed, squeezed dry and torn into small bits
4-5 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and minced (keep the soaking water)
1 tbsp soy sauce for the noodles plus 1 tbsp soy sauce paste

instructions: Soak the glass noodles in warm water until soft, drain, snip them shorter and toss with the soy sauce and soy sauce paste and the sesame oil.
Thaw the frozen tofu, squeeze it dry and tear it into small bits; press the firm tofu and crumble it small.
Squeeze the soaked shiitake dry and mince, keeping the soaking water, then mince the ginger, slice the chilies and chop the cilantro.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat, add the firm tofu then the frozen tofu, and fry, stirring, until golden and crisp.
Add the shiitake and ginger and fry until fragrant, then stir in the noodles with the mushroom water and a splash of fresh water.
