Stir until the liquid is absorbed and the noodles are glossy, fold in the chilies and cilantro, and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Pineapple Fried Rice

lines.text: 1 head broccoli, cut into small florets
1 cup frozen carrots and peas, thawed
14 ounces extra-firm tofu, pressed and cubed

instructions: Whisk the tamari, rice vinegar and sriracha, toss the tofu cubes in it and leave to marinate for 30 minutes while you prep.
Sauté the green onions in a wok or large skillet until soft.
Add the mushrooms and cook until browned, then add the broccoli and cook for a few minutes.
Add the bell pepper, peas and carrots and toss every few minutes, then add the pineapple.
Add the marinated tofu with any remaining sauce and the chilled rice and stir-fry until hot and coated.
Taste, add a little more sriracha if you like heat, and serve sprinkled with sesame seeds.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Peruvian Arroz Chaufa

lines.text: 1 white onion, cut into small wedges

instructions: Mix half the tamari with the aji amarillo paste, ginger and sesame oil in a small bowl.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil, crumble in the tofu and cook, stirring, until dry and scrambled-looking, about 8 minutes, then set aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a hot pan, cook the shiitake and onion until golden at the edges, then add the red pepper for another minute.
Pour in the aji amarillo sauce and cook until it reduces to a glaze on the vegetables, then set the vegetables aside.
Add the last tablespoon of oil and the white parts of the spring onion, then stir the rice until heated through, about 5 minutes.
Add the remaining tamari and the peas and stir for 1 minute, then fold in the tofu and vegetables and serve with the green spring onion on top.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Cauliflower, Chickpeas, and Couscous

lines.text: 1/4 cup olive oil for roasting and 1/3 cup for the dressing
3/4 tsp smoked paprika, split between the roast and the dressing
1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat the oven to 425F (218C) with a rimmed baking sheet on the middle rack.
Toss the cauliflower with the roasting oil, turmeric, half the paprika and half the salt, then spread it on the hot sheet and roast 25 to 30 minutes until crisp-tender.
Boil 1 1/2 cups water, stir in the couscous and remaining salt, cover and simmer about 10 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Shake the dressing oil, lemon juice, garlic and remaining paprika in a jar.
Combine the cauliflower, couscous, chickpeas, mint and parsley, pour over the dressing and toss.
Top with toasted almonds and serve warm or at room temperature.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Bulgur Pilaf with Chickpea

lines.text: 1 cup boiled or canned chickpeas, drained

instructions: Soak the bulgur in water for about 30 minutes, then drain it.
Heat the oil in a deep non-stick pan and cook the chopped onion and garlic until soft and translucent.
Add the drained bulgur and the chickpeas to the pan.
Stir in the turmeric, salt, coriander and tomato paste until the grains are coated and not sticking to the pan.
Pour in 2 cups of water, stir, cover and cook on low heat for 15 minutes.
Fluff the pilaf, scatter the sliced spring onion over the top and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Buckwheat Porridge with Mushrooms
instructions: Rinse the buckwheat, then simmer it in 2 cups of water with 1/2 tsp salt, covered, until the water is absorbed, and let it steam off the heat.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan and saute the chopped onion and carrot until soft.
Add the sliced mushrooms and garlic and cook until the mushrooms are browned.
Pour in the tomato sauce and simmer briefly, seasoning with black pepper.
Fold the steamed buckwheat into the vegetables until coated.
Top with chopped fresh dill and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Mango Fried Rice

lines.text: 1 cup carrots, peeled and small diced

instructions: Chop the onion, garlic, ginger, carrots, green onions and mango before you start; the dish moves fast.
Heat the sesame oil in a large wok or skillet over medium heat and saute the onion and carrots for 3 to 5 minutes until softened but not browned.
Add the ginger and garlic and cook for 1 more minute.
Stir in the rice wine vinegar and soy sauce and cook for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the cooked rice and chickpeas and combine.
Gently stir in the mango, green onions and peas and cook for about 5 minutes until heated through.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegetable Hakka Noodles

lines.text: 1/2 red and 1/2 green bell pepper, thinly sliced

instructions: Cook the noodles according to the package, drain, rinse with cold water and set aside.
Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok and cook the onion, garlic and ginger over medium-high heat for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the bell peppers, cabbage and carrots and cook for about 2 minutes until golden on some edges.
Stir the soy sauce, rice vinegar and sambal oelek together in a bowl and pour it into the skillet.
Add the noodles and toss well, season generously with black pepper, then cover and cook for a minute.
Taste, adjust the heat and pepper, and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Soya Fried Rice
instructions: Boil the soya chunks in salted water, drain and squeeze out the water.
Heat the oil in a kadai and fry the garlic and slit chilies on high heat until the garlic shrinks.
Add the sliced onion and stir-fry until it shrinks.
Add the peas, carrot and capsicum with a little salt and stir-fry until the vegetables turn crunchy.
Add the boiled soya chunks and fry for 2 minutes.
Add the cooked rice, soy sauce, vinegar and the remaining salt and stir-fry until the rice is coated.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegetarian Lagman

lines.text: 600 ml cooked Shanghai noodles or linguine
1 tsp mixed salt, black pepper, cumin, coriander and oregano

instructions: Dice the red pepper, carrot, turnip and daikon. Warm the olive oil in a large pot and cook the diced vegetables over medium heat, stirring, until they begin to soften.
Add the chopped tomatoes, tomato sauce, chickpeas, bay leaf and the spice mix. Pour in enough water to just cover the vegetables.
Simmer, partly covered, until the turnip and daikon are tender and the sauce has thickened.
Meanwhile cook the noodles in salted boiling water according to the package, then drain.
Stir half the chopped herbs into the stew and take it off the heat. Divide the noodles among bowls, ladle the stew over and top with the remaining herbs.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vietnamese Caramelized Lentil Bowls

lines.text: 2 tablespoons soy sauce (1 for the dressing, 1 for the pan)
2 tablespoons coconut sugar plus 2 teaspoons for the pan
4 cloves garlic, minced (1 for the dressing, 3 for the pan)
1 can (15 oz) lentils, drained (about 1 1/2 cups cooked)
4 cups cooked rice vermicelli (1 cup per bowl)

instructions: Whisk the miso, 1 tbsp soy sauce, lime juice, rice vinegar, pepper flakes, 2 tbsp coconut sugar, 1 minced garlic clove and 3 tbsp warm water until the miso and sugar dissolve.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the onion with a pinch of salt and sugar until golden at the edges, then add the remaining garlic and cook until fragrant.
Keep cooking, adding a splash of water if the pan dries out, until the onion is deep golden brown.
Stir in the lentils, the last 2 tsp coconut sugar, 1 tbsp soy sauce and 4 tablespoons of the dressing. Cook until the sauce bubbles, thickens and clings to the lentils.
Cook the rice vermicelli, drain and divide among four bowls with the cucumber. Top with the lentils and drizzle with the remaining dressing.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Tallarines Verdes

lines.text: 6 tablespoons olive oil (5 for frying, 1 for blending)

instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil with the bay leaves and a good pinch of salt. Cook the spaghetti according to the package.
Chop the onion and garlic and fry them in 5 tbsp of the olive oil for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the spinach and basil to the same pan and fry for about 1 1/2 minutes with a pinch of salt. Let the mixture cool a little.
Blend the cooled greens with the cashews, nutritional yeast, remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and almond milk until smooth.
Drain the spaghetti, pour the green sauce over and toss until every strand is coated. Serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Nigerian Fried Brown Rice
instructions: Rinse the brown rice. Bring the vegetable stock to a boil with the salt, curry powder and thyme, add the rice, cover and simmer until tender and the stock is absorbed.
Spread the cooked rice on a tray to cool and dry out.
Heat a large wok or pan. Cook the onion and garlic-ginger paste for a minute, then add the mushrooms and cook until their liquid has gone.
Add the bell pepper, mixed vegetables and spring onion with the black pepper and stir-fry until just tender.
Add the rice, toss everything together over high heat until hot and evenly seasoned, and taste for salt.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Gochujang Sesame Noodles
instructions: Cook the somen noodles in boiling water according to the package. If using edamame and broccoli, add them to the same pot for the last few minutes.
Stir the gochujang, tahini, rice vinegar and maple syrup together in a bowl until smooth.
Drain the noodles (and vegetables, if using). Rinse under cold water if you want to serve the dish cold.
Toss the noodles in the sauce until every strand is coated.
Top with sesame seeds and chopped green onion, if you like, and serve right away.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Masala Chickpea Stuffed Sweet Potatoes

lines.text: 3 small-medium sweet potatoes, scrubbed and halved lengthwise
2 1/2 tbsp avocado oil, divided (1 tbsp for the potatoes, 1 1/2 tbsp for the chickpeas)
1 tsp curry powder, rubbed on the potatoes
1 (15-ounce) can chickpeas, rinsed, drained and dried
2 tbsp ripe avocado, for a creamy chutney

instructions: Heat the oven to 400 F (204 C) and line two baking sheets with parchment. Blend the cilantro, garlic, lime juice, maple syrup and avocado into a pourable chutney and set it aside.
Rub the sweet potato halves with 1 tablespoon of the oil and, if you like, the curry powder, lay them cut side down on one sheet and bake on the upper rack for 25 minutes, until tender.
Toss the dried chickpeas with the remaining oil and the tandoori masala, spread them on the other sheet and bake on the lower rack alongside the potatoes for 20 to 25 minutes, until crisp.
Flip the potatoes cut side up and smash the centers lightly with a spoon. Top with the chickpeas and spoon over the chutney. Serve right away.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Bean Tostadas

lines.text: 1 (15-ounce) can reduced-sodium black beans, rinsed and drained
1/3 cup prepared salsa — use Pace Chunky Salsa Mild (US)

instructions: Heat the oven to 400 F (204 C). Spread the corn tortillas on a baking sheet and bake for about 6 minutes, flipping once, until crisp.
Meanwhile, warm the olive oil in a saucepan over medium-high heat and cook the diced red onion for 2 minutes until just soft.
Stir in the black beans and salsa and cook for about 4 minutes until hot. Mash the beans with the back of a spoon.
Dice the avocado and tomato, slice the cabbage and chop the cilantro while the tortillas bake.
Spoon the beans over the crisp tortillas, pile on the avocado, cabbage, tomato and cilantro, and squeeze over the lime juice. Serve right away.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Bean & Corn Flautas

lines.text: 2 tbsp vegetable oil, for cooking and brushing

instructions: Heat the oven to 400 F (204 C). Warm the corn tortillas so they roll without cracking.
Soften the onion and garlic in a little of the oil, then add the pinto beans, green chilies, chili powder, cumin and oregano.
Mash the beans into a thick paste, then stir in the corn and the lime juice. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Put a spoonful of filling on each warm tortilla and roll it tightly. Set the flautas seam side down on a baking sheet and brush them with oil.
Bake for about 25 minutes until golden and crisp, then serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Cabbage Crunch Salad with Sticky Ginger Tofu

lines.text: 5 tbsp soy sauce or tamari (2 for the tofu, 3 for the dressing)
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp toasted sesame oil (1 tsp for the tofu)
1 tbsp oil for frying plus 1 tbsp olive oil for the dressing
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
6 cups shredded cabbage (4 cups green, 2 cups red)
1/2 cup toasted and salted mixed nuts, roughly chopped

instructions: Pat the tofu dry and cut it into rectangular slices about 0.5 cm thick.
Stir 2 tablespoons of the soy sauce with 1 teaspoon maple syrup, 1 teaspoon sesame oil, 1 teaspoon rice vinegar, half the garlic and 1 teaspoon of the ginger.
Fry the tofu in 1 tablespoon oil over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side until golden. Pour the sauce over and let it absorb in the pan's heat.
Shake the remaining soy sauce, sesame oil, olive oil, rice vinegar, maple syrup, garlic and ginger together in a jar to make the dressing.
Toss the cabbage, carrot and bell pepper with the dressing until coated. Heap on a platter, top with the sticky tofu and the chopped nuts, and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Super Garlicky Tomato Soup with Smashed White Beans

lines.text: 10 medium-large garlic cloves, peeled and smashed
1 (14-ounce) can coconut milk, well shaken (a quarter stirred in, the rest to serve)

instructions: Smash the peeled garlic cloves flat with the bottom of a heavy pan.
Warm the olive oil in a large pot over medium-low heat and cook the garlic, stirring now and then, until slightly golden. Add the red pepper flakes and tomato paste and stir for a minute.
Add the white beans, crushed tomatoes, vegetable broth and salt. Bring to a low boil, then partly cover and simmer for about 15 minutes until slightly thickened.
Smash about half the beans with a potato masher. Stir in the maple syrup and a quarter of the coconut milk, then taste and adjust the salt, sweetness and heat.
Ladle into bowls and swirl the rest of the coconut milk over each, with an extra pinch of red pepper flakes.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Zuppa Toscana

lines.text: 1/3 cup cashews, blended with 3/4 cup water into cream

instructions: Blend the cashews with 3/4 cup water until completely smooth, resting and re-blending a couple of times.
Cook the chopped mushrooms in the oil in a large pot until golden at the edges, then add the lentils for a minute.
Stir in the Italian herbs, fennel, smoked paprika and garlic powder and cook until the crumble turns crisp; set aside a third for topping.
Add the potatoes, stock and nutritional yeast, partially cover and simmer until the potatoes are tender.
Pour in the cashew cream, bring to a boil, then stir in the spinach and turn off the heat.
Ladle into bowls and top with the reserved crumble.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Lasagna Soup

lines.text: 1 cup mixed peppers, carrots and zucchini, chopped
5 ounces lasagna sheets, broken into small pieces

instructions: Saute the onion and garlic in the oil on the Instant Pot saute setting with a pinch of salt for 2 minutes.
Stir in the chopped vegetables, red lentils, tomato puree, diced tomato and Italian seasoning.
Add the broken lasagna sheets and 2 cups water, mixing well so the pieces do not stick together.
Seal the lid and pressure cook on high for 3 minutes, then let the pressure release for 10 minutes before opening.
Stir in the nutritional yeast, adjust the seasoning, and fold in the spinach until just wilted.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Misal Pav

lines.text: 1 onion for the masala plus 1/2 onion chopped to top, finely chopped
2 cups farsan (mixture) — use Haldiram's Bombay Mix (UK 200 g formula)
6 pav — use Rhodes Bake-N-Serv Dinner Rolls, baked without butter, prepared ahead

instructions: Boil the sprouted moth beans with water until tender; set them aside with their cooking water.
Roast the onion, garlic, coconut and tomato in a little of the oil, then grind to a smooth masala paste.
Heat the remaining oil and crackle the cumin, then stir in the chilli powder, coriander powder and garam masala over low heat until fragrant.
Add the masala paste and cook until the oil separates, then add the cooked moth beans.
Pour in 5 cups water, cover and boil about 10 minutes until the oil floats, separating the thick usal from the thin kat gravy.
Plate the usal, top with farsan and raw onion, ladle kat gravy around the side and serve with pav.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Kimchi Fried Rice

lines.text: 2 1/2 cups carrots and snap peas, cut into bite-size pieces
1 cup kimchi plus 1 tablespoon kimchi juice, chopped

instructions: Boil the rinsed brown rice in a large pot of water for 30 minutes, then drain well.
Press the tofu for 10 minutes, cube it and toss with 1 tablespoon sesame oil and 2 tablespoons gochujang.
Bake the tofu at 204 C for 25 to 30 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and crisp.
Saute the onion, garlic and vegetables with 1 tablespoon sesame oil and a little soy sauce for about 4 minutes, then toss in the kimchi and kimchi juice.
Off the heat, coat the rice with the remaining sesame oil, soy sauce and ginger, then fry it undisturbed for 2 minutes, add the 1/4 cup gochujang and fry 2 minutes more.
Toss in the vegetables and baked tofu, taste for gochujang and soy sauce, and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Gumbo with Okra

lines.text: 1 red bell pepper and 1 green bell pepper, diced
1 can (28 ounces) diced tomatoes, not drained

instructions: Heat the olive oil, test it with a pinch of flour, then whisk in the flour and stir constantly for 8 to 10 minutes until the roux is the color of peanut butter.
Add the onion, okra, bell peppers, mushrooms and celery and cook about 10 minutes until tender and the okra slime has cooked down.
Stir in the Cajun seasoning, thyme and smoked paprika and cook for one minute.
Pour in the diced tomatoes with their juice and the kidney beans.
Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then.
Season to taste and serve over rice with parsley.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Baked Mixed Vegetable Pakora

lines.text: 3/4 cup chickpea flour (2/3 cup plus a tablespoon or so more)

instructions: Pulse the cauliflower, onion, broccoli, carrot, potato, green chili, ginger and cilantro in a food processor until finely chopped.
Mix in the amchur and semolina, then the chickpea flour, until the vegetables have a light coating, and rest the bowl for a few minutes while the oven heats to 425 F.
Stir in the oil and a little water, a teaspoon at a time, until the mixture just holds together in balls.
Scoop small mounds about 1.5 inches wide onto a parchment-lined tray and spray or brush them with oil.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden and crisp, then serve with mint or tamarind chutney.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Spiced Lentil Rice Casserole
instructions: Rinse and drain the red lentils and basmati rice.
Put the lentils, rice, cauliflower, carrots, peas, spinach and tomato into a large baking dish and add the coriander, cumin, curry powder, chili powder, salt and 4 cups of water.
Stir well, cover the dish with parchment and bake at 400 F for 40 to 45 minutes, checking at about 35 minutes that the lentils and rice are tender.
Fluff the casserole with a fork and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chataka Dal
instructions: Soak the toor dal in hot water for 10 minutes, then drain it.
Simmer the dal with the tomato, half the cilantro, turmeric, salt and 4 cups of water, partly covered, until the dal is soft.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the mustard seeds until they pop, then add the cumin and the curry leaves.
Add the garlic and cook until it just turns golden, then stir in the Kashmiri chili powder and cayenne and take the pan off the heat.
Pour the hot tadka over the dal, swirl it in lightly and top with the remaining cilantro.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Sindhi Kadhi
instructions: Heat the oil and cook the cumin and fenugreek seeds until fragrant, then add the curry leaves, ginger and green chili for a minute.
Stir in the chickpea flour and roast it for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring every minute.
Add the turmeric and 1 cup of the water, whisking until no lumps remain, then whisk in the rest of the 3 1/2 cups of water.
Add the potatoes and green beans, cover and cook over medium heat for 17 to 18 minutes.
Add the tomato and tamarind paste and simmer partly covered for 5 minutes, then adjust the tang and serve over rice or on its own.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Broccoli Zunka

lines.text: 1/2 green bell pepper and 1/2 red bell pepper, chopped
1 1/2 to 2 cups chopped broccoli, in small pieces

instructions: Dry roast the chickpea flour in a skillet over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes until toasty, stirring now and then, and set it aside.
Heat the oil in the same skillet and roast the cumin seeds for 1 to 2 minutes until they change color.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 3 minutes, then add the bell peppers and cook for 2 minutes more.
Add the broccoli, a pinch of salt and a splash of water and cook for 5 to 7 minutes until the broccoli is just tender.
Mix the turmeric, coriander, cayenne and remaining salt into the roasted chickpea flour, stir it into the skillet, cover and cook for 1 minute.
Sprinkle in 2 to 3 tablespoons of water, cover and cook for 3 minutes or more, adding water as needed, until the flour clumps around the vegetables with no dry flour left.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Turkish Sigara Borek with Lentils
instructions: Boil the green lentils until tender but still whole, then drain well.
Cook the chopped onion in a spoonful of the oil until soft, then stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the lentils, salt, black pepper and red pepper flakes, mix, and let the filling cool.
Spoon some filling along the wide edge of each yufka triangle, fold in the sides and roll up tightly into a cigar shape.
Fry the rolls in the remaining oil over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Sweet Potato Black Bean Tamales

lines.text: 3 to 4 medium-large sweet potatoes, baked and mashed
2 tsp sea salt, divided between the masa and the beans
1 chipotle pepper in adobo sauce, chopped

instructions: Bake the whole sweet potatoes at 375 F for 45 to 60 minutes until tender, and soak the corn husks in water for at least 15 minutes.
Stir the masa harina with 1 1/2 cups water and let it rest for 15 minutes to hydrate.
Soften the onion in a saucepan, add the black beans, chipotle, cumin and half the salt, cover and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes, then let it cool.
Peel and mash the sweet potatoes. Stir the remaining salt, baking powder and avocado oil into the masa, adding warm broth a little at a time until it forms a thick paste.
Pat the husks dry, spread 2 tablespoons of masa thinly on each, top with mashed sweet potato and black beans, then fold and roll each tamale closed.
Steam the tamales upright in a covered pot with a steamer basket for about 1 hour, until the masa is cooked through.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Cuban Picadillo

lines.text: 1 medium red or green bell pepper, diced
1 x 400 g can green lentils, drained and rinsed
250 g (1/2 lb) potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch cubes

instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large deep pan and cook the shallots and bell pepper for 3 to 4 minutes until slightly softened.
Add the garlic and cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the vegetable stock and bring to a simmer.
Add the lentils, chopped tomatoes and potatoes, cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the potatoes are fork-tender.
Stir in the raisins, capers and olives and heat through.
Serve over rice or with crusty bread, or on its own.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Ginataang Munggo Guisado

lines.text: 4 cloves garlic, peeled, crushed and minced
1 bunch malunggay (moringa) leaves, or spinach or kale

instructions: Cook the mung beans in water for about 45 minutes until soft and mushy, adding water as needed.
In a separate pot, saute the garlic, onion and ginger in the oil over medium heat until the onion softens.
Add the eggplant and salt and mix well, then add a little water, cover and simmer until the eggplant softens.
Mix in the cooked mung beans, fried tofu, spinach and tomatoes.
Pour in the coconut cream, stir well and simmer for 5 to 7 minutes, adjusting the seasoning.
Bring to a boil, turn off the heat and serve hot with rice.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Kabuli Pilaf Rice

lines.text: 3 cups basmati rice, washed and soaked

instructions: Wash the basmati and soak it in warm water for 1 hour, then drain. Dice the onion and julienne the carrots.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion until translucent, then stir in the ginger and garlic for a few minutes.
Add the carrots, chickpeas, black pepper and salt.
Pour in 4 cups of warm water and add the drained rice. Cover and cook on medium-low heat until the water has evaporated and the rice is about 80 percent cooked.
Stir in the ground cardamom and cumin, scatter the raisins on top, cover with foil and cook on low heat for 5 to 10 minutes.
Gently mix everything with a spoon and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Edamame and Mushrooms Stir-Fry

lines.text: 1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed in 1/4 cup water

instructions: Wipe the king oyster mushrooms clean and dice them into small cubes. Mash the tofu.
Heat a pan with 2 teaspoons of the oil and fry the mashed tofu over low-medium heat until dry and golden, then push it to the side.
Add more oil, cook the mushrooms until they brown and smell fragrant, then push them to the side.
Add the remaining oil and cook the ginger until fragrant, then add the chili and garlic for about 30 seconds and bring everything together.
Stir in the sesame oil, soy sauce and sugar, then add the edamame and toss.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry, turn off the heat and serve warm.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Japanese Hamburger Steak

lines.text: 1 tbsp soy sauce in the patties plus 1 tbsp for the wafu sauce
1 tbsp rice vinegar for the wafu sauce

instructions: Wrap the tofu in a towel and squeeze out as much water as you can, then crumble it into a bowl.
Finely chop the onion and shiitake and mix them into the tofu with the oats, soy sauce, nutmeg, paprika and black pepper until it holds together.
Divide the mixture in two and shape each half into a flat oval patty.
Heat the coconut oil in a pan over medium heat and pan-fry the patties until browned on both sides.
Stir the remaining soy sauce and the rice vinegar together for the wafu sauce, and top the patties with the sauce, grated daikon and shiso.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Lentil Meatballs with Swedish Sauce

lines.text: 15 oz cooked brown or green lentils
2 1/2 cups mushroom broth or vegetable stock
1 tsp in the meatballs plus 3 tbsp vegan Worcestershire sauce in the sauce — use The Wizard's Organic Vegan Worcestershire

instructions: Stir the ground flax with 2 tablespoons of water and leave it for 5 to 10 minutes to thicken into a flax egg.
Pulse the lentils, panko, red onion, allspice, nutmeg, 1 teaspoon of the Worcestershire sauce and the flax egg in a food processor until well combined.
Roll the mixture into 12 to 15 even balls with a cookie scoop.
Melt 3 tablespoons of the vegan butter in a large skillet over medium heat, brown the meatballs on all sides for 5 to 8 minutes and move them to a plate.
Melt the remaining 3 tablespoons of butter in the same skillet, whisk in the flour, then slowly whisk in the broth, coconut cream, the remaining Worcestershire sauce and the Dijon.
Simmer the sauce for 3 to 5 minutes until thick, return the meatballs to the pan and heat them through for 2 to 3 minutes before serving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Baked Beans on a Jacket Potato

lines.text: 2 (15-oz) cans white beans, drained and rinsed
2 cups fresh spinach, wilted, to top

instructions: Scrub the potatoes, prick them with a fork and bake at 400 F (200 C) for about 60 minutes, until the skins are crisp and the centers are soft.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the shallot with the salt for 3 to 5 minutes, until translucent.
Stir in the garlic powder, then add 1 1/4 cups water, the vinegar, tomato paste, mustard, maple syrup and molasses and stir until smooth.
Add the drained beans, turn the heat to medium-high and let the sauce reduce for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until it coats the beans.
Taste and adjust with more salt, maple syrup, vinegar or molasses, then cover to keep the beans warm.
Split the hot potatoes, spoon the beans over them and top with wilted spinach if using.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Mumbai Street Style Pav Bhaji

lines.text: 3 Tbsp canola oil, divided (replaces the butter)
1 3/4 tsp Kashmiri red chilli powder, divided
2 tsp prepared homemade pav bhaji masala, divided: coriander, cumin, bay leaf, cloves, cardamom, cinnamon, black pepper, fennel, dried chili, turmeric and dry mango only
8 pav — use Rhodes Bake-N-Serv Dinner Rolls, baked without butter, prepared ahead

instructions: Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large kadai, add the onion, ginger garlic paste and capsicum and cook until soft.
Add the tomatoes, peas, 1 tsp of the chilli powder and 1 tsp of the pav bhaji masala and cook until the tomatoes break down.
Stir in the boiled potatoes and mash everything together with a masher, adding a splash of water to loosen it.
Simmer the bhaji for 5 minutes, stirring in the lemon juice and half of the coriander, then taste and adjust the spice.
Heat the remaining oil, stir in the rest of the chilli powder and pav bhaji masala and toast the split pav rolls in it until golden.
Serve the bhaji topped with the remaining coriander, with the toasted pav on the side.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Veg Shami Kebab

lines.text: 2 cups black chickpeas (kala chana), soaked overnight
5 cloves, 1 inch cinnamon, 1 black cardamom and 1/2 tsp pepper

instructions: Pressure-cook the soaked chickpeas with the onion, ginger, garlic, green chilli, whole spices, cumin and coriander seeds and 2 cups of water for about 5 whistles.
Drain off the cooking water and blend the mixture coarsely without adding any water.
Mix in the roasted besan, mint, coriander and lemon juice until the spices are evenly combined.
Grease your hands with oil and shape the mixture into 10 patties.
Shallow-fry the patties in hot oil over medium heat, flipping once, until both sides are golden and crisp.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Curry Eggplant and Potato (Baigan and Aloo)

lines.text: 1 tsp prepared Caribbean green seasoning: olive oil, scallion, garlic, parsley, pimento, Scotch bonnet, cilantro, thyme, celery leaves and roasting pepper only

instructions: Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat and cook the garlic, black pepper, cumin seeds and curry powder for about 2 minutes.
Add the hot peppers, green seasoning and the potatoes cut into chunks and stir to coat them in the spices.
Add the cubed eggplant, which will wilt as it cooks, then pour in 1 cup of water and the salt.
Bring to a boil, reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for about 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the eggplant has broken down into a thick sauce.
Stir in the shado beni or cilantro if using, taste for salt and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Burmese Samosa Soup

lines.text: 1/4 cup kala chana (black chickpeas), soaked overnight

7 prepared potato-pea samosas: wheat pastry, avocado oil, potato, peas, ginger, chili, salt, ajwain, cumin, fennel, coriander, pure asafoetida resin, dry mango and cinnamon-cardamom-clove-black-pepper spice blend only

instructions: Soak the black chickpeas overnight, then drain them.
Dry-roast the besan in a pan for 3 to 4 minutes until fragrant, then whisk it into 1/2 cup of water and set aside.
Heat the oil in the pressure cooker on saute and fry the cumin seeds until they crackle, then cook the onion and garlic with 1/4 teaspoon of the salt for 3 minutes.
Stir in the turmeric, the besan water, the drained chickpeas, the chana dal, 4 cups of water, the remaining salt and the tamarind.
Seal and pressure-cook on high for 20 minutes, then quick-release the pressure.
Ladle the soup into bowls, break the samosas into 3 or 4 pieces each and add them, then top with the shredded cabbage.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Indonesian Tempeh Stew

lines.text: 1 small fresh hot chile, seeded and minced
1 large sweet potato, peeled and diced

instructions: Steam the tempeh for about 10 minutes, then cut it into pieces.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and brown the tempeh on all sides for about 5 minutes, then set it aside.
Heat the remaining oil in a saucepan and cook the shallots, garlic, chile and ginger for about 5 minutes until softened.
Add the sweet potato, 1 cup of water, the crushed tomatoes and the tamari, cover and cook, stirring now and then, for about 20 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Uncover, lower the heat, stir in the coconut milk and tempeh and simmer for about 10 minutes until thickened.
Stir in the cilantro and lime zest just before serving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vada Curry

lines.text: 1 cup chana dal, soaked for 2 hours
2 tablespoons oil for the gravy, plus oil for deep frying the vada
1/2 teaspoon fennel seeds in the vada and 1/2 teaspoon in the tempering
2 green chilies, 1 in the vada and 1 in the gravy
4 tablespoons chopped coriander leaves, 2 in the vada and 2 to finish
1 teaspoon salt, 1/2 teaspoon in the vada and 1/2 teaspoon in the gravy

instructions: Soak the chana dal in water for 2 hours, then drain it.
Blend the dal with 1/2 teaspoon fennel, 1 chili and half the salt into a coarse paste without adding water, then stir in half the coriander leaves.
Flatten small balls of the paste into patties and deep-fry them in hot oil over medium heat until golden and crisp, then drain and break them into pieces.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a wide pan and fry the remaining fennel until aromatic, then cook the onion, ginger garlic paste and the second chili until the onion changes color.
Lower the heat, stir in the turmeric, chilli powder and remaining salt, then add the tomato and cook until soft and mushy.
Pour in 1 cup of water and the coconut milk, cover and boil for 2 minutes, then add the vada pieces and simmer covered for 5 minutes.
Stir in the remaining coriander leaves and serve, thinning the gravy with water if it thickens.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Plant Based Huaraches

lines.text: 14 ounces black beans, cooked, drained and rinsed
3/4 cup diced onion for the beans and the cauliflower, plus 1 1/2 tablespoons diced red onion for the pico
1/2 cup diced tomatoes for the pico
5 1/2 teaspoons low-sodium tamari across the masa, beans, cauliflower and cream
3 tablespoons lime juice, 2 in the cream and 1 in the pico

instructions: Mix the masa harina with the first of the tamari and enough room-temperature water to form a soft ball, knead for a couple of minutes, then cover and preheat a pan.
Divide the dough into thirds, roll each into a 4-inch tube, press it flat between parchment sheets and roll it into a sandal shape.
Peel off the top parchment, flip the base onto the hot pan, peel the other sheet and cook about a minute per side, then keep the bases covered with a towel.
Saute part of the onion and garlic, add the black beans, chili powder and some tamari, cook for 5 minutes and mash into refried beans.
Saute the rest of the onion and garlic, then add the cauliflower, smoked paprika, tamari and 1 cup of water and cook about 15 minutes until tender.
Blend the avocado, scallions, 2 tablespoons of the lime juice, tamari and 1/3 cup water into a smooth cream, and stir the tomatoes, red onion and last tablespoon of lime juice into a pico.
Spread each base with a third of the beans, then add the cauliflower mince, avocado cream and pico.
sourceName: The Whole Food Plant Based Cooking Show
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Potato Rösti with Easy Baked Beans and Sauteed Green Veggies

lines.text: 1 1/2 teaspoons smoked paprika, 1 in the sauce and 1/2 in the rösti
3 tablespoons oil for frying the garlic and the rösti

instructions: Blend the diced tomatoes, then fry the chopped garlic in 1 tablespoon of the oil for a few minutes and stir in 1 teaspoon of the smoked paprika.
Add the blended tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes, then add the white beans and simmer another 15 minutes, seasoning with half the salt.
Grate the peeled potatoes, wrap them in a towel and squeeze out the excess water.
Mix the potatoes with the sliced onion, the remaining paprika, 1/2 teaspoon of the salt and the chickpea flour.
Fry the potato mixture in the remaining oil in a pan, in 2 batches, until golden on both sides.
Saute the diced zucchini in a little of the pan oil, add the spinach with the remaining salt and cook until wilted.
Serve the rösti with the beans, the zucchini and spinach and the sauerkraut.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Cassoulet

lines.text: 200 g dried white kidney beans (about 1 cup), soaked
3 medium carrots, cut into 2 cm chunks
4 sun-dried tomato halves, chopped (about 3 tbsp), soaked in 1/2 cup hot water
2 teaspoons vegetable bouillon powder — use Massel Premium Vegetable Stock Powder (168 g formula)
225 g (about 3 links) unMEAT Sausage (manufacturer Singapore formula), sliced into small pieces

instructions: Soak the dried white beans in plenty of water for 8 hours or overnight, then drain and rinse them.
Soak the chopped sun-dried tomatoes in 1/2 cup hot water until soft, and chop the onion, garlic, ginger, carrots and tomatoes.
On saute mode, heat 1 tablespoon of the oil and cook the onion, garlic and ginger for 2 minutes, then add the carrots for 1 minute.
Add the beans, thyme, sun-dried tomatoes with their water, bouillon powder, cumin and 2 cups of water, then pressure cook on high for 9 minutes and let the pressure fall naturally for 10 minutes.
On the stovetop, simmer covered for about 40 minutes instead.
Brown the sausages in the remaining tablespoon of oil, turning them, then slice them into chunks.
Stir the sausages and tomato wedges into the beans, cover and simmer for 7-10 minutes, adding water if you want it soupier, then serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Menudo

lines.text: 2.5 oz dried white (snow) fungus, about 3 large pieces, soaked 30 minutes
6 cups veggie broth and 2 cups water
1 tbsp olive oil for the onion and garlic saute (estimated; the source says a little)

instructions: Soak the dried snow fungus in cold water for 30 minutes, drain it and cut it into bite-size pieces.
Cut the stems off the chiles, shake out the seeds and dry-roast the chiles in a hot pan without burning them.
Soak the roasted chiles in boiling water for 25 minutes, drain them and blend with 2 cups of the broth.
Saute the onion and garlic in a little olive oil until translucent, then add the blended chiles, the rest of the broth, the water, salt, oregano and cumin.
Add the drained hominy, bring the pot to a boil and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the snow fungus 20 minutes before serving and ladle into bowls.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Omurice

lines.text: 1 tbsp olive oil in the batter, plus olive oil for cooking (about 2 tbsp)

instructions: Whisk the chickpea flour, water and 1 tablespoon of olive oil into a smooth batter, then rest it for 15 minutes and stir in the salt.
Chop the onion, carrot and tofu into small cubes.
Cook the onion, carrot and peas in oil over medium heat for 4-6 minutes, then add the tofu and heat it through.
Add the rice and cook for 2-3 minutes, stir in the tamari for 2-3 minutes, then the ketchup for 1-2 minutes.
Cook the batter in an oiled pan over medium heat, about 5-6 minutes a side, to make 2 omelets.
Spoon the fried rice into the center of each omelet, fold it around the rice, and divide with a little extra rice on the side.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Jjamppong

lines.text: 8 cups water with two 4x4 inch pieces of kombu, soaked at least 30 minutes
220 g extra firm tofu, cut into bite size strips
1/4 small head green, savoy or napa cabbage (120 g), thinly sliced
2-3 baby bok choy (120 g), cut into bite size pieces
handful of mung bean sprouts (70 g)
2 tablespoons fine gochugaru and 1 tablespoon coarse gochugaru

instructions: Wipe the kombu clean with a damp cloth and soak it in 8 cups of water for at least 30 minutes.
Cut the tofu into strips and slice the shiitake, carrot, cabbage and bok choy, then have everything within reach of the stove.
Stir-fry the tofu in 2 tablespoons of hot oil until golden, add the shiitake and cook until golden, then push both to one side.
Add the rest of the oil and the ginger to the empty side, then stir-fry the carrot and cabbage for 1-2 minutes.
Sprinkle over the gochugaru for 15 seconds, pour the soy sauce around the pan, then add the kombu dashi; take the kombu out before the pot boils and simmer for 15-20 minutes.
Boil the noodles 1-2 minutes short of the pack time, drain and rinse them, and divide them between three bowls.
Stir the bok choy and bean sprouts into the soup for 30 seconds to 1 minute, taste, then ladle it over the noodles.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Eggless Salad Sandwich
instructions: Crumble the tofu into a large bowl with your hands, leaving some small chunks.
Add the vegan mayonnaise, celery, green onions, garlic, nutritional yeast, turmeric and mustard, then mix until the tofu is evenly yellow and coated.
Season the filling with salt and pepper if you like and refrigerate it until you are ready to build the sandwiches; it keeps for up to 5 days.
Remove the kale stems and slice the leaves into thin ribbons. Slice the tomato and the cucumber.
Lightly toast the 8 slices of bread if you like.
Pile the tofu filling, kale, tomato and cucumber onto 4 slices, top with the other 4 slices and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Kachori Pinwheels

lines.text: 1/2 cup moong dal (split green mung beans), soaked at least 4 hours

instructions: Drain the soaked moong dal and pulse it in a blender or food processor into a coarse, textured mixture, not a smooth paste.
Warm the oil in a skillet, toast the fennel seeds until fragrant, then stir in the ground coriander, Kashmiri chili, turmeric, garam masala, garlic and ginger for about 30 seconds.
Add the ground dal, chickpea flour and salt. Cook for 3 to 5 minutes until the mixture starts to dry and roast, then splash in a little water and cook 1 to 2 minutes more. Cool completely.
Roll the thawed puff pastry into a larger rectangle, spread the cooled filling over it leaving a half inch border, then roll it up and seal the edge with a little water.
Slice the roll into pinwheels about half an inch thick and set them on a parchment lined baking sheet.
Bake at 400F (205C) for 17 to 19 minutes until golden, checking that the pastry centers are cooked through, and let them rest a few minutes before serving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Spinach Mushroom Tart

lines.text: 2 teaspoons flaxseed meal mixed with water for the crust, plus 1 tablespoon for the filling
6 ounces frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed

instructions: Mix the almond flour, whole wheat flour, half the salt, the crust flaxseed mixed with 2 teaspoons of water and 4 tablespoons of chilled soy milk into a crumbly dough, adding a little more milk if it will not hold together.
Press the dough evenly into a greased 9 inch tart pan, building up the sides, prick the base with a fork and bake at 350F (180C) for 11 to 12 minutes.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet and cook the garlic, onion and mushrooms with a pinch of salt until golden and much reduced, then cool the mixture.
Mash the white beans in a bowl until about three quarters are crushed, then mash in the onion and mushroom mixture.
Stir in the spinach, nutritional yeast, the remaining flaxseed mixed with water and the remaining salt until the mixture spreads easily, then spread it evenly in the baked crust.
Bake at 350F (180C) for 30 to 40 minutes, then let the tart cool for 10 minutes before slicing.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Lentil Sausage Rolls

lines.text: 1 1/2 cups cooked brown or green lentils
2 tablespoons finely chopped sun dried tomato

instructions: Cook the red onion in the oil with a pinch of salt until nicely golden.
Add the lentils, sun dried tomato, walnuts, fennel, sage, oregano, smoked paprika, garlic powder and the remaining salt, and cook 5 to 7 minutes, mashing about half of the lentils.
Roll the thawed pastry out larger and cut it into rectangles of about 2 to 3 by 5 inches.
Shape about 3 tablespoons of filling into a log for each rectangle, roll the pastry around it and seal the seam with a little water.
Set the rolls seam side down on a parchment lined sheet and cut a small vent in each one.
Bake at 400F (205C) for 18 to 20 minutes until golden brown and let them cool a few minutes before serving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Empanadas

lines.text: 15 oz can black beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Mix the flour with the coconut yogurt and a splash of water until it forms a dough, knead gently until smooth, then cover and rest it while you make the filling.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot and cook the onion for 2 to 3 minutes, then add the garlic, red pepper and corn and cook 5 to 6 minutes more.
Stir in the black beans, tomato paste, paprika, cumin and salt and cook another 5 minutes, then let the filling cool completely.
Preheat the oven to 350F (180C). Divide the dough in half, roll each piece out thin and cut it into rounds.
Put a spoonful of filling on each round, wet the edge with water, fold it over and seal with a fork, then set the empanadas on a lined baking tray.
Bake for about 15 minutes until lightly golden and serve with tomato salsa.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Tater Tot Casserole

lines.text: 1 15 ounce can red beans, drained and rinsed
1 15 ounce can black beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Preheat the oven to 450F (230C), or the temperature on the tater tot bag.
Heat the olive oil in an oven-safe pot, cook the onion, pepper and garlic about 5 minutes until the onion turns translucent, then lower the heat and stir in the chickpea flour for 3 minutes.
Slowly whisk in the soy milk, add the chili powder and simmer about 15 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce is thick enough to hold a trail when you drag a spoon across the pan.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the vegan cheese shreds while the sauce is hot, then mix in the red beans, black beans and corn.
Arrange the tater tots in a single layer on top and bake for about 20 minutes, following the bag, until the tots are crisp and golden.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Chilaquiles with Chickpeas

lines.text: 1 1/4 tsp ground cumin (3/4 tsp for the chickpeas, 1/2 tsp for the sauce)
1/2 tsp salt (1/4 tsp for the chickpeas, 1/3 tsp for the sauce)

instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion, garlic, carrot and a pinch of salt for 4 to 6 minutes until golden. Set half of this mixture aside for the sauce.
Stir the chickpeas, 3/4 teaspoon of the cumin, the coriander and 1/4 teaspoon salt into the skillet, cover and cook for 4 to 5 minutes.
Blend the tomato paste, tomato, chipotle, the remaining cumin, the reserved onion mixture, the remaining salt and about a cup of water until smooth.
Slice the corn tortillas and crisp them in a dry pan or oven until firm.
Add the crisped tortillas to the chickpeas, pour the blended sauce over, mix and bring to a boil. Taste for salt and heat.
Serve right away.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Cheesy Vegan Broccoli and Rice Casserole

lines.text: 1/2 cup plus 1 tbsp vegan butter (1 tbsp for the onions, 1/2 cup in the sauce)

instructions: Cook the brown rice and cook the broccoli florets until just tender, then set both aside.
Heat the oven to 350 F. Saute the onion and garlic in 1 tablespoon of the vegan butter for about 3 minutes until soft.
Blend the onion and garlic with the butter beans, oat milk, nutritional yeast, remaining vegan butter, salt, chickpea flour and half of the vegan parmesan for about 5 minutes until smooth and thick.
Mix the broccoli, rice, cheese sauce and 1 1/2 cups of the vegan cheddar in a large bowl.
Pour into a greased 9 by 13 inch dish and top with the remaining cheddar and parmesan.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden and bubbly, then rest for 5 minutes before serving.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Lentil & Eggplant Lasagna

lines.text: 2 medium eggplants, sliced lengthwise 1/4 inch thick
2 tbsp olive oil (1 tbsp for the eggplant, 1 tbsp in the ricotta)
3/4 cup red lentils, rinsed and drained
1/2 tsp sea salt, plus salt for sweating the eggplant

instructions: Salt the eggplant slices on both sides and rest them in a colander for 15 minutes, then rinse and pat them very dry.
Heat the oven to 425 F, brush the slices with some of the olive oil and roast them for 13 to 15 minutes, then lower the oven to 375 F.
Bring the marinara to a low boil, stir in the red lentils and simmer loosely covered for 15 to 20 minutes until the lentils are tender.
Pulse the tofu, lemon juice, nutritional yeast, basil, oregano, salt and the remaining olive oil until semi-smooth, leaving flecks of basil.
Layer lentil marinara, eggplant and tofu ricotta in a 9 by 13 inch dish, finishing with marinara, eggplant and marinara.
Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes, then uncover and bake 10 to 15 minutes more until bubbling.
Rest 10 to 15 minutes before slicing.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Black Pepper Mac and Cheese

lines.text: 1 tsp freshly ground black pepper, divided

instructions: Simmer the potato, carrot, garlic and onion in 2 1/4 cups water in a covered skillet for 17 to 19 minutes until the potato breaks apart easily, then cool slightly.
Cook the elbows until al dente and drain.
Blend the potato mixture with the nutritional yeast, soy sauce, lemon juice, olive oil and a little of the black pepper until smooth.
Return the sauce to the pan over medium heat, stir in the salt and some pepper, and bring to a boil. Adjust the salt and cheesiness.
Stir in the pasta and broccoli, cover and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Rest for 5 minutes, then stir in the remaining black pepper and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Carbonara

lines.text: 7 oz smoked tofu, cut into small cubes

instructions: Cook the whole wheat spaghetti in salted water according to the package, then drain.
Finely dice the onion, cut the smoked tofu into small cubes and chop the parsley.
Pan-fry the tofu cubes in the olive oil over high heat for about 5 minutes until crisp and browned.
Add the onion and cook for 3 more minutes, then stir in the soy sauce and paprika and cook for a minute.
Blend the cashews, soy milk, nutritional yeast, miso and garlic in a high speed blender until smooth. The sauce is thin at first.
Pour the sauce into the pan with the tofu and heat on medium for 1 to 2 minutes until it thickens, then add the parsley.
Toss in the cooked spaghetti, stir well and serve right away with more parsley.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Dairy-Free Fettuccine Alfredo with Silken Tofu

lines.text: 1 cup unsweetened plant milk of choice (soy milk)

instructions: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Meanwhile blend the silken tofu, soy milk, cornstarch, nutritional yeast, salt, pepper, garlic powder and lemon juice until completely smooth.
Cook the fettuccine according to the package directions, then drain it.
Pour the blended sauce into a large saute pan and heat over medium-low until it bubbles, then cook 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until thick and the starch taste is gone.
Stir the pasta into the sauce to coat it, take it off the heat and top with the chopped sun-dried tomatoes.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Pea Pesto Pasta with Sun-Dried Tomatoes and Arugula

lines.text: 1/2 cup packed flat leaf Italian parsley
4 cloves garlic for the pesto plus 2 cloves, chopped
1/4 cup olive oil for the pesto plus 1 Tbsp for the pan

instructions: Bring a large pot of generously salted water to a boil.
Blend the basil, parsley, peas, 4 cloves of garlic, pine nuts, lemon juice and a pinch of salt in a food processor, then stream in 1/4 cup of the olive oil until creamy. Taste and adjust.
Cook the pasta in the boiling water until al dente, drain it and return it to the pot off the heat.
Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large skillet over medium, then saute the 2 chopped garlic cloves and the sun-dried tomatoes for 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant, and take the pan off the heat.
Add the pasta to the skillet and toss, then transfer it to a bowl and toss with about three quarters of the pesto and the arugula. Serve with the rest of the pesto on the side.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Baked Ziti

lines.text: 1/2 medium onion, chopped, plus 1/4 small onion for the bechamel
2 cloves garlic for the mushrooms plus 2 cloves for the bechamel

instructions: Heat the oven to 350 F. Finely chop the mushrooms, toss them with half the onion, 2 cloves of chopped garlic and the tamari, and spread them on a lined baking sheet.
Roast the mushrooms 30 minutes, stirring at 20 minutes. Meanwhile boil the ziti until al dente and make the bechamel below.
For the bechamel, melt the vegan butter on low, soften the rest of the onion and the remaining garlic for 1 to 2 minutes, whisk in the flour a tablespoon at a time and cook 1 minute.
Whisk in the soy milk 1/4 cup at a time, then the nutritional yeast and salt, and stir 5 to 10 minutes until thick.

Stir the marinara through the cooked ziti with half the roasted mushrooms. Layer half in a casserole dish, spoon over half the bechamel, add the rest of the pasta and bechamel, and scatter the remaining mushrooms on top.
Bake 10 to 15 minutes until the sauce is bubbling and the top is golden.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Skillet Gnocchi with Sun-Dried Tomato Garlic Ricotta

lines.text: 12 ounces mini gnocchi — use DeLallo Mini Potato Gnocchi (US 1 lb)
16 to 20 ounces pasta sauce (tomato basil or marinara)
2 ounces frozen spinach, thawed and pressed
2 teaspoons olive oil for the ricotta plus 2 teaspoons for the pan
1/4 teaspoon salt for the ricotta plus 1/4 teaspoon for the gnocchi

instructions: Make the ricotta: crumble the tofu and mix or process it with the nutritional yeast, miso, lemon juice, 1/4 teaspoon of the salt and 2 teaspoons of the olive oil until fairly smooth, then mix in the spinach.
Heat the remaining 2 teaspoons of oil in a large skillet over medium and brown the gnocchi for about 5 minutes, stirring every 30 seconds so more edges turn golden.
Stir in the garlic for about 30 seconds, then the sun-dried tomatoes. Lower the heat and add 1/2 cup of the water.
Dollop the tofu ricotta over the gnocchi and spoon the pasta sauce around it. Pour the remaining 1/2 cup water around the edges, season with the remaining salt and cover.
Simmer covered on low until the gnocchi is cooked through and the sauce is hot, about 12 to 14 minutes, and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Mediterranean Sheet Pan Gnocchi

lines.text: 16 ounce shelf-stable or refrigerated potato gnocchi — use DeLallo Mini Potato Gnocchi (US 1 lb)
1 red bell pepper, chopped into 1/2 to 3/4 inch pieces
1 green bell pepper, chopped into 1/2 inch pieces

instructions: Heat the oven to 400 F and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.

Put the gnocchi, drained lentils, peppers, tomatoes and onion on the sheet. Drizzle with the olive oil, balsamic vinegar and lemon juice, sprinkle with the oregano and salt, and toss to coat and spread evenly.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes, then stir, bringing the center to the edges.
Return to the oven for about 5 more minutes, until the gnocchi is toasty and the vegetables are tender.
Fold in the chopped olives, bake 1 to 2 minutes more to warm them, and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Lemon and Garlic Pasta with White Beans

lines.text: 2/3 cup raw cashews, soaked in boiling water
6 cloves garlic (2 for the sauce, 4 pressed for the pan)
1 can (15 oz) cannellini beans, rinsed and drained
2 cups cherry or grape tomatoes, halved

instructions: Cover the cashews with boiling water and let them soak while you cook the pasta and vegetables.
Boil the pasta in well-salted water until al dente, then drain.
Warm the olive oil and 4 pressed garlic cloves over medium-low heat for 1 minute, then add the beans, tomatoes and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer on low.
Drain the cashews and blend them with 1 cup water, the lemon juice, nutritional yeast, 2 garlic cloves and the remaining salt until very smooth.
Stir the arugula into the beans until wilted, add the pasta and the cashew sauce and stir over medium-low heat until the sauce thickens slightly.
Serve warm.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Smoky Berbere Sheet Pan Veggie Dinner with Tahini Dressing

lines.text: 1 small zucchini, cut into thick slices
1 red bell pepper, cut into thick slices
7 oz firm tofu, pressed and cubed
1 tsp salt (3/4 tsp for the veg, 1/4 tsp for the dressing)
1 1/4 tsp garlic powder (1 tsp for the veg, 1/4 tsp for the dressing)

instructions: Heat the oven to 400 F (205 C). Put the mushrooms, zucchini, bell pepper, broccoli, tofu and beans on a large sheet pan.
Drizzle with the oil and toss to coat, then sprinkle over the berbere, 3/4 tsp of the salt and 1 tsp of the garlic powder and toss until everything is coated.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, moving the vegetables around at the 18 to 20 minute mark so the edges do not scorch.
Whisk the tahini with 1/4 cup warm water, the lemon juice, the remaining salt and garlic powder, adding water until creamy and pourable.
Plate the roasted vegetables, tofu and beans and drizzle with the tahini dressing.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Zucchini Pesto Pasta with Roasted Tomatoes and Chickpeas

lines.text: 5 cups zucchini, halved lengthwise and cut into 1/4-inch slices (about 650 g)
1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
1/4 cup fresh basil leaves, to serve

instructions: Heat the oven to 425 F (218 C) and line two baking sheets with parchment.
Put the zucchini on one sheet and the onion, tomatoes and chickpeas on the other, keeping the chickpeas to one side.
Toss each sheet with half the oil, salt and red pepper flakes and roast for 20 to 30 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the chickpeas are crisp.
Boil the pasta in salted water until al dente while the vegetables roast, then drain.
Return the pasta to the pot, stir in the pesto, then mix in the roasted vegetables and chickpeas.
Serve topped with fresh basil.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Penne alla Vodka

lines.text: 28 oz can whole San Marzano tomatoes in juice

instructions: Cook the onion and garlic in the olive oil over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, then add the red pepper flakes for 1 minute.
Add the whole tomatoes and the vodka and cook 5 to 7 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir in the tomato paste, balsamic vinegar and salt, turn the heat to low, partly cover and simmer for 20 minutes until reduced by half.
Boil the penne in salted water until al dente while the sauce simmers, then drain.
Blend the sauce with the basil until smooth, return it to the pan and stir in the coconut cream until warmed through.
Toss the sauce with the penne and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Baked Rigatoni with Lentil Meat Sauce

lines.text: 28 oz jar marinara or tomato basil pasta sauce

instructions: Heat the oven to 350 F (180 C). Spread the rigatoni in a 9 by 13 inch pan.
Add the marinara, red lentils, balsamic, Italian seasoning, garlic and 2 cups water, mix well, cover with foil and bake for 50 minutes.
Blend the tofu with the olive oil, garlic powder, miso, salt, flour and 1/2 cup water until smooth, and adjust the salt.
Uncover the pan, pour the tofu mozzarella over the pasta and broil for 3 to 4 minutes until browning.
Drizzle with a little olive oil and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Mushroom Walnut Bolognese

lines.text: 1 small head of broccoli, small dice
12 oz whole-wheat spaghetti (the video says serve over any pasta)

instructions: Dice the onions, broccoli and shiitake mushrooms small and mince the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and saute the onions, broccoli and mushrooms for 5 to 10 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic, then add the plum tomatoes, tomato sauce, bay leaf, Italian seasoning and salt, breaking the tomatoes up with a spoon.
Simmer the sauce for 20 to 30 minutes so the flavors come together.
Cook the spaghetti in salted water according to the package while the sauce simmers, then drain.
Stir the chopped walnuts into the sauce, taste and adjust the salt, remove the bay leaf and serve over the spaghetti.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Root Vegetable Stew with Smoked Tofu

lines.text: 500 g potatoes, peeled and cut in 2 cm cubes
300 g smoked tofu, cut into cubes
600 ml vegan vegetable stock — use Pacific Foods Organic Vegetable Broth (US)

instructions: Peel the potatoes, carrots and parsnips and cut them into cubes about 2 cm wide.
Wash and slice the leek into rings, chop the garlic and cube the smoked tofu.
Heat the oil in a large pot and stew the vegetables, garlic and caraway seeds for about 5 minutes.
Pour in the vegetable stock and simmer over medium heat for about 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Season with smoked paprika and salt, add the tofu and heat it through for 2 to 3 minutes.
Serve in bowls sprinkled with chopped parsley.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Homemade Vegan Ravioli

lines.text: 3 tbsp olive oil (2 for the quinoa, 1 for the ricotta)
4 tbsp nutritional yeast (1 for the quinoa, 3 for the ricotta)

instructions: Toss the cooked quinoa with the soy sauce, Italian seasoning, 2 tablespoons of the oil and 1 tablespoon of the nutritional yeast, then bake at 375 F for 30 to 35 minutes, stirring once, until brown and crisp.
Blend the tofu, cashews, spinach, onion, garlic, the remaining oil and 3 tablespoons nutritional yeast into a smooth ricotta.
Whisk the two flours, make a well, stir in 1 cup warm water and knead into a slightly sticky dough.
Roll the dough very thin in four batches and cut it into 3-inch squares.
Mix the ricotta with the baked quinoa, put 1 tablespoon on a square, cover with a second square and seal the edges with wet fingers and a fork.
Boil the ravioli for about 5 minutes until they float, then drain and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Whole Wheat Pizza with Tomato, Garlic and Coconut Mozzarella

lines.text: 1/2 cup whole wheat flour plus 2 tbsp for dusting
3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil (1 for the dough, 2 for brushing)
2/3 tsp salt (1/3 in the dough, 1/3 in the cheese)

instructions: Mix the warm water, sugar and yeast and let it sit for 5 minutes, then knead in the flour, gluten, half the salt and 1 tablespoon oil for 2 minutes.
Cover the dough and let it rise for 1 1/2 hours, then knead again for 2 minutes and shape it into a ball.

Warm the coconut milk, whisk in the agar powder until dissolved, add the remaining salt, whisk in the tapioca starch mixed with 1 tablespoon water, and pour into an oiled container to set in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 410 F. Roll the dough out thin on a lined sheet and brush it with oil.
Top with sliced tomatoes, garlic, salt and herbs, then the sliced coconut mozzarella.
Bake for 13 to 14 minutes, broil briefly, and serve.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: BBQ Chickpea Tortilla Pizza

lines.text: 3 tbsp BBQ sauce — use Sweet Baby Ray's Original Barbecue Sauce (UK cane-sugar formula)

instructions: Heat the oven to 425 F and put the flatbreads on a baking sheet.
Top each one with sliced tomato and red onion.
Toss the chickpeas with the BBQ sauce until coated and spread them over the vegetables, adding a little more sauce if needed.
Add the sliced mini peppers and a pinch of salt.
Scatter the shredded non-dairy cheese over the top.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, depending on the flatbread.
Sprinkle with parsley or cilantro, slice and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Butter Bean Parmigiana

lines.text: 4 ounces frozen spinach, thawed and lightly squeezed
1 can (15 ounces) butter beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat the oven to 400 F (205 C).
Mix the thawed spinach, crumbled tofu, nutritional yeast, Italian seasoning, onion powder, garlic powder and salt in the baking dish and spread it flat.
Lay the drained butter beans over the spinach and tofu mixture.
Pour the marinara over the beans and sprinkle with the balsamic vinegar, then drizzle with olive oil.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the sauce is bubbling.
Let the dish rest for a few minutes, then spoon it out warm.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Crispy Gnocchi with Muhammara Bean Dip

lines.text: 16 ounces potato gnocchi — use DeLallo Mini Potato Gnocchi (US 1 lb)

instructions: Toast the walnuts in a dry skillet over medium-low heat for 3 to 5 minutes until they smell nutty.
Heat the oven to 410 F (210 C). Toss the gnocchi, half of the beans and the cauliflower with half the oil, cumin, paprika and salt on an oiled tray.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until the gnocchi are crisp outside and the cauliflower is cooked.
Meanwhile, grind most of the walnuts in a food processor, then add the garlic, roasted peppers, remaining beans, pomegranate molasses, lemon juice and remaining oil.
Blend the dip until mostly smooth with some texture left from the walnuts, and taste for salt.
Spread the dip on a plate, top with the crisp gnocchi mixture and sprinkle with the remaining chopped walnuts.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Soup au Pistou

lines.text: 6 tablespoons olive oil, 2 for the soup and 1/4 cup for the pistou
1 can white beans, drained and rinsed
4 large chard leaves, chopped, stems included
2 cups fresh basil for the pistou

instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large pot and sweat the onion with a pinch of salt until translucent.
Add the fennel and garlic and cook a few minutes, then stir in the carrots and cook about 8 minutes more.
Add the drained tomatoes, vegetable broth and white beans and simmer 20 to 30 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Meanwhile, grind the basil, a little garlic, a pinch of salt and the remaining oil into a pistou in a mortar or food processor.
Stir the chard and the pasta into the soup and simmer about 10 minutes until the pasta is cooked.
Stir in the nutritional yeast, taste for salt and serve each bowl with a spoonful of pistou.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: White Bean Tomato Mushroom Soup
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion with salt and pepper until soft and lightly browned.
Stir in the squash and celery, then add the mushrooms and cook until they soften.
Add the garlic and stir for a minute.
Pour in the broth and tomatoes, add the beans and the bundle of thyme, and simmer for 30 minutes until thickened.
Remove the thyme stems, stir in the balsamic vinegar and the chopped kale, and cook about 5 minutes until wilted.
Taste for salt and pepper and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Beoseot Jeongol

lines.text: 3 ounces Korean radish, cut into big chunks
1 piece dried kelp (dashima), about 3 inch square
1 small onion, half in chunks for the broth and half sliced

instructions: Simmer the radish chunks, kelp, the onion chunks and 5 cups water for about 15 minutes, then discard the vegetables and kelp and season the broth with the soy sauce.
Soak the glass noodles in warm water until they soften, then drain them.
Slice the mushrooms about a quarter inch thick, or split the oyster mushrooms into bite size pieces, and cut the cabbage, tofu, carrot, sliced onion and scallions.
Arrange the mushrooms, cabbage, carrot, onion, tofu and scallions in clusters in a shallow pot and scatter the garlic over the top.
Pour in about 2 cups of the broth and boil over medium to medium high heat for 4 to 5 minutes until the mushrooms soften.
Add the noodles and more broth as you eat, cooking until the noodles are tender, and serve hot from the pot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Vegan Budae Jjigae

lines.text: 150 g unMEAT Sausage (manufacturer Singapore formula), sliced into small pieces
150 g vegan luncheon meat, about 4 slices — use unMEAT Luncheon Style Meat (manufacturer Singapore formula)
162 g Hakubaku Organic Dry Ramen (Australian formula) (2 portions), cooked according to the pack

instructions: Stir the gochujang, gochugaru, garlic and soy sauce into a smooth soup base and set it aside.
Pan-fry the vegan luncheon meat in a nonstick pan until lightly browned and firm, then slice it if needed.
Saute the kimchi in a medium pot over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes, then stir in the soup base.
Arrange the shiitake, king oyster mushrooms, tofu, luncheon meat and sliced sausage around the pot.
Pour in the vegetable broth, cover and bring to a boil, then cook until the mushrooms soften. Add salt if needed.
Add the noodles and cook until chewy, then serve hot straight from the pot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Pearl Barley Soup
instructions: Rinse the pearl barley in a colander under cold water and leave it to drain for a few minutes.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and cook the onion, carrot, celery, swede, mushrooms and garlic for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Add the thyme, bay leaves and salt and cook for 1 minute.
Add the barley and vegetable stock, bring to a boil, then simmer for 35 minutes until the barley is chewy with no hard centre.
Remove the bay leaves, ladle into bowls and serve hot.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Greek Black-Eyed Peas Salad

lines.text: 2 roasted red peppers from the jar, diced
1 heaping teaspoon dried oregano, plus 1 teaspoon for the dressing

instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil, add the black-eyed peas and cook for 25 minutes if soaked overnight or 40 to 45 minutes if not, until tender.
Drain the beans in a colander and tip them into a large bowl.
Pour the vinegar over the warm beans, season with salt and pepper and toss.
Add the scallions, roasted red peppers, tomatoes, capers and dill.
Whisk the olive oil, Dijon mustard and oregano in a small bowl, pour over the salad and toss to coat.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve right away or chill for 1 to 2 hours.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chipotle Black Bean Tortilla Soup

lines.text: 1 1/2 cups chipotle salsa — use Pace Chipotle Picante Sauce Medium (US)

instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion, garlic and red pepper with a pinch of salt for 4 to 5 minutes until the onion is translucent.
Stir in the cumin and chili powder, then add the salsa and vegetable stock and bring to a low boil.
Add the black beans and corn, lower the heat, cover and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir in the lime juice and taste for salt.
Ladle into bowls and top with tortilla chips.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Chickpea & Rice Tortilla Soup

lines.text: 2 tbsp vegetable oil, 1 for the soup and 1 for the tortilla chips
2 tbsp homemade burrito seasoning: mix 2 tsp ground cumin, 2 tsp paprika, 1 tsp dried oregano and 1 tsp pure garlic powder
2 vegetable bouillon cubes in 6 cups boiling water — use Massel 7's Vegetable Stock Cubes (7-pack)
4 large soft flour tortillas — use Mission Burrito Restaurant Style Flour Tortillas (US)
3/4 tsp salt in total, 1/4 tsp for the soup and 1/2 tsp for the tortilla chips

instructions: Heat half the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and cook the onion and garlic for 2 to 3 minutes until translucent.
Add the tomatoes and burrito seasoning and cook for 2 minutes, stirring often.
Add the boiling water with the bouillon, the chickpeas, rice and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt, bring to a simmer and cook uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes until the rice is cooked.
While the soup cooks, heat the oven to 400 F (200 C) and cut each tortilla into 12 pieces.
Toss the tortilla pieces with the remaining oil and salt, spread on lined trays and bake 3 to 4 minutes, flip and bake 3 to 4 minutes more until toasted at the edges.
Ladle the soup into bowls and serve with the tortilla chips.
license: Aptiva adaptation in its own words

title: Fire-Roasted Tomato and Mung Bean Soup
instructions: Soak the mung beans in cool water overnight (or at least 6 hours), then drain.
Simmer the soaked beans in 3 cups of water for 17 to 23 minutes until tender but not mushy, then drain and set aside.
In a large pot over medium heat, saute the diced onion in 3 tablespoons of water for 4 to 5 minutes until tender and lightly golden.
Add the carrots and celery and cook 4 to 5 minutes more, stirring often.
Stir in the zucchini, green beans, fire-roasted tomatoes, broth, salt and pepper, bring to a low boil, add the cooked mung beans and simmer 10 to 15 minutes.
Add the kale, cook 5 minutes, rest off the heat for 5 minutes and serve with minced garlic on top if you like.

title: Chana Chaat

lines.text: 1/2 tsp prepared homemade chaat masala: cumin, coriander, dried ginger, chili, black pepper, cloves, nutmeg, mint, dry mango, salt and pure asafoetida resin only

instructions: Put the boiled chickpeas in a large mixing bowl.
Add the chili powder, chaat masala, salt, green chutney and tamarind chutney and mix until everything is coated.
Fold in the chopped onion, tomato, cucumber and boiled potato, then move to a serving bowl.
Just before serving, top with the sev and chopped coriander.

title: Thai Salad with Chickpea Carrot Crumble

lines.text: 2 large carrots, one for the crumble and one sliced
2 cups crunchy lettuce or baby greens

instructions: Pulse the peanuts and ginger in a food processor to a coarse mixture.
Add the chickpeas and one grated carrot and pulse until crumbly, then taste and adjust.
Chop the lettuce, slice the second carrot and the cucumber, chop the bell pepper and cilantro.
Whisk the soy sauce, minced garlic, rice vinegar, sugar and a splash of water for the dressing.
Toss the lettuce, vegetables and cilantro, top with the chickpea carrot crumble and dress generously.
Serve right away so the lettuce stays crisp.

title: Kale Caesar Salad with Crispy Chickpea Croutons
instructions: Heat the oven to 375 F, toss the chickpeas with the coconut oil and garlic powder and spread them on a baking sheet.
Roast the chickpeas for 40 to 45 minutes, shaking the pan a few times, until golden and crisp.
Blend the tahini, hemp seeds, nutritional yeast, capers, Dijon, lemon juice, garlic and 1/4 cup water until smooth.
Wash the kale, strip the stems and tear the leaves into a large bowl.
Pour on the dressing and massage the kale until soft, then top with the chickpeas and pumpkin seeds.

title: Vegan Cobb Salad with Tempeh Bacon

lines.text: 2 tablespoons maple syrup, 1 for the tempeh and 1 for the dressing

instructions: Heat the oven to 350 F, line a baking sheet, slice the tempeh into thin strips and toss them with the olive oil, tamari, 1 tablespoon maple syrup and liquid smoke.
Spread the tempeh on the sheet and bake 35 to 40 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and lightly crisp, then let it cool.
While the tempeh bakes, steam or boil the corn for 5 to 7 minutes and slice the kernels off the cob.
Shake the tahini, lemon juice, 1 tablespoon maple syrup and a few tablespoons of water in a jar until pourable.
Divide the greens, corn, tomatoes, chickpeas and sliced avocado among four bowls, crumble the tempeh on top and drizzle with the dressing.

title: Vegan Greek Salad

lines.text: 2 Roma tomatoes, cored and cut into wedges

instructions: Chop the romaine, cucumber, green pepper and tomatoes, thinly slice the red onion, and add them to a large salad bowl with the olives.
Crumble the tofu feta over the vegetables.
Whisk the vinegar, mustard, agave, crushed garlic and oregano in a small bowl until combined.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss with tongs until everything is coated, then serve right away.

title: Vegan Nicoise Salad

lines.text: 1/2 cup pitted Nicoise or kalamata olives
1 can (15 ounces) chickpeas, drained and rinsed (about 1 1/4 cups)
2 1/2 teaspoons Dijon mustard (some for the chickpeas, some for the dressing)

instructions: Boil the whole small potatoes in lightly boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes until a knife slides off easily, then drain, cool and slice into quarter-inch rounds.
While the potatoes cook, blanch the green beans in boiling water for 2 to 4 minutes until bright green with a slight crunch, then chill them in ice water, drain and pat dry.
Stir the drained chickpeas with part of the mustard, the maple syrup and the sunflower seeds, mashing a few chickpeas to add texture.
Shake the shallot, remaining mustard, vinegar and olive oil in a jar until emulsified.
Divide the lettuce between two plates and arrange the chickpeas, green beans, potatoes, olives and tomato on top.
Serve with the vinaigrette on the side. Keep extra dressing sealed and add it just before eating.

title: Crunchy Thai Kale Salad

lines.text: 4 to 5 cups packed curly or lacinato kale
1 tablespoon lime juice (about 1 teaspoon for the kale and the rest in the sauce)

instructions: Press the tofu gently in a towel for 5 minutes, cube it and toss the cubes in the sesame seeds.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, brown sugar and most of the lime juice, then stir in hot water a spoonful at a time until the sauce pours.
Massage the kale for about a minute with the remaining lime juice, sesame oil and maple syrup until it softens.
Move the kale to a bowl and top with the carrot, radish and sesame tofu.
Drizzle the peanut sauce over the salad and serve right away.

title: Greek Lentil Soup (Fakes)

lines.text: 1 pound dry green or brown lentils

instructions: Cover the lentils with plenty of water, bring to a boil, then drain and set aside.
Cook the onion and carrots in the olive oil over medium heat for about 10 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and cook for 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the lentils, bay leaves, pureed tomatoes and oregano, pour in water to cover the lentils by an inch, and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, cover and simmer for about 30 minutes until the lentils are tender, adding water if needed.

title: Classic Spanish Chickpea Salad

lines.text: 20 oz canned chickpeas (570 g, about 2 cups), drained and rinsed

instructions: Rinse the chickpeas, drain them well and pat them dry, then tip them into a large bowl.
Chop the pepper, tomatoes and onion, slice the olives, and add them to the bowl with the parsley.
Whisk the olive oil, vinegar, grated garlic, salt and pepper in a small bowl.
Pour the dressing over the salad and fold gently until everything is coated.
Cover and chill for 2 hours, then serve in a dish.

title: Hesaru Bele Carrot Kosambari

lines.text: 1/2 cup moong dal, soaked 30 to 60 minutes and drained

instructions: Soak the moong dal for 30 to 60 minutes, then drain it well in a strainer and leave it to dry for a few minutes.
Mix the drained dal with the grated carrot, coconut and chopped coriander in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a small pan, crackle the mustard seeds, then fry the urad dal until red.
Add the curry leaves and asafoetida for a few seconds, then pour the tempering over the salad.
Just before serving, add salt and lime juice, mix well and top with the pomegranate seeds.

title: Creamy Corn Chowder

lines.text: 3 ears corn, charred, kernels cut from the cob
7 oz firm tofu, pressed and crumbled
1/2 cup non-dairy yogurt, as the non-dairy cream — use So Delicious Unsweetened Plain Coconutmilk Yogurt

instructions: Char the corn over a flame or hot pan, turning often, then cut the kernels from the cobs.
Toss the crumbled tofu with the soy sauce and half the paprika, spread it on a lined tray and bake at 400F (205C) for 25 minutes, stirring once.
Heat the oil in a pot, fry the garlic briefly, then cook the onion for 3 to 5 minutes and the carrot and celery for 2 minutes more.
Add the remaining paprika, potatoes, charred corn and stock, cover and simmer for about 15 minutes until the potatoes are very soft.
Stir in the non-dairy yogurt and bring back to a simmer, then blend part of the soup for creaminess, ladle into bowls and top with the tofu crumbles.

title: Creamy Chickpea Soup

lines.text: Sea salt to taste, about 1/2 tsp

instructions: Saute the onion, garlic, carrot and leek in 2 tbsp of the oil for 6 to 7 minutes, then stir in the paprika and cumin and take the pan off the heat.
Blend the chickpeas with their liquid until smooth, add the cooled vegetables, salt and pepper, and blend again.
Return the puree to the pan over low-medium heat and whisk in up to 1 cup of water until creamy, then simmer.
In a second pan, wilt the spinach in the remaining oil in batches and season with salt and pepper.
Ladle the soup into shallow bowls and top with the spinach.

title: West African Peanut Lentil Soup

lines.text: 2 tbsp peanuts, half in the soup and half to garnish

instructions: Soften the chopped onion in a splash of the stock over medium heat for about 5 minutes.
Blend the tomatoes, garlic, ginger, cumin and coriander until smooth, add to the pan and cook for 5 to 6 minutes.
Stir in the peanut butter, half the peanuts, the lentils, sweet potato and remaining stock, cover and simmer.
Stir at 15 minutes, then add the spinach and cook 5 minutes more until the lentils and sweet potato are tender.
Serve topped with the remaining peanuts.
